title: L.G. 32" Smart TV
body:
I purchased this T.V. on Amazon Prime Day as I thought it seemed like pretty good value for a 32" smart T.V. from L.G. who are a leading player in the T.V. market. Bought to replace an aging Polaroid 24" HD T.V. and an ancient Huawei "You View" box which was a freebie from my old broadband supplier donkey's years ago. It was painfully slow and had issues with screen freeze which required rebooting every couple of weeks or so. Rebooting took about 5 minutes and it was becoming a bit of an annoyance.

This smart T.V. is a revelation compared to my old 24" T.V. and set top box. Gone is the lag in boot time, and the T.V. menu and access to your apps is almost instant compared to my old set up. It does sometimes take a few seconds to load some of the T.V. programmes in the T.V. guide, but compared to my old set top box, it is lightening fast. The Web OS interface is easy to use and you can access different apps via the web store. Very easy to set up out of the box by just connecting the T.V. to your WiFi and aerial, and you will need to sign into your different apps, but I found it a relatively painless and pretty straightforward.

I did read quite a few of the reviews before purchasing this T.V. and one thing that kept coming up was that the L.G. standard remote that comes with the T.V. is a bit "meh". This did prove to be the case, but I took a punt and ordered an L.G. "Magic" remote from Amazon which was about £20 and it works perfectly with this T.V. Much better and easier to use than the one that came with the T.V. It has voice control and a mouse type pointer and scroll wheel which makes it a lot easier to navigate the operating system with. Definitely worth the upgrade from the L.G. standard remote which comes with the set.

One thing which is a little annoying compared to my old set top box, is that you don't seem to be able to select programmes from the T.V. guide to watch as catch up. Also accessing the list of programmes which have already been aired is awkward and not just a matter of scrolling back to the left of the timeline from the current programmes. It doesn't seem to have live playback so you can pause the T.V. programme, make a cup of tea, and return the the programme by pressing play. This was tried with a USB flash drive inserted for storage but it kept saying "storage device not compatible with live playback", or words to that effect. I ordered a PCIe SSD to use in an external enclosure via the USB-A input with a USB 3.2 cable and it seems to have solved the problem although it did cost an extra £30. At least I can access live playback now.

This is a decent smart T.V. for the price I paid (about £130) and it is a lot faster than my old set up. I am happy with the full HD resolution but it is only available in HD terrestrial channels for BBC, Channel 4, ITV3 and Channel 5. All other terrestrial channels are not as crisp and well defined although you get the full resolution in apps. Apart from that this is a pretty decent T.V. for the price I payed on Amazon Prime Day. Some features, or rather the lack of them, are a bit annoying, but overall I am happy with my purchase.

title: User interface tediously slow and clunky
body:
I bought the latest 2024 model. My wife wanted a TV with a white bezel for the kitchen!

Most TV reviews focus on the picture quality. But I think usability is just as important. This TV has a good picture but has deficiencies in the TV interface. The program guide can take several seconds to appear each time. And often the TV sound and picture stop until the guide is displayed (or dismissed). It sounds trivial but is something we use quite a lot and is incredibly annoying. My feeling is that the TV has a slow, cheap CPU that can't multitask properly and it probably has too little memory to store the guide as it is retrieved every time.

In addition, unbelievably, there is no Info button on the remote. So if you want to get a brief description of the current program, the only way is to bring up the guide, with all the problems previously mentioned.

I could also go on about things like lack of an Exit button to get back to live TV from an app. But you get the picture. Overall the user interface is tediously slow and clunky.

I have TVs that are many years old and have a better interface. On a modern TV this is just unacceptable.

Modern manufacturers seem to be ignoring live TV and focusing on apps. This is plain stupid, especially on a cheap TV like this which will probably be used by older people, in kitchens etc.

In any case, I won't be buying LG TVs in the future. I'll stick with Samsung which has a good user interface and an excellent picture.

title: Exactly what a living-room TV should be: crisp QLED picture, slick Fire TV, smart extras that matter
body:
I don’t usually leave long reviews, but this 65" Xiaomi really surprised me—in a good way.

Setup was painless. From unboxing to watching took minutes: screw on the feet, plug in, and Fire TV walked me through Wi-Fi and app logins without any faff. The TV itself looks premium for the price: slim bezels, neat finish, and it blends into the room instead of dominating it.

Picture quality is the headline. The QLED panel is bright and colourful, but still looks natural. HDR10+ support gives films real punch without blowing out highlights, and “Filmmaker Mode” is a great touch—it dials back the over-processing so movies look as intended. For sport, I left the motion smoothing on a low setting and football/F1 looked fluid without the weird soap-opera effect.

Gaming is better than I expected at this price. Switch on the Game/Boost mode and input lag drops noticeably—racing and shooters feel snappy and responsive. I’m not chasing spec sheets; I just know my controller inputs feel instant and smooth.

Sound is perfectly decent for a slim TV—clear dialogue and enough body for everyday viewing. I added a soundbar later for cinema nights, but you can happily live with the built-ins if you’re not chasing thunderous bass.

The smart side is excellent. Fire TV is quick and familiar, with all the main apps ready to go and sensible recommendations. Alexa voice control saves loads of scrolling. A big bonus for me is Apple AirPlay—it makes it effortless to throw photos or videos from my phone up on the screen, and guests can cast without faffing about.

A few practical things buyers will care about:

• Remote pairs instantly and works reliably from any angle.

• Wi-Fi has been stable; no random dropouts during matches or films.

• Plenty of ports for a console and streaming box, plus optical out if you’re using an older sound system.

Minor niggles: like most slim TVs, the speakers won’t rattle your windows (a soundbar fixes that), and you’ll want to play with picture presets for your room lighting—but that’s true of every TV I’ve owned.

Verdict: If you want a big-screen QLED with genuinely useful smart features, solid gaming responsiveness, and a premium look without the premium price, this Xiaomi nails it. After a week of films, sport, and gaming, I’m genuinely impressed. Easy 5 stars.

body:
For full transparency, this TV was provided to us for review, however the review will be completely honest.

This TV has a 55” QLED screen, and is roughly 4ft in width, so it’s not a small unit.  It comes with legs which are screwed into the base, but it can also be attached to a wall bracket (available separately).  Setup was very easy via their app; straightforward and no issues.

The quality of the picture is absolutely stunning, and the colour rendition is first class. Reds look vibrant and natural, without abnormal luminosity, and bright colours don’t bleed into each other.

There are plenty of ports for external devices, including 4 x HDMI, which makes connecting multiple devices a breeze.  Previously we had fewer ports, so it was a bit of a nightmare having to swap cables.

Apps are plentiful, and there are an enormous number available, including apps to view live TV. The main players, such as Netflix, Apple TV. Disney+, Amazon Prime Video, etc, are also available via a direct button on the remote control, which saves a lot of flicking through menu’s, it’s literally one press and you’re there.  They’ve even included a web browser!

The apps load really fast, and it detects when an external device is turned on and switches to that device automatically.  Everything is quick and responsive.

We’ve tested a number of different devices, such as Apple TV, Sky Q, Xbox, in addition to live TV and streaming, and no matter what device you are using, the quality is superb.  Even watching something which is only in 1080i HD, this TV still makes it look top quality.  It is almost like looking through a window at the real world, it’s that good.

Sound quality is really good, for built in speakers. We have tested this using both the built in speakers, and also via a sound bar with sub woofer, and we’ve not experienced any issue with sound out of sync, as we have with other TVs. Although the built in speakers can’t compare to an external sound bar, it’s nonetheless impressive.

There are different picture modes which automatically switch, such as filmmaker mode, which improves the viewing experience based on signals from the feature being screened.  There are lots of customisable options, so you can change the look to suit your personal preference.  I can’t see how anyone could be unhappy with the quality, particularly as it is so customisable.

My wife is never normally impressed by tech, but she has been extremely happy with the quality of this TV, and has commented several times about the superb quality, and that is highly unusual.

Game mode has changed the Xbox gaming experience for me. It’s smooth and immersive, and it really makes you feel like part of the game.  The TV will automatically detect the gaming console, and will adjust the refresh rate, and switch to gaming mode, automatically.  Again, everything is seamless, and the manufacturers has seemingly thought of everything.  Playing dark games during the day is no longer a problem, whereas previously it was hopeless, largely due to lack of detail in the dark areas; this TV addresses all of those issues.

The blacks, whites, and contrast are really well balanced, and coupled with a matt, rather than glossy, screen, makes it much easier, and more pleasant, to watch, especially in bright daylight. This has literally been a game changer for playing dark Xbox games in bright daylight.

The only negative is the Alexa voice control, which is useless, but that’s is more the fault of the Alexa skill than the TV.  The Alexa volume is really loud in comparison to the volume of programme being watched, which makes it unusable for me.  I wouldn’t recommend the voice control, but to be honest it’s not really needed for TV control.

Overall, this television is hard to fault. It excels in all areas, and I can highly recommend it.  You definitely will not be disappointed.

body: After living with the Hisense 43Q7STUK for a few weeks, I can honestly say it has exceeded my expectations. I wasn’t looking for anything overly complicated, just a TV with a great picture and easy-to-use features, and it delivers on both. The first thing that stood out was how straightforward everything was. From taking it out of the box to getting it connected and ready to watch, the whole process was refreshingly simple. Within a short time I was signed into my streaming services and browsing through content without needing to dig through manuals or menus. The picture quality is easily the star of the show. Films, sports and everyday TV all look sharp and vibrant, with colours that really stand out without looking unnatural. Even during bright afternoons, when sunlight fills the room, the screen remains clear enough to enjoy without constantly adjusting blinds or curtains. One feature I didn’t expect to use was the children’s remote, but it’s actually a thoughtful addition. It’s simple, colourful and gives younger viewers an easy way to access suitable content, which I can imagine being a real bonus for families. The smart TV interface is well laid out and includes all the apps I regularly use, meaning I’ve been able to retire my streaming stick completely. The dedicated app buttons on the remote are handy too, making it quick to jump straight into whatever I want to watch. There is occasionally a slight delay when navigating menus, but it’s minor and hasn’t affected my overall experience. Considering everything else the TV offers, it’s a small compromise. Overall, this TV feels like a fantastic all-round package. It looks stylish, performs brilliantly and is simple enough for everyone in the household to use. If you’re upgrading from an older set, you’ll definitely notice the difference.

body: Having previously owned a Hisense TV, I was curious to see how much they have improved over the years - and boy was I impressed! Starting with initial set-up. Very easy to use and get started. A QR code allowed access to the app to help set-up go smoothly and I was up and running within a few minutes. The user interface is very easy to use and intuitive to find your way about. Using the smart on demand features, finding apps, setting up your sound and pictures preferences - all very easy to utilise. The picture quality is superb - colours are rich and vibrant, blacks are clear and the auto adjustment features on the TV are great to ensure maximum quality when viewing darker movies. I particularly like the function where it automatically senses if a movie you are watching has Filmaker mode and it automatically switches to this to enhance your viewing.  The AI motion adjustments are great too - avoiding the motion blur effects you get with some TVs. This is particularly great when gaming - smooth motions and movements making it great to play on. Sound is very good too - a massive upgrade on previous Hisense models.  The remote is very easy to use and a good size - feels nice in your hands and the quick access to the most popular streaming apps makes for seamless switching between what your watching. Overall I am very impressed with this TV. It's an excellent choice for someone looking for a great quality TV for their living room or bedroom - great for movies, shows, streaming and gaming - all round, I highly recommend this TV.  5 Stars!

body:
I've previously had Hisense TVs so you would think I knew what I was in for — Wrong! I expected minor improvements but I was very pleased with what I saw. Let's go through some of the specs that matter and made a difference to my experience: - VIDAA smart platform — THIS IS THE ONE THAT REALLY SOLD ME THIS TV. VIDAA is a lightweight Linux-based smart TV platform. What this means to us is that you can launch apps like Netflix or YouTube really fast and smooth, adding to the overall experience. No more wondering what the hell happened to the app you just started — it's just there, instantly. - Hi-QLED with Quantum Dot colour — The screen is brighter and richer than my previous TV, which was already quite impressive. Colours feel more true-to-life and punchy without looking over-saturated. A genuine step up. - 144Hz panel — I don't think this made as much difference to me personally as it did to my 9-year-old son. The feedback is that gaming is smoother and more pleasant. WIN! There are other gaming features too — Game Mode Pro and the updated Game Bar give gamers quick access to VRR, frame rate counters, and input lag settings. Proper stuff. - All the HDR modes — This bad boy supports HDR10+, HDR10+ Gaming, Dolby Vision, Dolby Vision IQ, and HLG — essentially covering every format you're likely to encounter. You're not going to hit a wall with this one. - Hi-View AI Engine (MediaTek Pentonic 700 chip) — Enables enhancements such as AI Picture, AI Light Sensor, AI 4K Upscaling, AI Detail Enhancement, AI HDR Enhancement, and AI Smooth Motion. Basically you're fully "AI'd" up - Filmmaker Mode — Preserves the director's original frame rates and colour intent without any motion processing applied. If you're a film lover, this one matters more than you'd think. The only thing that's potentially not the best is the sound quality. It's OK but not exactly hi-fi, and let's be honest — at this price point you wouldn't expect it to be either. So this review still retains 5 stars. The remote is well laid out with shortcut buttons for all the major apps. It's also Bluetooth, so you don't even have to point it at the TV — which feels delightfully lazy. Ha!
I love this TV so much that I've actually set it up as a second computer monitor. Check out the picture. Overall, I would thoroughly recommend this TV.

body: From the moment I received this 43” TV, I was pleasantly surprised by how lightweight it was; it almost felt deceptive given its size. Unboxing was straightforward, and installing the pedestal feet was simple and stress-free. Although I plan to wall mount it later, the initial setup was smooth and user-friendly. Powering on the TV and setting it up via the VIDAA app was effortless. Downloading the app and connecting it to the TV was quick, and the mobile setup process worked seamlessly. The WiFi connection is strong, allowing the smart interface to run smoothly and making navigation intuitive and easy to use. One of the standout features is Freely, which removes the need for a traditional TV aerial. This is incredibly convenient, simplifying installation and eliminating the hassle of running additional cables or installing an aerial point. In terms of picture and sound quality, both are excellent. The display delivers vibrant, sharp visuals across all types of genres of programs. Sports, in particular, look fantastic; fast-moving scenes are clear, bright, and easy on the eyes, which is perfect for watching events like the World Cup. The sound is also impressive, offering clear and balanced audio across volume levels. While a surround sound system would enhance bass performance, the built-in speakers are more than sufficient for a bedroom setup. If I had one suggestion, it would be to make the feet more centrally positioned. This would provide greater flexibility when placing the TV on different types of furniture. That said, it currently fits on my chest of drawers, though this is only temporary as I intend to mount it on the wall. Overall, this is a great TV with a simple and intuitive navigation system, excellent picture quality and strong, clear audio performance. I had heard of the brand before but never considered purchasing; something I now see was a mistake. This TV proves they can compete with more established brands, especially when considering the excellent value for money."

body:
I don't know where to begin for reviewing my new MASSIVE 85" Hisense TV 85E78STUK PRO. I'm actually even more impressed with it than I was expecting.
The TV it's replacing was a decent 65" TV, so was only expecting a small improvement in the picture and sound quality, and got to admit the thought had crossed my mind that because of the 20" size difference, whatever increase in picture quality with the new telly, would be lost in this increase in size. I was wrong, the sharpness for a start, is much better, as are the depths and vibrancy of colours, proper black blacks, even in a darkened room. The Tv automatically upscales standard signal to 4K. I have not altered the colours in any way, I'm extremely happy with the way they are out of the box so to speak. For the technical it boasts Quantum Dot Colour and Dolby Vision IQ. You do have preset options, like cinema, game mode, sport etc. which again I have not needed to change, although I have used the sport mode to watch football. I was showing the TV off to (jealous) friends though. Same as picture options, there are preset sound options. I've tried the music and cinema sound modes, as with picture modes, there are more options, but can't remember them all. With the sound, I did increase the bass on the graphic equaliser as I like a lot of oomph. For the technically minded it boasts 2 x 15W + 20W speakers and has eARK audio via HDMI. Again for the technical the TV boasts Dolby Atmos and DTS Virtual X decoding for immersive sound. There are plenty of connection options e.g. several HDMI's USB etc., which I won't go into as the specs are on all the sales and Hisense websites. Setting up was simple, from initial setup, to connecting to Wi-Fi. I'd say most apps what you need are pre-installed like Netflix etc. I can't comment on the installed apps as I don't have Netflix account, I almost exclusively use Sky on my TV, which this TV compliments amazingly, the Sky remote pairs easily with the TV, for automatic turning the TV on and off. One slight downside (if you can call it that) I've noticed is you need to check the little white standby light on the bottom of the TV illuminates when turning off, as you can't tell it has gone into a standby state because of the darkness of the black colour. The TV has built in Freely for viewing live TV. This seems good, although only used very briefly when first setting the TV up with using Sky. The TV remote has built in voice control, enabling use of the built in Alexa for example. Can't comment on the use of that as I have Alexa in the room already set up and don't want them fighting over each other. I was pleased to find out this TV only weighs just over 32kg (85" without stand) which is a lot lighter than my previous 65" TV. I must also point out, I measured my chimney breast wall incorrectly when measuring up for the wall bracket/mount and the TV is bigger than my original measurements, so I need to move the wall bracket before I can mount it. I thought, oh no, I've made a terrible mistake, the TV is far too big for the room when I first started viewing, BUT I have quickly become used to the size. So be brave and order the biggest you can fit in your room, you won't regret it.
In a nutshell this TV gets a thumbs up for me, I absolutely love it and don't have one regret in purchasing it. From delivery in its extremely sturdy box, to sitting watching a movie, it has brought an enormous smile to my face. Can't wait till I can get it on the wall. I might then, find even more amazing features that I have probably missed. I haven't mentioned the value for money is also excellent, getting more to the £ than most other manufacturers. I hadn't taken much notice of the brand Hisense until a couple of years ago if I'm honest. Then I looked into their side by side fridge freezers, I was impressed with the build quality, innovation and price. When this TV came on the market and I had a chance of purchasing, I had no qualms on buying Hisense. As in my review, from packaging to use of the item, it's all first class, competition for the best

body: The Hisense 65E7STUK PRO delivers a genuinely impressive viewing experience for its price point. The picture quality is crisp and clear, with strong colour accuracy and sharp detail that really stands out whether you’re watching films, sports, or gaming. Motion handling is very responsive, and the 144Hz Game Mode Pro makes fast‑paced content feel smooth and immediate. The app store is decent, covering all the essentials without feeling bloated. VIDAA is straightforward to navigate, and the TV gives you a good amount of user modifiability — from picture presets to advanced calibration controls, it’s easy to tune the display exactly how you like it. body: Out of the box, the Hisense 50E7STUK PRO TV feels well made, and I was surprised by how light it is, useful for wall mounting. The remote control is easy to use, with buttons well laid out and dedicated buttons for all the major streaming services. Setup was very easy with no TV aerial connection needed. You just plug in the power cable and you’re ready to watch content. Speaking of content, this is the first TV I’ve used with Freely, and I was impressed with the service. There is a couple of seconds delay between switching channels, which takes some getting used to. But the Freely interface, TV guide, and navigation are excellent. After adjusting the picture settings, the quality is very good, with accurate colors and sharp details. The standard settings felt very bright, 100% backlight washed out blacks and made highlights too white. I found Cinema picture mode a good starting point, reducing the backlight to 75, brightness to 45, contrast to 70, color saturation to 60, and sharpness to 0. For my room and lighting, this produced the best results. The TV performs well across all types of content, from regular TV shows and movies to fast-action sports. The sound quality is good for a flat panel TV. I didn’t notice a significant improvement with Dolby Atmos, maybe I would with a compatible external speaker system. Our current amplifier and speakers connect to the TV via HDMI ARC, but the Hisense TV supports HDMI eARC. I need to upgrade our amplifier to use our existing speaker setup.  We connected a FreeSat box via HDMI, switching to this input, the sound was much quieter, we had to increase the volume to compensate. This caused an issue, because switching back to Freely the volume was now too loud. Turning on the auto volume control setting which prevents sudden volume changes when switching inputs, didn’t help. Maybe if’s a compatibility problem but now we have Freely built-in, we probably don’t need FreeSat anymore. Aside from the volume issue, the TV is a pleasure to use. The interface is well laid out, and very responsive. You can organise the home screen moving quicklinks for your favorite services around. Download new apps and mini-games. The games are fun and easy to play, but the ads are frustrating. The built-in screen sharing works seamlessly, letting you wirelessly share your mobile screen. It’s great for quickly playing videos, sharing photos, and more with others.

I recently purchased the Hisense 50U7STUK, initially intending to use it as a bedroom TV. After spending some time with it, I can confidently say it’s a genuinely good product that delivers incredible value for the money, though it definitely brings a "large room TV" energy to a smaller space.
Here is my breakdown of what makes this TV stand out, along with a couple of tips if you plan on setting it up yourself.
### The Screen & Picture Quality
The screen on this TV is absolutely fantastic. Because it uses Mini-LED technology, the contrast is superb. * **Rich Colours:** The Quantum Dot (QLED) tech really shows here. The colors are incredibly vibrant and punchy, making everything from movies to games look incredibly rich and lifelike. * **Very Bright:** This panel gets *seriously* bright. It handles HDR content beautifully and easily fights off daytime glare. However, because it gets so bright, it can almost feel a bit overwhelming in a pitch-black bedroom at night! You might find yourself turning the backlight down before going to sleep.
### Interface & Features
Hisense packs a lot into this model. It comes loaded with features, including support for Dolby Vision, Dolby Atmos, and high refresh rates (144Hz) if you are into gaming.
Despite the mountain of features, the smart interface (VIDAA) is surprisingly snappy and reasonably easy to navigate. It doesn't lag or stutter, and finding my favorite streaming apps was straightforward and intuitive.
### A Note on Wall Mounting (Read Before You Install!)
If you are planning to put this on the wall, **make sure you get the correct screws.** The TV requires specific VESA mounting screws (often M6), and the standard ones that come bundled in generic wall-mount kits might not be the exact length you need. Do yourself a favor and check the TV's manual for the exact screw depth required before you start drilling, or you'll be making an unexpected trip to the hardware store mid-installation.
### The Verdict
I bought this for the bedroom, but honestly, it performs like a premium main-room TV. Between the incredibly bright Mini-LED panel, the rich colors, and the sheer amount of features, it punches well above its weight. Just be prepared for a cinematic, large-room experience right at the foot of your bed—and double-check your wall bracket hardware before you start! Highly recommended."

They have deep base and high treble and the overall sound profile is very punchy and enjoyable. Another advantage of having Mini LED is that is does not have pixel burn in like OLED panels, but the local dimming array offer superb performance in HDR. The IMAX Enhancement also helps to lift the entire experience and this is one of the few products where this certification makes total sense. The built in remote is also quite comfortable and its bluetooth, so I do not need to point it at the TV to control it. Besides that, the remote has a built in microphone as well so I can use voice commands instead of typing manually which is  an absolute lifesaver. The TV also has Google TV built in which is quite versatile and user friendly, making it a breeze to start using right away. The TVs overall brightness is also commendable offering 1600 nits of peak brightness with HDR 10 and dolby vision which allows the user to enjoy supported content at unimaginable colours. Built-in ethernet is also an absolute lifesaver as I can just plug in the TV using a wired connection over wireless which makes the internet connection alot more stable and faster. The processor is also quite rapid and the interface does not lag at all even with multitasking using plex or jellyfin. Overall, I would highly recommend this TV to my friends and family. Its absolutely worth it for the price."

Gamers will love it too — it reacts instantly and won’t get screen burn marks over time. The menu is simple to use, and it connects easily to all your favourite apps like Netflix and YouTube. body: Brilliant TV

Unboxing the 65-inch Hisense U7STUK was a great experience. Straight out of the box, the build quality feels robust, and the nearly borderless, slim bezel gives it an elegant presence in my living room without looking overly bulky. The Mini-LED backlight colour provides fantastic picture quality. Watching movies in Dolby Vision and HDR10+ reveals stunning contrast, with bright highlights through deep, satisfying blacks. Fast-moving sports and action sequences stay crisp without nasty motion blur, this will be great to watch FiFa World Cup 2026. Navigating the VIDAA smart platform is swift and straightforward. Apps load almost instantly, and switching inputs is snappy. The integrated voice control responds well to natural commands, making hands-free searches simple. The remote control feels functional, though its layout takes a brief period to get used to. Acoustically, the built-in sound system supports Dolby Atmos and delivers clear dialogue along with a noticeable punch of bass, which is rare for standard built-in TV speakers. While the audio is great for daily viewing, adding an external soundbar could enhance the deepest cinema low-ends even further.  Ultimately, this display has massively upgraded my home entertainment setup, merging bright performance with serious gaming power.
author: localhost

body: After getting the Hisense 55U7STUK unboxed and mounted on the wall right above my desk, I am incredibly impressed with how it performs as a primary display. At fifty-five inches, the 4K picture quality is incredibly sharp. Because I sit relatively close to the screen at my workstation, the high pixel density makes a massive difference, allowing me to read small text, fine details, and complex instrument dials without any blurring. ​The Mini-LED backlighting is definitely the standout feature for me. The contrast is brilliant, delivering deep, true blacks that make dark or nighttime scenes feel completely immersive. There is no annoying backlight bleed, and the screen gets bright enough to easily handle room reflections during the day. ​What really seals the deal for gaming and fast-paced simulation is the native 144Hz refresh rate. Fast movement is fluid and completely stable, completely eliminating the motion blur I used to get on slower screens. The AI upscaling also does a fantastic job keeping older content looking crisp. On top of the visuals, the built-in subwoofer and audio system offer surprisingly rich, balanced sound right out of the box. It has truly transformed my desktop environment.
author: JayG33

body: I had the opportunity to test the 55U7STUK TV. This is a big step up in picture quality, the TV features the latest MiniLED backlighting technology. This greatly improves lighting control, enhances the contrast, giving the most natural picture possible. It has a powerful processor for detailed blur-free images and you get the optimal contrast levels whatever the time of day and from whichever signal input. The new AI Smooth Motion and AI Sports mode technology makes this TV great for sports and movies as the processing smooths the picture flow. Filmmaker Mode lets you experience the cinematic vision, by using the correct aspect ratio, colour and frame rate.  Game Mode reduces input lag, ensuring quicker reaction times. It's fitted with a built-in subwoofer,  for a deeper bass response and smoother immersive sound. It has the latest Freely TV system with the options of live TV channels and catch-up content. Freely also allows you to ‘pause’ live TV as well as restarting programmes on certain channels. This new service enables the use of just an Internet connection so there is no need for an aerial or satellite dish There’s also one-touch, direct access to the most popular apps - Netflix, Disney+, Amazon Prime etc. It seems the possibilities are endless on this TV and personally I have only just started exploring them all.  What I can say to sum it up is that it is a great way to get a truly cinematic experience in your own living room and it's a gamers dream.

body: Fantastic TV - Quick and easy set up followed by exceptional quality This quality comes in the form of amazingly crisp image for all types of viewing, whether that is film, TV shows or Youtube videos. With particularly bassy shows I sometimes stopped it as I thought that the sound was coming from somewhere else! I particularly love the screen mirroring as it allowed me to show pictures and videos from my camera roll on the big screen without there being a drop in quality over the air. The 50 inch screen also fit perfectly where we wanted it and it has a almost existent bezzle and central stand. This meant we didn't have to change our set up at all. Overall it has been 10/10 - haven't watched so much TV in my life! Would definitely recommend to a friend (and already have!)

body: The Hisense 85U7STUK television made a strong first impression. The design is impressive with a large screen housed in a slim profile. Once installed, the picture is exceptionally crisp and clear with vibrant colours. The Dolby Vision technology produces deep blacks that enhance the colour saturation. The sound quality is also superior to any television I have owned previously. Developed in conjunction with Devialet, it provides a better sound experience for users without an additional soundbar. While the hardware is impressive, the installed software has been somewhat disappointing. The Freely interface is novel and differs from my previous digital television experience. The combination of channels supplied via the aerial and over Wi-Fi is a promising development for the future of television broadcast. The television is capable of processing Dolby Atmos and Dolby Vision but most available apps and installed software only offer basic variations that do not utilise these features. It is surprising that the latest sound and vision technology is provided in the hardware but not accessible through the software.

"Good Picture but. TV arrived well packaged. It was super easy to unbox and fit to my existing wall mount. When you first turn it on it is so easy to follow the instructions to set it up and connect to Wi-Fi etc. It also has a QR code to download the app to your phone which also works good. Once it is all set up I make my first discovery. This is NOT an Android/Google TV. It has its own operating system and a bit of a poor app store. No way of adding play store. Anyway I carry on playing around with various functions and settings to get a feel of what I can do. The picture is really good but I did adjust the brightness and contrast slightly. Now to the sound. I had read about the built in base speaker and quality sound before buying it so I was looking forward to a great sound. Despite spending ages adjusting all the sound settings, still another big disappointment. The sound is way better than a standard TV but nothing like I was hoping for. Maybe after reading all the hype about it I was expecting a bit too much. Luckily I have a sound bar so I will be sticking with that. I love the feature when you turn the TV off and it is like curtains closing like at the cinema years ago. You can also adjust the speed of this which is nice, only problem is my grandson wants to keep turning the TV on and off. It has 4 HDMI sockets so should be good for most people. The remote is nice and easy to use and will also operate the firestick and its functions which is handy. The operating system does sometimes suffer from some slight lag but it is not a frequent or major problem. The WIFI connection speed is good so hopefully no problems there going forward. So to sum up. Set up super easy. Picture brilliant. Sound ok ish. Operating system not for me. If it had a proper OS yes I would recommend it because the sound is easily rectified with a sound bar which is the norm nowadays.
"

body:
The HISENSE 55U7NQTUK 55 Smart 4K Ultra HD HDR Mini LED TV offers everything I wanted at a lower price than LG, Samsung, and Sony. It supports 120 Hz refresh rates and HDR10+, ideal for PS5 gaming, with an easy-to-access gaming menu that activates AMD FreeSync and displays settings for various genres of video game i.e. FPS, RTS, RPG, Sport. 

While it has a specific mode for Black Myth: Wukong, I can’t assess its quality since I don’t own the game. The FPS monitor doesn't sync accurately with visual frame rates, but this could be how I am using it with the PS5, it may work better with a PC setup. The HDR10, HDR10+, and Dolby Vision provide great picture quality, but I had to adjust the settings to my liking. Apple TV and Prime Video support Dolby Vision, enhancing the viewing experience, especially with the smooth frame setting for better motion in animations.

The Freely App enables live TV, which I use for sports on BBC and ITV due to its better output quality, nevertheless, standard apps like iPlayer and ITVX are available to download. The remote is user-friendly, with quick access to Netflix, Disney+, YouTube and Prime, plus the convenience of solar charging and USB-C compatibility. It also controls the PS5 menu and Fire TV, although it recently stopped working with the Fire Stick, likely due to the Fire settings, not the TV.

Overall, I’m very pleased with this purchase, as it enhances my gaming and 4K HDR viewing experience while offering plenty of customizable settings. The 4 HDMI ports are also welcomed, although only 2 of them support the higher frame rates for gaming, which should be sufficient.

body:
Review of the Hisense 55U7NQTUK TV

Thanks to Feefo and Hisense for giving me the opportunity to review the Hisense 55U7NQTUK TV. It’s an excellent TV with a lot to offer. Here’s my take:

- Setup and Usability:
Setting up the Hisense 55U7NQTUK was super easy. As soon as I switched it on, I was taken straight to the home screen, which was a nice touch. Even assembling the stand was a breeze, and I'm not particularly DIY savvy.

- Performance:
The TV is incredibly fast and responsive. The remote works seamlessly, and there are no annoying loading screens. It's like using a high-end computer. Navigating through apps is simple too, with everything accessible right from the remote.

- Screen Mirroring and Connectivity:
I did encounter a couple of issues with screen mirroring. I couldn’t mirror my phone when using a VPN, and sometimes, when watching movies, the playback would get choppy for 5-6 seconds. However, this choppy mirroring issue is common with many TVs to varying degrees.

- Gaming Modes: 
The TV offers different modes for gaming, enhancing the overall gaming experience. 

- Sound Quality: 
The sound quality is really good, providing clear and immersive audio. - 

- Ease of Use:
Because of its simplicity and ease of use, my elderly parents could navigate through YouTube and other apps easily. The added bonus of voice control, which they got used to from using YouTube on an iPhone, makes it even more user-friendly. As I'm tech savvy I'm usually the one navigating and fixing tech issues like the WiFi etc for my parents, so if this sounds like you too the simplicity is a massive win!

- Temperature and Overall Recommendation:
Even after many hours of use, the TV's temperature remained normal, which is impressive and speaks to its quality. Despite the minor hiccups with mirroring, I’m really impressed with the Hisense 55U7NQTUK. The size, speed, ease of setup, and overall simplicity make it a fantastic choice, If you’re in the market for a new TV, this one is definitely worth considering.

Thanks again to Feefo and Hisense for the opportunity to review this excellent TV. Please don't hesitate to reach out again!

body:
This product is a definite must-buy. You'd end up paying twice the price for another brand offering the same level of quality.
Local dimming works wonders across all TV program genres, especially noticeable during scene transitions to black and the contrast on credits and titles. The TV can reach impressive brightness levels, which is a boon in well-lit rooms. However, in complete darkness, the effect is akin to being in a theater. Occasionally, there's a slight lag in brightness adjustment after a scene change, but this is rare.
Gaming performance is top-notch. I've had no issues playing at 120Hz with audio output through the TV. While my Nvidia graphics card doesn't support over 120Hz via HDMI, gaming at 144Hz would require a display port to HDMI adapter. I've experienced occasional frame drops and screen blackouts, but I'm unsure if this is due to the TV or my HDMI cable. Overall, gaming experience is excellent, with no noticeable latency.
Connecting other devices like sound systems and streaming boxes was hassle-free. Everything worked seamlessly upon setup.
Regarding HDR, there's a bit of uncertainty. SDR content often looks better than HDR, with Dolby Vision on Netflix appearing washed out. However, BBC iPlayer shows in HDR HLG are stunning, making it feel like the animals are in the room. Personal HLG content via Plex also looks good, suggesting the TV may struggle with certain HDR formats.
Surprisingly, the TV does an impressive job of sharpening highly-compressed content, such as streamed shows. For instance, even though "Trigger Point" is only 1080p on ITVx, the quality is noticeably better via the app compared to the sky box.
Additionally:
* The TV has a sleek design and doesn't heat up much, potentially making it more energy-efficient than older LCD models.
* The remote has a nice tactile feel and is easy to use even in the dark.
* The four HDMI ports come in handy, although only two support 144Hz

body:

Improvement Points: The Vidaa operating software is good but Google TV is better and is used on Hisense TVs in the US why not Europe? The sport mode is a great all-round setting for most viewings, punchy colours and good contrast. Watched Alien and the back light struggled a little with the space, star field scenes, though lots of Led TVs do. Hopefully some of these issues can be helped with firmware updates. For the technology involved it's a bargain. The equivalent Sony from last year was twice the price. Highly recommended.

body:
Good Points: Image Quality: HDR is punchy and has good clear colours, the refresh rate of 120hz is excellent when using Game Mode for the PS5 or XBox Series X. Motion blur is limited when watching Sports or whilst gaming giving you a quality picture with fast moving objects. Available ports HDMI 2.1 x 2 (eARC x 1) - HDMI 2.0 x 2, is able to run Dolby Vision IQ/HDR10+/HDR10 and Hybrid Log Gamma (HLG)

Audio: The rear speakers have excellent sound distribution and are possibly the best I have heard from a slimline TV. The speakers have 20W of power with Dolby Atmos.

Connectivity: App controls from Smart Device are excellent - allowing the user to use physical body gestures or smart commands to control the TV without the need of a remote control (although I still believe the remote is the easiest choice of operation) - Voice commands are also available via the Vidaa application (this can be done in any language which is a great accessibility feature more TV's should have!) Tv has built in WiFi as well as Bluetooth 5.0.

Improvement Points: Stand: As the stand is curved it would limit any possibility of adding a sound bar. The sound from the TV is excellent but for those who would want a sound bar directly under would have to seek a different method.

App Store: This could be good or bad but I feel like the app store could do with some more additions. The TV has the basics covered, BBC iPlayer, ITVX, Channel 4, Netflix, Prime, Disney+, YouTube, and more streaming services.

Remote Control: This is a personal preference but feel like the remote doesn't match the TV appearance, would prefer colour matching.

body:
Good Points: This TV offers an immersive viewing experience that surpassed my expectations. Its stunning picture quality, innovative features, and sleek design set a new standard for home entertainment. 

Incredible Picture Quality:
The ULED technology employed by Hisense takes the visual experience to the next level. With the 4K Ultra HD resolution, every scene comes to life with exceptional clarity, sharpness, and vibrant colours. The combination of Quantum Dot Colour and Dolby Vision HDR further enhances the picture quality, delivering deeper blacks and brighter whites.
Cutting-Edge Features:
The TV is packed with an array of advanced features that enhance both convenience and entertainment. The built-in voice control capabilities (powered by AI I think), allow you to navigate through the TV's functions effortlessly. Whether it's adjusting settings, searching for content, or accessing popular streaming platforms, a simple voice command is all it takes. The TV also supports popular voice assistants like Amazon Alexa or Google Assistant, providing seamless integration with your smart home ecosystem.
Smart TV Functionality:
It's a fully-fledged smart TV, offering a comprehensive range of applications and streaming services. With its integrated Wi-Fi connectivity, it easily connected to our home network and we quickly enjoyed our favourite content from the likes of Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, YouTube, and more. The intuitive user interface makes navigation a breeze, ensuring quick access to a vast library of movies, TV shows, and online content.
Immersive Audio Experience:
Complementing the stunning visuals, the audio performance of the 55U7KQTUK is equally impressive. With the inclusion of Dolby Atmos technology, the TVs built in speakers deliver a three-dimensional sound experience that immerses you in rich, detailed audio. We enjoyed watching action-packed movies and playing video games, the soundstage is wide and enveloping, providing an enhanced sense of realism.
Sleek Design and Connectivity Options:
The Hisense 55U7KQTUK TV has a sleek and modern design that effortlessly blends into our (and any) living space. The near-borderless display and slim bezels maximize the screen real estate, offering an immersive viewing experience. Additionally, the TV provides a wide range of connectivity options, including multiple HDMI ports, USB ports, and Bluetooth, ensuring easy integration with various devices such as gaming consoles, soundbars, or streaming devices.

Conclusion:
Thi Hisense 55U7KQTUK 55" ULED TV shines in the highly competitive TV market. Its stunning picture quality, cutting-edge features, smart functionality, immersive audio, and sleek design make it a top choice for anyone after low-cost high-quality device.

Improvement Points: While the Hisense 55U7KQTUK 55" ULED TV has many positive attributes, it does have a few drawbacks. Some small things I found were:
Unable to play sound through the soundbar and tv speakers at the same time, my old TV was able to do this so I was used to this. 
This point is only a small one, when watching Freeview, the channel information appears at the top of the screen and gets in the way of the picture, I would like to be able to move it to the bottom of the screen, but I have not been able to find a menu option to do this. The TV also has a limited viewing angle, which isn't a problem for my living room but other environments may pick up on this. 
However, when weighed against its numerous positive features, these limitations do not overshadow the overall appeal and value of the TV, particularly for those seeking an immersive and feature-rich home entertainment experience.

The menu UI is VERY easy to navigate (easier than SS) as it is pretty basic but you get what you are looking for very quickly.
The image quality is ULED tech which is supposed to be somewhere between QLED and OLED, the picture is very similar to my SS TV but is very clear and vibrant.
There's lots of HDR presets, I changed mine from default to HDR night as it displayed best for PS5 games.
As for the 144hz I only used upto 120hz as I have no games that output that fast, but still it's very nice to have now that some PS5 games are outputting 120hz in their settings. No sign of image tear but be sure to use a high quality/speed HDMI cable!!

The system has a built in Sub Woofer and outputs audio brilliantly, the audio can get very loud as I barely go over 30.

It also has advanced features and HDMI linking so you can control your ps5 main menu through the TV remote if needed.

I had no problems with the TV, but I would not spend quad figures on it. If you can get it for less then you won't be disappointed.

Overall, a very nice modern T.V, excellent picture quality and easy to use. Would recommend.

Improvement Points: It generates quite a bit of heat around the back of the TV, and it uses a little more energy consumption than the Samsung but that could be because it has a built in subwoofer.

"Brilliant Display. I've been looking for a new TV for my home office, I wanted something that was versatile enough for gaming and general use.

The inclusion of Freely makes watching TV quick and easy, a great option to get started especially for less tech savvy people, I hooked up a handheld pc with an EGPU to it. 
It took a while to get the correct settings for the 165hz display, but this was a windows thing not a TV thing, but once I got it set up, it's been working perfectly, no issues at all. 

The only "negative" I have is that HiSense include their own OS (VIDAA), which is lacking a bit compared to Android TV offerings. I use an android based device on my other TV's so I'll be doing the same for this one, it's just a shame that in this day and age with such widespread options HiSense have opted for their own proprietary offering. 

This is not by any means a deal-breaker, it's easily rectified with an android TV stick if required, but this is more to my use-case and may not affect others in the slightest.

Overall I would highly recommend this product, and I will certainly be replacing my other TV's with HiSense options when they eventually give up."

The sound quality is fantastic. You can hear every word spoken clearly and the TV automatically knows when an action heavy scene is showing and kicks in the subwoofer.

Setting up the TV was really quick when you use the VIDAA app at the same time. Settings like connecting to the WiFi is super quick as it matches the WiFi your phone or tablet is connected to, thus saving you time putting the password in manually.

The smart features are simple and easy to use as well as switching to your other input sources.

I am yet to try Game Mode as I need to get my PS3 (yes I know it’s old!) out of storage. Honestly I don’t use it for gaming anymore but still use it to watch my Blu-ray movies. Can’t wait to see what the extra hertz and upscaling looks like.

For me, the size of the TV is great and fits in the room just fine. Either way, I’d happily recommend this TV whatever size you pick."

body: Its amazing nice bright picture and reasonably priced
Using as large pc screen, good picture on tv

When I started the setup i.e. autoscan TV channels, i was immediately faced with setting up a parental pin before i was able to proceed any further. There was no explanation why i was compelled to do this at the very beginning of the set up and when I emailed Hisense they NEVER replied. I eventually found a hisense forum online which advised that this was part of some privacy policy and there was no workaround 

Once I had set the parental pin, I did the TV channel scan and proceeded to the next step which asked me to connect to the internet via wifi or ethernet which then installed Freely. 

Over the next few days I discovered that Freely takes over the TV and when viewing programmes using Freely, I am prevented from using the PVR function i.e. ability to time shift – pause live TV or create recordings. 

If I then reverted back to factory settings and went through the setup BUT without connecting to the internet which prevented Freely from being installed, I was able to watch the TV via Freeview and utilise the PVR function. However, if I wanted to use any of the catch up services i.e. iPlayer, C4, C5 etc.. I had to connect to the internet which then automatically installed Freely which took over the TV and I lost the PVR functionality. There was NO option to toggle between Freeview as a separate source and Freely. 

Before I purchased this TV, there was nothing in the specifications or reviews to warn me about the Frankenstein nature of how this TV operated. There was also NO manual on the Hisense website to refer to. I had to refer to ChatGPT to help me understand this so called ‘hybrid TV’. I subsequently returned the TV for a full refund. 

Furthermore, I found that the so called HD quality of the HD channels was not great and there was hardly any difference between picture quality for non and HD channels. This was another disappointment. Fortunately, the user interface was fine. 

I strongly suspect that other TVs with Freely and PVR will behave exactly the same. Competitor brands confirmed this was the case with their TV’s. This is all fine if you don’t require time shift.

But what is the point of providing time shift if you have to disconnect the TV from wifi in order to access this feature BUT then if you need to use any catch up services, you need to reconnect to wifi which installs Freely and disables time shift?!!!

body: "Hisense 32 inch Freely Tv. This 32 inch Freely TV is great in places such as kitchen and bedroom and has all the features that a Main Tv would have but in a small unit. Setup is quite simple, plug in select your country, enter your wireless code and it does the rest. After about 5 minutes and one download of new software it has found all channels and setup the freely channels. I have added Netflix, Amazon and Disney all through the scan app and enter Tv code and this also all worked fine and quickly with the use of a mobile phone. The remote has lots of quick select buttons including the usual Disney, Prime, Netflix, YouTube, and NowTV but also includes others. What I found really good is the Freely system as the picture quality is excellent and no interference as our previous Tv used an old coax aerial feed which was prone to glitches and interference from electrical items, so far none of this with Freely. The picture quality is very good and sound certainly good enough for a small TV with Dolby Dtx. There are many other features an enthusiast can play with in the settings but for me I prefer the plug and play options preset. The only small gripe I had was the new spacing of the wall hanging bracket threaded holes as they seem to have made them different to my old VESA backplate which was square and this new one is considerably longer gap in the portrait style (see photo). Another little thing is the white flashing light under the unit is not in the centre and this is made obvious as the Hisense logo text at the bottom of the TV is central so it looks a bit odd when the white light box is obviously mounted to the right of centre. Is it value for money, yes I would say so for the features and new Freely system."
author: geg87

body: "Excellent quality and value. For a small TV it packs a punch. It has useful shortcut buttons at the top of the remote, making things like YouTube and Netflix easy to use with the click of a button. The picture quality is excellent, with a good choice of picture settings. Once connected to WiFi, which was a very easy process, everything is easily accessible including the built in TV channels, as we do not have an aerial in the room it is in. The set up was simple and aesthetically pleasing, using simple colours and font. We have enjoyed using the TV every day, it has been a work horse and has taken everything we have asked of it. The speed of loading the apps is very good, taking usually less than a second to switch between apps. Overall, I would give this TV a five out of five, for ease of use, set up speed, picture quality and the number of apps pre installed."

body:
For a large TV this is light and sleek. With minimal edging the design really appeals. 

Setting the TV up was effortless with smart technology to easily link in to all my pre-existing apps. 

The remote control is clear and easy to understand without having to look at instructions and appears very touch responsive. Having the smart function buttons on one remote is great as saves having loads all over the place (fire stick etc) My only critique is that it looks and feels very cheap and a bit plasticky, this doesn't really fit with the aesthetic of the TV but it works and is just a remote control after all.  

The picture is clear and crisp with great colour definition, my grandson loved watching Pixar movies on it as the colour really pops.  The built in Freeview gives loads of choice and again is really easy to use. Sound quality is also great, sounds as good as my previous TV without having to use a sound bar.

Only real issue with this TV is there is no scart socket so if you're old like me and have an ancient DVD player and a stack of DVDs you're a bit out of luck though I'm sure some techies would be able to provide a sensible solution.

This TV does have an F energy rating so probably not the most environmentally friendly out there if that's of concern but all in all it's a great TV

body:
Make no mistake about it, this is a big TV!
It will dominate any smaller room and it's size is not to be underestimated, which on reflection, is a mistake I made!
However, after a few days, we've adapted to the sheer size and come to appreciate it's qualties.
The picture is very good, as is the sound, we now no longer need a soundbar.
We're old fashioned and just use it as stand alone smart TV, without need for the Google features, which have not been activated, as  we have little interest in focussed advetising or giving out too many details, such as passwords, logins etc.
 It has replaced an 8 year old 49 inch LG TV, which we do miss because some it's built in features are lacking in the TCL, such as the ability to pause/record/ rewind live TV, which we fortunately still have available thanks to a set top box.
These features are no doubt available on higher spec. more expensive TVs in the TCL range.
In closing, check and double check the size, unless you're considering an extension to your house,or perhaps have a dedicated TV room. You'll certainly need space to sit back and enjoy the full viewing experience!
As far as picture and sound are concerned, I don't think you'll be disappointed, but do check the features will be sufficient for your needs.
It's certainly provides excellent value for the money and taking everything into account, is a product I can recommend.
Great TV, sound, picture, and overall amazing. Fast processor, easy to navigate and great value for money.

body:
I wasn’t sure what to expect at this price, but I’ve been really impressed with the TCL 65" TV. Setup was quick and easy straight out of the box – the Google TV interface is super smooth and gives instant access to all the apps I use (Netflix, Disney+, YouTube, etc). Voice control through the remote is a nice bonus too – very handy when you're feeling lazy!
Picture quality is excellent for the price – crisp 4K resolution with vibrant colours and support for Dolby Vision and HDR10+, which makes films and TV shows look fantastic. The screen is big and bright enough for my living room, and even gaming looks great on it.
Sound is decent enough for everyday use, though I’ve paired it with a soundbar for a bit more punch when watching films – that said, the built-in Dolby Atmos support is a nice touch.
The design is sleek and modern, and the TV itself feels well made. It looks great on the wall and doesn't take up too much depth. It’s packed with features I didn’t expect to find in this price range – HDMI 2.1, Bluetooth, casting from my phone – it just ticks so many boxes.
Honestly, for the money, it’s one of the best TVs I’ve ever bought. It feels like a premium experience without the premium price tag. Highly recommend this if you're after a large, smart 4K TV without breaking the bank!

At first, the tv os was snappy, but after a few days of use, it became slightly less responsive likely due to the apps and their content. Sound quality is decent, but I was disappointed to find that the TV lacks a 3.5mm audio output for external devices. I wish this had been mentioned in the product details. However, the Google TV OS is fantastic and the voice control features add extra convenience.
Overall, this is a great TV for its price and I’ll definitely be buying TCL devices again!

body:
The picture is great vibrant. Bright. Integrated Google OS makes for excellent inter device communication. And the OS fies a great job of compiling suggestions from all my different streaming services. Better than their native applications. It's my first 4k device and I chose the p model because of it's nits rating 350 is pretty good in class. And qled doesn't suffer the burn in problems common with oled.  Gaming integration is pretty good as well the dedicated mode switching seamlessly when I activate a game.band apparently it can switch to a higher Hz display rating in applications which support that. It is mounted to a wall using a vepa mount and the mounting process was fairly easy.though it's a two person job with a 65inch screen. Sound is really very good to my previous TV. It actually has some bass. And reproduction is good enough to listen to some music and still enjoy the output. Overall I highly recommend this device. The only downside is that in a dark room on a black screen it's possible to see some led lights leak in a completely black image. Obviously this model doesn't have local dimming and it isn't oled. So for my needs that's fine. It doesn't affect dark movies or games. It's about relative light and dark, chiaroscuro. If there any light nearby on screen you will not see it ghosting. And it's only totally black images that seem to suffer with this. I have no issues with it personally. Tcl have done a good job of delivering a large, bright, and enjoyable viewing experience at a fair price. That doesn't compromise on sound or usability, with excellent software integration.
 A great buying experience from a great company, selling great products.  I cant reccomend them highly enough. Far out in front of their competitors.

body:
Firstly, the price and quality of this TV, and its intended use on my part, is pretty good. The unit feels solid, and the remote control has all of the functionality of what you expect at this price range. Picture quality is pretty good, too. Not quite up there with some of the more expensive counterparts on the market at 3 or 4 times the price. But it is good enough for the purposes I purchased this unit for. As for sound, well, let's just say that there is a reason for sound bars. It isn't like this model has the worst sounding speakers on the market. They are what they are for a television which is as thin and light as this unit it.

This model uses Google TV for its OS. This is excellent because some manufacturers use their own proprietary software, which, i feel, has limited functionality. Google TV just has a familiarity about it that makes me feel comfortable. And allows mole way more freedom to install apps that may not be available on proprietary operating systems. 

From when i first set this television up, there have been a couple of issues that I have found with this TV. I have experienced an issue that seems to only only occur when turning the television on from standby. The first is these multiple weird lines of graphical artifacts popping up and disappearing on screen. This has happened to me twice now inside of a week and I am unsure of why this happens. Another issue I have experienced has been an extreme brightness, again, when turning the unit on from standby.  It is like the whole screen is washed out in a very high brightness. With both issues explained above, simply turning the unit off into standby mode and switching back on again clears it.

Overall, I am happy with this model. I only use it for playing games on both PlayStation and Xbox, which does very well. With its low price and performance, for someone needing a unit for primarily playing video games on, you would be hard pressed to find a better alternative than this.
It is a good device, I am still exploring all the vast options which exist on this TV

body:
Extremely disappointing – nowhere near the picture quality advertised

TCL advertises this TV as an impressive, high-quality television with a fantastic picture. Unfortunately, my experience has been completely different.

The picture is unclear and faces look strangely soft and over-smoothed. Fine details are missing, even on people sitting in a studio. I have spent three days trying different picture settings, adjusting almost everything possible, and unfortunately I still cannot get a natural-looking picture.

The colours are also very strange. The green is extremely aggressive and unnatural, and there is a noticeable blue/green cast. The screen does not look properly black either — dark areas often appear more like a very dark, dirty green.

I have tried different picture modes and settings, including adjusting brightness, contrast, sharpness and the various picture-processing options. Nothing has solved the problem.

This is a brand-new television, straight from the shop, so I am starting to wonder whether there is something wrong with the panel or the software. Whatever the reason, the result is the same: the picture is simply not good enough to enjoy watching TV.

What makes this even more disappointing is that my 13-year-old LG produces a much sharper, more natural and more detailed picture. I genuinely expected a modern TCL like this to be a huge improvement, especially considering how impressive the picture is made to look in TCL's advertising and online reviews.

Instead, I feel extremely disappointed with this purchase. I expected something genuinely impressive, but unfortunately the picture quality is nowhere near what I expected.

After this experience, I would seriously think twice before buying another TCL television.

body:
Buckle up for this rollercoaster of a review

Each part of this reviews makes a star rating harder. I’m just going to tell you how it is….

I had an LG C3 65inch…. Long story short I needed a replacement. So…. I chose the Q7C 75inch

The installation, the good part. It was free, (you have to provide the bracket). That’s obviously great, you don’t have to pay for installation…. I used the same bracket the LG was on (saving them a job) the bracket was flat to the wall (my mistake, but worked fine on the LG). They turned up with the tv about 5pm ish (young guy with his even younger helper). It’s a massive TV box. They were happy to see the bracket on the wall… they took the tv out, and attached the brackets arms on the tv (these arms have an adjustable screw on top to help with alignment, very important part of the review)…. So they lifted up the tv and as they stood it up the younger lad peeled of all the protective screen covering (****, is he doing I thought) I asked him politely excuse me young chap why have you done that? That’s the last thing you do isn’t it? His reply was a disgruntled grunt… (English wasn’t his first language, but tbh I don’t have a 2nd language to fall back on). So they picked up the TV with their grubby hands now on the edges of the screen…. They proceed to clip the tv on to the bracket in place, instantly the tv is massively higher one side than the other…. No problem I thought just get your long screw driver out and make the adjustment…. Another problem arose, they didn’t have one…. So off the tv came, not as easy as you think Bcus the arms click in to place, and you have to pull the release strings whilst moving the tv towards you.. soooo the 2 guys did this whilst I’m pulling the strings…. And now if I had spoken a 2nd language it really would’ve come in handy at this point, Bcus they weren’t lifting at the same time I was pulling the strings, it became a difficult task…. So the tv came off and adjustments were made, and back on the wall it went, still not level. Off it came,,, (same break down in communication occurred). Further adjustments were made, back on the wall it went, I’m not going to bore you all, but this happened 5-6 times. They couldn’t figure out which way to turn the screws when it was off the wall and they didn’t understand me telling them… after 30/40 mins and tempers frayed, and I’m sure some derogatory language used (I could’ve leant a 2nd language in the time it was taken). We all got the tv on the wall and it was perfectly level (I had became an honorary member of their team). I then noticed a greyed out pixel (bottom left) it wasnt dead but wasn’t active. I mentioned this and again communication was an issue… I believe they said they could take it away again and I’d have to wait a week for another…. At this point they could see I wasn’t happy. Especially as I had already signed for it. So with it now being 6:30pm. Yep, one and a half hours to unpack and put it on the wall (I installed the LG C3 by myself in less time on the same bracket)… so they left and I got out a cloth to wipe there dirty sweaty finger prints off of the side of the tv……

So the TV

After some picture settings adjustments the picture is amazing…. UHD content is crystal clear and HD content is just as good. It does have to be seen to be believed that a £1000 75” TV is as good as the LG C3 (granted it is a new model). The game settings are also great… the sound is also another area that’s better than I thought especially with Dolby Atmos….. there’s not much to fault…. But here comes the downside…..

The menus are slow to react… there’s also an energy warning message when you change picture preset (and no it can’t be turn off) it gets annoying to say the least….

Oh the NOWtv app UHD isn’t compatible with the TCL TVS, (this is from the NOWtv support team) so don’t buy the NOWtv ultra boost. Don’t know why it’s just not compatible.

The discovery plus app is really laggy when watching HD/UHD live sport… apparently it’s to do with the processor of the TV (NETFLIX UHD works perfectly tho, so ***). The reason it’s the TVs processor is Bcus when I watch the Discovery Plus app through the Xbox, there’s no lag what’s so ever…

With it being an android tv… you’ll have to have a google account…. If you have that the tv is a breeze to set up once it’s connected to your WiFi.

Oh lastly the Disney app works fine in UHD and Tron really has to be seen to be amazed !!!

So the scores

Installation 0/5

(we can all agree on that)

Picture 5/5

Operating system 3/5

Sound 4/5

App 4/5

(When they work)

Value 5/5

Overall 4/5

If you want a tv with loads of features at the best price then this is the tv for you… but the cost comes with a few annoying features but size and actual picture isn’t two of them..!!

Mayb buy it else where or just get the LG C3 or C5 65” then you can’t really go wrong at all with those televisions.

UPDATED 14/03/26

Knocking it down

So the NEW scores

Installation 0/5

(we can all agree on that)

Picture 5/5

Operating system 1/5

Sound 4/5

App 2.5/5

(When they work)

Value 3.5/5

Overall 3/5

The operating system is so laggy… opening up Prime Video takes 20/30 seconds…. (Yes I know it’s not long but when comparing to opening the app on an Xbox, there’s a noticeable difference.)

You have to keep closing all the apps and deleting the cache, there’s an app called Safe Guard pre-installed, it specifically does the deleting, so obviously there aware of this issue.

Soooo….. would I buy it again knowing these issues??? I dunno tbh…. The picture is amazing… the system is terrible… so buy a fire stick, use a console with the apps on and these issues disappear… or buy an LG

body:
Make no mistake about it, this is a big TV!
It will dominate any smaller room and it's size is not to be underestimated, which on reflection, is a mistake I made!
However, after a few days, we've adapted to the sheer size and come to appreciate it's qualties.
The picture is very good, as is the sound, we now no longer need a soundbar.
We're old fashioned and just use it as stand alone smart TV, without need for the Google features, which have not been activated, as  we have little interest in focussed advetising or giving out too many details, such as passwords, logins etc.
 It has replaced an 8 year old 49 inch LG TV, which we do miss because some it's built in features are lacking in the TCL, such as the ability to pause/record/ rewind live TV, which we fortunately still have available thanks to a set top box.
These features are no doubt available on higher spec. more expensive TVs in the TCL range.
In closing, check and double check the size, unless you're considering an extension to your house,or perhaps have a dedicated TV room. You'll certainly need space to sit back and enjoy the full viewing experience!
As far as picture and sound are concerned, I don't think you'll be disappointed, but do check the features will be sufficient for your needs.
It's certainly provides excellent value for the money and taking everything into account, is a product I can recommend.

body:
I wasn’t sure what to expect at this price, but I’ve been really impressed with the TCL 65" TV. Setup was quick and easy straight out of the box – the Google TV interface is super smooth and gives instant access to all the apps I use (Netflix, Disney+, YouTube, etc). Voice control through the remote is a nice bonus too – very handy when you're feeling lazy!
Picture quality is excellent for the price – crisp 4K resolution with vibrant colours and support for Dolby Vision and HDR10+, which makes films and TV shows look fantastic. The screen is big and bright enough for my living room, and even gaming looks great on it.
Sound is decent enough for everyday use, though I’ve paired it with a soundbar for a bit more punch when watching films – that said, the built-in Dolby Atmos support is a nice touch.
The design is sleek and modern, and the TV itself feels well made. It looks great on the wall and doesn't take up too much depth. It’s packed with features I didn’t expect to find in this price range – HDMI 2.1, Bluetooth, casting from my phone – it just ticks so many boxes.
Honestly, for the money, it’s one of the best TVs I’ve ever bought. It feels like a premium experience without the premium price tag. Highly recommend this if you're after a large, smart 4K TV without breaking the bank!

Setting up the TCL 43V6C Google TV was a breeze! The on-screen instructions were easy to follow and in no time, I had access to all my streaming apps and live digital TV channels. The interface is well-designed with plenty of options, making navigation enjoyable.
At first, the tv os was snappy, but after a few days of use, it became slightly less responsive likely due to the apps and their content. That said, the picture quality is excellent, with clear and sharp resolution. Blacks are deep enough, though not on OLED levels, but that’s not a dealbreaker. The ultra-slim bezels enhance the immersive viewing experience, which I love.
Sound quality is decent, but I was disappointed to find that the TV lacks a 3.5mm audio output for external devices. I wish this had been mentioned in the product details. However, the Google TV OS is fantastic and the voice control features add extra convenience.
Overall, this is a great TV for its price and I’ll definitely be buying TCL devices again!

body:
Only had the TV for a couple of days, then returned it as it wasn’t what I expected. Don’t get me wrong, the value for money for an 85” is outstanding these days, but I just don’t have high picture quality expectations or expect it to pull off incredible HDR. 

Pros: size to value
          Ok picture quality 
          Cinematic size 

Cons: matte anti-reflective coating
           Micro stutter like all TCL TV’s
           Green push-in colour 
           Not that bright

So the size is amazing as you’re getting that cinematic immersion, with ok picture quality.
But the colours had a weird green tint out of the box, which I found very distracting. You can correct it to a degree with the white balance settings, but then you’ll be pushing other colours slightly off without realising it. Could have just been a slightly faulty unit though, so who knows as others may not be experiencing this. The matte screen is great, and you’ll love it if you only watch this tv in a sun-soaked room or a room with major lighting that you never turn off. It’s brilliant at handling reflections in these scenarios, but the downside of that is the contrast takes a massive hit. You have to keep this thing pretty much maxed out with brightness and contrast to actually look decent. So as soon as you dim the lights or switch them off, or you close your curtains as the sun’s gone down, then switch it into, say, filmmaker mode, which dims the unit down, then it struggled to look good as it’s having to fight the matte screen from within to push out the contrast to make the image look clean and clear, so it left it looking flat and dull, unfortunately.

So if you only watch in daytime bright rooms, then yes, get this tv but if you have a mixed usage and like watching in the evenings or darker room movie nights, then I’d probably skip this tv altogether.
