I recently purchased the Hisense 50U7STUK, initially intending to use it as a bedroom TV. After spending some time with it, I can confidently say it’s a genuinely good product that delivers incredible value for the money, though it definitely brings a "large room TV" energy to a smaller space.
Here is my breakdown of what makes this TV stand out, along with a couple of tips if you plan on setting it up yourself.
### The Screen & Picture Quality
The screen on this TV is absolutely fantastic. Because it uses Mini-LED technology, the contrast is superb. * **Rich Colours:** The Quantum Dot (QLED) tech really shows here. The colors are incredibly vibrant and punchy, making everything from movies to games look incredibly rich and lifelike. * **Very Bright:** This panel gets *seriously* bright. It handles HDR content beautifully and easily fights off daytime glare. However, because it gets so bright, it can almost feel a bit overwhelming in a pitch-black bedroom at night! You might find yourself turning the backlight down before going to sleep.
### Interface & Features
Hisense packs a lot into this model. It comes loaded with features, including support for Dolby Vision, Dolby Atmos, and high refresh rates (144Hz) if you are into gaming.
Despite the mountain of features, the smart interface (VIDAA) is surprisingly snappy and reasonably easy to navigate. It doesn't lag or stutter, and finding my favorite streaming apps was straightforward and intuitive.
### A Note on Wall Mounting (Read Before You Install!)
If you are planning to put this on the wall, **make sure you get the correct screws.** The TV requires specific VESA mounting screws (often M6), and the standard ones that come bundled in generic wall-mount kits might not be the exact length you need. Do yourself a favor and check the TV's manual for the exact screw depth required before you start drilling, or you'll be making an unexpected trip to the hardware store mid-installation.
### The Verdict
I bought this for the bedroom, but honestly, it performs like a premium main-room TV. Between the incredibly bright Mini-LED panel, the rich colors, and the sheer amount of features, it punches well above its weight. Just be prepared for a cinematic, large-room experience right at the foot of your bed—and double-check your wall bracket hardware before you start! Highly recommended."

body: Before you buy this TV, double-check your wall mount! It requires a specific 400 x 300 bracket. I wrongly assumed my old equal-hole bracket would work and had to learn the hard way. Once it is up, the build quality is impressive for a mid-range set. The ultra-thin bezel gives it a premium, modern look that looks well in the room. The initial setup is very user-friendly too. The VIDAA app prompts you through the Wi-Fi connection process in just a few simple steps, and you are up and running in no time. The software is where this TV really shines. The operating system feels exceptionally snappy and responsive. The TV features two full-bandwidth HDMI 2.1 inputs that fully support a 4K resolution at a smooth 144Hz refresh rate.  You will want to spend a few minutes adjusting the picture settings out of the box. Initially, the factory colours looked a bit oversaturated, and I noticed some slight backlight clouding during darker scenes. Luckily, switching the TV straight into Filmmaker Mode instantly balanced the contrast and helped with the issue. The biggest surprise by far is the audio quality. The built-in 2.1-channel speaker system delivers deep bass and clear dialogue. It packs enough of a punch that you might not even need to buy a separate soundbar.  I don't think I will need one. Overall, this is an impressive TV at this level.

body:
I’ve been genuinely impressed with the Hisense 55Q7STUK. For a mid‑range TV, it delivers far more than I expected, especially when it comes to sound. The built‑in speakers are surprisingly powerful and full-bodied, offering clear dialogue and a punchy, room‑filling sound that doesn’t leave you immediately feeling the need for a soundbar. For everyday viewing, films, and sport, the audio performance stands out as one of the TV’s biggest strengths.
Picture quality is equally strong. Straight out of the box it looks good, but with a little fine‑tuning initially the tv is really bright in light controlled room so I turned that down slightly the colours become natural and vibrant without drifting into oversaturation. Contrast is solid, motion is smooth, and Dolby Vision support gives films a noticeable boost. Whether you’re watching live sport or streaming your favourite series, the overall viewing experience feels consistently high‑quality.
Ease of use is another highlight. The TV is thin, lightweight, and simple to set up, with clear instructions and a responsive operating system that makes navigating apps and menus easy. Everything loads quickly, and although there are plenty of pre‑installed apps, you can remove what you don’t need to keep things tidy. The Freely app meansyou can stream live TV without needing an aerial as long as you’re connected to Wi‑Fi.
After spending some time with it, this feels like a well‑rounded, easy‑to‑use TV that offers excellent performance for the price — especially if you want great sound without adding a soundbar. 
There were a couple of small negatives I need to point out, First when installing the TV the casing on the back must be slightly twisted as when I installed the wall brackets the tv sat out further at one end more than the other, I added a couple of washers and this sorted the issue. Secondly the tv auto morning wakeup for some reason is an hour out?? even though the date and time are correct the tv still switches on an hour later, i'm sure this will be sorted by an update but for now ive turned it off.

body: This years’ Hisense 85 inch (85U7S) has absolutely blown me off. I am a huge fan of the slim bezels that enrapture the beautiful 4k 144hz panel. What’s impressive about this particular model is that it has filmmaker mode which allows me to watch movies as the director intended for them to be seen, which is a big plus for all movie enthusiasts. Not only that, but its also very high refresh rate which means its perfect for gaming and goes very well with my PS5. I was also really impressed with the build in speakers. They have deep base and high treble and the overall sound profile is very punchy and enjoyable. Being Mini-LED, it also offers really good contrast ratio which makes the whole process of TV watching much more enjoyable. Another advantage of having Mini LED is that is does not have pixel burn in like OLED panels, but the local dimming array offer superb performance in HDR. The IMAX Enhancement also helps to lift the entire experience and this is one of the few products where this certification makes total sense. The built in remote is also quite comfortable and its bluetooth, so I do not need to point it at the TV to control it. Besides that, the remote has a built in microphone as well so I can use voice commands instead of typing manually which is  an absolute lifesaver. The TV also has Google TV built in which is quite versatile and user friendly, making it a breeze to start using right away. The TVs overall brightness is also commendable offering 1600 nits of peak brightness with HDR 10 and dolby vision which allows the user to enjoy supported content at unimaginable colours. Built-in ethernet is also an absolute lifesaver as I can just plug in the TV using a wired connection over wireless which makes the internet connection alot more stable and faster. The processor is also quite rapid and the interface does not lag at all even with multitasking using plex or jellyfin. Overall, I would highly recommend this TV to my friends and family. Its absolutely worth it for the price."

body: Brilliant TV

Unboxing the 65-inch Hisense U7STUK was a great experience. Straight out of the box, the build quality feels robust, and the nearly borderless, slim bezel gives it an elegant presence in my living room without looking overly bulky. The Mini-LED backlight colour provides fantastic picture quality. Watching movies in Dolby Vision and HDR10+ reveals stunning contrast, with bright highlights through deep, satisfying blacks. Fast-moving sports and action sequences stay crisp without nasty motion blur, this will be great to watch FiFa World Cup 2026. Navigating the VIDAA smart platform is swift and straightforward. Apps load almost instantly, and switching inputs is snappy. The integrated voice control responds well to natural commands, making hands-free searches simple. The remote control feels functional, though its layout takes a brief period to get used to. Acoustically, the built-in sound system supports Dolby Atmos and delivers clear dialogue along with a noticeable punch of bass, which is rare for standard built-in TV speakers. While the audio is great for daily viewing, adding an external soundbar could enhance the deepest cinema low-ends even further.  Ultimately, this display has massively upgraded my home entertainment setup, merging bright performance with serious gaming power.

body: After getting the Hisense 55U7STUK unboxed and mounted on the wall right above my desk, I am incredibly impressed with how it performs as a primary display. At fifty-five inches, the 4K picture quality is incredibly sharp. Because I sit relatively close to the screen at my workstation, the high pixel density makes a massive difference, allowing me to read small text, fine details, and complex instrument dials without any blurring. ​The Mini-LED backlighting is definitely the standout feature for me. The contrast is brilliant, delivering deep, true blacks that make dark or nighttime scenes feel completely immersive. There is no annoying backlight bleed, and the screen gets bright enough to easily handle room reflections during the day. ​What really seals the deal for gaming and fast-paced simulation is the native 144Hz refresh rate. Fast movement is fluid and completely stable, completely eliminating the motion blur I used to get on slower screens. The AI upscaling also does a fantastic job keeping older content looking crisp. On top of the visuals, the built-in subwoofer and audio system offer surprisingly rich, balanced sound right out of the box. It has truly transformed my desktop environment.

body: I had the opportunity to test the 55U7STUK TV. This is a big step up in picture quality, the TV features the latest MiniLED backlighting technology. This greatly improves lighting control, enhances the contrast, giving the most natural picture possible. It has a powerful processor for detailed blur-free images and you get the optimal contrast levels whatever the time of day and from whichever signal input. The new AI Smooth Motion and AI Sports mode technology makes this TV great for sports and movies as the processing smooths the picture flow. Filmmaker Mode lets you experience the cinematic vision, by using the correct aspect ratio, colour and frame rate.  Game Mode reduces input lag, ensuring quicker reaction times. It's fitted with a built-in subwoofer,  for a deeper bass response and smoother immersive sound. It has the latest Freely TV system with the options of live TV channels and catch-up content. Freely also allows you to ‘pause’ live TV as well as restarting programmes on certain channels. This new service enables the use of just an Internet connection so there is no need for an aerial or satellite dish There’s also one-touch, direct access to the most popular apps - Netflix, Disney+, Amazon Prime etc. It seems the possibilities are endless on this TV and personally I have only just started exploring them all.  What I can say to sum it up is that it is a great way to get a truly cinematic experience in your own living room and it's a gamers dream.

body:
"Excellent 144hz HDR quality at a great price The Hisense 50U7QTUK MiniLED 144Hz 2025 is a great budget choice to enjoy 4k content at vivid HDR and at fast refresh rates 

I tested the 50U7QTUK out with some video games and nature shows to see how well it performed with HDR and content that benefits from faster refresh rates and it performd very well. For gaming, this is great value allowing you to hit higher frame rates than most 4k TVs that typically top out at 120hz.

The 50U7QTUK is a MiniLED panel, not OLED, yet the colours popped. Blacks were not as good but not bad at all.  

The sound quality was also pretty good for TV speakers and the remote that comes with the 50U7QTUK is very nicely designed with the essential buttons easy to reach and those sponsored easy access buttons for streaming services at the top. 

The 50U7QTUK is a great value budget option for those looking for a top spec 4k HDR TV that more than competes with other competitors who would charge much more for the feature set you are getting with the 50U7QTUK. 

The 50" panel is also a nice inbetween size that doesnt feel too big, but provides a great easy viewing experience. 
                                "

body:
"Good Picture but. TV arrived well packaged. It was super easy to unbox and fit to my existing wall mount. When you first turn it on it is so easy to follow the instructions to set it up and connect to Wi-Fi etc. It also has a QR code to download the app to your phone which also works good. Once it is all set up I make my first discovery. This is NOT an Android/Google TV. It has its own operating system and a bit of a poor app store. No way of adding play store. Anyway I carry on playing around with various functions and settings to get a feel of what I can do. The picture is really good but I did adjust the brightness and contrast slightly. Now to the sound. I had read about the built in base speaker and quality sound before buying it so I was looking forward to a great sound. Despite spending ages adjusting all the sound settings, still another big disappointment. The sound is way better than a standard TV but nothing like I was hoping for. Maybe after reading all the hype about it I was expecting a bit too much. Luckily I have a sound bar so I will be sticking with that. I love the feature when you turn the TV off and it is like curtains closing like at the cinema years ago. You can also adjust the speed of this which is nice, only problem is my grandson wants to keep turning the TV on and off. It has 4 HDMI sockets so should be good for most people. The remote is nice and easy to use and will also operate the firestick and its functions which is handy. The operating system does sometimes suffer from some slight lag but it is not a frequent or major problem. The WIFI connection speed is good so hopefully no problems there going forward. So to sum up. Set up super easy. Picture brilliant. Sound ok ish. Operating system not for me. If it had a proper OS yes I would recommend it because the sound is easily rectified with a sound bar which is the norm nowadays.
"

body: Great. Enjoying the TV

"Great quality TV with incredibly easy setup. I recently purchased the Hisense 50U7QTUK and was immediately impressed by how straightforward the installation process was. From unboxing to getting everything up and running, it took less than 20 minutes — even with wall mounting. The instructions were clear, the interface user-friendly, and everything just worked right out of the box.

Visually, the TV looks incredible. It has a sleek, modern design that really adds a premium feel to the room. It's thin, well-built, and has a minimalist aesthetic that blends in beautifully with any setup.

Picture quality is generally good — sharp, vibrant, and enjoyable for everyday viewing. However, I did notice that in some darker scenes or more demanding 4K content, the contrast and detail could be a bit better. It’s not a dealbreaker by any means, but if you’re used to high-end OLED or QLED panels, you might spot the difference.

Overall, for the price, the Hisense 50U7QTUK offers great value with a stress-free setup and a visually appealing design. A few minor tweaks in picture quality would make it perfect, but it’s still a solid choice for most households."

body:
The HISENSE 55U7NQTUK 55 Smart 4K Ultra HD HDR Mini LED TV offers everything I wanted at a lower price than LG, Samsung, and Sony. It supports 120 Hz refresh rates and HDR10+, ideal for PS5 gaming, with an easy-to-access gaming menu that activates AMD FreeSync and displays settings for various genres of video game i.e. FPS, RTS, RPG, Sport. 

While it has a specific mode for Black Myth: Wukong, I can’t assess its quality since I don’t own the game. The FPS monitor doesn't sync accurately with visual frame rates, but this could be how I am using it with the PS5, it may work better with a PC setup. The HDR10, HDR10+, and Dolby Vision provide great picture quality, but I had to adjust the settings to my liking. Apple TV and Prime Video support Dolby Vision, enhancing the viewing experience, especially with the smooth frame setting for better motion in animations.

The Freely App enables live TV, which I use for sports on BBC and ITV due to its better output quality, nevertheless, standard apps like iPlayer and ITVX are available to download. The remote is user-friendly, with quick access to Netflix, Disney+, YouTube and Prime, plus the convenience of solar charging and USB-C compatibility. It also controls the PS5 menu and Fire TV, although it recently stopped working with the Fire Stick, likely due to the Fire settings, not the TV.

Overall, I’m very pleased with this purchase, as it enhances my gaming and 4K HDR viewing experience while offering plenty of customizable settings. The 4 HDMI ports are also welcomed, although only 2 of them support the higher frame rates for gaming, which should be sufficient.

body:
This TV is a great value option. It has very good brightness, colours and clarity. Out of the box the picture settings aren't the best for accurate colours but its not difficult to adjust the settings to get it how you want it. It has a lot of local dimming zones for the backlight which makes the blacks look darker, not as good as OLED but for the price can't complain. The model I got uses a VA panel which usually have really good contract levels and colours that pop more if you like turning saturation up a lot (I don't)

It comes with a lot of streaming apps pre-installed. Hisense's OS is pretty easy to navigate and I haven't noticed any serious slowdowns or lag yet.

There is HDMI eARC for those that want to hook up their own AV receiver for speakers and it works very well. The TV recognises immediately when you have an ARC device connected and will switch the audio output to that automatically

The built in speakers are actually decent compared to other TVs I've heard. Not as good as standalone home theatre speakers but it's got good clarity, has some type of woofer which adds more depth with the bass. Overall an ok speaker

I tested the TV with a PS5 and it has support for Variable Refresh Rate and up to 120Hz. There is a game mode that reduces latency a lot too which makes it usable for more competitive games but I found it best for story games

body:
Review of the Hisense 55U7NQTUK TV

Thanks to Feefo and Hisense for giving me the opportunity to review the Hisense 55U7NQTUK TV. It’s an excellent TV with a lot to offer. Here’s my take:

- Setup and Usability:
Setting up the Hisense 55U7NQTUK was super easy. As soon as I switched it on, I was taken straight to the home screen, which was a nice touch. Even assembling the stand was a breeze, and I'm not particularly DIY savvy.

- Performance:
The TV is incredibly fast and responsive. The remote works seamlessly, and there are no annoying loading screens. It's like using a high-end computer. Navigating through apps is simple too, with everything accessible right from the remote.

- Screen Mirroring and Connectivity:
I did encounter a couple of issues with screen mirroring. I couldn’t mirror my phone when using a VPN, and sometimes, when watching movies, the playback would get choppy for 5-6 seconds. However, this choppy mirroring issue is common with many TVs to varying degrees.

- Gaming Modes: 
The TV offers different modes for gaming, enhancing the overall gaming experience. 

- Sound Quality: 
The sound quality is really good, providing clear and immersive audio. - 

- Ease of Use:
Because of its simplicity and ease of use, my elderly parents could navigate through YouTube and other apps easily. The added bonus of voice control, which they got used to from using YouTube on an iPhone, makes it even more user-friendly. As I'm tech savvy I'm usually the one navigating and fixing tech issues like the WiFi etc for my parents, so if this sounds like you too the simplicity is a massive win!

- Temperature and Overall Recommendation:
Even after many hours of use, the TV's temperature remained normal, which is impressive and speaks to its quality. Despite the minor hiccups with mirroring, I’m really impressed with the Hisense 55U7NQTUK. The size, speed, ease of setup, and overall simplicity make it a fantastic choice, If you’re in the market for a new TV, this one is definitely worth considering.

Thanks again to Feefo and Hisense for the opportunity to review this excellent TV. Please don't hesitate to reach out again!

body:
This product is a definite must-buy. You'd end up paying twice the price for another brand offering the same level of quality.
Local dimming works wonders across all TV program genres, especially noticeable during scene transitions to black and the contrast on credits and titles. The TV can reach impressive brightness levels, which is a boon in well-lit rooms. However, in complete darkness, the effect is akin to being in a theater. Occasionally, there's a slight lag in brightness adjustment after a scene change, but this is rare.
Gaming performance is top-notch. I've had no issues playing at 120Hz with audio output through the TV. While my Nvidia graphics card doesn't support over 120Hz via HDMI, gaming at 144Hz would require a display port to HDMI adapter. I've experienced occasional frame drops and screen blackouts, but I'm unsure if this is due to the TV or my HDMI cable. Overall, gaming experience is excellent, with no noticeable latency.
Connecting other devices like sound systems and streaming boxes was hassle-free. Everything worked seamlessly upon setup.
Regarding HDR, there's a bit of uncertainty. SDR content often looks better than HDR, with Dolby Vision on Netflix appearing washed out. However, BBC iPlayer shows in HDR HLG are stunning, making it feel like the animals are in the room. Personal HLG content via Plex also looks good, suggesting the TV may struggle with certain HDR formats.
Surprisingly, the TV does an impressive job of sharpening highly-compressed content, such as streamed shows. For instance, even though "Trigger Point" is only 1080p on ITVx, the quality is noticeably better via the app compared to the sky box.
Additionally:
* The TV has a sleek design and doesn't heat up much, potentially making it more energy-efficient than older LCD models.
* The remote has a nice tactile feel and is easy to use even in the dark.
* The four HDMI ports come in handy, although only two support 144Hz

Cast YouTube from my phone instantly unlike my very sluggish Sony Bravia. Virtually bezel less design, stand has cable management built in and room for a sound bar if you want.

Improvement Points: The Vidaa operating software is good but Google TV is better and is used on Hisense TVs in the US why not Europe? Some of the presets are not great with washed out images or overly saturated ones, Filmmaker and Dynamic respectively. The sport mode is a great all-round setting for most viewings, punchy colours and good contrast. Watched Alien and the back light struggled a little with the space, star field scenes, though lots of Led TVs do. Hopefully some of these issues can be helped with firmware updates. For the technology involved it's a bargain. The equivalent Sony from last year was twice the price. Highly recommended.

body:

The different visual options enable user to apply perfect settings to all ports or customise each and every connection. Motion blur is limited when watching Sports or whilst gaming giving you a quality picture with fast moving objects. Available ports HDMI 2.1 x 2 (eARC x 1) - HDMI 2.0 x 2, is able to run Dolby Vision IQ/HDR10+/HDR10 and Hybrid Log Gamma (HLG)

Audio: The rear speakers have excellent sound distribution and are possibly the best I have heard from a slimline TV. The speakers have 20W of power with Dolby Atmos.

Connectivity: App controls from Smart Device are excellent - allowing the user to use physical body gestures or smart commands to control the TV without the need of a remote control (although I still believe the remote is the easiest choice of operation) - Voice commands are also available via the Vidaa application (this can be done in any language which is a great accessibility feature more TV's should have!) Tv has built in WiFi as well as Bluetooth 5.0.

Improvement Points: Stand: As the stand is curved it would limit any possibility of adding a sound bar. The sound from the TV is excellent but for those who would want a sound bar directly under would have to seek a different method.

App Store: This could be good or bad but I feel like the app store could do with some more additions. The TV has the basics covered, BBC iPlayer, ITVX, Channel 4, Netflix, Prime, Disney+, YouTube, and more streaming services.

Remote Control: This is a personal preference but feel like the remote doesn't match the TV appearance, would prefer colour matching.

body:
Good Points: This TV offers an immersive viewing experience that surpassed my expectations. Its stunning picture quality, innovative features, and sleek design set a new standard for home entertainment. 

Incredible Picture Quality:
The ULED technology employed by Hisense takes the visual experience to the next level. With the 4K Ultra HD resolution, every scene comes to life with exceptional clarity, sharpness, and vibrant colours. The combination of Quantum Dot Colour and Dolby Vision HDR further enhances the picture quality, delivering deeper blacks and brighter whites.
Cutting-Edge Features:
The TV is packed with an array of advanced features that enhance both convenience and entertainment. The built-in voice control capabilities (powered by AI I think), allow you to navigate through the TV's functions effortlessly. Whether it's adjusting settings, searching for content, or accessing popular streaming platforms, a simple voice command is all it takes. The TV also supports popular voice assistants like Amazon Alexa or Google Assistant, providing seamless integration with your smart home ecosystem.
Smart TV Functionality:
It's a fully-fledged smart TV, offering a comprehensive range of applications and streaming services. With its integrated Wi-Fi connectivity, it easily connected to our home network and we quickly enjoyed our favourite content from the likes of Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, YouTube, and more. The intuitive user interface makes navigation a breeze, ensuring quick access to a vast library of movies, TV shows, and online content.
Immersive Audio Experience:
Complementing the stunning visuals, the audio performance of the 55U7KQTUK is equally impressive. With the inclusion of Dolby Atmos technology, the TVs built in speakers deliver a three-dimensional sound experience that immerses you in rich, detailed audio. We enjoyed watching action-packed movies and playing video games, the soundstage is wide and enveloping, providing an enhanced sense of realism.
Sleek Design and Connectivity Options:
The Hisense 55U7KQTUK TV has a sleek and modern design that effortlessly blends into our (and any) living space. The near-borderless display and slim bezels maximize the screen real estate, offering an immersive viewing experience. Additionally, the TV provides a wide range of connectivity options, including multiple HDMI ports, USB ports, and Bluetooth, ensuring easy integration with various devices such as gaming consoles, soundbars, or streaming devices.

Conclusion:
Thi Hisense 55U7KQTUK 55" ULED TV shines in the highly competitive TV market. Its stunning picture quality, cutting-edge features, smart functionality, immersive audio, and sleek design make it a top choice for anyone after low-cost high-quality device.

Improvement Points: While the Hisense 55U7KQTUK 55" ULED TV has many positive attributes, it does have a few drawbacks. Some small things I found were:
Unable to play sound through the soundbar and tv speakers at the same time, my old TV was able to do this so I was used to this. 
This point is only a small one, when watching Freeview, the channel information appears at the top of the screen and gets in the way of the picture, I would like to be able to move it to the bottom of the screen, but I have not been able to find a menu option to do this. The TV also has a limited viewing angle, which isn't a problem for my living room but other environments may pick up on this. 
However, when weighed against its numerous positive features, these limitations do not overshadow the overall appeal and value of the TV, particularly for those seeking an immersive and feature-rich home entertainment experience.

It also has advanced features and HDMI linking so you can control your ps5 main menu through the TV remote if needed.

I had no problems with the TV, but I would not spend quad figures on it. If you can get it for less then you won't be disappointed.

Overall, a very nice modern T.V, excellent picture quality and easy to use. Would recommend.

body:
"Brilliant Display. I've been looking for a new TV for my home office, I wanted something that was versatile enough for gaming and general use.

The 55U7QTUK PRO has not disappointed, after years of using other brands TV's throughout my house, I may have just been converted, the screen is bright and vivid, whilst there is glare from the window, that is to be expected as most TV's would have this unless it was a matte panel anyway.

The inclusion of Freely makes watching TV quick and easy, a great option to get started especially for less tech savvy people, I hooked up a handheld pc with an EGPU to it. 
It took a while to get the correct settings for the 165hz display, but this was a windows thing not a TV thing, but once I got it set up, it's been working perfectly, no issues at all. 

The only "negative" I have is that HiSense include their own OS (VIDAA), which is lacking a bit compared to Android TV offerings. I use an android based device on my other TV's so I'll be doing the same for this one, it's just a shame that in this day and age with such widespread options HiSense have opted for their own proprietary offering. 

This is not by any means a deal-breaker, it's easily rectified with an android TV stick if required, but this is more to my use-case and may not affect others in the slightest.

Overall I would highly recommend this product, and I will certainly be replacing my other TV's with HiSense options when they eventually give up."

body:
"Hisense 55U7QTUK PRO - Gamers Delight. I'm fairly new to Hisense, and had done some research previously. However what attracted me to this was the 165Hz Game Mode Ultra. Wow, just wow! It means you need to play around a bit, but once you get it right, the sound for gaming and movies adds to the experience (without the need for additional speakers). Some nice additional features, including IMAX Enhanced and Filmmaker mode - allowing you to watch the film just the filmmakers intended! Also has Freely built in - which allows you to watch a mixture of live channel and catch up content using an internet connection. Still finding my way, but has some nice features, including allowing you to 'pause' live TV. Finally all the usual mainstream apps are integrated, Amazon Prime Video, Disney+ and Netflix to name a few. Oh a small mention for the remove control - it has a nice solar remote for sustainable power. Excellent touch. All in all a great TV!

"Thank you Hisense!. Just got this TV and I love it! It was super easy to set up. The build quality feels solid and modern, and the picture is impressive. It's really sharp and the colors are vibrant – the mini led screen makes everything look amazing.
The remote is actually one of my favorite things. It’s super easy to use, and it charges itself with solar power! No more battery swapping. It also has handy shortcut buttons at the top, for things like YouTube and Netflix, so you can jump right in with just one click.
Apps load really fast too, switching between them usually takes less than a second, which is very helpful.
The picture stays clear even in a bright room, which I really appreciate. The menu is simple to navigate, nothing confusing or clunky.
As for sound, it seems pretty good, but we usually use a separate sound system (my husband’s choice), so I can’t really comment too much on the built-in sound.
It comes with the Freely option, you can watch live UK channels over the internet, no aerial needed.
The only small downside is that since it’s a Chinese brand, it doesn’t come with Google built in, so no Google Assistant or Play Store. But honestly, we haven’t missed it.
All in all, super happy with this TV., totally worth it! Thank you Hisense!"

body:
"Quality picture with superb sound . Having finally jumped onto the 4K TV bandwagon, I have to honestly say I’m truly impressed by the increased picture quality.

I normally just use Sky to watch TV and my subscribed apps (purely because they’re all located in one place) . I also have the HD package for the channels. After going from a non-4K TV to one that is, with the added benefit of an AI chip installed, the picture clarity is greatly improved. The usual text you see on programs and films like the intro text and end credits are crystal clear. I literally haven’t seen one blurred word or number since plugging it in. I’ve also set the picture smoothing settings to low which improves the quality without getting the soap opera effect.

The sound quality is fantastic. You can hear every word spoken clearly and the TV automatically knows when an action heavy scene is showing and kicks in the subwoofer.

Setting up the TV was really quick when you use the VIDAA app at the same time. Settings like connecting to the WiFi is super quick as it matches the WiFi your phone or tablet is connected to, thus saving you time putting the password in manually.

The smart features are simple and easy to use as well as switching to your other input sources.

I am yet to try Game Mode as I need to get my PS3 (yes I know it’s old!) out of storage. Honestly I don’t use it for gaming anymore but still use it to watch my Blu-ray movies. Can’t wait to see what the extra hertz and upscaling looks like.

For me, the size of the TV is great and fits in the room just fine. Either way, I’d happily recommend this TV whatever size you pick."

body:
"A Brilliant All-Rounder with a Near Perfect UI I’ve been really impressed with this TV since setting it up. The AI picture settings are genuinely brilliant - everything looks fantastic without needing to constantly adjust things manually. After looking into them a bit more it's based on ambient light and the type of programme so that's pretty epic!

Whether we've had animated films on for the kids or I've been able to kick back and watch the rugby, the picture is vibrant, smooth, and full of detail. Even during the day in a bright room, there’s no issue with glare or fading colours - we have big dormer windows and it handles bright light really well, which is something we were hoping for in this TV.

I’ve also been pleased with the sound. It’s clear and balanced, and we haven’t felt the need for extra speakers. Dialogue is crisp, and there’s a decent amount of depth, which makes a big difference for movies and action scenes. The built-in sound system gives a full, room-filling experience without needing to add a soundbar. Definitely play around with the sound settings as well for the best experience!

Apps load quickly, and everything on the smart system runs smoothly. Switching between streaming services is quick and responsive. The remote is thoughtfully designed too - it’s got all the main app buttons built in, and I especially like that you can customise one of the buttons to go directly to a specific app or device input. That’s been a nice bonus. It even charges by sunlight and has a USB-C port, so it never runs out of battery...well it hasn't yet and I live in Scotland!

The overall design of the TV is really modern and premium-looking. It sits nicely on our unit but would also look great wall-mounted (which it will be soon). The stand offers two height positions, which is helpful if you’re using a soundbar or want it a bit higher if you're a giant like me. 

The set-up was simple and guided me through everything clearly - I was up and running in less than 10 minutes. Note, it is fairly heavy to lift onto the stand yourself but with some careful positioning and the multifunctional packaging (that's not even a joke just wait 'til you see the instructions) you can manage it yourself.

Overall, this TV has been a fantastic addition to our home. It looks good, performs well in all kinds of situations, and is easy to use every day. Definitely recommend if you're looking for a feature-packed, smart and reliable upgrade."

body:
"Great tv for a great price! I’ve been checking out the new Hisense 55U8QTUK MiniLED 165Hz Smart AI, and honestly… it’s amazing for the price. If you want a TV that looks high-end without paying crazy money… this might be the one.
The screen is super bright, even in the middle of the day with sunlight coming in. The colors are rich, and the black parts of the screen actually look sooo dark not washed out. It’s awesome for watching movies or Netflix. The picture looks really sharp and smooth, even during fast scenes.
if you are into gaming ( like me) PS5, Xbox, or even PC—this TV is a beast. It can do 4K at 165Hz, which is faster than most TVs. Games feel smooth and super responsive and very low input lag. Basically, it’s made for gaming.
The sound is better than I expected. It has built-in speakers with Dolby Atmos, and it even has a little subwoofer in the back for bass. Movies and games sound full, and you might not even need a soundbar. Just a heads-up… if you mount it on the wall, the bass can make the wall vibrate a little.
It’s a solid… well-built TV with a sleek design. The stand is adjustable, and the whole thing looks and feels like a premium product. Definitely doesn’t look cheap.
This is one of the best TVs you can buy right now if you want awesome quality without paying OLED prices. Great for movies, sports, and especially gaming. Hisense really nailed it with this one.
Would totally recommend. It is bright, fast, great sounding, and full of features. Definitely feels like you’re getting more than what you paid for.

"
author: Leaderek88

body:
"Feature packed and well built Hisense is not a brand I have previously considered generally tending to look at more well known brands. However I was pleasantly surprised with my latest purchase of the 55U8QTUK. The TV was extremely well packaged, something I was grateful for given the weight of the TV. At first this might sound like a negative but I consider this a big postive. Many TV's now are so thin and light and can often feel fragile, not so with this model from Hisense, It feels quality and robust and well engineerd. 

The unboxing experience was good with everything well packaged and easily identifiable. I have the TV wall mounted and therefore didn't use the included stand however I have no doubt from the build quality of the stand it would have no problem supporting the TV should you choose to mount yours on a media unit. 

Powering up the TV I was greeted by an unfamiliar VIDAA operating system for the TV. I'm pleased to say it was fast and responsive with pleasent graphics and an easy to navigate and intuative design. I was able to setup all of my frequently used apps quickly and easily. 

One thing I must emphasize is the features and quality feel of the supplied remote in hand, also the fact that it doesn't need batteries and is powered by sunlight is a novel but useful highlight. 

I have a number of the latest gaming consoles and was pleased to see that all of the HDMI inputs are of the latest 2.1 generation and also supported my high-end gaming PC up to 165Hz refresh rate something not supported by many other TV's currently. 

Also a really nice unique feature of this TV and something which I cannot find on any other TV is a USB-C input this means I could connect my tablet and laptop via a single USB-C cable and again I was able to get full 4K resolution!

It comes with a solid heavy TV stand if you want to make it stand, but because we have a child, we preferred to have it on the wall. It was easy to have it up on the wall and the setup was relatively quick. 

Image is great. We have used the same cartoons my son is watching to compare with our previous TV, and I believe Hisense offers a more natural, bright image. 

VIDAA App - you can control the TV from an app installed on your phone. We were using the Apple Box before to do the same thing, but we found it fascinating that the TV itself allows us to do this. 

VIDAA Voice - helps you control your tv hands free

Freely - Live TV. Even though we pay for the TV License we never used to watch live channels because of the inconvenience trying to find the TV remote control. Picture Mode Settings, Advanced Settings - you can adjust the brightness , color, motion, clarity and overscan. 

Picture Mode Game Settings- it comes with its own picture settings for games

Amazon Alexa- we don’t currently have it set up, but it is available

BBC Account - you can connect prior to your BBC Account when you use hands free voice 

I am very happy to have tried Hisense and I would recommend it with my eyes closed. Great quality for a very good price. My husband is in love with the design and the finish of the remote control, the tv itself. Very sleek design.

body:
First of all I must say that the box is big, as well as heavy and you'll need a second pair of hands to get the TV out safely and to lift it into its final position after fitting the very substantial centre stand, which gave me confidence that it would remain put. I advise reading the manual on how to attach the stand and don't just guess.

Having viewed this Hisense 65U8NQTUK 65" 4K Ultra HD MiniLED Smart TV for the last 10 days I am really impressed with its performance, looks and build quality. The picture is clear and detailed, especially when viewing in 4K content from Netflix and the sound is good for a LED, although I have finally connected it to a soundbar usingthe HDMI ARC port. No trace of lipsync issues.

I particulary like the layout and feel of the remote control and the built in solar charger to save having to find batteries when you least expect. Its reassuring to see the effort put into the remote rather than leaving it to chance with a flimsy unintuative lump of plastic.

I don't have an external aerial and I rely on a well known satellite system but I was eager to see what free to air channels I could get using the Freely streaming app which is slowly rolling out. Unfortunately I hit a hurdle here and the App failed to install.

PROS
- Very clear detailed 4K and HD picture from those Mini LEDs
- Good sound with Dolby Atmos quality and built in sub-woofer
- Solid centre stand
- Plenty of connection options
- Excellent build quality and style, inc remote
- Easy setup
- Good GUI
- 2 year manufacturer warranty


CONS
- The Freely App failed to install - reason unknown - Freely servers?
- Slight motion blur when people running during a movie scene
- Stand a bit fiddley to assemble and fit to TV (read manual)
- It's heavy, need two people but it's a 65" TV so really to be expected

So to sum up, this new 65" U8NQT model for 2024 should be on your shortlist if you're looking for a fully featured sub £2k 4K smart TV.

You won't regret it.

body:
Firstly might I say, If you're looking for a great image, sound and a user friendly UI then this really is the Tv for you.

Hisense have come a long way in the recent months with making a really high quality product that can easily compete with the top brands. Both the TV and the included remote feel high quality and gives me a sense that it will last for a good number of years.

I have this tv mounted on my wall with a standard 400x600 wall mount and it looks great. As advertised, I have minimal glare from both light coming through the window in the day and internal lights at night. The sound quality is as great as any other premium TV sound output and wouldn't need any further aid from a sound bar but I already had one so I connected it and used that after testing. 

The picture quality from the TV is fantastic when you get a 4k video up. The blacks are so dark and there is no light bleed whatsoever. The only issues I have found is there are some vertical bars visible when the picture pans sideways (noticed during a football match), these are minor and can only be seen under certain conditions but once I have seen them I can't unsee them (those who know, know). This could be a manufacture defect or maybe even settings that need changing in the TV but more searching is required for me on this front as when in a dynamic picture mode, the TV will decide what's the best colours and contrast.

The apps built into the TV are great and I would argue you no longer need a coax feed to the back of the TV as all of the major channels are accessible over the internet apps.

I did try to use the mobile phone app during set up but it struggled to pair with the TV. I would class myself as an average user of tech so I know my way around a phone and how to try other methods if something isn't quiet working. Once the TV was set up, you can use the app as a remote but I haven't really done so as the included TV remote is fantastic.

So, in summary. Would I recommend this TV to you if you're reading this?
Yes! The picture quality and sound is great and certainly a big contender with the top TVs out there right now. Even with the minor issue with my TV picture (probably is a setting somewhere), 99% of the time I'm blown away with how crisp and clear the image is. I truly haven't seen a TV yet without light bleed into the blacks until I watched this one!

This TV really feels like a top quality premium television. It has a great modern design with a very thin frame but the overall build quality feels really good and durable. The central pedestal is thin but wide and heavy, so the TV is really stable once placed on the furniture unit.

It has plenty of connections available on the back (USB, 4 HDMI's, 3.5mm headphones, etc...) The HDMIs were particularly fast when playing content from external devices (laptop, Roku stick).

Image and sound quality are fantastic, with very smooth movements and very good image depth (sometimes, it looks almost 3D, like if you were inside the movie or the documentary).

We also set up Vidaa and Freely accounts. We were impressed with Vidaa (everything is streamed in HD or 4K) but we didn't like the fact that you cannot finish the Freely session once started (you can end sessions in any other app or channel).

The TV comes with all the streaming apps ready, you don't have to set up anything, just provide your account username and password and start watching. The screen and content sharing features also work very well and we liked a lot the fact that the remote has a USB rechargeable battery (and PV cells, so it lasts for ages).

I would definitively recommend this TV.

The tv comes with a great number of inputs including 4 hdmi slots, one of which is a 144hz eARC for connecting other smart peripherals. I’m glad it has an optical input as I can still connect my Gen 1 Sonos soundbar. The slight downside with this setup is that I can’t change the volume on the soundbar as that requires an IR remote which this one isn’t. However I’m sure this wouldn’t be a problem if I had connected the tv to my Gen 2 Sonos soundbar through the eARC hdmi connection.

Improvement Points: As the viewing angle increases the colours lose some of the vibrancy with a slight tendency to look a bit washed out at the extremes. 

I can’t reorder the channels like I can on my LG, so I can’t put all of the HD channels at 1-8. I find this frustrating but bearable!

body:
Make no mistake about it, this is a big TV!
It will dominate any smaller room and it's size is not to be underestimated, which on reflection, is a mistake I made!
However, after a few days, we've adapted to the sheer size and come to appreciate it's qualties.
The picture is very good, as is the sound, we now no longer need a soundbar.
We're old fashioned and just use it as stand alone smart TV, without need for the Google features, which have not been activated, as  we have little interest in focussed advetising or giving out too many details, such as passwords, logins etc.
 It has replaced an 8 year old 49 inch LG TV, which we do miss because some it's built in features are lacking in the TCL, such as the ability to pause/record/ rewind live TV, which we fortunately still have available thanks to a set top box.
These features are no doubt available on higher spec. more expensive TVs in the TCL range.
In closing, check and double check the size, unless you're considering an extension to your house,or perhaps have a dedicated TV room. You'll certainly need space to sit back and enjoy the full viewing experience!
As far as picture and sound are concerned, I don't think you'll be disappointed, but do check the features will be sufficient for your needs.
It's certainly provides excellent value for the money and taking everything into account, is a product I can recommend.

body:
I wasn’t sure what to expect at this price, but I’ve been really impressed with the TCL 65" TV. Setup was quick and easy straight out of the box – the Google TV interface is super smooth and gives instant access to all the apps I use (Netflix, Disney+, YouTube, etc). Voice control through the remote is a nice bonus too – very handy when you're feeling lazy!
Picture quality is excellent for the price – crisp 4K resolution with vibrant colours and support for Dolby Vision and HDR10+, which makes films and TV shows look fantastic. The screen is big and bright enough for my living room, and even gaming looks great on it.
Sound is decent enough for everyday use, though I’ve paired it with a soundbar for a bit more punch when watching films – that said, the built-in Dolby Atmos support is a nice touch.
The design is sleek and modern, and the TV itself feels well made. It looks great on the wall and doesn't take up too much depth. It’s packed with features I didn’t expect to find in this price range – HDMI 2.1, Bluetooth, casting from my phone – it just ticks so many boxes.
Honestly, for the money, it’s one of the best TVs I’ve ever bought. It feels like a premium experience without the premium price tag. Highly recommend this if you're after a large, smart 4K TV without breaking the bank!

Setting up the TCL 43V6C Google TV was a breeze! The on-screen instructions were easy to follow and in no time, I had access to all my streaming apps and live digital TV channels. The interface is well-designed with plenty of options, making navigation enjoyable.
At first, the tv os was snappy, but after a few days of use, it became slightly less responsive likely due to the apps and their content. That said, the picture quality is excellent, with clear and sharp resolution. Blacks are deep enough, though not on OLED levels, but that’s not a dealbreaker. The ultra-slim bezels enhance the immersive viewing experience, which I love.
Sound quality is decent, but I was disappointed to find that the TV lacks a 3.5mm audio output for external devices. I wish this had been mentioned in the product details. However, the Google TV OS is fantastic and the voice control features add extra convenience.
Overall, this is a great TV for its price and I’ll definitely be buying TCL devices again!

body:
Only had the TV for a couple of days, then returned it as it wasn’t what I expected. Don’t get me wrong, the value for money for an 85” is outstanding these days, but I just don’t have high picture quality expectations or expect it to pull off incredible HDR. 

Pros: size to value
          Ok picture quality 
          Cinematic size 

Cons: matte anti-reflective coating
           Micro stutter like all TCL TV’s
           Green push-in colour 
           Not that bright

So the size is amazing as you’re getting that cinematic immersion, with ok picture quality.
But the colours had a weird green tint out of the box, which I found very distracting. You can correct it to a degree with the white balance settings, but then you’ll be pushing other colours slightly off without realising it. Could have just been a slightly faulty unit though, so who knows as others may not be experiencing this. The matte screen is great, and you’ll love it if you only watch this tv in a sun-soaked room or a room with major lighting that you never turn off. It’s brilliant at handling reflections in these scenarios, but the downside of that is the contrast takes a massive hit. You have to keep this thing pretty much maxed out with brightness and contrast to actually look decent. So as soon as you dim the lights or switch them off, or you close your curtains as the sun’s gone down, then switch it into, say, filmmaker mode, which dims the unit down, then it struggled to look good as it’s having to fight the matte screen from within to push out the contrast to make the image look clean and clear, so it left it looking flat and dull, unfortunately.

So if you only watch in daytime bright rooms, then yes, get this tv but if you have a mixed usage and like watching in the evenings or darker room movie nights, then I’d probably skip this tv altogether.

body: After living with the Hisense 43Q7STUK for a few weeks, I can honestly say it has exceeded my expectations. I wasn’t looking for anything overly complicated, just a TV with a great picture and easy-to-use features, and it delivers on both. The first thing that stood out was how straightforward everything was. From taking it out of the box to getting it connected and ready to watch, the whole process was refreshingly simple. Within a short time I was signed into my streaming services and browsing through content without needing to dig through manuals or menus. The picture quality is easily the star of the show. Films, sports and everyday TV all look sharp and vibrant, with colours that really stand out without looking unnatural. Even during bright afternoons, when sunlight fills the room, the screen remains clear enough to enjoy without constantly adjusting blinds or curtains. One feature I didn’t expect to use was the children’s remote, but it’s actually a thoughtful addition. It’s simple, colourful and gives younger viewers an easy way to access suitable content, which I can imagine being a real bonus for families. The smart TV interface is well laid out and includes all the apps I regularly use, meaning I’ve been able to retire my streaming stick completely. The dedicated app buttons on the remote are handy too, making it quick to jump straight into whatever I want to watch. There is occasionally a slight delay when navigating menus, but it’s minor and hasn’t affected my overall experience. Considering everything else the TV offers, it’s a small compromise. Overall, this TV feels like a fantastic all-round package. It looks stylish, performs brilliantly and is simple enough for everyone in the household to use. If you’re upgrading from an older set, you’ll definitely notice the difference.
author: TheBladeUk

body: I have had this tv a few weeks now.  Delivery and set up was surprisingly easy. The box is designed so you dont have to lift it up, it opens round the TV.  Assembling the legs was straight forward, there are 2 widths depending on where you are putting it. Once on, we used wider settings its very stable even on our temporary table as we plan a media wall to give this great tv its max effect.  Setting up took a couple of mins and was all done, very easy to follow steps. Its compatibility to link with home features makes it more impressive. It was super easy to sign in to our subscriptions we have.  First impressions when we got it set up were wow... the sound is great, clear and well projected round the room we have. We decided on a larger than planned as my little boy is visually impaired. This TV size means he can join in on watching and movie nights. The subtitles are a brilliant size, actually had to move back which really adds for us. The picture is crystal clear, even when closer its not pixilated or blurry.  The app feature is great, can turn off when the children forget too.  We have also tried a console on it and wow its made that really fun to play. The children were all able to play together as my boy could see clearly!  So far this is definitely worth it, sleek thin and so light compared to our old 55" one."
author: Charmers88

body: Having previously owned a Hisense TV, I was curious to see how much they have improved over the years - and boy was I impressed! Starting with initial set-up. Very easy to use and get started. A QR code allowed access to the app to help set-up go smoothly and I was up and running within a few minutes. The user interface is very easy to use and intuitive to find your way about. Using the smart on demand features, finding apps, setting up your sound and pictures preferences - all very easy to utilise. The picture quality is superb - colours are rich and vibrant, blacks are clear and the auto adjustment features on the TV are great to ensure maximum quality when viewing darker movies. I particularly like the function where it automatically senses if a movie you are watching has Filmaker mode and it automatically switches to this to enhance your viewing.  The AI motion adjustments are great too - avoiding the motion blur effects you get with some TVs. This is particularly great when gaming - smooth motions and movements making it great to play on. Sound is very good too - a massive upgrade on previous Hisense models.  The remote is very easy to use and a good size - feels nice in your hands and the quick access to the most popular streaming apps makes for seamless switching between what your watching. Overall I am very impressed with this TV. It's an excellent choice for someone looking for a great quality TV for their living room or bedroom - great for movies, shows, streaming and gaming - all round, I highly recommend this TV.  5 Stars!
author: Derek1graham

body:
I've previously had Hisense TVs so you would think I knew what I was in for — Wrong! I expected minor improvements but I was very pleased with what I saw. Let's go through some of the specs that matter and made a difference to my experience: - VIDAA smart platform — THIS IS THE ONE THAT REALLY SOLD ME THIS TV. VIDAA is a lightweight Linux-based smart TV platform. What this means to us is that you can launch apps like Netflix or YouTube really fast and smooth, adding to the overall experience. No more wondering what the hell happened to the app you just started — it's just there, instantly. - Hi-QLED with Quantum Dot colour — The screen is brighter and richer than my previous TV, which was already quite impressive. Colours feel more true-to-life and punchy without looking over-saturated. A genuine step up. - 144Hz panel — I don't think this made as much difference to me personally as it did to my 9-year-old son. The feedback is that gaming is smoother and more pleasant. WIN! There are other gaming features too — Game Mode Pro and the updated Game Bar give gamers quick access to VRR, frame rate counters, and input lag settings. Proper stuff. - All the HDR modes — This bad boy supports HDR10+, HDR10+ Gaming, Dolby Vision, Dolby Vision IQ, and HLG — essentially covering every format you're likely to encounter. You're not going to hit a wall with this one. - Hi-View AI Engine (MediaTek Pentonic 700 chip) — Enables enhancements such as AI Picture, AI Light Sensor, AI 4K Upscaling, AI Detail Enhancement, AI HDR Enhancement, and AI Smooth Motion. Basically you're fully "AI'd" up - Filmmaker Mode — Preserves the director's original frame rates and colour intent without any motion processing applied. If you're a film lover, this one matters more than you'd think. The only thing that's potentially not the best is the sound quality. It's OK but not exactly hi-fi, and let's be honest — at this price point you wouldn't expect it to be either. So this review still retains 5 stars. The remote is well laid out with shortcut buttons for all the major apps. It's also Bluetooth, so you don't even have to point it at the TV — which feels delightfully lazy. Ha!
I love this TV so much that I've actually set it up as a second computer monitor. Check out the picture. Overall, I would thoroughly recommend this TV.

body: From the moment I received this 43” TV, I was pleasantly surprised by how lightweight it was; it almost felt deceptive given its size. Unboxing was straightforward, and installing the pedestal feet was simple and stress-free. The protective cardboard over the screen was a thoughtful touch, making setup much easier without worrying about accidental damage. Although I plan to wall mount it later, the initial setup was smooth and user-friendly. Powering on the TV and setting it up via the VIDAA app was effortless. Downloading the app and connecting it to the TV was quick, and the mobile setup process worked seamlessly. The WiFi connection is strong, allowing the smart interface to run smoothly and making navigation intuitive and easy to use. One of the standout features is Freely, which removes the need for a traditional TV aerial. This is incredibly convenient, simplifying installation and eliminating the hassle of running additional cables or installing an aerial point. In terms of picture and sound quality, both are excellent. The display delivers vibrant, sharp visuals across all types of genres of programs. Sports, in particular, look fantastic; fast-moving scenes are clear, bright, and easy on the eyes, which is perfect for watching events like the World Cup. The sound is also impressive, offering clear and balanced audio across volume levels. While a surround sound system would enhance bass performance, the built-in speakers are more than sufficient for a bedroom setup. If I had one suggestion, it would be to make the feet more centrally positioned. This would provide greater flexibility when placing the TV on different types of furniture. That said, it currently fits on my chest of drawers, though this is only temporary as I intend to mount it on the wall. Overall, this is a great TV with a simple and intuitive navigation system, excellent picture quality and strong, clear audio performance. I had heard of the brand before but never considered purchasing; something I now see was a mistake. This TV proves they can compete with more established brands, especially when considering the excellent value for money."

body:
Our new Hisense TV has provided a hit for our teenage son's bedroom. The picture quality is outstanding, very clear and crisp with excellent dark blacks. 
As it has built in Freely, we don't need to organise an aerial connection as it streams freeview channels online over wifi or ethernet. Alongside this, there's every paid for streaming app you could want if you subscribe to them. Totally easy to set all this up and have the latest streaming sport and movies on the screen from Netflix, HBO Max, Youtube, NowTV, iPlayer etc.
It looks slick in the corner of the room, we are wall mounting it eventually, but the stand feet it comes with are small and fits on compact units.
He's going to use this with his PS5, so the gaming modes and refresh rate optimisation for that is ideal, and the 4K picture is outstanding. There's enough HDMI connections including ARC for a soundbar connection.
This is an upper range TV, with a price to match, however it's worth it in our opinion and we are already looking at upgrading another tv to this Hisense range in time for the world cup.
author: mdmedia

body:
I don't know where to begin for reviewing my new MASSIVE 85" Hisense TV 85E78STUK PRO. I'm actually even more impressed with it than I was expecting.
The TV it's replacing was a decent 65" TV, so was only expecting a small improvement in the picture and sound quality, and got to admit the thought had crossed my mind that because of the 20" size difference, whatever increase in picture quality with the new telly, would be lost in this increase in size. I was wrong, the sharpness for a start, is much better, as are the depths and vibrancy of colours, proper black blacks, even in a darkened room. The Tv automatically upscales standard signal to 4K. I have not altered the colours in any way, I'm extremely happy with the way they are out of the box so to speak. For the technical it boasts Quantum Dot Colour and Dolby Vision IQ. You do have preset options, like cinema, game mode, sport etc. which again I have not needed to change, although I have used the sport mode to watch football. I was showing the TV off to (jealous) friends though. Same as picture options, there are preset sound options. I've tried the music and cinema sound modes, as with picture modes, there are more options, but can't remember them all. With the sound, I did increase the bass on the graphic equaliser as I like a lot of oomph. For the technically minded it boasts 2 x 15W + 20W speakers and has eARK audio via HDMI. Again for the technical the TV boasts Dolby Atmos and DTS Virtual X decoding for immersive sound. There are plenty of connection options e.g. several HDMI's USB etc., which I won't go into as the specs are on all the sales and Hisense websites. Setting up was simple, from initial setup, to connecting to Wi-Fi. I'd say most apps what you need are pre-installed like Netflix etc. I can't comment on the installed apps as I don't have Netflix account, I almost exclusively use Sky on my TV, which this TV compliments amazingly, the Sky remote pairs easily with the TV, for automatic turning the TV on and off. One slight downside (if you can call it that) I've noticed is you need to check the little white standby light on the bottom of the TV illuminates when turning off, as you can't tell it has gone into a standby state because of the darkness of the black colour. The TV has built in Freely for viewing live TV. This seems good, although only used very briefly when first setting the TV up with using Sky. The TV remote has built in voice control, enabling use of the built in Alexa for example. Can't comment on the use of that as I have Alexa in the room already set up and don't want them fighting over each other. I was pleased to find out this TV only weighs just over 32kg (85" without stand) which is a lot lighter than my previous 65" TV. I must also point out, I measured my chimney breast wall incorrectly when measuring up for the wall bracket/mount and the TV is bigger than my original measurements, so I need to move the wall bracket before I can mount it. I thought, oh no, I've made a terrible mistake, the TV is far too big for the room when I first started viewing, BUT I have quickly become used to the size. So be brave and order the biggest you can fit in your room, you won't regret it.
In a nutshell this TV gets a thumbs up for me, I absolutely love it and don't have one regret in purchasing it. From delivery in its extremely sturdy box, to sitting watching a movie, it has brought an enormous smile to my face. Can't wait till I can get it on the wall. I might then, find even more amazing features that I have probably missed. I haven't mentioned the value for money is also excellent, getting more to the £ than most other manufacturers. I hadn't taken much notice of the brand Hisense until a couple of years ago if I'm honest. Then I looked into their side by side fridge freezers, I was impressed with the build quality, innovation and price. When this TV came on the market and I had a chance of purchasing, I had no qualms on buying Hisense. As in my review, from packaging to use of the item, it's all first class, competition for the best

author: MileyT

body:
Having had 3 weeks with this TV, I have found the picture and sound quality to be excellent. The high refresh rate is uncommon at this size so great to have in the size I needed. Sound quality is impressive for a TV of this size providing decent bass and clear vocals. The DSP audio modes are great. Freely works well, and there's a wide range of additional streaming channels and most streaming apps are available. 
Voice search is available using the microphone in the remote and this works well. It's a great TV, easy to navigate, great picture, great sound. There are a couple of negatives, though. Vidaa has pretty good app availability, but there's no Emby client available, although Plex is present. The remote is massively over-sensitive with the buttons having very little resistance before engaging. The 9 app-specific launcher buttons may be useful for some, but it feels like they're taking up far too much space on the remote. Overall it's a great TV, and I'd recommend it to anyone looking for a TV of this size - if they can live with the remote.

body:
I was very excited when my Hisense 75E7STUK PRO was delivered... having used the same TV  for over 6 years, it was time for an upgrade! First impressions arrived before it was even switched on, it's so much lighter than my previous set, long gone are the days 2 people struggled to pick up the TV, this was light and very easy to move into position. Then it was time for the setup, you use the Vidaa app to setup the TV and this made it much easier than having to type in Wi-Fi details with your remote... setup connects you to the internet, sets everything up and you're good to go... anyone could do this. Once setup I was shocked just how many apps and channels you could receive without even connecting an aerial... Freely works great and let me watch shows I hadn't even considered watching.
One item I hadn't considered was just how quick the TV is to use, apps load so fast I no longer have time to get a drink before it's ready to watch! Picture quality is great, colours are vibrant and sound was surprisingly good for such small TV speakers. We placed the TV in a very light heavy room and the brightness of the tv is more than enough to punch through, there's only a slight light bleed on very dark pictures. I haven't had a chance to really push the TV to it's limits on gaming but gaming on the Switch was flawless. All in, very happy and would recommend this TV.
author: Mabbs

body:
My first impression of the Hisense 75E7STUK – It’s BIG, fast, and surprisingly good! For both the picture and sound it is very good value for money.
The good - Stunning picture quality for the money. Replacing my 55 inch OLED I was worried that the picture would not hold up. Overall, I had nothing to be concern about! It’s clean, and responsive. Gaming (I’m a PS5 gamer) is great. The Game mode kicks in and supports variable refresh rate, Auto Low Latency Mode etc making it a pleasure to use. Even at close range (couple of meters away) it looks good. 
The sound is balanced and the built-in subwoofers provides surprisingly robust audio, way better than the TV it’s replacing. I have a soundbar/sub but haven’t plugged it in as I’m not sure it’s needed! Likewise, the OS works very well, with fast access to apps. The Freely tuner is also very good, making it much easier to watch programmes without changes between the on demand apps i.e. it lets you watch live TV over Wi-Fi without needing an aerial, and it just works. I’ve also found the supporting mobile app really good and allows use of the TV without the remote. 
The less good - Contrast in low light. Being a QLED, the black levels and local dimming cannot match the blacks of my older OLED and you can see the backlighting “Leak” from the edges where the picture on the TV is dark. 
To conclude - Value for Money! - Massive 75" screen, that’s great for gaming, a surprisingly good sound, and great tech makes it a no brainer for the price.

author: Motys

body: The Hisense 65E7STUK PRO delivers a genuinely impressive viewing experience for its price point. The picture quality is crisp and clear, with strong colour accuracy and sharp detail that really stands out whether you’re watching films, sports, or gaming. Motion handling is very responsive, and the 144Hz Game Mode Pro makes fast‑paced content feel smooth and immediate. The app store is decent, covering all the essentials without feeling bloated. VIDAA is straightforward to navigate, and the TV gives you a good amount of user modifiability — from picture presets to advanced calibration controls, it’s easy to tune the display exactly how you like it. Audio is the one area where the TV shows its mid‑range positioning. The speakers are perfectly usable once you spend a few minutes adjusting the equaliser, and they can sound reasonably balanced after tuning. However, they’re not on the same level as the mid‑range speakers you’d find on competing brands, especially when it comes to depth and fullness. A soundbar will noticeably elevate the experience. Overall, the E7STUK PRO is a strong performer with excellent picture quality, fast responsiveness, and a flexible user experience
author: Mustafa00467

body: Out of the box, the Hisense 50E7STUK PRO TV feels well made, and I was surprised by how light it is, useful for wall mounting. The remote control is easy to use, with buttons well laid out and dedicated buttons for all the major streaming services. Setup was very easy with no TV aerial connection needed. You just plug in the power cable and you’re ready to watch content. Speaking of content, this is the first TV I’ve used with Freely, and I was impressed with the service. There is a couple of seconds delay between switching channels, which takes some getting used to. But the Freely interface, TV guide, and navigation are excellent. After adjusting the picture settings, the quality is very good, with accurate colors and sharp details. The standard settings felt very bright, 100% backlight washed out blacks and made highlights too white. I found Cinema picture mode a good starting point, reducing the backlight to 75, brightness to 45, contrast to 70, color saturation to 60, and sharpness to 0. For my room and lighting, this produced the best results. The TV performs well across all types of content, from regular TV shows and movies to fast-action sports. The sound quality is good for a flat panel TV. I didn’t notice a significant improvement with Dolby Atmos, maybe I would with a compatible external speaker system. Our current amplifier and speakers connect to the TV via HDMI ARC, but the Hisense TV supports HDMI eARC. I need to upgrade our amplifier to use our existing speaker setup.  We connected a FreeSat box via HDMI, switching to this input, the sound was much quieter, we had to increase the volume to compensate. This caused an issue, because switching back to Freely the volume was now too loud. Turning on the auto volume control setting which prevents sudden volume changes when switching inputs, didn’t help. Maybe if’s a compatibility problem but now we have Freely built-in, we probably don’t need FreeSat anymore. Aside from the volume issue, the TV is a pleasure to use. The interface is well laid out, and very responsive. You can organise the home screen moving quicklinks for your favorite services around. Download new apps and mini-games. The games are fun and easy to play, but the ads are frustrating. The built-in screen sharing works seamlessly, letting you wirelessly share your mobile screen. It’s great for quickly playing videos, sharing photos, and more with others.

body: The Hisense 43Q7STUK was an upgrade for me and boy what an upgrade! It is so light compared to the weight of my previous tv. The sleek, minimalist look of it is just gorgeous and it sits neatly and sturdily on my unit.  Unpacking the box was a delight. Two feet which are secured in place with two screws was all the setup required. It was so easy that my teenage daughter happily took over at this point. Once the tv was in place and plugged in, it could not have been easier to setup. A QR code was scanned with my smart phone and the tv was connected to my internet. For all the streaming apps etc, again it was just a case of scanning the QR code and logging in. An absolute delight for someone who loves technology but can sometimes become overwhelmed with how quickly things change. I had plugged in my firestick but I don’t need it as everything is right there on the tv menu (on demand, internet browser etc.) The picture is so crystal clear, I still mention it every time we’re watching anything and this is 3 weeks on! I don’t have young children but I was intrigued by the kids remote that comes with it. I put the batteries in and switched it on to find all the children’s tv right there. It’s a great add on for families with young ones as you know they are only accessing age appropriate programs and with an easy to use, simple remote.  The main remote has specific buttons for the more popular apps but is incredibly easy to use. There can sometimes be a slight lag between pressing the buttons and the tv reacting but I have become used to it now and know to wait a couple of seconds. It’s honestly the only fault I can find with it.  Easy to unbox, setup and use. Completely foolproof and the whole family enjoy using it. It is sat in quite a sunny part of the room which meant we could often not see the old tv for the glare but the Hisense doesn’t seem to have that problem and although the sun will lighten the picture a little, it is still easy to watch. Highly recommend this tv.
