I've had this TV for a few weeks now and really put it through its paces with Sport and animated Kids Movies in particular. I have to say...I'm really impressed with it. The 85-inch screen is absolutely massive and has completely changed how we've been watching sport and films at home. Watching football, rugby and the F1 on it feels more like being in a sports bar than sitting in the living room. The 4K picture quality is excellent with plenty of detail and really vibrant colours. Bright scenes look fantastic and the TV handles daytime viewing much better than my previous set. I spent some time testing the different picture modes and found Standard mode gave the most natural image. The AI upscaling works well with most content, although I personally found the picture looked best with some of the processing toned down...not sure why but you get a weird blur with some AI modes. Motion handling is generally very good, although on really fast-moving sports you can tell this isn't one of the higher refresh rate models. That's not a criticism as such, just something I noticed when comparing it to more expensive TVs. For everyday viewing it still looks excellent. The built-in subwoofer is probably what surprised me most. Sound is rich and punchy with enough bass that I haven't felt the need to add a soundbar yet. Dialogue is clear and films have much more depth than I expected from a TV speaker setup. Given this TV will be going in our media wall (when built) this is a massive bonus as we wont have to waste space with speakers. Setup was straightforward, the interface is responsive and apps load quickly.  Overall, if you're looking for a huge screen with great picture quality, strong built-in audio and excellent value for money, I think this TV is hard to beat.

body: The Hisense 50E7STUK 50-inch 4K QLED smart television is equipped with modern technology with incredible picture quality and good aesthetics. It offers a balance between affordability and premium features. It is designed to meet the needs of everyday viewers who value strong picture performance, intuitive smart features, and cinematic enhancements without the high price tag. I took my time writing this review to fully explore all the features first. One of the most notable aspects of this TV is the picture quality and brightness. It is important that I'm able to mirror the screen from my phone, and I'm glad I was able to do this seamlessly. The use of QLED technology allows the television to produce vibrant and rich colours, enhancing the overall viewing experience bringing scenes to life. The inclusion of Dolby Vision further elevates its performance by improving contrast and detail in HDR content, making movies and shows appear more dynamic and immersive. Even when displaying non-4K content, its upscaling capabilities ensure that images remain sharp and watchable, with an enhanced audio experience. Users seeking a more cinematic sound experience may benefit from pairing it with an external sound system or soundbar. Nevertheless, the inclusion of advanced audio formats at this price point demonstrates Hisense’s commitment to delivering value. I created an account on the VIDAA platform for additional viewing features. The interface is user-friendly and allows quick access to popular streaming services such as Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Disney+, YouTube and more. TV CHANNELS+, Freely Live TV, NOW and VOD are easily accessible on the remote. It is extremely easy to set up and lightweight, even though it looks bigger and not a slim TV. The only downside for me is that the TV stands are placed widely apart meaning the TV takes up much space when placed on a tabletop or TV stand. It's best to consider the measurements carefully before setup. This will not be an issue if mounting it on the wall. Also, I find the remote quite long which is unusual compared to other modern brands. The addition of a second remote for kids is absolutely brilliant, providing a safe and secure viewing mode for children of all ages.  Overall, this TV offers a perfect alternative viewing experience and I would highly recommend this brand to everyone.

body: I’ve been really impressed with the Hisense 55Q7STUK so far. The first thing that stands out is the design. It looks modern and premium, with an extremely narrow bezel that allows the screen to fill almost the entire front of the TV. This gives it a much more immersive feel when watching films, sports, or gaming, and it looks great mounted on a wall or sitting on a stand. The user interface is another strong point. Navigation between apps is quick and intuitive, and everything feels well organised. I particularly like how easily the TV connects to external speakers and audio devices. The setup process is straightforward, and switching between different inputs and streaming services is seamless, making everyday use hassle-free. Picture quality is very good, especially considering the price point. Colours are vibrant, detail is sharp, and content looks impressive across a range of viewing conditions. Even when the TV automatically switches into energy-saving mode, the picture remains bright and enjoyable, without a dramatic drop in quality. This is a nice balance between performance and efficiency. The only minor criticism I have is the plastic trim along the bottom of the screen. While it doesn’t detract from the overall appearance, it feels a little flimsy compared to the rest of the TV and doesn’t seem to secure the panel as firmly as I would have expected. It’s not a major issue, but it does stand out against an otherwise well-built product. Overall, the Hisense 55Q7STUK offers excellent value for money, combining stylish design, a user-friendly interface, and strong picture quality into a package that’s easy to recommend.

body: The unboxing process was nice and easy, with the TV well protected in the packaging. Once out of the packaging, I fitted the TV stand legs quickly and easily with the provided screws. The TV itself was quite light and easy to pick up considering the size. Once turned on, the TV loaded up quite quickly and went into setup mode. I chose the recommended option of downloading an app to help with a quicker setup (i.e. typing much quicker on the mobile device app). It wasn't long before the TV was all ready to go! I then tested the TV out on both HD mode and found some 4k/ULTRA HD content to see what the best resolution looked like, I have to say I didn't see any glitches or faults in the picture at all, even at 4K and with fast moving images. The colours were true to life and looked natural. The sound (especially on 4k content) was impressive considering it was from the inbuilt speakers.  I found the excellent Filmmaker mode to work well in most situations (replicating the intended appearance of the originally produced content).  Overall, I am yet to find fault with this TV in terms of it more than meeting my expectations,
author: tony.harrison

body:

body: Fantastic tv..very easy to set up..picture quality exellent..real value for your money.

body: I was surprised at how light the box was on delivery. Great TV, and the design was sleek and thin. Set up was straightforward, and the remote was very easy to use, but it looked busy. body:

author: peterkennedyuk

body:
The Hisense 65Q7STUK is a large good-looking television.  We as a family are looking for a television for family viewing, gaming, and streaming, and this television fulfilled all of these requirements perfectly.
The standout feature of this TV is the picture quality for both movies, sports and gaming.  The Hi-QLED panel produces a wonderful and accurate range of colours. It supports a huge range of HDR formats, including HDR10, 10+ adaptive and Dolby Vision IQ.  
Gaming has a Game Mode Plus feature, which has some good settings for tweaking, native panel is still 60hz refresh rate
Hisense has a proprietary VIDAA operating system which is constantly improving with updates.  This is my second Hisense TV, and the interface is fast, clean and highly intuitive.  All the APPS i need and supported and work very well with the TV.  There are some dedicated shortcut buttons on the remote control as well.
The TV also comes with Freely integration, which i think is excellent in the UK.  Effectively it allows the user to stream live UK television over Wifi using a unified TV guide!  No aerial or satellite dish needed.  Perfect and works well.
TV has a slim bezel, however for those that are not wall mounting - the feet and quite widely spaced out, this caught me out a little on my tv stand - the feet sit about 100cm apart.
Audio is good and handled by a standard two speak setup which support Dolby Atmos and DTS Virtual:X.
If you are looking for 65” superb family all-rounder television, this is the one.  Very excited that it has arrived in time for the Football World Cup 2026!
author: Dane77

body:
I was mind blown by the amazingly vivid colours, it’s absolutely fantastic! I was captivated by the intensity of them when we watched Avatar,  it even looked 4D.  The sound quality is brilliant, really fills a large room, which we wondered about before we got it. We’ve a cinema sofa so expected we might use that, it was very easy to link the TV up to it, but, the TV made the sofa redundant as it’s sound quality is so good. It’s easy to set up and navigate through the different options available (and there are loads). 
My other half’s really impressed with how it automatically adjusts the screen to create a crisp, clean picture and how fluid motion is when watching sports. Voice control is great to have, makes life so much easier. He was also surprised and impressed with how the TV turns off, like curtains closing across the screen. A small thing but then it’s the little things that take you by surprise that leave a big impression as it shows attention to detail, which most definitely is the case when this TV was designed. 
The layout of the home page is so clear and easy to use, with all the channels and apps at your fingertips. The only regret is we didn’t get this TV sooner!"
author: kirstin.mclellan

body:

author: sharon2061

body:
I’ve had the Hisense 65Q7STUK for a while now and overall I’m genuinely happy with it. The picture is the main reason: it looks punchy and sharp, colours pop without feeling cartoonish, and HDR movies/series look properly “cinema-like”. Motion is solid too — when I was watching NBA games, fast plays and camera pans stayed clear instead of turning into a blurry mess. For gaming it feels responsive, and the screen size works perfectly for a living room setup.
Sound is better than I expected for a flat TV, and for everyday watching it’s totally fine (a soundbar is still a bonus, but not a must). Setup was quick, menus are easy, and day-to-day use is straightforward. The only thing that occasionally annoys me is the built-in browser and the on-screen keyboard: sometimes there’s a noticeable delay after typing, like the TV reacts a few seconds later. It’s not a dealbreaker, and I’m hoping a firmware update will smooth that out. Overall: excellent TV for the money, and I’d still recommend it.
author: dm_stt

body:
I've been really pleased with my Hisense TV since getting it. As a busy mum with a house full of different viewing tastes, it gets used for everything from films and series to YouTube and gaming, and it's handled everything well.
The picture quality is excellent, with bright colours and a clear, sharp image. Watching sport and films on it has been particularly impressive, and the larger screen makes a real difference. The sound is also better than I expected without needing any extra speakers.
Setup was straightforward and I was able to get everything connected quickly. The smart features are easy to use, and switching between apps is simple, which is important when different family members are constantly wanting to watch different things.
Overall, it's been a great purchase and offers excellent value for money. It looks modern, performs well, and has become a big part of our day-to-day family entertainment. I would happily recommend a Hisense TV to friends and family.
author: emma61289

body: I have been testing the Hisense 43Q7STUK and my first impressions have been extremely positive. From unboxing to everyday use, the whole experience has been simple, smooth and enjoyable. The setup was incredibly easy. After wall-mounting the TV, I connected it to my Wi-Fi and followed the clear on-screen instructions. Within minutes, everything was ready to use. The tv is super light, it does come with feet for table mounting. The design is sleek and modern, with slim bezels and a discreet Hisense logo that allows the screen to take centre stage. Mounted on the wall, it sits flush and looks stylish and premium in my kitchen. Picture quality is excellent. Colours are vibrant, images are sharp, and the overall viewing experience feels immersive. Whether watching films, TV shows or sports, the screen delivers impressive clarity and detail. A real highlight is how easy it is to access streaming services. I connected Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV, Spotify, Netflix and Disney+ with ease, and everything runs smoothly. The TV also includes Freely, giving access to live and on-demand TV channels without the need for an aerial. There's the VIDAA app that allows you to use you phone as a remote control, amongst other things, which is a cool feature. I particularly like that the TV comes with two remote controls. There is a standard remote for everyday use and a cute white-and-blue remote designed specifically for children. The kids’ remote works alongside the parental control features, helping to restrict content and giving children safe, easy access to age-appropriate entertainment. Navigation is quick and intuitive, and switching between apps is seamless. Overall, the Hisense 43Q7STUK combines excellent picture quality, a stylish design, easy setup and thoughtful family-friendly features. It has exceeded my expectations and is a fantastic smart TV for both adults and children.
author: MumTwo

body: We’ve been using the 55” Hisense TV for a little while now and overall we’re really impressed with it.  The setup process was incredibly easy, pretty much plug in and follow the on-screen instructions and you’re away.  Connecting everything was straightforward too.  We hooked it up to our existing TV box and even our old-school DVD player, and both worked perfectly first time with no issues at all. The remote control is simple and easy to use, and navigating around the menus and apps is really smooth.  One feature we particularly liked was how easy it is to add and log into apps using QR codes on your phone, such a quick and hassle free process.  There’s also a huge range of apps available, definitely enough choice for anyone. The sound quality is surprisingly good for a flat screen TV, clear and more than powerful enough for everyday viewing. The TV itself looks sleek and modern sitting on our living room cabinet, even though it’s only in a temporary position until our media wall is built.  It's also surprisingly lightweight considering its size. The only small downside for me personally is that I haven’t quite managed to get the picture as vivid as I’d ideally like. I’ve tried adjusting the various settings including Cinema, Dynamic, contrast and sharpness, and while the picture is still very good, it’s just slightly less punchy than my own personal preference.  That said, this is very much subjective and won’t bother everyone. Overall though, this is a great value TV, easy to set up, easy to use, packed with features and apps, and looks great too. Very happy with it so far.

body: I have been using the Hisense 55Q7STUK in my living room and overall I have been really impressed. The size is brilliant for the space and the TV looks premium, with thin bezels, a sturdy feel and a clean design that fits nicely into the room. Setup was simple and the smart TV experience has been one of the biggest highlights for me. The menus feel easy to use, apps are simple to navigate and connecting devices, including my console and Alexa, was straightforward. Picture quality is very good in many situations, especially films, TV shows and YouTube. Colours are bright and vibrant, the screen gets more than bright enough during the day and I have noticed very little glare. Gaming also feels responsive, with no noticeable input lag in my experience. There are a few areas where it is not perfect. Live sport has sometimes looked a little inconsistent in quality, although I am not sure whether this is the TV, the stream or my network. The black levels are also not the deepest and can look a little grey in darker scenes. Sound is better than I expected from built-in speakers, especially with dialogue enhancement, but it still will not replace a proper soundbar. Overall, I would definitely recommend it as a strong mid-range TV, especially if you want a good balance of picture quality, smart features and value.
author: kaithomson

body: The Hisense comes well packaged and is easy to get to by removing the outer sleeve rather than having to lift the TV out of the box. Fitting the stand was easy with 4 screws and the feet have protective pads for the surface the TV will stand on. Turning on for the first time there is an easy option using the Vidaa app and your smart phone if you already have a Hisense TV. The TV connects to your wireless through the Phone and then everything is done. Setting up the apps is easy with QR scanning and within 5 minutes had the TV setup with all the usual streaming services all setup. The picture quality is excellent with clear vibrant colours and crisp edges and things like football and films are nice and clear even though this is a big 65 inch screen it doesn't loose the image quality like some TVs do.  The sound of this TV is amazing and gives surround effect which in the large room it was located gives a really realistic effect. The menu system is simple and intuitive and to be fair it doesn't need much interaction of changing of things as default settings are good enough for me. A number of features like wake up on LAN or wake up when it detects you are awake are interesting but not really something I would need on this large model as it is not for the bedroom but for an outdoor cabin. The TV has Freely built in which works fine and saves the need for an aerial connection giving all the terrestrial stations and accessible via the guide. The remote has all the usual buttons and easy to use and automatically sets up when the TV turns on. it has a number of useful shortcuts too the standard streaming apps and Freely it is quite large which may not appeal to some people but didn't bother me. I really like this TV both for picture, sound and features and it is probably the best purchase I have made for a TV.

body:

body:
My first impression of the Hisense TV was that it was surprisingly light to handle, with a sleek design and a good-quality finish and feel. But it’s very good! The sound from the TV speakers themselves is also very good.  For gaming, the picture quality is fantastic, with sharp visuals, movement and vibrant colours that really enhance the experience after setting to Sport settings. Again, the standard setting seemed a little flat. Overall, I’m very impressed with the quality and performance of the TV. I’m very happy with the purchase.

body:
When this TV arrived, it couldn't have come at a better time as my old TV had finally given up. I've been using it for a while now and overall I'm really happy with it. Set up was very straightforward and I could log in to most apps from my phone, using QR codes. The picture quality is excellent, with bright colours and a clear, sharp display. The sound is surprisingly good too – I don't have to turn the volume up very high to hear everything clearly.
Having apps such as YouTube, Netflix and BBC iPlayer built in is super useful, and I've enjoyed browsing some of the internet-powered TV channels as well. It's nice having everything in one place rather than needing extra devices.

body: The Hisense Q7STUK 55" is a masterclass in combining high-end entertainment features with everyday practical usability, with its sleek, capable display, this model hits all the right marks. ​Stylish Aesthetics & Picture Brilliance  ​Straight out of the box, the TV commands attention with its stylish looks. body: I've been using the Hisense 65Q7STUK for two weeks now and I'm really impressed. It looks fantastic in my living room, with its slim profile and minimal bezel giving it a clean, modern look. Setting it up was straightforward. The stand feet need to be screwed in with a screwdriver, which only took a few minutes (but is a 2 person job - one to hold the TV while the other screws in). I won't need a soundbar. The Freely app is a great feature, delivering live TV channels over your internet connection without needing an aerial or satellite dish. I've connected mine via an ethernet cable for a stable connection. There are three HDMI ports... I've got a PC and a games console hooked up and still have one spare port. Overall, the Hisense 65Q7STUK is a brilliant TV that ticks all the boxes for picture quality, sound and smart features.

body:
I've been pleasantly surprised by the Hisense 55Q7STUK. The TV itself is impressively thin and lightweight, making it easy to mount and set up. The operating system is responsive and easy to navigate, with apps opening quickly and menus feeling snappy. There are quite a few apps pre-installed out of the box, but most can be removed if you prefer a cleaner home screen. body: Just delighted with my New HiSense 75" TV.  UPgrading from an older OLED 65" set (6 years old), I wasn't sure what to expect from HiSense.  First thing we noticed was the weight difference - so much lighter than the old TV which made the seamless install nice and easy (but still a 2-person job). The difference in size was delightful - seems to be a slightly different ratio to the old set, but nice and slimline, so sits beautifully flush to the wall.  Set-up was sooo seamless and really quick.  Particularly impressed with Freely as a way to access terrestrial TV - makes everything HD without having to select the specific HD channels. Really sharp images and dealt really well with movement - whether in movies or sports.  Particularly looking forward to the World Cup matches now. body: It's a very good value TV for the price, it also has composite inputs which I required, and all the usual apps and sockets including a satellite socket! But buyers need to understand two things about Freely: firstly there is no longer an option in the inputs menu for terrestrial TV only. Terrestrial channels (and maybe satellite too - I haven't tried) are all incorporated into the hybrid TV guide if not available from the internet, with no obvious indication whether they come from the aerial or the internet. This does of course mean that the channels that do come from the internet will be great HD quality and in many cases pausable and rewindable. Secondly you will have to sign in to the five main free TV channels because those ones will certainly come from the internet without the option. That's quite a process and means setup takes time. body:
"Brilliant Display. I've been looking for a new TV for my home office, I wanted something that was versatile enough for gaming and general use.

The 55U7QTUK PRO has not disappointed, after years of using other brands TV's throughout my house, I may have just been converted, the screen is bright and vivid, whilst there is glare from the window, that is to be expected as most TV's would have this unless it was a matte panel anyway.

The inclusion of Freely makes watching TV quick and easy, a great option to get started especially for less tech savvy people, I hooked up a handheld pc with an EGPU to it. 
It took a while to get the correct settings for the 165hz display, but this was a windows thing not a TV thing, but once I got it set up, it's been working perfectly, no issues at all. 

The only "negative" I have is that HiSense include their own OS (VIDAA), which is lacking a bit compared to Android TV offerings. I use an android based device on my other TV's so I'll be doing the same for this one, it's just a shame that in this day and age with such widespread options HiSense have opted for their own proprietary offering. 

This is not by any means a deal-breaker, it's easily rectified with an android TV stick if required, but this is more to my use-case and may not affect others in the slightest.

Overall I would highly recommend this product, and I will certainly be replacing my other TV's with HiSense options when they eventually give up."

body:
"Hisense 55U7QTUK PRO - Gamers Delight. I'm fairly new to Hisense, and had done some research previously. However what attracted me to this was the 165Hz Game Mode Ultra. Wow, just wow! Immersive gaming, either playing sport simulation games, to first-person shooters, the picture, colours and refresh rate are just amazing. Then add the 2.1.2 Channel sound with Dolby Atmos, and it is next level. I also liked that fact that there is a built-in subwoofer. It means you need to play around a bit, but once you get it right, the sound for gaming and movies adds to the experience (without the need for additional speakers). Some nice additional features, including IMAX Enhanced and Filmmaker mode - allowing you to watch the film just the filmmakers intended! Also has Freely built in - which allows you to watch a mixture of live channel and catch up content using an internet connection. Still finding my way, but has some nice features, including allowing you to 'pause' live TV. Finally all the usual mainstream apps are integrated, Amazon Prime Video, Disney+ and Netflix to name a few. Oh a small mention for the remove control - it has a nice solar remote for sustainable power. Excellent touch. All in all a great TV!
"

The picture stays clear even in a bright room, which I really appreciate. The menu is simple to navigate, nothing confusing or clunky.
As for sound, it seems pretty good, but we usually use a separate sound system (my husband’s choice), so I can’t really comment too much on the built-in sound.
It comes with the Freely option, you can watch live UK channels over the internet, no aerial needed.
The only small downside is that since it’s a Chinese brand, it doesn’t come with Google built in, so no Google Assistant or Play Store. But honestly, we haven’t missed it.
All in all, super happy with this TV., totally worth it! Thank you Hisense!"

body:
"Quality picture with superb sound . Having finally jumped onto the 4K TV bandwagon, I have to honestly say I’m truly impressed by the increased picture quality.

I normally just use Sky to watch TV and my subscribed apps (purely because they’re all located in one place) . I also have the HD package for the channels. After going from a non-4K TV to one that is, with the added benefit of an AI chip installed, the picture clarity is greatly improved. The usual text you see on programs and films like the intro text and end credits are crystal clear. I literally haven’t seen one blurred word or number since plugging it in. I’ve also set the picture smoothing settings to low which improves the quality without getting the soap opera effect.

The sound quality is fantastic. You can hear every word spoken clearly and the TV automatically knows when an action heavy scene is showing and kicks in the subwoofer.

Setting up the TV was really quick when you use the VIDAA app at the same time. Settings like connecting to the WiFi is super quick as it matches the WiFi your phone or tablet is connected to, thus saving you time putting the password in manually.

The smart features are simple and easy to use as well as switching to your other input sources.

I am yet to try Game Mode as I need to get my PS3 (yes I know it’s old!) out of storage. Honestly I don’t use it for gaming anymore but still use it to watch my Blu-ray movies. Can’t wait to see what the extra hertz and upscaling looks like.

For me, the size of the TV is great and fits in the room just fine. Either way, I’d happily recommend this TV whatever size you pick."

body:
"A Brilliant All-Rounder with a Near Perfect UI I’ve been really impressed with this TV since setting it up. The AI picture settings are genuinely brilliant - everything looks fantastic without needing to constantly adjust things manually. After looking into them a bit more it's based on ambient light and the type of programme so that's pretty epic!

Whether we've had animated films on for the kids or I've been able to kick back and watch the rugby, the picture is vibrant, smooth, and full of detail. Even during the day in a bright room, there’s no issue with glare or fading colours - we have big dormer windows and it handles bright light really well, which is something we were hoping for in this TV.

I’ve also been pleased with the sound. It’s clear and balanced, and we haven’t felt the need for extra speakers. Dialogue is crisp, and there’s a decent amount of depth, which makes a big difference for movies and action scenes. The built-in sound system gives a full, room-filling experience without needing to add a soundbar. Definitely play around with the sound settings as well for the best experience!

Apps load quickly, and everything on the smart system runs smoothly. Switching between streaming services is quick and responsive. The remote is thoughtfully designed too - it’s got all the main app buttons built in, and I especially like that you can customise one of the buttons to go directly to a specific app or device input. That’s been a nice bonus. It even charges by sunlight and has a USB-C port, so it never runs out of battery...well it hasn't yet and I live in Scotland!

The overall design of the TV is really modern and premium-looking. It sits nicely on our unit but would also look great wall-mounted (which it will be soon). The stand offers two height positions, which is helpful if you’re using a soundbar or want it a bit higher if you're a giant like me. 

The set-up was simple and guided me through everything clearly - I was up and running in less than 10 minutes. Note, it is fairly heavy to lift onto the stand yourself but with some careful positioning and the multifunctional packaging (that's not even a joke just wait 'til you see the instructions) you can manage it yourself.

Overall, this TV has been a fantastic addition to our home. It looks good, performs well in all kinds of situations, and is easy to use every day. Definitely recommend if you're looking for a feature-packed, smart and reliable upgrade."

body:
"Great tv for a great price! I’ve been checking out the new Hisense 55U8QTUK MiniLED 165Hz Smart AI, and honestly… it’s amazing for the price. If you want a TV that looks high-end without paying crazy money… this might be the one.
The screen is super bright, even in the middle of the day with sunlight coming in. The colors are rich, and the black parts of the screen actually look sooo dark not washed out. It’s awesome for watching movies or Netflix. The picture looks really sharp and smooth, even during fast scenes.
if you are into gaming ( like me) PS5, Xbox, or even PC—this TV is a beast. It can do 4K at 165Hz, which is faster than most TVs. Games feel smooth and super responsive and very low input lag. Basically, it’s made for gaming.
The sound is better than I expected. It has built-in speakers with Dolby Atmos, and it even has a little subwoofer in the back for bass. Movies and games sound full, and you might not even need a soundbar. Just a heads-up… if you mount it on the wall, the bass can make the wall vibrate a little.
It’s a solid… well-built TV with a sleek design. The stand is adjustable, and the whole thing looks and feels like a premium product. Definitely doesn’t look cheap.
This is one of the best TVs you can buy right now if you want awesome quality without paying OLED prices. Great for movies, sports, and especially gaming. Hisense really nailed it with this one.
Would totally recommend. It is bright, fast, great sounding, and full of features. Definitely feels like you’re getting more than what you paid for.

"

body:
"Feature packed and well built Hisense is not a brand I have previously considered generally tending to look at more well known brands. However I was pleasantly surprised with my latest purchase of the 55U8QTUK. The TV was extremely well packaged, something I was grateful for given the weight of the TV. At first this might sound like a negative but I consider this a big postive. Many TV's now are so thin and light and can often feel fragile, not so with this model from Hisense, It feels quality and robust and well engineerd. 

The unboxing experience was good with everything well packaged and easily identifiable. I have the TV wall mounted and therefore didn't use the included stand however I have no doubt from the build quality of the stand it would have no problem supporting the TV should you choose to mount yours on a media unit. 

Powering up the TV I was greeted by an unfamiliar VIDAA operating system for the TV. I'm pleased to say it was fast and responsive with pleasent graphics and an easy to navigate and intuative design. I was able to setup all of my frequently used apps quickly and easily. 

One thing I must emphasize is the features and quality feel of the supplied remote in hand, also the fact that it doesn't need batteries and is powered by sunlight is a novel but useful highlight. 

I have a number of the latest gaming consoles and was pleased to see that all of the HDMI inputs are of the latest 2.1 generation and also supported my high-end gaming PC up to 165Hz refresh rate something not supported by many other TV's currently. 

Also a really nice unique feature of this TV and something which I cannot find on any other TV is a USB-C input this means I could connect my tablet and laptop via a single USB-C cable and again I was able to get full 4K resolution!

Overall I have been massively impressed by both the design, features and quality of this TV and will be sure to consider Hisense products in the future based on this purchase."

body: Very impressed with the picture even without any changes to the 'out of the box' settings. Great upscaling of SD signal. It comes with a solid heavy TV stand if you want to make it stand, but because we have a child, we preferred to have it on the wall. It was easy to have it up on the wall and the setup was relatively quick. 

Image is great. We have used the same cartoons my son is watching to compare with our previous TV, and I believe Hisense offers a more natural, bright image. 

VIDAA App - you can control the TV from an app installed on your phone. We were using the Apple Box before to do the same thing, but we found it fascinating that the TV itself allows us to do this. 

VIDAA Voice - helps you control your tv hands free

Freely - Live TV. Even though we pay for the TV License we never used to watch live channels because of the inconvenience trying to find the TV remote control. Picture Mode: It has so many options such as Enhanced ACR, Filmmaker, HDR Standard, etc. I love the fact that it has Max Cinema Too. It is something I look forward trying in the coming weeks.

Picture Mode Settings, Advanced Settings - you can adjust the brightness , color, motion, clarity and overscan. 

Picture Mode Game Settings- it comes with its own picture settings for games

Amazon Alexa- we don’t currently have it set up, but it is available

BBC Account - you can connect prior to your BBC Account when you use hands free voice 

I am very happy to have tried Hisense and I would recommend it with my eyes closed. Great quality for a very good price. My husband is in love with the design and the finish of the remote control, the tv itself. Very sleek design.

I particulary like the layout and feel of the remote control and the built in solar charger to save having to find batteries when you least expect. Its reassuring to see the effort put into the remote rather than leaving it to chance with a flimsy unintuative lump of plastic.

I don't have an external aerial and I rely on a well known satellite system but I was eager to see what free to air channels I could get using the Freely streaming app which is slowly rolling out. Unfortunately I hit a hurdle here and the App failed to install.

PROS
- Very clear detailed 4K and HD picture from those Mini LEDs
- Good sound with Dolby Atmos quality and built in sub-woofer
- Solid centre stand
- Plenty of connection options
- Excellent build quality and style, inc remote
- Easy setup
- Good GUI
- 2 year manufacturer warranty


CONS
- The Freely App failed to install - reason unknown - Freely servers?
- Slight motion blur when people running during a movie scene
- Stand a bit fiddley to assemble and fit to TV (read manual)
- It's heavy, need two people but it's a 65" TV so really to be expected

So to sum up, this new 65" U8NQT model for 2024 should be on your shortlist if you're looking for a fully featured sub £2k 4K smart TV.

You won't regret it.

body:
Firstly might I say, If you're looking for a great image, sound and a user friendly UI then this really is the Tv for you.

Hisense have come a long way in the recent months with making a really high quality product that can easily compete with the top brands. Both the TV and the included remote feel high quality and gives me a sense that it will last for a good number of years.

I have this tv mounted on my wall with a standard 400x600 wall mount and it looks great. As advertised, I have minimal glare from both light coming through the window in the day and internal lights at night. The sound quality is as great as any other premium TV sound output and wouldn't need any further aid from a sound bar but I already had one so I connected it and used that after testing. 

The picture quality from the TV is fantastic when you get a 4k video up. The blacks are so dark and there is no light bleed whatsoever. The only issues I have found is there are some vertical bars visible when the picture pans sideways (noticed during a football match), these are minor and can only be seen under certain conditions but once I have seen them I can't unsee them (those who know, know). This could be a manufacture defect or maybe even settings that need changing in the TV but more searching is required for me on this front as when in a dynamic picture mode, the TV will decide what's the best colours and contrast.

The apps built into the TV are great and I would argue you no longer need a coax feed to the back of the TV as all of the major channels are accessible over the internet apps.

I did try to use the mobile phone app during set up but it struggled to pair with the TV. I would class myself as an average user of tech so I know my way around a phone and how to try other methods if something isn't quiet working. Once the TV was set up, you can use the app as a remote but I haven't really done so as the included TV remote is fantastic.

So, in summary. Would I recommend this TV to you if you're reading this?
Yes! The picture quality and sound is great and certainly a big contender with the top TVs out there right now. Even with the minor issue with my TV picture (probably is a setting somewhere), 99% of the time I'm blown away with how crisp and clear the image is. I truly haven't seen a TV yet without light bleed into the blacks until I watched this one!

body:
Only had the TV for a couple of days, then returned it as it wasn’t what I expected. Don’t get me wrong, the value for money for an 85” is outstanding these days, but I just don’t have high picture quality expectations or expect it to pull off incredible HDR. 

Pros: size to value
          Ok picture quality 
          Cinematic size 

Cons: matte anti-reflective coating
           Micro stutter like all TCL TV’s
           Green push-in colour 
           Not that bright

So the size is amazing as you’re getting that cinematic immersion, with ok picture quality.
But the colours had a weird green tint out of the box, which I found very distracting. You can correct it to a degree with the white balance settings, but then you’ll be pushing other colours slightly off without realising it. Could have just been a slightly faulty unit though, so who knows as others may not be experiencing this. The matte screen is great, and you’ll love it if you only watch this tv in a sun-soaked room or a room with major lighting that you never turn off. It’s brilliant at handling reflections in these scenarios, but the downside of that is the contrast takes a massive hit. You have to keep this thing pretty much maxed out with brightness and contrast to actually look decent. So as soon as you dim the lights or switch them off, or you close your curtains as the sun’s gone down, then switch it into, say, filmmaker mode, which dims the unit down, then it struggled to look good as it’s having to fight the matte screen from within to push out the contrast to make the image look clean and clear, so it left it looking flat and dull, unfortunately.

So if you only watch in daytime bright rooms, then yes, get this tv but if you have a mixed usage and like watching in the evenings or darker room movie nights, then I’d probably skip this tv altogether.

body: Right out of the box, the Hisense 32A5NQTUK impresses with its sleek, modern panel design. It's surprisingly lightweight, making it easy to mount on my bedroom TV stand without any hassle. The setup process is simple and straightforward, I just followed the on-screen prompts, connected to Wi-Fi, and was good to go in no time. Even without tweaking any settings, the picture quality is sharp and clear, delivering vibrant colours and good contrast. There are plenty of customisable options available if you want to fine tune it further for your preferences. The remote is a nice, slim size with responsive button presses. I especially like the quick access buttons for popular streaming apps like Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video, Disney+, and more. The user interface is intuitive and user-friendly, making navigation around menus and features feel effortless. This TV comes loaded with built-in apps, live TV channels, and a wide variety of content, including games. It's a solid hub for entertainment without needing extra devices. Integration with Alexa works well, I can turn on the TV, adjust the volume, and issue other commands hands-free. AirPlay support is also excellent, allowing easy streaming from my Apple devices. The VIDAA app is another great feature; it lets me customise the app order, search for movies, videos, and shows, and even control the TV remotely via my phone. The setup process is simple and straightforward, I just followed the on-screen prompts, connected to Wi-Fi, and was good to go in no time.

The user interface is intuitive and user-friendly, making navigation around menus and features feel effortless.

This TV comes loaded with built-in apps, live TV channels, and a wide variety of content, including games. It's a solid hub for entertainment without needing extra devices.

Integration with Alexa works well, I can turn on the TV, adjust the volume, and issue other commands hands-free. AirPlay support is also excellent, allowing easy streaming from my Apple devices. The VIDAA app is another great feature; it lets me customise the app order, search for movies, videos, and shows, and even control the TV remotely via my phone. This is particularly handy since I'm always misplacing my remotes!

Overall, the Hisense TV is a great value for a compact smart TV, offering strong performance in a bedroom or secondary room setup. While the sound can be a bit underwhelming for larger spaces, the visuals and smart capabilities more than make up for it.

body: Its amazing nice bright picture and reasonably priced
Using as large pc screen, good picture on tv

When I started the setup i.e. autoscan TV channels, i was immediately faced with setting up a parental pin before i was able to proceed any further. There was no explanation why i was compelled to do this at the very beginning of the set up and when I emailed Hisense they NEVER replied. I eventually found a hisense forum online which advised that this was part of some privacy policy and there was no workaround 

Once I had set the parental pin, I did the TV channel scan and proceeded to the next step which asked me to connect to the internet via wifi or ethernet which then installed Freely. 

Over the next few days I discovered that Freely takes over the TV and when viewing programmes using Freely, I am prevented from using the PVR function i.e. ability to time shift – pause live TV or create recordings. 

If I then reverted back to factory settings and went through the setup BUT without connecting to the internet which prevented Freely from being installed, I was able to watch the TV via Freeview and utilise the PVR function. However, if I wanted to use any of the catch up services i.e. iPlayer, C4, C5 etc.. I had to connect to the internet which then automatically installed Freely which took over the TV and I lost the PVR functionality. There was NO option to toggle between Freeview as a separate source and Freely. 

Before I purchased this TV, there was nothing in the specifications or reviews to warn me about the Frankenstein nature of how this TV operated. There was also NO manual on the Hisense website to refer to. I had to refer to ChatGPT to help me understand this so called ‘hybrid TV’. I subsequently returned the TV for a full refund. 

Furthermore, I found that the so called HD quality of the HD channels was not great and there was hardly any difference between picture quality for non and HD channels. This was another disappointment. Fortunately, the user interface was fine. 

I strongly suspect that other TVs with Freely and PVR will behave exactly the same. Competitor brands confirmed this was the case with their TV’s. This is all fine if you don’t require time shift.

But what is the point of providing time shift if you have to disconnect the TV from wifi in order to access this feature BUT then if you need to use any catch up services, you need to reconnect to wifi which installs Freely and disables time shift?!!!

body: "Hisense 32 inch Freely Tv. This 32 inch Freely TV is great in places such as kitchen and bedroom and has all the features that a Main Tv would have but in a small unit. Setup is quite simple, plug in select your country, enter your wireless code and it does the rest. After about 5 minutes and one download of new software it has found all channels and setup the freely channels. I have added Netflix, Amazon and Disney all through the scan app and enter Tv code and this also all worked fine and quickly with the use of a mobile phone. The remote has lots of quick select buttons including the usual Disney, Prime, Netflix, YouTube, and NowTV but also includes others. What I found really good is the Freely system as the picture quality is excellent and no interference as our previous Tv used an old coax aerial feed which was prone to glitches and interference from electrical items, so far none of this with Freely. The picture quality is very good and sound certainly good enough for a small TV with Dolby Dtx. There are many other features an enthusiast can play with in the settings but for me I prefer the plug and play options preset. The only small gripe I had was the new spacing of the wall hanging bracket threaded holes as they seem to have made them different to my old VESA backplate which was square and this new one is considerably longer gap in the portrait style (see photo). Another little thing is the white flashing light under the unit is not in the centre and this is made obvious as the Hisense logo text at the bottom of the TV is central so it looks a bit odd when the white light box is obviously mounted to the right of centre. Is it value for money, yes I would say so for the features and new Freely system."

body: "Excellent quality and value. For a small TV it packs a punch. It has useful shortcut buttons at the top of the remote, making things like YouTube and Netflix easy to use with the click of a button. Once connected to WiFi, which was a very easy process, everything is easily accessible including the built in TV channels, as we do not have an aerial in the room it is in. The set up was simple and aesthetically pleasing, using simple colours and font. We have enjoyed using the TV every day, it has been a work horse and has taken everything we have asked of it. The speed of loading the apps is very good, taking usually less than a second to switch between apps. Overall, I would give this TV a five out of five, for ease of use, set up speed, picture quality and the number of apps pre installed."

body:
For a large TV this is light and sleek. With minimal edging the design really appeals. 

Setting the TV up was effortless with smart technology to easily link in to all my pre-existing apps. 

The remote control is clear and easy to understand without having to look at instructions and appears very touch responsive. Having the smart function buttons on one remote is great as saves having loads all over the place (fire stick etc) My only critique is that it looks and feels very cheap and a bit plasticky, this doesn't really fit with the aesthetic of the TV but it works and is just a remote control after all.  

The picture is clear and crisp with great colour definition, my grandson loved watching Pixar movies on it as the colour really pops.  The built in Freeview gives loads of choice and again is really easy to use. Sound quality is also great, sounds as good as my previous TV without having to use a sound bar.

Only real issue with this TV is there is no scart socket so if you're old like me and have an ancient DVD player and a stack of DVDs you're a bit out of luck though I'm sure some techies would be able to provide a sensible solution.

This TV does have an F energy rating so probably not the most environmentally friendly out there if that's of concern but all in all it's a great TV

The VOD, TV+ and VIDAA services are just a waste I will never use them.

All in all wish I kept my old dumb TV and bought a Roku box.

body: Right out of the box, the Hisense 32A5NQTUK impresses with its sleek, modern panel design. It's surprisingly lightweight, making it easy to mount on my bedroom TV stand without any hassle. The setup process is simple and straightforward, I just followed the on-screen prompts, connected to Wi-Fi, and was good to go in no time. Even without tweaking any settings, the picture quality is sharp and clear, delivering vibrant colours and good contrast. There are plenty of customisable options available if you want to fine tune it further for your preferences. The remote is a nice, slim size with responsive button presses. I especially like the quick access buttons for popular streaming apps like Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video, Disney+, and more. The user interface is intuitive and user-friendly, making navigation around menus and features feel effortless. This TV comes loaded with built-in apps, live TV channels, and a wide variety of content, including games. It's a solid hub for entertainment without needing extra devices. Integration with Alexa works well, I can turn on the TV, adjust the volume, and issue other commands hands-free. AirPlay support is also excellent, allowing easy streaming from my Apple devices. The VIDAA app is another great feature; it lets me customise the app order, search for movies, videos, and shows, and even control the TV remotely via my phone. This is particularly handy since I'm always misplacing my remotes! Overall, the Hisense TV is a great value for a compact smart TV, offering strong performance in a bedroom or secondary room setup. While the sound can be a bit underwhelming for larger spaces, the visuals and smart capabilities more than make up for it.

My wife also said it was a much better picture then she was expecting too. The sound had a good balance for such a small tv, not tinny in the highs and had some lows too. It was very well balanced, voices sounded natural and were rather clear for a tv of this size with a small footprint. The Tv remote has a good variety of buttons for the major apps and are clearly marked so made navigating it easy. The Tv’s menu was easy to follow and navigate and is exceptionally well set out and obviously well planned. The navigation of the menu was smooth and when watching any of the streaming services via the apps it is very smooth and with no buffering, lagging or hesitation. Overall this tv is amazing, when you compare the features, picture quality and ease of use with others of this size it definitely holds it own and the price is absolutely the cherry on top, I would not hesitate to recommend this size for any kids bedroom or spare room.

body: After living with the Hisense 43Q7STUK for a few weeks, I can honestly say it has exceeded my expectations. I wasn’t looking for anything overly complicated, just a TV with a great picture and easy-to-use features, and it delivers on both. The first thing that stood out was how straightforward everything was. From taking it out of the box to getting it connected and ready to watch, the whole process was refreshingly simple. Within a short time I was signed into my streaming services and browsing through content without needing to dig through manuals or menus. The picture quality is easily the star of the show. Films, sports and everyday TV all look sharp and vibrant, with colours that really stand out without looking unnatural. Even during bright afternoons, when sunlight fills the room, the screen remains clear enough to enjoy without constantly adjusting blinds or curtains. One feature I didn’t expect to use was the children’s remote, but it’s actually a thoughtful addition. It’s simple, colourful and gives younger viewers an easy way to access suitable content, which I can imagine being a real bonus for families. The smart TV interface is well laid out and includes all the apps I regularly use, meaning I’ve been able to retire my streaming stick completely. The dedicated app buttons on the remote are handy too, making it quick to jump straight into whatever I want to watch. There is occasionally a slight delay when navigating menus, but it’s minor and hasn’t affected my overall experience. Considering everything else the TV offers, it’s a small compromise. Overall, this TV feels like a fantastic all-round package. It looks stylish, performs brilliantly and is simple enough for everyone in the household to use. If you’re upgrading from an older set, you’ll definitely notice the difference.

body: I have had this tv a few weeks now.  Delivery and set up was surprisingly easy. The box is designed so you dont have to lift it up, it opens round the TV.  Assembling the legs was straight forward, there are 2 widths depending on where you are putting it. Once on, we used wider settings its very stable even on our temporary table as we plan a media wall to give this great tv its max effect.  Setting up took a couple of mins and was all done, very easy to follow steps. Its compatibility to link with home features makes it more impressive. It was super easy to sign in to our subscriptions we have.  First impressions when we got it set up were wow... the sound is great, clear and well projected round the room we have. We decided on a larger than planned as my little boy is visually impaired. This TV size means he can join in on watching and movie nights. The subtitles are a brilliant size, actually had to move back which really adds for us. The picture is crystal clear, even when closer its not pixilated or blurry.  The app feature is great, can turn off when the children forget too.  We have also tried a console on it and wow its made that really fun to play. The children were all able to play together as my boy could see clearly!  So far this is definitely worth it, sleek thin and so light compared to our old 55" one."

body: Having previously owned a Hisense TV, I was curious to see how much they have improved over the years - and boy was I impressed! Starting with initial set-up. Very easy to use and get started. A QR code allowed access to the app to help set-up go smoothly and I was up and running within a few minutes. The user interface is very easy to use and intuitive to find your way about. Using the smart on demand features, finding apps, setting up your sound and pictures preferences - all very easy to utilise. The picture quality is superb - colours are rich and vibrant, blacks are clear and the auto adjustment features on the TV are great to ensure maximum quality when viewing darker movies. I particularly like the function where it automatically senses if a movie you are watching has Filmaker mode and it automatically switches to this to enhance your viewing.  The AI motion adjustments are great too - avoiding the motion blur effects you get with some TVs. This is particularly great when gaming - smooth motions and movements making it great to play on. Sound is very good too - a massive upgrade on previous Hisense models.  The remote is very easy to use and a good size - feels nice in your hands and the quick access to the most popular streaming apps makes for seamless switching between what your watching. body:
I've previously had Hisense TVs so you would think I knew what I was in for — Wrong! I expected minor improvements but I was very pleased with what I saw. Let's go through some of the specs that matter and made a difference to my experience: - VIDAA smart platform — THIS IS THE ONE THAT REALLY SOLD ME THIS TV. VIDAA is a lightweight Linux-based smart TV platform. What this means to us is that you can launch apps like Netflix or YouTube really fast and smooth, adding to the overall experience. No more wondering what the hell happened to the app you just started — it's just there, instantly. - Hi-QLED with Quantum Dot colour — The screen is brighter and richer than my previous TV, which was already quite impressive. Colours feel more true-to-life and punchy without looking over-saturated. A genuine step up. - 144Hz panel — I don't think this made as much difference to me personally as it did to my 9-year-old son. The feedback is that gaming is smoother and more pleasant. WIN! There are other gaming features too — Game Mode Pro and the updated Game Bar give gamers quick access to VRR, frame rate counters, and input lag settings. Proper stuff. - All the HDR modes — This bad boy supports HDR10+, HDR10+ Gaming, Dolby Vision, Dolby Vision IQ, and HLG — essentially covering every format you're likely to encounter. You're not going to hit a wall with this one. - Hi-View AI Engine (MediaTek Pentonic 700 chip) — Enables enhancements such as AI Picture, AI Light Sensor, AI 4K Upscaling, AI Detail Enhancement, AI HDR Enhancement, and AI Smooth Motion. Basically you're fully "AI'd" up - Filmmaker Mode — Preserves the director's original frame rates and colour intent without any motion processing applied. If you're a film lover, this one matters more than you'd think. The only thing that's potentially not the best is the sound quality. It's OK but not exactly hi-fi, and let's be honest — at this price point you wouldn't expect it to be either. So this review still retains 5 stars. The remote is well laid out with shortcut buttons for all the major apps. It's also Bluetooth, so you don't even have to point it at the TV — which feels delightfully lazy. Ha!
I love this TV so much that I've actually set it up as a second computer monitor. Check out the picture. Overall, I would thoroughly recommend this TV.

body: From the moment I received this 43” TV, I was pleasantly surprised by how lightweight it was; it almost felt deceptive given its size. Unboxing was straightforward, and installing the pedestal feet was simple and stress-free. The protective cardboard over the screen was a thoughtful touch, making setup much easier without worrying about accidental damage. Although I plan to wall mount it later, the initial setup was smooth and user-friendly. Powering on the TV and setting it up via the VIDAA app was effortless. Downloading the app and connecting it to the TV was quick, and the mobile setup process worked seamlessly. The WiFi connection is strong, allowing the smart interface to run smoothly and making navigation intuitive and easy to use. One of the standout features is Freely, which removes the need for a traditional TV aerial. This is incredibly convenient, simplifying installation and eliminating the hassle of running additional cables or installing an aerial point. In terms of picture and sound quality, both are excellent. The display delivers vibrant, sharp visuals across all types of genres of programs. Sports, in particular, look fantastic; fast-moving scenes are clear, bright, and easy on the eyes, which is perfect for watching events like the World Cup. The sound is also impressive, offering clear and balanced audio across volume levels. While a surround sound system would enhance bass performance, the built-in speakers are more than sufficient for a bedroom setup. If I had one suggestion, it would be to make the feet more centrally positioned. This would provide greater flexibility when placing the TV on different types of furniture. That said, it currently fits on my chest of drawers, though this is only temporary as I intend to mount it on the wall. Overall, this is a great TV with a simple and intuitive navigation system, excellent picture quality and strong, clear audio performance. I had heard of the brand before but never considered purchasing; something I now see was a mistake. This TV proves they can compete with more established brands, especially when considering the excellent value for money."

body:
I don't know where to begin for reviewing my new MASSIVE 85" Hisense TV 85E78STUK PRO. I'm actually even more impressed with it than I was expecting.
The TV it's replacing was a decent 65" TV, so was only expecting a small improvement in the picture and sound quality, and got to admit the thought had crossed my mind that because of the 20" size difference, whatever increase in picture quality with the new telly, would be lost in this increase in size. I was wrong, the sharpness for a start, is much better, as are the depths and vibrancy of colours, proper black blacks, even in a darkened room. The Tv automatically upscales standard signal to 4K. I have not altered the colours in any way, I'm extremely happy with the way they are out of the box so to speak. For the technical it boasts Quantum Dot Colour and Dolby Vision IQ. You do have preset options, like cinema, game mode, sport etc. which again I have not needed to change, although I have used the sport mode to watch football. I was showing the TV off to (jealous) friends though. Same as picture options, there are preset sound options. I've tried the music and cinema sound modes, as with picture modes, there are more options, but can't remember them all. With the sound, I did increase the bass on the graphic equaliser as I like a lot of oomph. For the technically minded it boasts 2 x 15W + 20W speakers and has eARK audio via HDMI. Again for the technical the TV boasts Dolby Atmos and DTS Virtual X decoding for immersive sound. There are plenty of connection options e.g. several HDMI's USB etc., which I won't go into as the specs are on all the sales and Hisense websites. Setting up was simple, from initial setup, to connecting to Wi-Fi. I'd say most apps what you need are pre-installed like Netflix etc. I can't comment on the installed apps as I don't have Netflix account, I almost exclusively use Sky on my TV, which this TV compliments amazingly, the Sky remote pairs easily with the TV, for automatic turning the TV on and off. One slight downside (if you can call it that) I've noticed is you need to check the little white standby light on the bottom of the TV illuminates when turning off, as you can't tell it has gone into a standby state because of the darkness of the black colour. The TV has built in Freely for viewing live TV. This seems good, although only used very briefly when first setting the TV up with using Sky. The TV remote has built in voice control, enabling use of the built in Alexa for example. Can't comment on the use of that as I have Alexa in the room already set up and don't want them fighting over each other. I was pleased to find out this TV only weighs just over 32kg (85" without stand) which is a lot lighter than my previous 65" TV. I must also point out, I measured my chimney breast wall incorrectly when measuring up for the wall bracket/mount and the TV is bigger than my original measurements, so I need to move the wall bracket before I can mount it. I thought, oh no, I've made a terrible mistake, the TV is far too big for the room when I first started viewing, BUT I have quickly become used to the size. So be brave and order the biggest you can fit in your room, you won't regret it.
In a nutshell this TV gets a thumbs up for me, I absolutely love it and don't have one regret in purchasing it. From delivery in its extremely sturdy box, to sitting watching a movie, it has brought an enormous smile to my face. Can't wait till I can get it on the wall. I might then, find even more amazing features that I have probably missed. I haven't mentioned the value for money is also excellent, getting more to the £ than most other manufacturers. I hadn't taken much notice of the brand Hisense until a couple of years ago if I'm honest. Then I looked into their side by side fridge freezers, I was impressed with the build quality, innovation and price. When this TV came on the market and I had a chance of purchasing, I had no qualms on buying Hisense. As in my review, from packaging to use of the item, it's all first class, competition for the best

Gaming (I’m a PS5 gamer) is great. The Game mode kicks in and supports variable refresh rate, Auto Low Latency Mode etc making it a pleasure to use. The sound is balanced and the built-in subwoofers provides surprisingly robust audio, way better than the TV it’s replacing. I have a soundbar/sub but haven’t plugged it in as I’m not sure it’s needed! Likewise, the OS works very well, with fast access to apps. The Freely tuner is also very good, making it much easier to watch programmes without changes between the on demand apps i.e. it lets you watch live TV over Wi-Fi without needing an aerial, and it just works. I’ve also found the supporting mobile app really good and allows use of the TV without the remote. 
The less good - Contrast in low light. Being a QLED, the black levels and local dimming cannot match the blacks of my older OLED and you can see the backlighting “Leak” from the edges where the picture on the TV is dark. 
To conclude - Value for Money! - Massive 75" screen, that’s great for gaming, a surprisingly good sound, and great tech makes it a no brainer for the price.

body: The Hisense 65E7STUK PRO delivers a genuinely impressive viewing experience for its price point. The picture quality is crisp and clear, with strong colour accuracy and sharp detail that really stands out whether you’re watching films, sports, or gaming. Motion handling is very responsive, and the 144Hz Game Mode Pro makes fast‑paced content feel smooth and immediate. The app store is decent, covering all the essentials without feeling bloated. VIDAA is straightforward to navigate, and the TV gives you a good amount of user modifiability — from picture presets to advanced calibration controls, it’s easy to tune the display exactly how you like it. Audio is the one area where the TV shows its mid‑range positioning. The speakers are perfectly usable once you spend a few minutes adjusting the equaliser, and they can sound reasonably balanced after tuning. However, they’re not on the same level as the mid‑range speakers you’d find on competing brands, especially when it comes to depth and fullness. A soundbar will noticeably elevate the experience. Overall, the E7STUK PRO is a strong performer with excellent picture quality, fast responsiveness, and a flexible user experience

body: Out of the box, the Hisense 50E7STUK PRO TV feels well made, and I was surprised by how light it is, useful for wall mounting. The remote control is easy to use, with buttons well laid out and dedicated buttons for all the major streaming services. Setup was very easy with no TV aerial connection needed. You just plug in the power cable and you’re ready to watch content. Speaking of content, this is the first TV I’ve used with Freely, and I was impressed with the service. There is a couple of seconds delay between switching channels, which takes some getting used to. But the Freely interface, TV guide, and navigation are excellent. After adjusting the picture settings, the quality is very good, with accurate colors and sharp details. The standard settings felt very bright, 100% backlight washed out blacks and made highlights too white. I found Cinema picture mode a good starting point, reducing the backlight to 75, brightness to 45, contrast to 70, color saturation to 60, and sharpness to 0. For my room and lighting, this produced the best results. The TV performs well across all types of content, from regular TV shows and movies to fast-action sports. The sound quality is good for a flat panel TV. I didn’t notice a significant improvement with Dolby Atmos, maybe I would with a compatible external speaker system. Our current amplifier and speakers connect to the TV via HDMI ARC, but the Hisense TV supports HDMI eARC. I need to upgrade our amplifier to use our existing speaker setup.  We connected a FreeSat box via HDMI, switching to this input, the sound was much quieter, we had to increase the volume to compensate. This caused an issue, because switching back to Freely the volume was now too loud. Turning on the auto volume control setting which prevents sudden volume changes when switching inputs, didn’t help. Maybe if’s a compatibility problem but now we have Freely built-in, we probably don’t need FreeSat anymore. Aside from the volume issue, the TV is a pleasure to use. The interface is well laid out, and very responsive. You can organise the home screen moving quicklinks for your favorite services around. Download new apps and mini-games. The games are fun and easy to play, but the ads are frustrating. The built-in screen sharing works seamlessly, letting you wirelessly share your mobile screen. It’s great for quickly playing videos, sharing photos, and more with others.

body: The Hisense 50E7STUK 50-inch 4K QLED smart television is equipped with modern technology with incredible picture quality and good aesthetics. It offers a balance between affordability and premium features. It is designed to meet the needs of everyday viewers who value strong picture performance, intuitive smart features, and cinematic enhancements without the high price tag. I took my time writing this review to fully explore all the features first. One of the most notable aspects of this TV is the picture quality and brightness. It is important that I'm able to mirror the screen from my phone, and I'm glad I was able to do this seamlessly. The use of QLED technology allows the television to produce vibrant and rich colours, enhancing the overall viewing experience bringing scenes to life. The inclusion of Dolby Vision further elevates its performance by improving contrast and detail in HDR content, making movies and shows appear more dynamic and immersive. Even when displaying non-4K content, its upscaling capabilities ensure that images remain sharp and watchable, with an enhanced audio experience. Users seeking a more cinematic sound experience may benefit from pairing it with an external sound system or soundbar. Nevertheless, the inclusion of advanced audio formats at this price point demonstrates Hisense’s commitment to delivering value. I created an account on the VIDAA platform for additional viewing features. The interface is user-friendly and allows quick access to popular streaming services such as Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Disney+, YouTube and more. TV CHANNELS+, Freely Live TV, NOW and VOD are easily accessible on the remote. It is extremely easy to set up and lightweight, even though it looks bigger and not a slim TV. The only downside for me is that the TV stands are placed widely apart meaning the TV takes up much space when placed on a tabletop or TV stand. It's best to consider the measurements carefully before setup. This will not be an issue if mounting it on the wall. Also, I find the remote quite long which is unusual compared to other modern brands. The addition of a second remote for kids is absolutely brilliant, providing a safe and secure viewing mode for children of all ages.  Overall, this TV offers a perfect alternative viewing experience and I would highly recommend this brand to everyone.
