Overall, it's been a great purchase and offers excellent value for money. It looks modern, performs well, and has become a big part of our day-to-day family entertainment. I would happily recommend a Hisense TV to friends and family.
author: emma61289

body: I have been testing the Hisense 43Q7STUK and my first impressions have been extremely positive. From unboxing to everyday use, the whole experience has been simple, smooth and enjoyable. The setup was incredibly easy. After wall-mounting the TV, I connected it to my Wi-Fi and followed the clear on-screen instructions. Within minutes, everything was ready to use. The tv is super light, it does come with feet for table mounting. The design is sleek and modern, with slim bezels and a discreet Hisense logo that allows the screen to take centre stage. Mounted on the wall, it sits flush and looks stylish and premium in my kitchen. Picture quality is excellent. Colours are vibrant, images are sharp, and the overall viewing experience feels immersive. Whether watching films, TV shows or sports, the screen delivers impressive clarity and detail. A real highlight is how easy it is to access streaming services. I connected Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV, Spotify, Netflix and Disney+ with ease, and everything runs smoothly. The TV also includes Freely, giving access to live and on-demand TV channels without the need for an aerial. There's the VIDAA app that allows you to use you phone as a remote control, amongst other things, which is a cool feature. I particularly like that the TV comes with two remote controls. There is a standard remote for everyday use and a cute white-and-blue remote designed specifically for children. The kids’ remote works alongside the parental control features, helping to restrict content and giving children safe, easy access to age-appropriate entertainment. Navigation is quick and intuitive, and switching between apps is seamless. Overall, the Hisense 43Q7STUK combines excellent picture quality, a stylish design, easy setup and thoughtful family-friendly features. It has exceeded my expectations and is a fantastic smart TV for both adults and children.
author: MumTwo

body: We’ve been using the 55” Hisense TV for a little while now and overall we’re really impressed with it.  The setup process was incredibly easy, pretty much plug in and follow the on-screen instructions and you’re away.  Connecting everything was straightforward too.  We hooked it up to our existing TV box and even our old-school DVD player, and both worked perfectly first time with no issues at all. The remote control is simple and easy to use, and navigating around the menus and apps is really smooth.  One feature we particularly liked was how easy it is to add and log into apps using QR codes on your phone, such a quick and hassle free process.  There’s also a huge range of apps available, definitely enough choice for anyone. The sound quality is surprisingly good for a flat screen TV, clear and more than powerful enough for everyday viewing. The TV itself looks sleek and modern sitting on our living room cabinet, even though it’s only in a temporary position until our media wall is built.  It's also surprisingly lightweight considering its size. The only small downside for me personally is that I haven’t quite managed to get the picture as vivid as I’d ideally like. I’ve tried adjusting the various settings including Cinema, Dynamic, contrast and sharpness, and while the picture is still very good, it’s just slightly less punchy than my own personal preference.  That said, this is very much subjective and won’t bother everyone. Overall though, this is a great value TV, easy to set up, easy to use, packed with features and apps, and looks great too. Very happy with it so far.

author: hyperpainter

body: I have been using the Hisense 55Q7STUK in my living room and overall I have been really impressed. The size is brilliant for the space and the TV looks premium, with thin bezels, a sturdy feel and a clean design that fits nicely into the room. Setup was simple and the smart TV experience has been one of the biggest highlights for me. The menus feel easy to use, apps are simple to navigate and connecting devices, including my console and Alexa, was straightforward. Picture quality is very good in many situations, especially films, TV shows and YouTube. Colours are bright and vibrant, the screen gets more than bright enough during the day and I have noticed very little glare. Gaming also feels responsive, with no noticeable input lag in my experience. There are a few areas where it is not perfect. Live sport has sometimes looked a little inconsistent in quality, although I am not sure whether this is the TV, the stream or my network. The black levels are also not the deepest and can look a little grey in darker scenes. Sound is better than I expected from built-in speakers, especially with dialogue enhancement, but it still will not replace a proper soundbar. Overall, I would definitely recommend it as a strong mid-range TV, especially if you want a good balance of picture quality, smart features and value.
author: kaithomson

body: The Hisense comes well packaged and is easy to get to by removing the outer sleeve rather than having to lift the TV out of the box. Fitting the stand was easy with 4 screws and the feet have protective pads for the surface the TV will stand on. Turning on for the first time there is an easy option using the Vidaa app and your smart phone if you already have a Hisense TV. The TV connects to your wireless through the Phone and then everything is done. Setting up the apps is easy with QR scanning and within 5 minutes had the TV setup with all the usual streaming services all setup. The picture quality is excellent with clear vibrant colours and crisp edges and things like football and films are nice and clear even though this is a big 65 inch screen it doesn't loose the image quality like some TVs do.  The sound of this TV is amazing and gives surround effect which in the large room it was located gives a really realistic effect. The menu system is simple and intuitive and to be fair it doesn't need much interaction of changing of things as default settings are good enough for me. A number of features like wake up on LAN or wake up when it detects you are awake are interesting but not really something I would need on this large model as it is not for the bedroom but for an outdoor cabin. The TV has Freely built in which works fine and saves the need for an aerial connection giving all the terrestrial stations and accessible via the guide. The remote has all the usual buttons and easy to use and automatically sets up when the TV turns on. it has a number of useful shortcuts too the standard streaming apps and Freely it is quite large which may not appeal to some people but didn't bother me. I really like this TV both for picture, sound and features and it is probably the best purchase I have made for a TV.
author: geg87

body:
My experience of this TV has been a very positive one. Unboxing and setting up is a fairly simple experience. 
You have to screw the legs in which is a bit fidgety. I would have expected a click in to secure. This is the first TV I have setup by downloading an app on my phone. I found it great being from a technical background. Really simple, download the app, follow the basic instructions and you are good. The picture is crisp and impressive. The apps were easy to navigate and open Two controllers, one for kids is a nice touch
author: Falkirkfan1985

body:
My first impression of the Hisense TV was that it was surprisingly light to handle, with a sleek design and a good-quality finish and feel. I mounted it onto my wall bracket with no issues using the spacers provided, although I did have to purchase some M6 bolts.  The setup process was very simple and straightforward, with connection to the internet and linking the associated VIDAA app quick and easy.  Initially, I found the picture quality and colour settings weren’t quite right out of the box, but after switching around and trying Cinema mode, the picture looked much more natural and enjoyable. The built-in apps felt a bit like navigating a spider’s web at first, but they became easier to use with time, although the interface could still be simplified. Connecting the TV to my soundbar via optical was super easy. Syncing the sound to the picture took some doing but with the advanced settings I managed in the end. 
The sound quality wasn’t as crisp as I expected initially, but again the advanced settings are straightforward to adjust and I think there’s still room for further fine-tuning from me. But it’s very good! The sound from the TV speakers themselves is also very good.  For gaming, the picture quality is fantastic, with sharp visuals, movement and vibrant colours that really enhance the experience after setting to Sport settings. Again, the standard setting seemed a little flat. Overall, I’m very impressed with the quality and performance of the TV. I’m very happy with the purchase.
author: ChristineKH

body: The Hisense 85Q7STUK is a very good quality TV for the price, and yes — it will feel like a massive upgrade from a 5‑year‑old Samsung. The jump to 85 inches, QLED brightness, and modern motion handling makes it especially good for football. Much brighter screen make football pitches look vivid even in daylight. Better motion handling reduces blur during fast passes and camera movements. Quantum Dot colour is richer greens, blues, and skin tones. It delivers bright, punchy colours, sharp 4K detail, and smooth motion, which is exactly what I want for fast‑paced sports. Hisense’s newer panels are far brighter and more vibrant than older Samsung mid‑range models, so the difference are immediately noticeable. Love fact that aerial is not needed for the freview.
author: Kam1l

body: Really pleased with this TV. The picture quality is fantastic, colours are vibrant, and the sound is much better than I expected. Easy to set up and navigate. Great value for money and would definitely recommend.
author: KAYLA

body: Its a really good tv and picture quality is so good and clear would defo recommend the tv
Nice looking TV, with very easy set-up.
author: Mark

body:
When this TV arrived, it couldn't have come at a better time as my old TV had finally given up. I've been using it for a while now and overall I'm really happy with it. Set up was very straightforward and I could log in to most apps from my phone, using QR codes. The picture quality is excellent, with bright colours and a clear, sharp display. The sound is surprisingly good too – I don't have to turn the volume up very high to hear everything clearly.
Having apps such as YouTube, Netflix and BBC iPlayer built in is super useful, and I've enjoyed browsing some of the internet-powered TV channels as well. It's nice having everything in one place rather than needing extra devices.
The TV itself is also much lighter than my previous TV, which made setting it up easier than expected. I find the 43-inch size ideal for my conservatory - not too big but also not too small. My only criticism is that navigating between the different menus can sometimes feel like a bit of a faff. Moving between Freely, live TV and streaming apps isn't always as straightforward as I'd like, and the remote takes a little getting used to. I was also initially confused by the subtitles button, which seems to actually be the mute button.  The only other issue I ran into was trying to register the warranty. I couldn't find my model listed on the Hisense website, which was a bit frustrating and left me unsure whether I'd completed the process correctly. Those are fairly minor complaints though. Overall, it's a great TV with excellent picture quality, good sound and plenty of viewing options, and I'd happily recommend it.
author: Shxron26

body: The Hisense Q7STUK 55" is a masterclass in combining high-end entertainment features with everyday practical usability, with its sleek, capable display, this model hits all the right marks. ​Stylish Aesthetics & Picture Brilliance  ​Straight out of the box, the TV commands attention with its stylish looks. Its ultra-slim bezels and premium stand offer a high-end, minimalist aesthetic that complements any modern interior. Turn it on, and the fabulous picture quality immediately takes center stage. Powered by advanced QLED technology, the display outputs incredibly vibrant colours and rich contrast. Whether you are watching a dark, moody thriller or a bright nature documentary, the screen pops with lifelike depth and absolute clarity.  ​Seamless Connectivity & Smart Navigation  ​Where this model truly shines is its painless integration with your entire media stack. Setting up external devices is effortless: ​other connectable media ntegrates seamlessly, passing through crisp 4K imagery. ​Digital gaming devices The TV acts as a perfect companion, unlocking smooth gaming performance, ultra-low input lag, and automatic optimizations via its dedicated Game Bar.  ​Navigating the system is remarkably fluid. The built-in Freely platform lets you stream live UK television without needing an aerial, stitching everything together beautifully. The interface is incredibly intuitive, making menu navigation completely stress-free. Furthermore, getting to your favorite streaming services is instant; dedicated one-touch buttons on the remote provide lightning-fast, straightforward access to loaded media and entertainment apps. ​Audio Performance  ​While thin displays usually compromise on audio, the Q7STUK defies expectations. Backed by Dolby Atmos processing, it delivers surprisingly great sound with clear dialogue and balanced bass, eliminating the immediate need for an external soundbar. It is a fantastic, well-rounded 55-inch package."
author: Sparkyebb

body:

body: Love my new TV, its a big upgrade from my old brand of TV. The built in apps are great as no need now for a separate device.The kiddy remote is very user friendly even my 4 year old quickly got to grips with it. The user interface is easy to use and navigate and the setup was easyv o follow using my phone.
author: ttmatt

body:
The Hisense 75-inch 75Q7STUK delivers a huge-screen cinema experience without the eye-watering price tag. Brilliant picture quality, smooth motion, intuitive smart features, and surprisingly good sound make it a joy to use. The only downside? Friends suddenly finding excuses to come round for movie night."
For gaming, it's equally impressive. The large 75-inch display creates a truly immersive experience, while responsive performance and smooth motion handling keep fast-paced action looking sharp and fluid. Whether you're exploring open worlds, racing at high speed, or competing online, the 75Q7STUK makes every gaming session feel bigger, brighter, and far more exciting.
The sound is impressive straight out of the box, dialogue is clear, and sports fans will appreciate how smoothly fast-paced action is handled. Streaming apps load quickly, navigation is straightforward, and the smart features feel genuinely useful rather than just being there for the marketing brochure.
My only real complaint is that it has ruined other TVs for me. Watching a smaller screen now feels a bit like going from first class back to economy. If you're looking for a television that delivers premium performance without a premium-brand price tag, the Hisense 75Q7STUK is an outstanding choice.

body: I've been using the Hisense 65Q7STUK for two weeks now and I'm really impressed. It looks fantastic in my living room, with its slim profile and minimal bezel giving it a clean, modern look. Setting it up was straightforward. The stand feet need to be screwed in with a screwdriver, which only took a few minutes (but is a 2 person job - one to hold the TV while the other screws in). Batteries are included for the lightweight remote control. I downloaded the VIDAA app on my phone to handle the initial setup, and I'd strongly recommend doing this... It's so much easier typing passwords and search terms on your phone keyboard rather than fiddling with the onscreen keyboard. There's a wide range of apps preloaded (main reason I upgraded from my old TV was the lack of support for apps after 9 years!) The display really delivers on picture quality. I've been watching 4K and HDR content through various streaming services and the colours are vibrant and true to life. It performs fairly well in the day in a well lit room, there is a bit of reflection on the screen. Sound quality has genuinely surprised me. For built-in speakers, the output is rich and immersive. I won't need a soundbar. The Freely app is a great feature, delivering live TV channels over your internet connection without needing an aerial or satellite dish. I've connected mine via an ethernet cable for a stable connection. There are three HDMI ports... I've got a PC and a games console hooked up and still have one spare port. Overall, the Hisense 65Q7STUK is a brilliant TV that ticks all the boxes for picture quality, sound and smart features.

body:
I've been pleasantly surprised by the Hisense 55Q7STUK. The TV itself is impressively thin and lightweight, making it easy to mount and set up. The operating system is responsive and easy to navigate, with apps opening quickly and menus feeling snappy. There are quite a few apps pre-installed out of the box, but most can be removed if you prefer a cleaner home screen. Picture quality is very good for a mid-range TV, although it definitely benefits from spending a little time adjusting the picture settings. Once optimised, colours look natural and vibrant without appearing over-saturated or washed out. Contrast is solid and the overall viewing experience is excellent for films, sport and everyday TV. Sound from the built-in speakers is perfectly acceptable for casual viewing, but pairing it with a dedicated surround sound system makes a noticeable difference. I've connected mine to a Denon AVR and it works seamlessly. I haven't explored the AI features enough to give a fair assessment yet, but based on everything else, this feels like a well-rounded TV that offers strong performance for the price. 
Overall, I'd recommend it to anyone looking for a capable mid-range 55-inch TV without breaking the bank.

body: Just delighted with my New HiSense 75" TV.  UPgrading from an older OLED 65" set (6 years old), I wasn't sure what to expect from HiSense.  First thing we noticed was the weight difference - so much lighter than the old TV which made the seamless install nice and easy (but still a 2-person job). The difference in size was delightful - seems to be a slightly different ratio to the old set, but nice and slimline, so sits beautifully flush to the wall.  Set-up was sooo seamless and really quick.  Particularly impressed with Freely as a way to access terrestrial TV - makes everything HD without having to select the specific HD channels.  Not something I was expecting to be delighted by, but it is a very cool app.  When it was tuned in and ready to go, I was blown away by the picture quality.  Really sharp images and dealt really well with movement - whether in movies or sports.  Particularly looking forward to the World Cup matches now.  The scale of the picture obviously helps, but the sharpness and true blacks it was producing were what I would have expected on a TV twice as expensive as this!.  I paired the TV with a soundbar set-up from a different Brand ad half-expected issues with the compatibility, but I needen't have worried.  It took a bit of time to dig into the instruction manual to figure it out (could definitely have been clearer!), but once you get the relevant HDMI connector for the Arc set-up (it's #3 BTW) the sound came through beautifully.  What I would say is that the actual TV sound was really very good on its own - much better than my previous.  If not for the additional bellow of the sub-woofer, I wouldn't have noticed it wasn't connected to the sound bar!.  The part my kids love is when you switch the TV off and the closing motion is like the curtains closing in from the side at a theatre.  Very fun and distinctive!  Overall a very impressive TV.  I know I didn't go for the Pro version, but honestly I'm not sure how much better it could be than this. An absolute 5-star powerhouse to put on your wall and enjoy for years to come.

body: It's a very good value TV for the price, it also has composite inputs which I required, and all the usual apps and sockets including a satellite socket! But buyers need to understand two things about Freely: firstly there is no longer an option in the inputs menu for terrestrial TV only. Terrestrial channels (and maybe satellite too - I haven't tried) are all incorporated into the hybrid TV guide if not available from the internet, with no obvious indication whether they come from the aerial or the internet. This does of course mean that the channels that do come from the internet will be great HD quality and in many cases pausable and rewindable. Secondly you will have to sign in to the five main free TV channels because those ones will certainly come from the internet without the option. That's quite a process and means setup takes time. You could force it to be a terrestrial TV by starving it of an internet connection from the word go, but the moment you connect, Freely takes over.

I recently purchased the Hisense 50U7STUK, initially intending to use it as a bedroom TV. After spending some time with it, I can confidently say it’s a genuinely good product that delivers incredible value for the money, though it definitely brings a "large room TV" energy to a smaller space.
Here is my breakdown of what makes this TV stand out, along with a couple of tips if you plan on setting it up yourself.
### The Screen & Picture Quality
The screen on this TV is absolutely fantastic. Because it uses Mini-LED technology, the contrast is superb. * **Rich Colours:** The Quantum Dot (QLED) tech really shows here. The colors are incredibly vibrant and punchy, making everything from movies to games look incredibly rich and lifelike. * **Very Bright:** This panel gets *seriously* bright. It handles HDR content beautifully and easily fights off daytime glare. However, because it gets so bright, it can almost feel a bit overwhelming in a pitch-black bedroom at night! You might find yourself turning the backlight down before going to sleep.
### Interface & Features
Hisense packs a lot into this model. It comes loaded with features, including support for Dolby Vision, Dolby Atmos, and high refresh rates (144Hz) if you are into gaming.
Despite the mountain of features, the smart interface (VIDAA) is surprisingly snappy and reasonably easy to navigate. It doesn't lag or stutter, and finding my favorite streaming apps was straightforward and intuitive.
### A Note on Wall Mounting (Read Before You Install!)
If you are planning to put this on the wall, **make sure you get the correct screws.** The TV requires specific VESA mounting screws (often M6), and the standard ones that come bundled in generic wall-mount kits might not be the exact length you need. Do yourself a favor and check the TV's manual for the exact screw depth required before you start drilling, or you'll be making an unexpected trip to the hardware store mid-installation.
### The Verdict
I bought this for the bedroom, but honestly, it performs like a premium main-room TV. Between the incredibly bright Mini-LED panel, the rich colors, and the sheer amount of features, it punches well above its weight. Just be prepared for a cinematic, large-room experience right at the foot of your bed—and double-check your wall bracket hardware before you start! Highly recommended."

body: Before you buy this TV, double-check your wall mount! It requires a specific 400 x 300 bracket. I wrongly assumed my old equal-hole bracket would work and had to learn the hard way. The VIDAA app prompts you through the Wi-Fi connection process in just a few simple steps, and you are up and running in no time. The software is where this TV really shines. The operating system feels exceptionally snappy and responsive. The TV features two full-bandwidth HDMI 2.1 inputs that fully support a 4K resolution at a smooth 144Hz refresh rate.  You will want to spend a few minutes adjusting the picture settings out of the box. Initially, the factory colours looked a bit oversaturated, and I noticed some slight backlight clouding during darker scenes. Luckily, switching the TV straight into Filmmaker Mode instantly balanced the contrast and helped with the issue. The biggest surprise by far is the audio quality. The built-in 2.1-channel speaker system delivers deep bass and clear dialogue. It packs enough of a punch that you might not even need to buy a separate soundbar.  I don't think I will need one. I’ve been genuinely impressed with the Hisense 55Q7STUK. For a mid‑range TV, it delivers far more than I expected, especially when it comes to sound. The built‑in speakers are surprisingly powerful and full-bodied, offering clear dialogue and a punchy, room‑filling sound that doesn’t leave you immediately feeling the need for a soundbar. For everyday viewing, films, and sport, the audio performance stands out as one of the TV’s biggest strengths.
Picture quality is equally strong. Straight out of the box it looks good, but with a little fine‑tuning initially the tv is really bright in light controlled room so I turned that down slightly the colours become natural and vibrant without drifting into oversaturation. Contrast is solid, motion is smooth, and Dolby Vision support gives films a noticeable boost. Whether you’re watching live sport or streaming your favourite series, the overall viewing experience feels consistently high‑quality.
Ease of use is another highlight. The TV is thin, lightweight, and simple to set up, with clear instructions and a responsive operating system that makes navigating apps and menus easy. Everything loads quickly, and although there are plenty of pre‑installed apps, you can remove what you don’t need to keep things tidy. The Freely app meansyou can stream live TV without needing an aerial as long as you’re connected to Wi‑Fi.
After spending some time with it, this feels like a well‑rounded, easy‑to‑use TV that offers excellent performance for the price — especially if you want great sound without adding a soundbar. 
There were a couple of small negatives I need to point out, First when installing the TV the casing on the back must be slightly twisted as when I installed the wall brackets the tv sat out further at one end more than the other, I added a couple of washers and this sorted the issue. body: This years’ Hisense 85 inch (85U7S) has absolutely blown me off. I am a huge fan of the slim bezels that enrapture the beautiful 4k 144hz panel. What’s impressive about this particular model is that it has filmmaker mode which allows me to watch movies as the director intended for them to be seen, which is a big plus for all movie enthusiasts. Not only that, but its also very high refresh rate which means its perfect for gaming and goes very well with my PS5. I was also really impressed with the build in speakers. They have deep base and high treble and the overall sound profile is very punchy and enjoyable. Being Mini-LED, it also offers really good contrast ratio which makes the whole process of TV watching much more enjoyable. Another advantage of having Mini LED is that is does not have pixel burn in like OLED panels, but the local dimming array offer superb performance in HDR. The IMAX Enhancement also helps to lift the entire experience and this is one of the few products where this certification makes total sense. The built in remote is also quite comfortable and its bluetooth, so I do not need to point it at the TV to control it. Besides that, the remote has a built in microphone as well so I can use voice commands instead of typing manually which is  an absolute lifesaver. The TV also has Google TV built in which is quite versatile and user friendly, making it a breeze to start using right away. The TVs overall brightness is also commendable offering 1600 nits of peak brightness with HDR 10 and dolby vision which allows the user to enjoy supported content at unimaginable colours. Built-in ethernet is also an absolute lifesaver as I can just plug in the TV using a wired connection over wireless which makes the internet connection alot more stable and faster. The processor is also quite rapid and the interface does not lag at all even with multitasking using plex or jellyfin. Overall, I would highly recommend this TV to my friends and family. Its absolutely worth it for the price."

Gamers will love it too — it reacts instantly and won’t get screen burn marks over time. The menu is simple to use, and it connects easily to all your favourite apps like Netflix and YouTube. body: Brilliant TV

Unboxing the 65-inch Hisense U7STUK was a great experience. Straight out of the box, the build quality feels robust, and the nearly borderless, slim bezel gives it an elegant presence in my living room without looking overly bulky. The Mini-LED backlight colour provides fantastic picture quality. Watching movies in Dolby Vision and HDR10+ reveals stunning contrast, with bright highlights through deep, satisfying blacks. Fast-moving sports and action sequences stay crisp without nasty motion blur, this will be great to watch FiFa World Cup 2026. Navigating the VIDAA smart platform is swift and straightforward. Apps load almost instantly, and switching inputs is snappy. The integrated voice control responds well to natural commands, making hands-free searches simple. The remote control feels functional, though its layout takes a brief period to get used to. Acoustically, the built-in sound system supports Dolby Atmos and delivers clear dialogue along with a noticeable punch of bass, which is rare for standard built-in TV speakers. While the audio is great for daily viewing, adding an external soundbar could enhance the deepest cinema low-ends even further.  Ultimately, this display has massively upgraded my home entertainment setup, merging bright performance with serious gaming power.

body: After getting the Hisense 55U7STUK unboxed and mounted on the wall right above my desk, I am incredibly impressed with how it performs as a primary display. At fifty-five inches, the 4K picture quality is incredibly sharp. Because I sit relatively close to the screen at my workstation, the high pixel density makes a massive difference, allowing me to read small text, fine details, and complex instrument dials without any blurring. ​The Mini-LED backlighting is definitely the standout feature for me. The contrast is brilliant, delivering deep, true blacks that make dark or nighttime scenes feel completely immersive. There is no annoying backlight bleed, and the screen gets bright enough to easily handle room reflections during the day. ​What really seals the deal for gaming and fast-paced simulation is the native 144Hz refresh rate. Fast movement is fluid and completely stable, completely eliminating the motion blur I used to get on slower screens. The AI upscaling also does a fantastic job keeping older content looking crisp. On top of the visuals, the built-in subwoofer and audio system offer surprisingly rich, balanced sound right out of the box. It has truly transformed my desktop environment.
author: JayG33

body: I had the opportunity to test the 55U7STUK TV. This is a big step up in picture quality, the TV features the latest MiniLED backlighting technology. This greatly improves lighting control, enhances the contrast, giving the most natural picture possible. It has a powerful processor for detailed blur-free images and you get the optimal contrast levels whatever the time of day and from whichever signal input. The new AI Smooth Motion and AI Sports mode technology makes this TV great for sports and movies as the processing smooths the picture flow. Filmmaker Mode lets you experience the cinematic vision, by using the correct aspect ratio, colour and frame rate.  Game Mode reduces input lag, ensuring quicker reaction times. It's fitted with a built-in subwoofer,  for a deeper bass response and smoother immersive sound. It has the latest Freely TV system with the options of live TV channels and catch-up content. Freely also allows you to ‘pause’ live TV as well as restarting programmes on certain channels. This new service enables the use of just an Internet connection so there is no need for an aerial or satellite dish There’s also one-touch, direct access to the most popular apps - Netflix, Disney+, Amazon Prime etc. It seems the possibilities are endless on this TV and personally I have only just started exploring them all.  What I can say to sum it up is that it is a great way to get a truly cinematic experience in your own living room and it's a gamers dream.

With particularly bassy shows I sometimes stopped it as I thought that the sound was coming from somewhere else! I particularly love the screen mirroring as it allowed me to show pictures and videos from my camera roll on the big screen without there being a drop in quality over the air. The 50 inch screen also fit perfectly where we wanted it and it has a almost existent bezzle and central stand. This meant we didn't have to change our set up at all. Overall it has been 10/10 - haven't watched so much TV in my life! Would definitely recommend to a friend (and already have!)

body: The Hisense 85U7STUK television made a strong first impression. The design is impressive with a large screen housed in a slim profile. Once installed, the picture is exceptionally crisp and clear with vibrant colours. The Dolby Vision technology produces deep blacks that enhance the colour saturation. The sound quality is also superior to any television I have owned previously. Developed in conjunction with Devialet, it provides a better sound experience for users without an additional soundbar. While the hardware is impressive, the installed software has been somewhat disappointing. The Freely interface is novel and differs from my previous digital television experience. The combination of channels supplied via the aerial and over Wi-Fi is a promising development for the future of television broadcast. The television is capable of processing Dolby Atmos and Dolby Vision but most available apps and installed software only offer basic variations that do not utilise these features. It is surprising that the latest sound and vision technology is provided in the hardware but not accessible through the software.

"Good Picture but. TV arrived well packaged. It was super easy to unbox and fit to my existing wall mount. When you first turn it on it is so easy to follow the instructions to set it up and connect to Wi-Fi etc. It also has a QR code to download the app to your phone which also works good. Once it is all set up I make my first discovery. This is NOT an Android/Google TV. It has its own operating system and a bit of a poor app store. No way of adding play store. Anyway I carry on playing around with various functions and settings to get a feel of what I can do. The picture is really good but I did adjust the brightness and contrast slightly. Now to the sound. I had read about the built in base speaker and quality sound before buying it so I was looking forward to a great sound. Despite spending ages adjusting all the sound settings, still another big disappointment. The sound is way better than a standard TV but nothing like I was hoping for. Maybe after reading all the hype about it I was expecting a bit too much. Luckily I have a sound bar so I will be sticking with that. I love the feature when you turn the TV off and it is like curtains closing like at the cinema years ago. You can also adjust the speed of this which is nice, only problem is my grandson wants to keep turning the TV on and off. It has 4 HDMI sockets so should be good for most people. The remote is nice and easy to use and will also operate the firestick and its functions which is handy. The operating system does sometimes suffer from some slight lag but it is not a frequent or major problem. The WIFI connection speed is good so hopefully no problems there going forward. So to sum up. Set up super easy. Picture brilliant. Sound ok ish. Operating system not for me. If it had a proper OS yes I would recommend it because the sound is easily rectified with a sound bar which is the norm nowadays.
"

body:
The HISENSE 55U7NQTUK 55 Smart 4K Ultra HD HDR Mini LED TV offers everything I wanted at a lower price than LG, Samsung, and Sony. It supports 120 Hz refresh rates and HDR10+, ideal for PS5 gaming, with an easy-to-access gaming menu that activates AMD FreeSync and displays settings for various genres of video game i.e. FPS, RTS, RPG, Sport. 

While it has a specific mode for Black Myth: Wukong, I can’t assess its quality since I don’t own the game. The FPS monitor doesn't sync accurately with visual frame rates, but this could be how I am using it with the PS5, it may work better with a PC setup. The HDR10, HDR10+, and Dolby Vision provide great picture quality, but I had to adjust the settings to my liking. Apple TV and Prime Video support Dolby Vision, enhancing the viewing experience, especially with the smooth frame setting for better motion in animations.

The Freely App enables live TV, which I use for sports on BBC and ITV due to its better output quality, nevertheless, standard apps like iPlayer and ITVX are available to download. The remote is user-friendly, with quick access to Netflix, Disney+, YouTube and Prime, plus the convenience of solar charging and USB-C compatibility. It also controls the PS5 menu and Fire TV, although it recently stopped working with the Fire Stick, likely due to the Fire settings, not the TV.

Overall, I’m very pleased with this purchase, as it enhances my gaming and 4K HDR viewing experience while offering plenty of customizable settings. The 4 HDMI ports are also welcomed, although only 2 of them support the higher frame rates for gaming, which should be sufficient.

body:
Review of the Hisense 55U7NQTUK TV

Thanks to Feefo and Hisense for giving me the opportunity to review the Hisense 55U7NQTUK TV. It’s an excellent TV with a lot to offer. Here’s my take:

- Setup and Usability:
Setting up the Hisense 55U7NQTUK was super easy. As soon as I switched it on, I was taken straight to the home screen, which was a nice touch. Even assembling the stand was a breeze, and I'm not particularly DIY savvy.

- Performance:
The TV is incredibly fast and responsive. The remote works seamlessly, and there are no annoying loading screens. It's like using a high-end computer. Navigating through apps is simple too, with everything accessible right from the remote.

- Screen Mirroring and Connectivity:
I did encounter a couple of issues with screen mirroring. I couldn’t mirror my phone when using a VPN, and sometimes, when watching movies, the playback would get choppy for 5-6 seconds. However, this choppy mirroring issue is common with many TVs to varying degrees.

- Gaming Modes: 
The TV offers different modes for gaming, enhancing the overall gaming experience. 

- Sound Quality: 
The sound quality is really good, providing clear and immersive audio. - 

- Ease of Use:
Because of its simplicity and ease of use, my elderly parents could navigate through YouTube and other apps easily. The added bonus of voice control, which they got used to from using YouTube on an iPhone, makes it even more user-friendly. As I'm tech savvy I'm usually the one navigating and fixing tech issues like the WiFi etc for my parents, so if this sounds like you too the simplicity is a massive win!

- Temperature and Overall Recommendation:
Even after many hours of use, the TV's temperature remained normal, which is impressive and speaks to its quality. Despite the minor hiccups with mirroring, I’m really impressed with the Hisense 55U7NQTUK. The size, speed, ease of setup, and overall simplicity make it a fantastic choice, If you’re in the market for a new TV, this one is definitely worth considering.

Thanks again to Feefo and Hisense for the opportunity to review this excellent TV. Please don't hesitate to reach out again!

body:
This product is a definite must-buy. You'd end up paying twice the price for another brand offering the same level of quality.
Local dimming works wonders across all TV program genres, especially noticeable during scene transitions to black and the contrast on credits and titles. The TV can reach impressive brightness levels, which is a boon in well-lit rooms. However, in complete darkness, the effect is akin to being in a theater. Occasionally, there's a slight lag in brightness adjustment after a scene change, but this is rare.
Gaming performance is top-notch. I've had no issues playing at 120Hz with audio output through the TV. While my Nvidia graphics card doesn't support over 120Hz via HDMI, gaming at 144Hz would require a display port to HDMI adapter. I've experienced occasional frame drops and screen blackouts, but I'm unsure if this is due to the TV or my HDMI cable. Overall, gaming experience is excellent, with no noticeable latency.
Connecting other devices like sound systems and streaming boxes was hassle-free. Everything worked seamlessly upon setup.
Regarding HDR, there's a bit of uncertainty. SDR content often looks better than HDR, with Dolby Vision on Netflix appearing washed out. However, BBC iPlayer shows in HDR HLG are stunning, making it feel like the animals are in the room. Personal HLG content via Plex also looks good, suggesting the TV may struggle with certain HDR formats.
Surprisingly, the TV does an impressive job of sharpening highly-compressed content, such as streamed shows. For instance, even though "Trigger Point" is only 1080p on ITVx, the quality is noticeably better via the app compared to the sky box.
Additionally:
* The TV has a sleek design and doesn't heat up much, potentially making it more energy-efficient than older LCD models.
* The remote has a nice tactile feel and is easy to use even in the dark.
* The four HDMI ports come in handy, although only two support 144Hz

body:

Improvement Points: The stand is beautiful but wobbles slightly even with screws fastened as tight as possible!

Thicker than other modern day competitors, however I understand this is due to the powerhouse nature of this television, more of an observation than a point of improvement to be fair.

The 1 Button on/off "smart settings" e.g Ultra Smooth, don't really seem to make any noticale differences, however this is true with most TVs.

Have seen sharper images with some of the top competitors but isn't a huge complaint, still quite clean lines.

Ghosting and slight tearing visible when fast images are against a high contrast background, but only really noticale if you're looking for it, again not a huge complaint.
author: Ollie

body:
Good Points: This is a bright TV, perfect for brightly lit or rooms with lots of day light. Beautiful 4k image and punchy colours with the right settings. I'm an advocate for sound bars trust me you don't need one, for a flat screen TV the sound is great. Has a snappy processor, no delay with commands. Cast YouTube from my phone instantly unlike my very sluggish Sony Bravia. Virtually bezel less design, stand has cable management built in and room for a sound bar if you want.

Improvement Points: The Vidaa operating software is good but Google TV is better and is used on Hisense TVs in the US why not Europe? Some of the presets are not great with washed out images or overly saturated ones, Filmmaker and Dynamic respectively. The sport mode is a great all-round setting for most viewings, punchy colours and good contrast. Watched Alien and the back light struggled a little with the space, star field scenes, though lots of Led TVs do. Hopefully some of these issues can be helped with firmware updates. For the technology involved it's a bargain. The equivalent Sony from last year was twice the price. Highly recommended.
author: Steven

body:
Good Points: Image Quality: HDR is punchy and has good clear colours, the refresh rate of 120hz is excellent when using Game Mode for the PS5 or XBox Series X. The different visual options enable user to apply perfect settings to all ports or customise each and every connection. Motion blur is limited when watching Sports or whilst gaming giving you a quality picture with fast moving objects. Available ports HDMI 2.1 x 2 (eARC x 1) - HDMI 2.0 x 2, is able to run Dolby Vision IQ/HDR10+/HDR10 and Hybrid Log Gamma (HLG)

Audio: The rear speakers have excellent sound distribution and are possibly the best I have heard from a slimline TV. The speakers have 20W of power with Dolby Atmos.

Connectivity: App controls from Smart Device are excellent - allowing the user to use physical body gestures or smart commands to control the TV without the need of a remote control (although I still believe the remote is the easiest choice of operation) - Voice commands are also available via the Vidaa application (this can be done in any language which is a great accessibility feature more TV's should have!) Tv has built in WiFi as well as Bluetooth 5.0.

Improvement Points: Stand: As the stand is curved it would limit any possibility of adding a sound bar. The sound from the TV is excellent but for those who would want a sound bar directly under would have to seek a different method.

App Store: This could be good or bad but I feel like the app store could do with some more additions. The TV has the basics covered, BBC iPlayer, ITVX, Channel 4, Netflix, Prime, Disney+, YouTube, and more streaming services.

Remote Control: This is a personal preference but feel like the remote doesn't match the TV appearance, would prefer colour matching.

body:
Good Points: This TV offers an immersive viewing experience that surpassed my expectations. Its stunning picture quality, innovative features, and sleek design set a new standard for home entertainment. 

Incredible Picture Quality:
The ULED technology employed by Hisense takes the visual experience to the next level. With the 4K Ultra HD resolution, every scene comes to life with exceptional clarity, sharpness, and vibrant colours. The combination of Quantum Dot Colour and Dolby Vision HDR further enhances the picture quality, delivering deeper blacks and brighter whites.
Cutting-Edge Features:
The TV is packed with an array of advanced features that enhance both convenience and entertainment. The built-in voice control capabilities (powered by AI I think), allow you to navigate through the TV's functions effortlessly. Whether it's adjusting settings, searching for content, or accessing popular streaming platforms, a simple voice command is all it takes. The TV also supports popular voice assistants like Amazon Alexa or Google Assistant, providing seamless integration with your smart home ecosystem.
Smart TV Functionality:
It's a fully-fledged smart TV, offering a comprehensive range of applications and streaming services. With its integrated Wi-Fi connectivity, it easily connected to our home network and we quickly enjoyed our favourite content from the likes of Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, YouTube, and more. The intuitive user interface makes navigation a breeze, ensuring quick access to a vast library of movies, TV shows, and online content.
Immersive Audio Experience:
Complementing the stunning visuals, the audio performance of the 55U7KQTUK is equally impressive. With the inclusion of Dolby Atmos technology, the TVs built in speakers deliver a three-dimensional sound experience that immerses you in rich, detailed audio. We enjoyed watching action-packed movies and playing video games, the soundstage is wide and enveloping, providing an enhanced sense of realism.
Sleek Design and Connectivity Options:
The Hisense 55U7KQTUK TV has a sleek and modern design that effortlessly blends into our (and any) living space. The near-borderless display and slim bezels maximize the screen real estate, offering an immersive viewing experience. Additionally, the TV provides a wide range of connectivity options, including multiple HDMI ports, USB ports, and Bluetooth, ensuring easy integration with various devices such as gaming consoles, soundbars, or streaming devices.

Conclusion:
Thi Hisense 55U7KQTUK 55" ULED TV shines in the highly competitive TV market. Its stunning picture quality, cutting-edge features, smart functionality, immersive audio, and sleek design make it a top choice for anyone after low-cost high-quality device.

Improvement Points: While the Hisense 55U7KQTUK 55" ULED TV has many positive attributes, it does have a few drawbacks. Some small things I found were:
Unable to play sound through the soundbar and tv speakers at the same time, my old TV was able to do this so I was used to this. 
This point is only a small one, when watching Freeview, the channel information appears at the top of the screen and gets in the way of the picture, I would like to be able to move it to the bottom of the screen, but I have not been able to find a menu option to do this. The TV also has a limited viewing angle, which isn't a problem for my living room but other environments may pick up on this. 
However, when weighed against its numerous positive features, these limitations do not overshadow the overall appeal and value of the TV, particularly for those seeking an immersive and feature-rich home entertainment experience.

body:
Good Points: I compared this to a similar Samsung QLED T.V,  the results are interesting. So, first off physically the T.V is nice and light, easy to setup and the remote keys have a nice grippy feel to them (unlike the SS). The menu UI is VERY easy to navigate (easier than SS) as it is pretty basic but you get what you are looking for very quickly.
The image quality is ULED tech which is supposed to be somewhere between QLED and OLED, the picture is very similar to my SS TV but is very clear and vibrant.
There's lots of HDR presets, I changed mine from default to HDR night as it displayed best for PS5 games.
As for the 144hz I only used upto 120hz as I have no games that output that fast, but still it's very nice to have now that some PS5 games are outputting 120hz in their settings. No sign of image tear but be sure to use a high quality/speed HDMI cable!!

The system has a built in Sub Woofer and outputs audio brilliantly, the audio can get very loud as I barely go over 30.

It also has advanced features and HDMI linking so you can control your ps5 main menu through the TV remote if needed.

I had no problems with the TV, but I would not spend quad figures on it. If you can get it for less then you won't be disappointed.

Overall, a very nice modern T.V, excellent picture quality and easy to use. Would recommend.

Improvement Points: It generates quite a bit of heat around the back of the TV, and it uses a little more energy consumption than the Samsung but that could be because it has a built in subwoofer.

body: My review is of the 50” 50E6STUK model.   My initial impression of the tv was very good.  It’s about 5 years since I last bought a tv and for the size, I found this model very lightweight when I lifted it so I figured set up would be straightforward myself - and it was, up to a point.  The stands screwed on ok, though still felt a slightly wobbly when I tightened them, and then I discovered they were too wide for the unit the previous 32” had come off of.  I suspect this is common to other manufacturers, not just Hisense but the measurement of the stands from the edge of the tv would be a useful inclusion in the instruction book.  I got round the problem by buying another stand which fits in the middle and this worked fine.  The power cable comes separate from the tv and during set up, was prone to coming out on a couple of occasions but has been stable since.  I’ve plugged an aerial into the tv and so have the choice of freeview or streaming.  Set up on the tv itself was very straightforward and in terms of using the remote and navigating through the apps, I’ve found this fairly intuitive and easy.  I’m not a gamer so can’t comment on that aspect but in terms of watching live tv or apps such as i-player, the picture quality and sound is excellent.  All in all, this would have been a 5 star, had the design features not slightly let it down but it’s still excellent value for money.

I recently got the Hisense 55E6STUK and have been using it for a week now. Picture – picture quality is excellent, I’ve watched using the built in apps, Netflix & Prime, and have my Sky box connected,  and I’m very impressed, this was an upgrade from my last TV that was over 15 years old, so I was expecting something a lot better,  and I’m finding the picture on this to be excellent. I like that you can easily change picture modes, so when watching a move I change to Filmmaker mode, it does make a difference. Sound – for a TV that is so slim, the sound is excellent, with good bass as well, for this level of sound I would have expected large speakers, but Hisense have been able to keep the TV really slim and also have very good sound. Apps – the home screen has all the apps that you need, and are easily to find and use.  
One other thing I liked is that the TV came with 2 remotes, the standard one and then also a much simpler one designed for children, which limits what they can do, I think this is an great idea as it means your kids can’t change the settings.  Overall a great TV that I would recommemnd."

body:
The first thing I noticed about my new Hisense TV is that it felt sturdy and well made when I removed it from the box. It also has a sleek and slim modern design and feel to it. At 50 inches It is a really good size but slim and light enough to be easily mounted on a wall if you wanted to. If you don't want to put it on a wall I find that the stands it comes with make it very stable to stand on a unit or table etc.
Setting up the TV is very easy you just plug it in and follow the instructions on the screen. No aerial is needed only WIFI internet but you can use it with an arial though I have not tried it that way.
I found that cinema mode is best for me, this gives you a great picture with lots of depth and sharp detail but you can try the other modes and sound settings to find out what is best for you and what you like to watch. As the screen is nice and big and clear it is superb for subtitles on foreign language movies or the captions on sports like formula 1.
I have not used Freely before and was initially a little disappointed that a couple of my favourite channels from Freeview are not yet available on Freely but other that that it is really good and easy to use with lots of channels to choose from. I also think that Freely will continue to be updated with more channels.
The remote control is light and slim and also simple to navigate. The internal speakers are very adequate and provide a punchy sound but we invested in a Hisense sound bar to make the sound deeper and fuller for movies as we watch them a lot. There is no need to have the sound bar on all the time though.
I am very impressed with this TV especially for watching films, drama, foreign language TV and movies, manga and action movies which are all especially good. It is also great for any kind of sport or things like nature documentaries. I would recommend it mainly for its ease of use and the great picture and sound quality.

body:
After giving my TV a good few days of use I want to share what has impressed me and also the bad bits too!
The tv is pleasantly light in weight which is really useful for someone who has health conditions and struggles with heavy things. It came supplied with the feet for ease of use. The picture is extremely clear and has a great game mode for the gamers, colours are vibrant which enhances the overall experience, it is very quick to respond and has a nice easy simple set up altho I can’t say this would be the case for someone elderly that does not understand qr codes or have the tech required to complete set up by themselves.

The tv has an ample amount of outputs e.g HDMI etc if needed altho I wonder if more could be added. The bad bits are something that could be improved. I found the speakers were not really on par with the picture quality, the sound is good but it could be better.
There wasn’t a wall bracket which limits how you display your tv, I feel this should be included on the more bigger models rather than an extra optional.
The build of the tv could be improved, I found gaps at the bottom (included in pics)  where the plastics are not as flush as they could be which is disappointing.
Batteries were provided for the remote but sadly not for the kids remote which I would have expected to be standard.
The length of the power cable could definitely do with being longer so there are no restrictions for placement of tv. Overall I am very happy, love the clear bright picture display and cannot wait to have a good film night with friends!"

body:
This is a massive 65-inch television usually means expecting a bargain-basement picture. I bought the Hisense 65E6STUK bracing for major compromises, but after setting it up, my only real regret is that I didn't buy a second one. 
The 4K display panel is easily the biggest selling point. The bad bit in the hardware, it is definitely the built-in sound system. The TV is equipped with a basic 2.0 channel speaker array putting out 20W of total power. While the software tries its best with onboard DTS Virtual:X processing to widen the soundstage, it does not achieve. The down-firing drivers lack low-end punch. Bass is virtually non-existent, and high volumes can get slightly muddy. It is perfectly fine for the news, but it simply does not match the grand scale of the 65-inch picture. This was no issue for me as I use a separates with digital AV amp which is an easy fix for such a great price. Overall The user interface is powered by VIDAA, which is fast, lightweight, and completely free from the sluggish navigation lag that plagues other budget smart platforms. All my streaming apps load up instantly. Buy this twice if you get a chance

body: Does what it says on the tin!

Great budget tv. I found it relatively easy to navigate (after not having a tv for quite a few years), does everything I want from a tv. The colour is great but for me I am struggling a bit with the sound (maybe where I have it positioned and my hearing is starting to go a little), so I will be getting a sound bar to enhance my experience. However there are loads of settings for both picture and sound and these help as I have reflections from the conservatory roof too so can mitigate this to a certain degree in the different picture setting and for the sound there is a speech setting that I find is better for me too. The main reason I bought this tv was that it still provides an RCA connection (the red, white & yellow cables) so I am able to connect my old WII directly to the tv. I have also connected my computer to it and the screen quality is fabulous. This means I can watch my own DVD films directly on the big Tv screen directly connected via a HDMI cable. 
Overall, for a budget tv I am more than satisfied and would recommend.

body: After living with the Hisense 43Q7STUK for a few weeks, I can honestly say it has exceeded my expectations. I wasn’t looking for anything overly complicated, just a TV with a great picture and easy-to-use features, and it delivers on both. The first thing that stood out was how straightforward everything was. From taking it out of the box to getting it connected and ready to watch, the whole process was refreshingly simple. Within a short time I was signed into my streaming services and browsing through content without needing to dig through manuals or menus. The picture quality is easily the star of the show. Films, sports and everyday TV all look sharp and vibrant, with colours that really stand out without looking unnatural. Even during bright afternoons, when sunlight fills the room, the screen remains clear enough to enjoy without constantly adjusting blinds or curtains. One feature I didn’t expect to use was the children’s remote, but it’s actually a thoughtful addition. It’s simple, colourful and gives younger viewers an easy way to access suitable content, which I can imagine being a real bonus for families. The smart TV interface is well laid out and includes all the apps I regularly use, meaning I’ve been able to retire my streaming stick completely. The dedicated app buttons on the remote are handy too, making it quick to jump straight into whatever I want to watch. There is occasionally a slight delay when navigating menus, but it’s minor and hasn’t affected my overall experience. Considering everything else the TV offers, it’s a small compromise. Overall, this TV feels like a fantastic all-round package. It looks stylish, performs brilliantly and is simple enough for everyone in the household to use. If you’re upgrading from an older set, you’ll definitely notice the difference.
author: TheBladeUk

body: I have had this tv a few weeks now.  Delivery and set up was surprisingly easy. The box is designed so you dont have to lift it up, it opens round the TV.  Assembling the legs was straight forward, there are 2 widths depending on where you are putting it. Once on, we used wider settings its very stable even on our temporary table as we plan a media wall to give this great tv its max effect.  Setting up took a couple of mins and was all done, very easy to follow steps. Its compatibility to link with home features makes it more impressive. It was super easy to sign in to our subscriptions we have.  First impressions when we got it set up were wow... the sound is great, clear and well projected round the room we have. The subtitles are a brilliant size, actually had to move back which really adds for us. The picture is crystal clear, even when closer its not pixilated or blurry.  The app feature is great, can turn off when the children forget too.  We have also tried a console on it and wow its made that really fun to play. The children were all able to play together as my boy could see clearly!  So far this is definitely worth it, sleek thin and so light compared to our old 55" one."

body: Having previously owned a Hisense TV, I was curious to see how much they have improved over the years - and boy was I impressed! Starting with initial set-up. Very easy to use and get started. A QR code allowed access to the app to help set-up go smoothly and I was up and running within a few minutes. The user interface is very easy to use and intuitive to find your way about. Using the smart on demand features, finding apps, setting up your sound and pictures preferences - all very easy to utilise. The picture quality is superb - colours are rich and vibrant, blacks are clear and the auto adjustment features on the TV are great to ensure maximum quality when viewing darker movies. I particularly like the function where it automatically senses if a movie you are watching has Filmaker mode and it automatically switches to this to enhance your viewing.  The AI motion adjustments are great too - avoiding the motion blur effects you get with some TVs. This is particularly great when gaming - smooth motions and movements making it great to play on. Sound is very good too - a massive upgrade on previous Hisense models.  The remote is very easy to use and a good size - feels nice in your hands and the quick access to the most popular streaming apps makes for seamless switching between what your watching. Overall I am very impressed with this TV. It's an excellent choice for someone looking for a great quality TV for their living room or bedroom - great for movies, shows, streaming and gaming - all round, I highly recommend this TV.  5 Stars!
author: Derek1graham

body:
I've previously had Hisense TVs so you would think I knew what I was in for — Wrong! I expected minor improvements but I was very pleased with what I saw. Let's go through some of the specs that matter and made a difference to my experience: - VIDAA smart platform — THIS IS THE ONE THAT REALLY SOLD ME THIS TV. VIDAA is a lightweight Linux-based smart TV platform. What this means to us is that you can launch apps like Netflix or YouTube really fast and smooth, adding to the overall experience. No more wondering what the hell happened to the app you just started — it's just there, instantly. - Hi-QLED with Quantum Dot colour — The screen is brighter and richer than my previous TV, which was already quite impressive. Colours feel more true-to-life and punchy without looking over-saturated. A genuine step up. - 144Hz panel — I don't think this made as much difference to me personally as it did to my 9-year-old son. The feedback is that gaming is smoother and more pleasant. WIN! There are other gaming features too — Game Mode Pro and the updated Game Bar give gamers quick access to VRR, frame rate counters, and input lag settings. Proper stuff. - All the HDR modes — This bad boy supports HDR10+, HDR10+ Gaming, Dolby Vision, Dolby Vision IQ, and HLG — essentially covering every format you're likely to encounter. You're not going to hit a wall with this one. - Hi-View AI Engine (MediaTek Pentonic 700 chip) — Enables enhancements such as AI Picture, AI Light Sensor, AI 4K Upscaling, AI Detail Enhancement, AI HDR Enhancement, and AI Smooth Motion. Basically you're fully "AI'd" up - Filmmaker Mode — Preserves the director's original frame rates and colour intent without any motion processing applied. If you're a film lover, this one matters more than you'd think. The only thing that's potentially not the best is the sound quality. It's OK but not exactly hi-fi, and let's be honest — at this price point you wouldn't expect it to be either. So this review still retains 5 stars. The remote is well laid out with shortcut buttons for all the major apps. It's also Bluetooth, so you don't even have to point it at the TV — which feels delightfully lazy. Ha!
I love this TV so much that I've actually set it up as a second computer monitor. Check out the picture. Overall, I would thoroughly recommend this TV.

body: From the moment I received this 43” TV, I was pleasantly surprised by how lightweight it was; it almost felt deceptive given its size. Unboxing was straightforward, and installing the pedestal feet was simple and stress-free. The protective cardboard over the screen was a thoughtful touch, making setup much easier without worrying about accidental damage. Although I plan to wall mount it later, the initial setup was smooth and user-friendly. Powering on the TV and setting it up via the VIDAA app was effortless. Downloading the app and connecting it to the TV was quick, and the mobile setup process worked seamlessly. The WiFi connection is strong, allowing the smart interface to run smoothly and making navigation intuitive and easy to use. One of the standout features is Freely, which removes the need for a traditional TV aerial. This is incredibly convenient, simplifying installation and eliminating the hassle of running additional cables or installing an aerial point. In terms of picture and sound quality, both are excellent. The display delivers vibrant, sharp visuals across all types of genres of programs. Sports, in particular, look fantastic; fast-moving scenes are clear, bright, and easy on the eyes, which is perfect for watching events like the World Cup. The sound is also impressive, offering clear and balanced audio across volume levels. While a surround sound system would enhance bass performance, the built-in speakers are more than sufficient for a bedroom setup. If I had one suggestion, it would be to make the feet more centrally positioned. This would provide greater flexibility when placing the TV on different types of furniture. That said, it currently fits on my chest of drawers, though this is only temporary as I intend to mount it on the wall. Overall, this is a great TV with a simple and intuitive navigation system, excellent picture quality and strong, clear audio performance. I had heard of the brand before but never considered purchasing; something I now see was a mistake. This TV proves they can compete with more established brands, especially when considering the excellent value for money."

body:
Our new Hisense TV has provided a hit for our teenage son's bedroom. The picture quality is outstanding, very clear and crisp with excellent dark blacks.

This is an upper range TV, with a price to match, however it's worth it in our opinion and we are already looking at upgrading another tv to this Hisense range in time for the world cup.
author: mdmedia

body:
I don't know where to begin for reviewing my new MASSIVE 85" Hisense TV 85E78STUK PRO. I'm actually even more impressed with it than I was expecting.
The TV it's replacing was a decent 65" TV, so was only expecting a small improvement in the picture and sound quality, and got to admit the thought had crossed my mind that because of the 20" size difference, whatever increase in picture quality with the new telly, would be lost in this increase in size. I was wrong, the sharpness for a start, is much better, as are the depths and vibrancy of colours, proper black blacks, even in a darkened room. The Tv automatically upscales standard signal to 4K. I have not altered the colours in any way, I'm extremely happy with the way they are out of the box so to speak. For the technical it boasts Quantum Dot Colour and Dolby Vision IQ. You do have preset options, like cinema, game mode, sport etc. which again I have not needed to change, although I have used the sport mode to watch football. I was showing the TV off to (jealous) friends though. Same as picture options, there are preset sound options. I've tried the music and cinema sound modes, as with picture modes, there are more options, but can't remember them all. With the sound, I did increase the bass on the graphic equaliser as I like a lot of oomph. For the technically minded it boasts 2 x 15W + 20W speakers and has eARK audio via HDMI. Again for the technical the TV boasts Dolby Atmos and DTS Virtual X decoding for immersive sound. There are plenty of connection options e.g. several HDMI's USB etc., which I won't go into as the specs are on all the sales and Hisense websites. Setting up was simple, from initial setup, to connecting to Wi-Fi. I'd say most apps what you need are pre-installed like Netflix etc. I can't comment on the installed apps as I don't have Netflix account, I almost exclusively use Sky on my TV, which this TV compliments amazingly, the Sky remote pairs easily with the TV, for automatic turning the TV on and off. One slight downside (if you can call it that) I've noticed is you need to check the little white standby light on the bottom of the TV illuminates when turning off, as you can't tell it has gone into a standby state because of the darkness of the black colour. The TV has built in Freely for viewing live TV. This seems good, although only used very briefly when first setting the TV up with using Sky. The TV remote has built in voice control, enabling use of the built in Alexa for example. Can't comment on the use of that as I have Alexa in the room already set up and don't want them fighting over each other. I was pleased to find out this TV only weighs just over 32kg (85" without stand) which is a lot lighter than my previous 65" TV. I must also point out, I measured my chimney breast wall incorrectly when measuring up for the wall bracket/mount and the TV is bigger than my original measurements, so I need to move the wall bracket before I can mount it. I thought, oh no, I've made a terrible mistake, the TV is far too big for the room when I first started viewing, BUT I have quickly become used to the size. So be brave and order the biggest you can fit in your room, you won't regret it.
In a nutshell this TV gets a thumbs up for me, I absolutely love it and don't have one regret in purchasing it. From delivery in its extremely sturdy box, to sitting watching a movie, it has brought an enormous smile to my face. Can't wait till I can get it on the wall. I might then, find even more amazing features that I have probably missed. I haven't mentioned the value for money is also excellent, getting more to the £ than most other manufacturers. I hadn't taken much notice of the brand Hisense until a couple of years ago if I'm honest. Then I looked into their side by side fridge freezers, I was impressed with the build quality, innovation and price. When this TV came on the market and I had a chance of purchasing, I had no qualms on buying Hisense. As in my review, from packaging to use of the item, it's all first class, competition for the best

body:
Having had 3 weeks with this TV, I have found the picture and sound quality to be excellent. The high refresh rate is uncommon at this size so great to have in the size I needed. Sound quality is impressive for a TV of this size providing decent bass and clear vocals. The DSP audio modes are great. Freely works well, and there's a wide range of additional streaming channels and most streaming apps are available. 
Voice search is available using the microphone in the remote and this works well. It's a great TV, easy to navigate, great picture, great sound. There are a couple of negatives, though. Vidaa has pretty good app availability, but there's no Emby client available, although Plex is present. The remote is massively over-sensitive with the buttons having very little resistance before engaging. The 9 app-specific launcher buttons may be useful for some, but it feels like they're taking up far too much space on the remote. Overall it's a great TV, and I'd recommend it to anyone looking for a TV of this size - if they can live with the remote.

body:

First impressions arrived before it was even switched on, it's so much lighter than my previous set, long gone are the days 2 people struggled to pick up the TV, this was light and very easy to move into position. Then it was time for the setup, you use the Vidaa app to setup the TV and this made it much easier than having to type in Wi-Fi details with your remote... setup connects you to the internet, sets everything up and you're good to go... anyone could do this. Once setup I was shocked just how many apps and channels you could receive without even connecting an aerial... Freely works great and let me watch shows I hadn't even considered watching.

We placed the TV in a very light heavy room and the brightness of the tv is more than enough to punch through, there's only a slight light bleed on very dark pictures. I haven't had a chance to really push the TV to it's limits on gaming but gaming on the Switch was flawless. All in, very happy and would recommend this TV.
author: Mabbs

body:
My first impression of the Hisense 75E7STUK – It’s BIG, fast, and surprisingly good! For both the picture and sound it is very good value for money.
The good - Stunning picture quality for the money. Replacing my 55 inch OLED I was worried that the picture would not hold up. Overall, I had nothing to be concern about! It’s clean, and responsive. Gaming (I’m a PS5 gamer) is great. The Game mode kicks in and supports variable refresh rate, Auto Low Latency Mode etc making it a pleasure to use. Even at close range (couple of meters away) it looks good. 
The sound is balanced and the built-in subwoofers provides surprisingly robust audio, way better than the TV it’s replacing. I have a soundbar/sub but haven’t plugged it in as I’m not sure it’s needed! Likewise, the OS works very well, with fast access to apps. The Freely tuner is also very good, making it much easier to watch programmes without changes between the on demand apps i.e. it lets you watch live TV over Wi-Fi without needing an aerial, and it just works. I’ve also found the supporting mobile app really good and allows use of the TV without the remote. 
The less good - Contrast in low light. Being a QLED, the black levels and local dimming cannot match the blacks of my older OLED and you can see the backlighting “Leak” from the edges where the picture on the TV is dark. 
To conclude - Value for Money! - Massive 75" screen, that’s great for gaming, a surprisingly good sound, and great tech makes it a no brainer for the price.
