body:
"Feature packed and well built Hisense is not a brand I have previously considered generally tending to look at more well known brands. However I was pleasantly surprised with my latest purchase of the 55U8QTUK. The TV was extremely well packaged, something I was grateful for given the weight of the TV. At first this might sound like a negative but I consider this a big postive. Many TV's now are so thin and light and can often feel fragile, not so with this model from Hisense, It feels quality and robust and well engineerd. 

The unboxing experience was good with everything well packaged and easily identifiable. I have the TV wall mounted and therefore didn't use the included stand however I have no doubt from the build quality of the stand it would have no problem supporting the TV should you choose to mount yours on a media unit. 

Powering up the TV I was greeted by an unfamiliar VIDAA operating system for the TV. I'm pleased to say it was fast and responsive with pleasent graphics and an easy to navigate and intuative design. I was able to setup all of my frequently used apps quickly and easily. 

One thing I must emphasize is the features and quality feel of the supplied remote in hand, also the fact that it doesn't need batteries and is powered by sunlight is a novel but useful highlight. 

I have a number of the latest gaming consoles and was pleased to see that all of the HDMI inputs are of the latest 2.1 generation and also supported my high-end gaming PC up to 165Hz refresh rate something not supported by many other TV's currently. 

Also a really nice unique feature of this TV and something which I cannot find on any other TV is a USB-C input this means I could connect my tablet and laptop via a single USB-C cable and again I was able to get full 4K resolution!

Overall I have been massively impressed by both the design, features and quality of this TV and will be sure to consider Hisense products in the future based on this purchase."

Picture Mode Settings, Advanced Settings - you can adjust the brightness , color, motion, clarity and overscan. 

Picture Mode Game Settings- it comes with its own picture settings for games

Amazon Alexa- we don’t currently have it set up, but it is available

BBC Account - you can connect prior to your BBC Account when you use hands free voice 

I am very happy to have tried Hisense and I would recommend it with my eyes closed. Great quality for a very good price. My husband is in love with the design and the finish of the remote control, the tv itself. Very sleek design.

body:
First of all I must say that the box is big, as well as heavy and you'll need a second pair of hands to get the TV out safely and to lift it into its final position after fitting the very substantial centre stand, which gave me confidence that it would remain put. I advise reading the manual on how to attach the stand and don't just guess.

Having viewed this Hisense 65U8NQTUK 65" 4K Ultra HD MiniLED Smart TV for the last 10 days I am really impressed with its performance, looks and build quality. The picture is clear and detailed, especially when viewing in 4K content from Netflix and the sound is good for a LED, although I have finally connected it to a soundbar usingthe HDMI ARC port. No trace of lipsync issues.

I particulary like the layout and feel of the remote control and the built in solar charger to save having to find batteries when you least expect. Its reassuring to see the effort put into the remote rather than leaving it to chance with a flimsy unintuative lump of plastic.

I don't have an external aerial and I rely on a well known satellite system but I was eager to see what free to air channels I could get using the Freely streaming app which is slowly rolling out. Unfortunately I hit a hurdle here and the App failed to install.

PROS
- Very clear detailed 4K and HD picture from those Mini LEDs
- Good sound with Dolby Atmos quality and built in sub-woofer
- Solid centre stand
- Plenty of connection options
- Excellent build quality and style, inc remote
- Easy setup
- Good GUI
- 2 year manufacturer warranty


CONS
- The Freely App failed to install - reason unknown - Freely servers?
- Slight motion blur when people running during a movie scene
- Stand a bit fiddley to assemble and fit to TV (read manual)
- It's heavy, need two people but it's a 65" TV so really to be expected

So to sum up, this new 65" U8NQT model for 2024 should be on your shortlist if you're looking for a fully featured sub £2k 4K smart TV.

You won't regret it.

body:
Firstly might I say, If you're looking for a great image, sound and a user friendly UI then this really is the Tv for you.

Hisense have come a long way in the recent months with making a really high quality product that can easily compete with the top brands. Both the TV and the included remote feel high quality and gives me a sense that it will last for a good number of years.

I have this tv mounted on my wall with a standard 400x600 wall mount and it looks great. As advertised, I have minimal glare from both light coming through the window in the day and internal lights at night. The sound quality is as great as any other premium TV sound output and wouldn't need any further aid from a sound bar but I already had one so I connected it and used that after testing. 

The picture quality from the TV is fantastic when you get a 4k video up. The blacks are so dark and there is no light bleed whatsoever. The only issues I have found is there are some vertical bars visible when the picture pans sideways (noticed during a football match), these are minor and can only be seen under certain conditions but once I have seen them I can't unsee them (those who know, know). This could be a manufacture defect or maybe even settings that need changing in the TV but more searching is required for me on this front as when in a dynamic picture mode, the TV will decide what's the best colours and contrast.

The apps built into the TV are great and I would argue you no longer need a coax feed to the back of the TV as all of the major channels are accessible over the internet apps.

I did try to use the mobile phone app during set up but it struggled to pair with the TV. I would class myself as an average user of tech so I know my way around a phone and how to try other methods if something isn't quiet working. Once the TV was set up, you can use the app as a remote but I haven't really done so as the included TV remote is fantastic.

So, in summary. Would I recommend this TV to you if you're reading this?
Yes! The picture quality and sound is great and certainly a big contender with the top TVs out there right now. Even with the minor issue with my TV picture (probably is a setting somewhere), 99% of the time I'm blown away with how crisp and clear the image is. I truly haven't seen a TV yet without light bleed into the blacks until I watched this one!

body:
This TV really feels like a top quality premium television. It has a great modern design with a very thin frame but the overall build quality feels really good and durable. The central pedestal is thin but wide and heavy, so the TV is really stable once placed on the furniture unit.

It has plenty of connections available on the back (USB, 4 HDMI's, 3.5mm headphones, etc...) The HDMIs were particularly fast when playing content from external devices (laptop, Roku stick).

Image and sound quality are fantastic, with very smooth movements and very good image depth (sometimes, it looks almost 3D, like if you were inside the movie or the documentary).

We also set up Vidaa and Freely accounts. We were impressed with Vidaa (everything is streamed in HD or 4K) but we didn't like the fact that you cannot finish the Freely session once started (you can end sessions in any other app or channel).

The TV comes with all the streaming apps ready, you don't have to set up anything, just provide your account username and password and start watching. The screen and content sharing features also work very well and we liked a lot the fact that the remote has a USB rechargeable battery (and PV cells, so it lasts for ages).

I would definitively recommend this TV.

body:
Good Points: The Hisense tv looks great mounted on my wall. It is very intuitive to use and amazingly quick loading all of my favourite apps which are all there. When looking directly at the tv, the colours are vibrant and sharp, producing a really nice picture. 

Alexa works well and was very easy to sync with the rest of my household setup. 

The remote is sleek and comes with a number of quick buttons to take you straight to the apps you need. 

The tv comes with a great number of inputs including 4 hdmi slots, one of which is a 144hz eARC for connecting other smart peripherals. I’m glad it has an optical input as I can still connect my Gen 1 Sonos soundbar. The slight downside with this setup is that I can’t change the volume on the soundbar as that requires an IR remote which this one isn’t. However I’m sure this wouldn’t be a problem if I had connected the tv to my Gen 2 Sonos soundbar through the eARC hdmi connection.

Improvement Points: As the viewing angle increases the colours lose some of the vibrancy with a slight tendency to look a bit washed out at the extremes. 

I can’t reorder the channels like I can on my LG, so I can’t put all of the HD channels at 1-8. I find this frustrating but bearable!

body:
"A Brilliant All-Rounder with a Near Perfect UI I’ve been really impressed with this TV since setting it up. The AI picture settings are genuinely brilliant - everything looks fantastic without needing to constantly adjust things manually. After looking into them a bit more it's based on ambient light and the type of programme so that's pretty epic!

Whether we've had animated films on for the kids or I've been able to kick back and watch the rugby, the picture is vibrant, smooth, and full of detail. Even during the day in a bright room, there’s no issue with glare or fading colours - we have big dormer windows and it handles bright light really well, which is something we were hoping for in this TV.

I’ve also been pleased with the sound. It’s clear and balanced, and we haven’t felt the need for extra speakers. Dialogue is crisp, and there’s a decent amount of depth, which makes a big difference for movies and action scenes. The built-in sound system gives a full, room-filling experience without needing to add a soundbar. Definitely play around with the sound settings as well for the best experience!

Apps load quickly, and everything on the smart system runs smoothly. Switching between streaming services is quick and responsive. The remote is thoughtfully designed too - it’s got all the main app buttons built in, and I especially like that you can customise one of the buttons to go directly to a specific app or device input. That’s been a nice bonus. It even charges by sunlight and has a USB-C port, so it never runs out of battery...well it hasn't yet and I live in Scotland!

The overall design of the TV is really modern and premium-looking. It sits nicely on our unit but would also look great wall-mounted (which it will be soon). The stand offers two height positions, which is helpful if you’re using a soundbar or want it a bit higher if you're a giant like me. 

The set-up was simple and guided me through everything clearly - I was up and running in less than 10 minutes. Note, it is fairly heavy to lift onto the stand yourself but with some careful positioning and the multifunctional packaging (that's not even a joke just wait 'til you see the instructions) you can manage it yourself.

Overall, this TV has been a fantastic addition to our home. It looks good, performs well in all kinds of situations, and is easy to use every day. Definitely recommend if you're looking for a feature-packed, smart and reliable upgrade."

body:
"Great tv for a great price! I’ve been checking out the new Hisense 55U8QTUK MiniLED 165Hz Smart AI, and honestly… it’s amazing for the price. If you want a TV that looks high-end without paying crazy money… this might be the one.
The screen is super bright, even in the middle of the day with sunlight coming in. The colors are rich, and the black parts of the screen actually look sooo dark not washed out. It’s awesome for watching movies or Netflix. The picture looks really sharp and smooth, even during fast scenes.
if you are into gaming ( like me) PS5, Xbox, or even PC—this TV is a beast. It can do 4K at 165Hz, which is faster than most TVs. Games feel smooth and super responsive and very low input lag. Basically, it’s made for gaming.
The sound is better than I expected. It has built-in speakers with Dolby Atmos, and it even has a little subwoofer in the back for bass. Movies and games sound full, and you might not even need a soundbar. Just a heads-up… if you mount it on the wall, the bass can make the wall vibrate a little.
It’s a solid… well-built TV with a sleek design. The stand is adjustable, and the whole thing looks and feels like a premium product. Definitely doesn’t look cheap.
This is one of the best TVs you can buy right now if you want awesome quality without paying OLED prices. Great for movies, sports, and especially gaming. Hisense really nailed it with this one.
Would totally recommend. It is bright, fast, great sounding, and full of features. Definitely feels like you’re getting more than what you paid for.

"

body:
"Feature packed and well built Hisense is not a brand I have previously considered generally tending to look at more well known brands. However I was pleasantly surprised with my latest purchase of the 55U8QTUK. The TV was extremely well packaged, something I was grateful for given the weight of the TV. At first this might sound like a negative but I consider this a big postive. Many TV's now are so thin and light and can often feel fragile, not so with this model from Hisense, It feels quality and robust and well engineerd. 

The unboxing experience was good with everything well packaged and easily identifiable. I have the TV wall mounted and therefore didn't use the included stand however I have no doubt from the build quality of the stand it would have no problem supporting the TV should you choose to mount yours on a media unit. 

Powering up the TV I was greeted by an unfamiliar VIDAA operating system for the TV. I'm pleased to say it was fast and responsive with pleasent graphics and an easy to navigate and intuative design. I was able to setup all of my frequently used apps quickly and easily. 

One thing I must emphasize is the features and quality feel of the supplied remote in hand, also the fact that it doesn't need batteries and is powered by sunlight is a novel but useful highlight. 

I have a number of the latest gaming consoles and was pleased to see that all of the HDMI inputs are of the latest 2.1 generation and also supported my high-end gaming PC up to 165Hz refresh rate something not supported by many other TV's currently. 

Also a really nice unique feature of this TV and something which I cannot find on any other TV is a USB-C input this means I could connect my tablet and laptop via a single USB-C cable and again I was able to get full 4K resolution!

Overall I have been massively impressed by both the design, features and quality of this TV and will be sure to consider Hisense products in the future based on this purchase."

This Hisense TV has brought more life to our Living Room. I have imagined it being very big, but while it has 65 inch, it looks perfect above the living room furniture. The finish of the edges of the screen is sleek and elegant. 

It comes with a solid heavy TV stand if you want to make it stand, but because we have a child, we preferred to have it on the wall. It was easy to have it up on the wall and the setup was relatively quick. 

Image is great. We have used the same cartoons my son is watching to compare with our previous TV, and I believe Hisense offers a more natural, bright image. 

VIDAA App - you can control the TV from an app installed on your phone. We were using the Apple Box before to do the same thing, but we found it fascinating that the TV itself allows us to do this. 

VIDAA Voice - helps you control your tv hands free

Freely - Live TV. Even though we pay for the TV License we never used to watch live channels because of the inconvenience trying to find the TV remote control. Since we are having Hisense, we love having news on the background because I can control everything from my phone while working at my desk.

Picture Mode: It has so many options such as Enhanced ACR, Filmmaker, HDR Standard, etc. I love the fact that it has Max Cinema Too. It is something I look forward trying in the coming weeks.

Picture Mode Settings, Advanced Settings - you can adjust the brightness , color, motion, clarity and overscan. 

Picture Mode Game Settings- it comes with its own picture settings for games

Amazon Alexa- we don’t currently have it set up, but it is available

BBC Account - you can connect prior to your BBC Account when you use hands free voice 

I am very happy to have tried Hisense and I would recommend it with my eyes closed. Great quality for a very good price. My husband is in love with the design and the finish of the remote control, the tv itself. Very sleek design.

body: The Hisense TV offers outstanding picture quality with a sharp, clear, and lifelike display. Its vibrant colours are dynamic and bright, providing vivid imagery. The sound quality is impressive, creating a cinematic experience that immerses you. Even at high volume, there is no distortion, ensuring clear dialogue and excellent overall audio quality. With built in subs enhancing sound performance, the TV delivers deep and rich audio. The gaming features are exceptional, making feel fully immersed in the game with vivid colours and high quality sound.  The TV includes a variety of apps such as Netflix, Prime Video, YouTube, Disney, Freely, Apple TV, and Amazon, providing a wide range of options from Sci-Fi and comedy to TV shows, sports, kids content, documentaries, and numerous games. body:
First of all I must say that the box is big, as well as heavy and you'll need a second pair of hands to get the TV out safely and to lift it into its final position after fitting the very substantial centre stand, which gave me confidence that it would remain put. I advise reading the manual on how to attach the stand and don't just guess.

Having viewed this Hisense 65U8NQTUK 65" 4K Ultra HD MiniLED Smart TV for the last 10 days I am really impressed with its performance, looks and build quality. The picture is clear and detailed, especially when viewing in 4K content from Netflix and the sound is good for a LED, although I have finally connected it to a soundbar usingthe HDMI ARC port. No trace of lipsync issues.

I particulary like the layout and feel of the remote control and the built in solar charger to save having to find batteries when you least expect. Its reassuring to see the effort put into the remote rather than leaving it to chance with a flimsy unintuative lump of plastic.

I don't have an external aerial and I rely on a well known satellite system but I was eager to see what free to air channels I could get using the Freely streaming app which is slowly rolling out. Unfortunately I hit a hurdle here and the App failed to install.

PROS
- Very clear detailed 4K and HD picture from those Mini LEDs
- Good sound with Dolby Atmos quality and built in sub-woofer
- Solid centre stand
- Plenty of connection options
- Excellent build quality and style, inc remote
- Easy setup
- Good GUI
- 2 year manufacturer warranty


CONS
- The Freely App failed to install - reason unknown - Freely servers?
- Slight motion blur when people running during a movie scene
- Stand a bit fiddley to assemble and fit to TV (read manual)
- It's heavy, need two people but it's a 65" TV so really to be expected

So to sum up, this new 65" U8NQT model for 2024 should be on your shortlist if you're looking for a fully featured sub £2k 4K smart TV.

You won't regret it.

body:
Firstly might I say, If you're looking for a great image, sound and a user friendly UI then this really is the Tv for you.

Hisense have come a long way in the recent months with making a really high quality product that can easily compete with the top brands. Both the TV and the included remote feel high quality and gives me a sense that it will last for a good number of years.

I have this tv mounted on my wall with a standard 400x600 wall mount and it looks great. As advertised, I have minimal glare from both light coming through the window in the day and internal lights at night. The sound quality is as great as any other premium TV sound output and wouldn't need any further aid from a sound bar but I already had one so I connected it and used that after testing. 

The picture quality from the TV is fantastic when you get a 4k video up. The blacks are so dark and there is no light bleed whatsoever. The only issues I have found is there are some vertical bars visible when the picture pans sideways (noticed during a football match), these are minor and can only be seen under certain conditions but once I have seen them I can't unsee them (those who know, know). This could be a manufacture defect or maybe even settings that need changing in the TV but more searching is required for me on this front as when in a dynamic picture mode, the TV will decide what's the best colours and contrast.

The apps built into the TV are great and I would argue you no longer need a coax feed to the back of the TV as all of the major channels are accessible over the internet apps.

I did try to use the mobile phone app during set up but it struggled to pair with the TV. I would class myself as an average user of tech so I know my way around a phone and how to try other methods if something isn't quiet working. Once the TV was set up, you can use the app as a remote but I haven't really done so as the included TV remote is fantastic.

So, in summary. Would I recommend this TV to you if you're reading this?
Yes! The picture quality and sound is great and certainly a big contender with the top TVs out there right now. Even with the minor issue with my TV picture (probably is a setting somewhere), 99% of the time I'm blown away with how crisp and clear the image is. I truly haven't seen a TV yet without light bleed into the blacks until I watched this one!

This TV really feels like a top quality premium television. It has a great modern design with a very thin frame but the overall build quality feels really good and durable. The central pedestal is thin but wide and heavy, so the TV is really stable once placed on the furniture unit.

It has plenty of connections available on the back (USB, 4 HDMI's, 3.5mm headphones, etc...) The HDMIs were particularly fast when playing content from external devices (laptop, Roku stick).

Image and sound quality are fantastic, with very smooth movements and very good image depth (sometimes, it looks almost 3D, like if you were inside the movie or the documentary).

We also set up Vidaa and Freely accounts. We were impressed with Vidaa (everything is streamed in HD or 4K) but we didn't like the fact that you cannot finish the Freely session once started (you can end sessions in any other app or channel).

The TV comes with all the streaming apps ready, you don't have to set up anything, just provide your account username and password and start watching. The screen and content sharing features also work very well and we liked a lot the fact that the remote has a USB rechargeable battery (and PV cells, so it lasts for ages).

I would definitively recommend this TV.

Good Points: The Hisense tv looks great mounted on my wall. It is very intuitive to use and amazingly quick loading all of my favourite apps which are all there. When looking directly at the tv, the colours are vibrant and sharp, producing a really nice picture. 

Alexa works well and was very easy to sync with the rest of my household setup. 

The remote is sleek and comes with a number of quick buttons to take you straight to the apps you need. 

The tv comes with a great number of inputs including 4 hdmi slots, one of which is a 144hz eARC for connecting other smart peripherals. I’m glad it has an optical input as I can still connect my Gen 1 Sonos soundbar. The slight downside with this setup is that I can’t change the volume on the soundbar as that requires an IR remote which this one isn’t. However I’m sure this wouldn’t be a problem if I had connected the tv to my Gen 2 Sonos soundbar through the eARC hdmi connection.

Improvement Points: As the viewing angle increases the colours lose some of the vibrancy with a slight tendency to look a bit washed out at the extremes. 

I can’t reorder the channels like I can on my LG, so I can’t put all of the HD channels at 1-8. I find this frustrating but bearable!

body:
The first thing I noticed about my new Hisense TV is that it felt sturdy and well made when I removed it from the box. It also has a sleek and slim modern design and feel to it. At 50 inches It is a really good size but slim and light enough to be easily mounted on a wall if you wanted to. If you don't want to put it on a wall I find that the stands it comes with make it very stable to stand on a unit or table etc.
Setting up the TV is very easy you just plug it in and follow the instructions on the screen. No aerial is needed only WIFI internet but you can use it with an arial though I have not tried it that way.
I found that cinema mode is best for me, this gives you a great picture with lots of depth and sharp detail but you can try the other modes and sound settings to find out what is best for you and what you like to watch. As the screen is nice and big and clear it is superb for subtitles on foreign language movies or the captions on sports like formula 1.
I have not used Freely before and was initially a little disappointed that a couple of my favourite channels from Freeview are not yet available on Freely but other that that it is really good and easy to use with lots of channels to choose from. I also think that Freely will continue to be updated with more channels.
The remote control is light and slim and also simple to navigate. The internal speakers are very adequate and provide a punchy sound but we invested in a Hisense sound bar to make the sound deeper and fuller for movies as we watch them a lot. There is no need to have the sound bar on all the time though.
I am very impressed with this TV especially for watching films, drama, foreign language TV and movies, manga and action movies which are all especially good. It is also great for any kind of sport or things like nature documentaries. I would recommend it mainly for its ease of use and the great picture and sound quality.

body:
This is a massive 65-inch television usually means expecting a bargain-basement picture. I bought the Hisense 65E6STUK bracing for major compromises, but after setting it up, my only real regret is that I didn't buy a second one. 
The 4K display panel is easily the biggest selling point. The bad bit in the hardware, it is definitely the built-in sound system. The TV is equipped with a basic 2.0 channel speaker array putting out 20W of total power. While the software tries its best with onboard DTS Virtual:X processing to widen the soundstage, it does not achieve. The down-firing drivers lack low-end punch. Bass is virtually non-existent, and high volumes can get slightly muddy. It is perfectly fine for the news, but it simply does not match the grand scale of the 65-inch picture. This was no issue for me as I use a separates with digital AV amp which is an easy fix for such a great price. Overall The user interface is powered by VIDAA, which is fast, lightweight, and completely free from the sluggish navigation lag that plagues other budget smart platforms. All my streaming apps load up instantly. Buy this twice if you get a chance

body:
Excited to receive my new 43" Hisense TV. The box looked slick and was easy to open. Remote controls and two tiny plastic feet easy to remove from the box along with the TV itself. Within two minutes the TV was on and I was installing the VIDDA app to help with setup. Love how quick and easy it was and within another few minutes the TV was on and Freely was working.
Really impressed with how lite the TV was and great build quality. Remote is really slick and jad all the main app buttons. There was even a second app for "kids" which made me smile as my kids have been able to operate any remote controls since they were about 2 or 3 years old and it more my elderly relatives who would benefit from a simple remote.
Picture quality was very impressive whether watching Sports, Movies or general TV. The different picture and sound modes gave added quality of both picture and sound when selected for the type of program you're watching.
Swapping between apps, Live TV etc was seamless and even at start up you didn't need to wait ages for wifi connection. 
Very happy with the look and sound of the TV, the remote controls and the overall experience. Would 100% recommend it to all.

Its very smart and suggests ideas when changing to certain things, for example if you are watching a film it will suggest cinema mode, also the same if playing a game. 
The sound  is so clear on this model you dont even need it up high at all, it clearly has  great speakers. Its easy to turn off and shuts down like a slow closing down, it has a kids remote which is a gamechanger for anyone with kids and an bigger remote for us adults with all the quick keys you need. Overall im so impressed with my purchase and have already recommended. My only negative would be the power cable needs to be slighty longer, as we put it on the wall.

Sound quality is poor, I play my tv through the hi-fi to achieve a decent sound

body: Does what it says on the tin!

Great budget tv. I found it relatively easy to navigate (after not having a tv for quite a few years), does everything I want from a tv. The colour is great but for me I am struggling a bit with the sound (maybe where I have it positioned and my hearing is starting to go a little), so I will be getting a sound bar to enhance my experience. However there are loads of settings for both picture and sound and these help as I have reflections from the conservatory roof too so can mitigate this to a certain degree in the different picture setting and for the sound there is a speech setting that I find is better for me too. The main reason I bought this tv was that it still provides an RCA connection (the red, white & yellow cables) so I am able to connect my old WII directly to the tv. I have also connected my computer to it and the screen quality is fabulous. This means I can watch my own DVD films directly on the big Tv screen directly connected via a HDMI cable. 
Overall, for a budget tv I am more than satisfied and would recommend.

body: My review is of the 50” 50E6STUK model.   My initial impression of the tv was very good.  It’s about 5 years since I last bought a tv and for the size, I found this model very lightweight when I lifted it so I figured set up would be straightforward myself - and it was, up to a point.  The stands screwed on ok, though still felt a slightly wobbly when I tightened them, and then I discovered they were too wide for the unit the previous 32” had come off of.  I suspect this is common to other manufacturers, not just Hisense but the measurement of the stands from the edge of the tv would be a useful inclusion in the instruction book.  I got round the problem by buying another stand which fits in the middle and this worked fine.  The power cable comes separate from the tv and during set up, was prone to coming out on a couple of occasions but has been stable since.  I’ve plugged an aerial into the tv and so have the choice of freeview or streaming.  Set up on the tv itself was very straightforward and in terms of using the remote and navigating through the apps, I’ve found this fairly intuitive and easy.  I’m not a gamer so can’t comment on that aspect but in terms of watching live tv or apps such as i-player, the picture quality and sound is excellent.  All in all, this would have been a 5 star, had the design features not slightly let it down but it’s still excellent value for money.

body:
I recently got the Hisense 55E6STUK and have been using it for a week now. Firstly I really like the size, its 55 inch screen, but does not take up a lot of room as the bezels are really thin, I was glad that it has standard VESA mount holes as I was able to wall mount.  It is a really thin and light tv.  Initial set up was quick and easy, I just followed the steps on the screen, was able to connect to my WIFI and away in fewer than 15 minutes. Picture – picture quality is excellent, I’ve watched using the built in apps, Netflix & Prime, and have my Sky box connected,  and I’m very impressed, this was an upgrade from my last TV that was over 15 years old, so I was expecting something a lot better,  and I’m finding the picture on this to be excellent. I like that you can easily change picture modes, so when watching a move I change to Filmmaker mode, it does make a difference. Sound – for a TV that is so slim, the sound is excellent, with good bass as well, for this level of sound I would have expected large speakers, but Hisense have been able to keep the TV really slim and also have very good sound. Apps – the home screen has all the apps that you need, and are easily to find and use.  
One other thing I liked is that the TV came with 2 remotes, the standard one and then also a much simpler one designed for children, which limits what they can do, I think this is an great idea as it means your kids can’t change the settings.  Overall a great TV that I would recommemnd."

body:
The first thing I noticed about my new Hisense TV is that it felt sturdy and well made when I removed it from the box. It also has a sleek and slim modern design and feel to it. At 50 inches It is a really good size but slim and light enough to be easily mounted on a wall if you wanted to. If you don't want to put it on a wall I find that the stands it comes with make it very stable to stand on a unit or table etc.
Setting up the TV is very easy you just plug it in and follow the instructions on the screen. No aerial is needed only WIFI internet but you can use it with an arial though I have not tried it that way.
I found that cinema mode is best for me, this gives you a great picture with lots of depth and sharp detail but you can try the other modes and sound settings to find out what is best for you and what you like to watch. As the screen is nice and big and clear it is superb for subtitles on foreign language movies or the captions on sports like formula 1.
I have not used Freely before and was initially a little disappointed that a couple of my favourite channels from Freeview are not yet available on Freely but other that that it is really good and easy to use with lots of channels to choose from. I also think that Freely will continue to be updated with more channels.
The remote control is light and slim and also simple to navigate. The internal speakers are very adequate and provide a punchy sound but we invested in a Hisense sound bar to make the sound deeper and fuller for movies as we watch them a lot. There is no need to have the sound bar on all the time though.
I am very impressed with this TV especially for watching films, drama, foreign language TV and movies, manga and action movies which are all especially good. It is also great for any kind of sport or things like nature documentaries. I would recommend it mainly for its ease of use and the great picture and sound quality.

body:
After giving my TV a good few days of use I want to share what has impressed me and also the bad bits too!
The tv is pleasantly light in weight which is really useful for someone who has health conditions and struggles with heavy things. It came supplied with the feet for ease of use. The picture is extremely clear and has a great game mode for the gamers, colours are vibrant which enhances the overall experience, it is very quick to respond and has a nice easy simple set up altho I can’t say this would be the case for someone elderly that does not understand qr codes or have the tech required to complete set up by themselves.
I really love that the tv came with a separate kids remote, this will help make little people feel included/in charge of their own tv experience while parents can feel confident.
The regular remote I felt was a bit on the long side however the buttons are placed nicely and you have fast access to the popular apps at the click of a button.
The tv has an ample amount of outputs e.g HDMI etc if needed altho I wonder if more could be added. The bad bits are something that could be improved. I found the speakers were not really on par with the picture quality, the sound is good but it could be better.
There wasn’t a wall bracket which limits how you display your tv, I feel this should be included on the more bigger models rather than an extra optional.
The build of the tv could be improved, I found gaps at the bottom (included in pics)  where the plastics are not as flush as they could be which is disappointing.
Batteries were provided for the remote but sadly not for the kids remote which I would have expected to be standard.
The length of the power cable could definitely do with being longer so there are no restrictions for placement of tv. Overall I am very happy, love the clear bright picture display and cannot wait to have a good film night with friends!"

body:
This is a massive 65-inch television usually means expecting a bargain-basement picture. I bought the Hisense 65E6STUK bracing for major compromises, but after setting it up, my only real regret is that I didn't buy a second one. 
The 4K display panel is easily the biggest selling point. The bad bit in the hardware, it is definitely the built-in sound system. The TV is equipped with a basic 2.0 channel speaker array putting out 20W of total power. While the software tries its best with onboard DTS Virtual:X processing to widen the soundstage, it does not achieve. The down-firing drivers lack low-end punch. Bass is virtually non-existent, and high volumes can get slightly muddy. It is perfectly fine for the news, but it simply does not match the grand scale of the 65-inch picture. This was no issue for me as I use a separates with digital AV amp which is an easy fix for such a great price. Overall The user interface is powered by VIDAA, which is fast, lightweight, and completely free from the sluggish navigation lag that plagues other budget smart platforms. All my streaming apps load up instantly. Buy this twice if you get a chance

body: Does what it says on the tin!

Great budget tv. I found it relatively easy to navigate (after not having a tv for quite a few years), does everything I want from a tv. The colour is great but for me I am struggling a bit with the sound (maybe where I have it positioned and my hearing is starting to go a little), so I will be getting a sound bar to enhance my experience. However there are loads of settings for both picture and sound and these help as I have reflections from the conservatory roof too so can mitigate this to a certain degree in the different picture setting and for the sound there is a speech setting that I find is better for me too. The main reason I bought this tv was that it still provides an RCA connection (the red, white & yellow cables) so I am able to connect my old WII directly to the tv. I have also connected my computer to it and the screen quality is fabulous. This means I can watch my own DVD films directly on the big Tv screen directly connected via a HDMI cable. 
Overall, for a budget tv I am more than satisfied and would recommend.

The only downside is that the TV does not allow downloading additional apps, which limits customization. It would be a great improvement if Hisense added an option to install apps from Google Play—especially useful tools like ad blockers or additional streaming apps.

✔ What I liked  
Clear picture quality
Nice and balanced sound
Perfect viewing experience overall

✘ What could be improved  
Ability to download apps like ad-blocker** (Google Play support would make the TV even better)

Final Thoughts  
A great TV with excellent visuals and sound, but limited app flexibility. If Hisense adds app-download support in future updates, this model would be close to perfect.

body: The Hisense 43Q7STUK was an upgrade for me and boy what an upgrade! It is so light compared to the weight of my previous tv. The sleek, minimalist look of it is just gorgeous and it sits neatly and sturdily on my unit.  Unpacking the box was a delight. Two feet which are secured in place with two screws was all the setup required. It was so easy that my teenage daughter happily took over at this point. Once the tv was in place and plugged in, it could not have been easier to setup. A QR code was scanned with my smart phone and the tv was connected to my internet. For all the streaming apps etc, again it was just a case of scanning the QR code and logging in. An absolute delight for someone who loves technology but can sometimes become overwhelmed with how quickly things change. I had plugged in my firestick but I don’t need it as everything is right there on the tv menu (on demand, internet browser etc.) The picture is so crystal clear, I still mention it every time we’re watching anything and this is 3 weeks on! I don’t have young children but I was intrigued by the kids remote that comes with it. I put the batteries in and switched it on to find all the children’s tv right there. It’s a great add on for families with young ones as you know they are only accessing age appropriate programs and with an easy to use, simple remote.  The main remote has specific buttons for the more popular apps but is incredibly easy to use. There can sometimes be a slight lag between pressing the buttons and the tv reacting but I have become used to it now and know to wait a couple of seconds. It’s honestly the only fault I can find with it.  Easy to unbox, setup and use. Completely foolproof and the whole family enjoy using it. It is sat in quite a sunny part of the room which meant we could often not see the old tv for the glare but the Hisense doesn’t seem to have that problem and although the sun will lighten the picture a little, it is still easy to watch. Highly recommend this tv.

I've had this TV for a few weeks now and really put it through its paces with Sport and animated Kids Movies in particular. I have to say...I'm really impressed with it. The 85-inch screen is absolutely massive and has completely changed how we've been watching sport and films at home. Watching football, rugby and the F1 on it feels more like being in a sports bar than sitting in the living room. The 4K picture quality is excellent with plenty of detail and really vibrant colours. Bright scenes look fantastic and the TV handles daytime viewing much better than my previous set. I spent some time testing the different picture modes and found Standard mode gave the most natural image. The AI upscaling works well with most content, although I personally found the picture looked best with some of the processing toned down...not sure why but you get a weird blur with some AI modes. Motion handling is generally very good, although on really fast-moving sports you can tell this isn't one of the higher refresh rate models. That's not a criticism as such, just something I noticed when comparing it to more expensive TVs. For everyday viewing it still looks excellent. The built-in subwoofer is probably what surprised me most. Sound is rich and punchy with enough bass that I haven't felt the need to add a soundbar yet. Dialogue is clear and films have much more depth than I expected from a TV speaker setup. Given this TV will be going in our media wall (when built) this is a massive bonus as we wont have to waste space with speakers. Setup was straightforward, the interface is responsive and apps load quickly.  Overall, if you're looking for a huge screen with great picture quality, strong built-in audio and excellent value for money, I think this TV is hard to beat.

body: The Hisense 50E7STUK 50-inch 4K QLED smart television is equipped with modern technology with incredible picture quality and good aesthetics. It offers a balance between affordability and premium features. It is designed to meet the needs of everyday viewers who value strong picture performance, intuitive smart features, and cinematic enhancements without the high price tag. I took my time writing this review to fully explore all the features first. One of the most notable aspects of this TV is the picture quality and brightness. It is important that I'm able to mirror the screen from my phone, and I'm glad I was able to do this seamlessly. The use of QLED technology allows the television to produce vibrant and rich colours, enhancing the overall viewing experience bringing scenes to life. The inclusion of Dolby Vision further elevates its performance by improving contrast and detail in HDR content, making movies and shows appear more dynamic and immersive. Even when displaying non-4K content, its upscaling capabilities ensure that images remain sharp and watchable, with an enhanced audio experience. Users seeking a more cinematic sound experience may benefit from pairing it with an external sound system or soundbar. Nevertheless, the inclusion of advanced audio formats at this price point demonstrates Hisense’s commitment to delivering value. I created an account on the VIDAA platform for additional viewing features. The interface is user-friendly and allows quick access to popular streaming services such as Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Disney+, YouTube and more. TV CHANNELS+, Freely Live TV, NOW and VOD are easily accessible on the remote. It is extremely easy to set up and lightweight, even though it looks bigger and not a slim TV. The only downside for me is that the TV stands are placed widely apart meaning the TV takes up much space when placed on a tabletop or TV stand. It's best to consider the measurements carefully before setup. This will not be an issue if mounting it on the wall. Also, I find the remote quite long which is unusual compared to other modern brands. The addition of a second remote for kids is absolutely brilliant, providing a safe and secure viewing mode for children of all ages.  Overall, this TV offers a perfect alternative viewing experience and I would highly recommend this brand to everyone.

body: I’ve been really impressed with the Hisense 55Q7STUK so far. The first thing that stands out is the design. It looks modern and premium, with an extremely narrow bezel that allows the screen to fill almost the entire front of the TV. This gives it a much more immersive feel when watching films, sports, or gaming, and it looks great mounted on a wall or sitting on a stand. The user interface is another strong point. Navigation between apps is quick and intuitive, and everything feels well organised. I particularly like how easily the TV connects to external speakers and audio devices. The setup process is straightforward, and switching between different inputs and streaming services is seamless, making everyday use hassle-free. Picture quality is very good, especially considering the price point. Colours are vibrant, detail is sharp, and content looks impressive across a range of viewing conditions. Even when the TV automatically switches into energy-saving mode, the picture remains bright and enjoyable, without a dramatic drop in quality. This is a nice balance between performance and efficiency. The only minor criticism I have is the plastic trim along the bottom of the screen. While it doesn’t detract from the overall appearance, it feels a little flimsy compared to the rest of the TV and doesn’t seem to secure the panel as firmly as I would have expected. It’s not a major issue, but it does stand out against an otherwise well-built product. Overall, the Hisense 55Q7STUK offers excellent value for money, combining stylish design, a user-friendly interface, and strong picture quality into a package that’s easy to recommend.

body:
The Hisense 65Q7STUK is a large good-looking television.  We as a family are looking for a television for family viewing, gaming, and streaming, and this television fulfilled all of these requirements perfectly.
The standout feature of this TV is the picture quality for both movies, sports and gaming.  The Hi-QLED panel produces a wonderful and accurate range of colours. It supports a huge range of HDR formats, including HDR10, 10+ adaptive and Dolby Vision IQ.  
Gaming has a Game Mode Plus feature, which has some good settings for tweaking, native panel is still 60hz refresh rate
Hisense has a proprietary VIDAA operating system which is constantly improving with updates.  This is my second Hisense TV, and the interface is fast, clean and highly intuitive.  All the APPS i need and supported and work very well with the TV.  There are some dedicated shortcut buttons on the remote control as well.
The TV also comes with Freely integration, which i think is excellent in the UK.  Effectively it allows the user to stream live UK television over Wifi using a unified TV guide!  No aerial or satellite dish needed.  Perfect and works well.
TV has a slim bezel, however for those that are not wall mounting - the feet and quite widely spaced out, this caught me out a little on my tv stand - the feet sit about 100cm apart.
Audio is good and handled by a standard two speak setup which support Dolby Atmos and DTS Virtual:X.
If you are looking for 65” superb family all-rounder television, this is the one.  Very excited that it has arrived in time for the Football World Cup 2026!

body:
I was mind blown by the amazingly vivid colours, it’s absolutely fantastic! I was captivated by the intensity of them when we watched Avatar,  it even looked 4D.  The sound quality is brilliant, really fills a large room, which we wondered about before we got it. We’ve a cinema sofa so expected we might use that, it was very easy to link the TV up to it, but, the TV made the sofa redundant as it’s sound quality is so good. It’s easy to set up and navigate through the different options available (and there are loads). 
My other half’s really impressed with how it automatically adjusts the screen to create a crisp, clean picture and how fluid motion is when watching sports. Voice control is great to have, makes life so much easier. He was also surprised and impressed with how the TV turns off, like curtains closing across the screen. A small thing but then it’s the little things that take you by surprise that leave a big impression as it shows attention to detail, which most definitely is the case when this TV was designed. 
The layout of the home page is so clear and easy to use, with all the channels and apps at your fingertips. The only regret is we didn’t get this TV sooner!"

body:
I’ve had the Hisense 65Q7STUK for a while now and overall I’m genuinely happy with it. The picture is the main reason: it looks punchy and sharp, colours pop without feeling cartoonish, and HDR movies/series look properly “cinema-like”. Motion is solid too — when I was watching NBA games, fast plays and camera pans stayed clear instead of turning into a blurry mess. For gaming it feels responsive, and the screen size works perfectly for a living room setup.
Sound is better than I expected for a flat TV, and for everyday watching it’s totally fine (a soundbar is still a bonus, but not a must). Setup was quick, menus are easy, and day-to-day use is straightforward. The only thing that occasionally annoys me is the built-in browser and the on-screen keyboard: sometimes there’s a noticeable delay after typing, like the TV reacts a few seconds later. It’s not a dealbreaker, and I’m hoping a firmware update will smooth that out. Overall: excellent TV for the money, and I’d still recommend it.
author: dm_stt

body:
I've been really pleased with my Hisense TV since getting it. As a busy mum with a house full of different viewing tastes, it gets used for everything from films and series to YouTube and gaming, and it's handled everything well.
The picture quality is excellent, with bright colours and a clear, sharp image. Watching sport and films on it has been particularly impressive, and the larger screen makes a real difference. The sound is also better than I expected without needing any extra speakers.
Setup was straightforward and I was able to get everything connected quickly. The smart features are easy to use, and switching between apps is simple, which is important when different family members are constantly wanting to watch different things.
Overall, it's been a great purchase and offers excellent value for money. It looks modern, performs well, and has become a big part of our day-to-day family entertainment. I would happily recommend a Hisense TV to friends and family.
author: emma61289

body: I have been testing the Hisense 43Q7STUK and my first impressions have been extremely positive. From unboxing to everyday use, the whole experience has been simple, smooth and enjoyable. The setup was incredibly easy. After wall-mounting the TV, I connected it to my Wi-Fi and followed the clear on-screen instructions. Within minutes, everything was ready to use. The tv is super light, it does come with feet for table mounting. The design is sleek and modern, with slim bezels and a discreet Hisense logo that allows the screen to take centre stage. Mounted on the wall, it sits flush and looks stylish and premium in my kitchen. Picture quality is excellent. Colours are vibrant, images are sharp, and the overall viewing experience feels immersive. Whether watching films, TV shows or sports, the screen delivers impressive clarity and detail. A real highlight is how easy it is to access streaming services. I connected Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV, Spotify, Netflix and Disney+ with ease, and everything runs smoothly. The TV also includes Freely, giving access to live and on-demand TV channels without the need for an aerial. There's the VIDAA app that allows you to use you phone as a remote control, amongst other things, which is a cool feature. I particularly like that the TV comes with two remote controls. There is a standard remote for everyday use and a cute white-and-blue remote designed specifically for children. The kids’ remote works alongside the parental control features, helping to restrict content and giving children safe, easy access to age-appropriate entertainment. Navigation is quick and intuitive, and switching between apps is seamless. Overall, the Hisense 43Q7STUK combines excellent picture quality, a stylish design, easy setup and thoughtful family-friendly features. It has exceeded my expectations and is a fantastic smart TV for both adults and children.
author: MumTwo

body: We’ve been using the 55” Hisense TV for a little while now and overall we’re really impressed with it.  The setup process was incredibly easy, pretty much plug in and follow the on-screen instructions and you’re away.  Connecting everything was straightforward too.  We hooked it up to our existing TV box and even our old-school DVD player, and both worked perfectly first time with no issues at all. The remote control is simple and easy to use, and navigating around the menus and apps is really smooth.  One feature we particularly liked was how easy it is to add and log into apps using QR codes on your phone, such a quick and hassle free process.  There’s also a huge range of apps available, definitely enough choice for anyone. The sound quality is surprisingly good for a flat screen TV, clear and more than powerful enough for everyday viewing. The TV itself looks sleek and modern sitting on our living room cabinet, even though it’s only in a temporary position until our media wall is built.  It's also surprisingly lightweight considering its size. The only small downside for me personally is that I haven’t quite managed to get the picture as vivid as I’d ideally like. I’ve tried adjusting the various settings including Cinema, Dynamic, contrast and sharpness, and while the picture is still very good, it’s just slightly less punchy than my own personal preference.  That said, this is very much subjective and won’t bother everyone. Overall though, this is a great value TV, easy to set up, easy to use, packed with features and apps, and looks great too. Very happy with it so far.

author: hyperpainter

body: I have been using the Hisense 55Q7STUK in my living room and overall I have been really impressed. The size is brilliant for the space and the TV looks premium, with thin bezels, a sturdy feel and a clean design that fits nicely into the room. Setup was simple and the smart TV experience has been one of the biggest highlights for me. The menus feel easy to use, apps are simple to navigate and connecting devices, including my console and Alexa, was straightforward. Picture quality is very good in many situations, especially films, TV shows and YouTube. Colours are bright and vibrant, the screen gets more than bright enough during the day and I have noticed very little glare. Gaming also feels responsive, with no noticeable input lag in my experience. There are a few areas where it is not perfect. Live sport has sometimes looked a little inconsistent in quality, although I am not sure whether this is the TV, the stream or my network. The black levels are also not the deepest and can look a little grey in darker scenes. Sound is better than I expected from built-in speakers, especially with dialogue enhancement, but it still will not replace a proper soundbar. Overall, I would definitely recommend it as a strong mid-range TV, especially if you want a good balance of picture quality, smart features and value.
author: kaithomson

body: The Hisense comes well packaged and is easy to get to by removing the outer sleeve rather than having to lift the TV out of the box. Fitting the stand was easy with 4 screws and the feet have protective pads for the surface the TV will stand on. Turning on for the first time there is an easy option using the Vidaa app and your smart phone if you already have a Hisense TV. The TV connects to your wireless through the Phone and then everything is done. Setting up the apps is easy with QR scanning and within 5 minutes had the TV setup with all the usual streaming services all setup. The picture quality is excellent with clear vibrant colours and crisp edges and things like football and films are nice and clear even though this is a big 65 inch screen it doesn't loose the image quality like some TVs do.  The sound of this TV is amazing and gives surround effect which in the large room it was located gives a really realistic effect. The menu system is simple and intuitive and to be fair it doesn't need much interaction of changing of things as default settings are good enough for me. A number of features like wake up on LAN or wake up when it detects you are awake are interesting but not really something I would need on this large model as it is not for the bedroom but for an outdoor cabin. The TV has Freely built in which works fine and saves the need for an aerial connection giving all the terrestrial stations and accessible via the guide. The remote has all the usual buttons and easy to use and automatically sets up when the TV turns on. it has a number of useful shortcuts too the standard streaming apps and Freely it is quite large which may not appeal to some people but didn't bother me. I really like this TV both for picture, sound and features and it is probably the best purchase I have made for a TV.

body:
My first impression of the Hisense TV was that it was surprisingly light to handle, with a sleek design and a good-quality finish and feel. I mounted it onto my wall bracket with no issues using the spacers provided, although I did have to purchase some M6 bolts.  The setup process was very simple and straightforward, with connection to the internet and linking the associated VIDAA app quick and easy.  Initially, I found the picture quality and colour settings weren’t quite right out of the box, but after switching around and trying Cinema mode, the picture looked much more natural and enjoyable. The built-in apps felt a bit like navigating a spider’s web at first, but they became easier to use with time, although the interface could still be simplified. Connecting the TV to my soundbar via optical was super easy. Syncing the sound to the picture took some doing but with the advanced settings I managed in the end. 
The sound quality wasn’t as crisp as I expected initially, but again the advanced settings are straightforward to adjust and I think there’s still room for further fine-tuning from me. But it’s very good! The sound from the TV speakers themselves is also very good.  For gaming, the picture quality is fantastic, with sharp visuals, movement and vibrant colours that really enhance the experience after setting to Sport settings. Again, the standard setting seemed a little flat. Overall, I’m very impressed with the quality and performance of the TV. I’m very happy with the purchase.

Better motion handling reduces blur during fast passes and camera movements. Quantum Dot colour is richer greens, blues, and skin tones. It delivers bright, punchy colours, sharp 4K detail, and smooth motion, which is exactly what I want for fast‑paced sports. body:
When this TV arrived, it couldn't have come at a better time as my old TV had finally given up. I've been using it for a while now and overall I'm really happy with it. Set up was very straightforward and I could log in to most apps from my phone, using QR codes. The picture quality is excellent, with bright colours and a clear, sharp display. The sound is surprisingly good too – I don't have to turn the volume up very high to hear everything clearly.
Having apps such as YouTube, Netflix and BBC iPlayer built in is super useful, and I've enjoyed browsing some of the internet-powered TV channels as well. It's nice having everything in one place rather than needing extra devices.
The TV itself is also much lighter than my previous TV, which made setting it up easier than expected. I find the 43-inch size ideal for my conservatory - not too big but also not too small. My only criticism is that navigating between the different menus can sometimes feel like a bit of a faff. Moving between Freely, live TV and streaming apps isn't always as straightforward as I'd like, and the remote takes a little getting used to. I was also initially confused by the subtitles button, which seems to actually be the mute button.  The only other issue I ran into was trying to register the warranty. I couldn't find my model listed on the Hisense website, which was a bit frustrating and left me unsure whether I'd completed the process correctly. Those are fairly minor complaints though. Overall, it's a great TV with excellent picture quality, good sound and plenty of viewing options, and I'd happily recommend it.

body: The Hisense Q7STUK 55" is a masterclass in combining high-end entertainment features with everyday practical usability, with its sleek, capable display, this model hits all the right marks. ​Stylish Aesthetics & Picture Brilliance  ​Straight out of the box, the TV commands attention with its stylish looks. Its ultra-slim bezels and premium stand offer a high-end, minimalist aesthetic that complements any modern interior. Turn it on, and the fabulous picture quality immediately takes center stage. Powered by advanced QLED technology, the display outputs incredibly vibrant colours and rich contrast. Whether you are watching a dark, moody thriller or a bright nature documentary, the screen pops with lifelike depth and absolute clarity.  ​Seamless Connectivity & Smart Navigation  ​Where this model truly shines is its painless integration with your entire media stack. Setting up external devices is effortless: ​other connectable media ntegrates seamlessly, passing through crisp 4K imagery. ​Digital gaming devices The TV acts as a perfect companion, unlocking smooth gaming performance, ultra-low input lag, and automatic optimizations via its dedicated Game Bar.  ​Navigating the system is remarkably fluid. The built-in Freely platform lets you stream live UK television without needing an aerial, stitching everything together beautifully. The interface is incredibly intuitive, making menu navigation completely stress-free. Furthermore, getting to your favorite streaming services is instant; dedicated one-touch buttons on the remote provide lightning-fast, straightforward access to loaded media and entertainment apps. ​Audio Performance  ​While thin displays usually compromise on audio, the Q7STUK defies expectations. Backed by Dolby Atmos processing, it delivers surprisingly great sound with clear dialogue and balanced bass, eliminating the immediate need for an external soundbar. body:
The Hisense 75-inch 75Q7STUK delivers a huge-screen cinema experience without the eye-watering price tag. Brilliant picture quality, smooth motion, intuitive smart features, and surprisingly good sound make it a joy to use. The only downside? Friends suddenly finding excuses to come round for movie night."
For gaming, it's equally impressive. The large 75-inch display creates a truly immersive experience, while responsive performance and smooth motion handling keep fast-paced action looking sharp and fluid. The sound is impressive straight out of the box, dialogue is clear, and sports fans will appreciate how smoothly fast-paced action is handled. body: So pleased we got to test this new Hisense TV.  My partner has been after a bigger screen for ages, so this was the perfect opportunity for him to get his wish.  We had a 55" and we chose the 75".  The screen looked huge to start with, but we have adjusted to it's size now.  We were impressed how easy it was to set up. It talks you through the whole process.  We are very impressed with the Freely option. We don't have an aerial connection in our living rooms, so this is great for us.  We noticed instantly on how bright and clear the picture is. The colours are so vivid! We watch a lot of football and this tv enables you to adjust the picture to avoid juddering. This tv has all the apps you could possibly need already downloaded - Netflix, BBC iPlayer, ITVX, 4, 5, Now TV, Disney+, Amazon Prime, HBO Max and Freely.  The sound quality is excellent too. body: I've been using the Hisense 65Q7STUK for two weeks now and I'm really impressed. It looks fantastic in my living room, with its slim profile and minimal bezel giving it a clean, modern look. Setting it up was straightforward. The stand feet need to be screwed in with a screwdriver, which only took a few minutes (but is a 2 person job - one to hold the TV while the other screws in). Batteries are included for the lightweight remote control. I downloaded the VIDAA app on my phone to handle the initial setup, and I'd strongly recommend doing this... It's so much easier typing passwords and search terms on your phone keyboard rather than fiddling with the onscreen keyboard. There's a wide range of apps preloaded (main reason I upgraded from my old TV was the lack of support for apps after 9 years!) The display really delivers on picture quality. I've been watching 4K and HDR content through various streaming services and the colours are vibrant and true to life. It performs fairly well in the day in a well lit room, there is a bit of reflection on the screen. Sound quality has genuinely surprised me. For built-in speakers, the output is rich and immersive. I won't need a soundbar. The Freely app is a great feature, delivering live TV channels over your internet connection without needing an aerial or satellite dish. I've connected mine via an ethernet cable for a stable connection. There are three HDMI ports... I've got a PC and a games console hooked up and still have one spare port. Overall, the Hisense 65Q7STUK is a brilliant TV that ticks all the boxes for picture quality, sound and smart features.

body:
I've been pleasantly surprised by the Hisense 55Q7STUK. The TV itself is impressively thin and lightweight, making it easy to mount and set up. The operating system is responsive and easy to navigate, with apps opening quickly and menus feeling snappy. There are quite a few apps pre-installed out of the box, but most can be removed if you prefer a cleaner home screen. Picture quality is very good for a mid-range TV, although it definitely benefits from spending a little time adjusting the picture settings. Once optimised, colours look natural and vibrant without appearing over-saturated or washed out. Contrast is solid and the overall viewing experience is excellent for films, sport and everyday TV. Sound from the built-in speakers is perfectly acceptable for casual viewing, but pairing it with a dedicated surround sound system makes a noticeable difference. I've connected mine to a Denon AVR and it works seamlessly. I haven't explored the AI features enough to give a fair assessment yet, but based on everything else, this feels like a well-rounded TV that offers strong performance for the price. 
Overall, I'd recommend it to anyone looking for a capable mid-range 55-inch TV without breaking the bank.
author: prit84

body: Just delighted with my New HiSense 75" TV.  UPgrading from an older OLED 65" set (6 years old), I wasn't sure what to expect from HiSense.  First thing we noticed was the weight difference - so much lighter than the old TV which made the seamless install nice and easy (but still a 2-person job). The difference in size was delightful - seems to be a slightly different ratio to the old set, but nice and slimline, so sits beautifully flush to the wall.  Set-up was sooo seamless and really quick.  Particularly impressed with Freely as a way to access terrestrial TV - makes everything HD without having to select the specific HD channels.  Not something I was expecting to be delighted by, but it is a very cool app.  When it was tuned in and ready to go, I was blown away by the picture quality.  Really sharp images and dealt really well with movement - whether in movies or sports.  Particularly looking forward to the World Cup matches now.  The scale of the picture obviously helps, but the sharpness and true blacks it was producing were what I would have expected on a TV twice as expensive as this!.  I paired the TV with a soundbar set-up from a different Brand ad half-expected issues with the compatibility, but I needen't have worried.  It took a bit of time to dig into the instruction manual to figure it out (could definitely have been clearer!), but once you get the relevant HDMI connector for the Arc set-up (it's #3 BTW) the sound came through beautifully.  What I would say is that the actual TV sound was really very good on its own - much better than my previous.  If not for the additional bellow of the sub-woofer, I wouldn't have noticed it wasn't connected to the sound bar!.  The part my kids love is when you switch the TV off and the closing motion is like the curtains closing in from the side at a theatre.  Very fun and distinctive!  Overall a very impressive TV.  I know I didn't go for the Pro version, but honestly I'm not sure how much better it could be than this. An absolute 5-star powerhouse to put on your wall and enjoy for years to come.

body: It's a very good value TV for the price, it also has composite inputs which I required, and all the usual apps and sockets including a satellite socket! But buyers need to understand two things about Freely: firstly there is no longer an option in the inputs menu for terrestrial TV only. Terrestrial channels (and maybe satellite too - I haven't tried) are all incorporated into the hybrid TV guide if not available from the internet, with no obvious indication whether they come from the aerial or the internet. This does of course mean that the channels that do come from the internet will be great HD quality and in many cases pausable and rewindable. Secondly you will have to sign in to the five main free TV channels because those ones will certainly come from the internet without the option. That's quite a process and means setup takes time. You could force it to be a terrestrial TV by starving it of an internet connection from the word go, but the moment you connect, Freely takes over.

body: After living with the Hisense 43Q7STUK for a few weeks, I can honestly say it has exceeded my expectations. I wasn’t looking for anything overly complicated, just a TV with a great picture and easy-to-use features, and it delivers on both. The first thing that stood out was how straightforward everything was. From taking it out of the box to getting it connected and ready to watch, the whole process was refreshingly simple. Within a short time I was signed into my streaming services and browsing through content without needing to dig through manuals or menus. The picture quality is easily the star of the show. Films, sports and everyday TV all look sharp and vibrant, with colours that really stand out without looking unnatural. Even during bright afternoons, when sunlight fills the room, the screen remains clear enough to enjoy without constantly adjusting blinds or curtains. One feature I didn’t expect to use was the children’s remote, but it’s actually a thoughtful addition. It’s simple, colourful and gives younger viewers an easy way to access suitable content, which I can imagine being a real bonus for families. The smart TV interface is well laid out and includes all the apps I regularly use, meaning I’ve been able to retire my streaming stick completely. The dedicated app buttons on the remote are handy too, making it quick to jump straight into whatever I want to watch. There is occasionally a slight delay when navigating menus, but it’s minor and hasn’t affected my overall experience. Considering everything else the TV offers, it’s a small compromise. Overall, this TV feels like a fantastic all-round package. It looks stylish, performs brilliantly and is simple enough for everyone in the household to use. If you’re upgrading from an older set, you’ll definitely notice the difference.

body: I have had this tv a few weeks now.  Delivery and set up was surprisingly easy. The box is designed so you dont have to lift it up, it opens round the TV. Once on, we used wider settings its very stable even on our temporary table as we plan a media wall to give this great tv its max effect.  Setting up took a couple of mins and was all done, very easy to follow steps. Its compatibility to link with home features makes it more impressive. It was super easy to sign in to our subscriptions we have.  First impressions when we got it set up were wow... the sound is great, clear and well projected round the room we have. The app feature is great, can turn off when the children forget too.  We have also tried a console on it and wow its made that really fun to play. body: Having previously owned a Hisense TV, I was curious to see how much they have improved over the years - and boy was I impressed! Starting with initial set-up. Very easy to use and get started. A QR code allowed access to the app to help set-up go smoothly and I was up and running within a few minutes. The user interface is very easy to use and intuitive to find your way about. Using the smart on demand features, finding apps, setting up your sound and pictures preferences - all very easy to utilise. The picture quality is superb - colours are rich and vibrant, blacks are clear and the auto adjustment features on the TV are great to ensure maximum quality when viewing darker movies. I particularly like the function where it automatically senses if a movie you are watching has Filmaker mode and it automatically switches to this to enhance your viewing.  The AI motion adjustments are great too - avoiding the motion blur effects you get with some TVs. This is particularly great when gaming - smooth motions and movements making it great to play on. Sound is very good too - a massive upgrade on previous Hisense models.  The remote is very easy to use and a good size - feels nice in your hands and the quick access to the most popular streaming apps makes for seamless switching between what your watching. Overall I am very impressed with this TV. It's an excellent choice for someone looking for a great quality TV for their living room or bedroom - great for movies, shows, streaming and gaming - all round, I highly recommend this TV.  5 Stars!
author: Derek1graham

body:
I've previously had Hisense TVs so you would think I knew what I was in for — Wrong! I expected minor improvements but I was very pleased with what I saw. Let's go through some of the specs that matter and made a difference to my experience: - VIDAA smart platform — THIS IS THE ONE THAT REALLY SOLD ME THIS TV. VIDAA is a lightweight Linux-based smart TV platform. What this means to us is that you can launch apps like Netflix or YouTube really fast and smooth, adding to the overall experience. No more wondering what the hell happened to the app you just started — it's just there, instantly. - Hi-QLED with Quantum Dot colour — The screen is brighter and richer than my previous TV, which was already quite impressive. Colours feel more true-to-life and punchy without looking over-saturated. A genuine step up. - 144Hz panel — I don't think this made as much difference to me personally as it did to my 9-year-old son. The feedback is that gaming is smoother and more pleasant. WIN! There are other gaming features too — Game Mode Pro and the updated Game Bar give gamers quick access to VRR, frame rate counters, and input lag settings. Proper stuff. - All the HDR modes — This bad boy supports HDR10+, HDR10+ Gaming, Dolby Vision, Dolby Vision IQ, and HLG — essentially covering every format you're likely to encounter. You're not going to hit a wall with this one. - Hi-View AI Engine (MediaTek Pentonic 700 chip) — Enables enhancements such as AI Picture, AI Light Sensor, AI 4K Upscaling, AI Detail Enhancement, AI HDR Enhancement, and AI Smooth Motion. Basically you're fully "AI'd" up - Filmmaker Mode — Preserves the director's original frame rates and colour intent without any motion processing applied. If you're a film lover, this one matters more than you'd think. The only thing that's potentially not the best is the sound quality. It's OK but not exactly hi-fi, and let's be honest — at this price point you wouldn't expect it to be either. So this review still retains 5 stars. The remote is well laid out with shortcut buttons for all the major apps. It's also Bluetooth, so you don't even have to point it at the TV — which feels delightfully lazy. Ha!
I love this TV so much that I've actually set it up as a second computer monitor. Check out the picture. Overall, I would thoroughly recommend this TV.
