body: From the moment I received this 43” TV, I was pleasantly surprised by how lightweight it was; it almost felt deceptive given its size. Unboxing was straightforward, and installing the pedestal feet was simple and stress-free. The protective cardboard over the screen was a thoughtful touch, making setup much easier without worrying about accidental damage. Although I plan to wall mount it later, the initial setup was smooth and user-friendly. Powering on the TV and setting it up via the VIDAA app was effortless. Downloading the app and connecting it to the TV was quick, and the mobile setup process worked seamlessly. The WiFi connection is strong, allowing the smart interface to run smoothly and making navigation intuitive and easy to use. One of the standout features is Freely, which removes the need for a traditional TV aerial. This is incredibly convenient, simplifying installation and eliminating the hassle of running additional cables or installing an aerial point. In terms of picture and sound quality, both are excellent. The display delivers vibrant, sharp visuals across all types of genres of programs. Sports, in particular, look fantastic; fast-moving scenes are clear, bright, and easy on the eyes, which is perfect for watching events like the World Cup. The sound is also impressive, offering clear and balanced audio across volume levels. While a surround sound system would enhance bass performance, the built-in speakers are more than sufficient for a bedroom setup. If I had one suggestion, it would be to make the feet more centrally positioned. This would provide greater flexibility when placing the TV on different types of furniture. That said, it currently fits on my chest of drawers, though this is only temporary as I intend to mount it on the wall. Overall, this is a great TV with a simple and intuitive navigation system, excellent picture quality and strong, clear audio performance. I had heard of the brand before but never considered purchasing; something I now see was a mistake. This TV proves they can compete with more established brands, especially when considering the excellent value for money."

body:
I don't know where to begin for reviewing my new MASSIVE 85" Hisense TV 85E78STUK PRO. I'm actually even more impressed with it than I was expecting.
The TV it's replacing was a decent 65" TV, so was only expecting a small improvement in the picture and sound quality, and got to admit the thought had crossed my mind that because of the 20" size difference, whatever increase in picture quality with the new telly, would be lost in this increase in size. I was wrong, the sharpness for a start, is much better, as are the depths and vibrancy of colours, proper black blacks, even in a darkened room. The Tv automatically upscales standard signal to 4K. I have not altered the colours in any way, I'm extremely happy with the way they are out of the box so to speak. For the technical it boasts Quantum Dot Colour and Dolby Vision IQ. You do have preset options, like cinema, game mode, sport etc. which again I have not needed to change, although I have used the sport mode to watch football. I was showing the TV off to (jealous) friends though. Same as picture options, there are preset sound options. I've tried the music and cinema sound modes, as with picture modes, there are more options, but can't remember them all. With the sound, I did increase the bass on the graphic equaliser as I like a lot of oomph. For the technically minded it boasts 2 x 15W + 20W speakers and has eARK audio via HDMI. Again for the technical the TV boasts Dolby Atmos and DTS Virtual X decoding for immersive sound. There are plenty of connection options e.g. several HDMI's USB etc., which I won't go into as the specs are on all the sales and Hisense websites. Setting up was simple, from initial setup, to connecting to Wi-Fi. I'd say most apps what you need are pre-installed like Netflix etc. I can't comment on the installed apps as I don't have Netflix account, I almost exclusively use Sky on my TV, which this TV compliments amazingly, the Sky remote pairs easily with the TV, for automatic turning the TV on and off. One slight downside (if you can call it that) I've noticed is you need to check the little white standby light on the bottom of the TV illuminates when turning off, as you can't tell it has gone into a standby state because of the darkness of the black colour. The TV has built in Freely for viewing live TV. This seems good, although only used very briefly when first setting the TV up with using Sky. The TV remote has built in voice control, enabling use of the built in Alexa for example. Can't comment on the use of that as I have Alexa in the room already set up and don't want them fighting over each other. I was pleased to find out this TV only weighs just over 32kg (85" without stand) which is a lot lighter than my previous 65" TV. I must also point out, I measured my chimney breast wall incorrectly when measuring up for the wall bracket/mount and the TV is bigger than my original measurements, so I need to move the wall bracket before I can mount it. I thought, oh no, I've made a terrible mistake, the TV is far too big for the room when I first started viewing, BUT I have quickly become used to the size. So be brave and order the biggest you can fit in your room, you won't regret it.
In a nutshell this TV gets a thumbs up for me, I absolutely love it and don't have one regret in purchasing it. From delivery in its extremely sturdy box, to sitting watching a movie, it has brought an enormous smile to my face. Can't wait till I can get it on the wall. I might then, find even more amazing features that I have probably missed. I haven't mentioned the value for money is also excellent, getting more to the £ than most other manufacturers. I hadn't taken much notice of the brand Hisense until a couple of years ago if I'm honest. Then I looked into their side by side fridge freezers, I was impressed with the build quality, innovation and price. When this TV came on the market and I had a chance of purchasing, I had no qualms on buying Hisense. As in my review, from packaging to use of the item, it's all first class, competition for the best

body:
​"I just got this colossal 85-inch Hisense PRO QLED set up on my dining table for an initial test, and I am already in love. My first experience with this TV has been fantastic.
​Right out of the box, the first thing you notice is, of course, the size. It is huge! An 85-inch screen completely transforms a space. Perfect for hosting the upcoming world cup! We had to temporarily place it on our large dining table to get it unboxed and turned on, but it makes an incredible first impression.
​After a straightforward setup, the QLED picture quality is really good! The colors are incredibly vibrant and the contrast is impressive for an initial test. I mainly bought this for gaming, and i can't wait to test this connected up to my PS5. The channels and streaming apps are great with everything you need. 
It’s clearly built for a serious home cinema wall which is pending as we get our renovations done. My initial test gives me full confidence in my purchase. This TV is an absolute showstopper for anyone looking to go big. I will be recommending to my friends and family! 10/10
author: MileyT

body:
Having had 3 weeks with this TV, I have found the picture and sound quality to be excellent. The high refresh rate is uncommon at this size so great to have in the size I needed. Sound quality is impressive for a TV of this size providing decent bass and clear vocals. The DSP audio modes are great. Freely works well, and there's a wide range of additional streaming channels and most streaming apps are available. 
Voice search is available using the microphone in the remote and this works well. It's a great TV, easy to navigate, great picture, great sound. There are a couple of negatives, though. Vidaa has pretty good app availability, but there's no Emby client available, although Plex is present. The remote is massively over-sensitive with the buttons having very little resistance before engaging. The 9 app-specific launcher buttons may be useful for some, but it feels like they're taking up far too much space on the remote. Overall it's a great TV, and I'd recommend it to anyone looking for a TV of this size - if they can live with the remote.

body:
I was very excited when my Hisense 75E7STUK PRO was delivered... having used the same TV  for over 6 years, it was time for an upgrade! First impressions arrived before it was even switched on, it's so much lighter than my previous set, long gone are the days 2 people struggled to pick up the TV, this was light and very easy to move into position. Then it was time for the setup, you use the Vidaa app to setup the TV and this made it much easier than having to type in Wi-Fi details with your remote... setup connects you to the internet, sets everything up and you're good to go... anyone could do this. Once setup I was shocked just how many apps and channels you could receive without even connecting an aerial... Freely works great and let me watch shows I hadn't even considered watching.
One item I hadn't considered was just how quick the TV is to use, apps load so fast I no longer have time to get a drink before it's ready to watch! Picture quality is great, colours are vibrant and sound was surprisingly good for such small TV speakers. We placed the TV in a very light heavy room and the brightness of the tv is more than enough to punch through, there's only a slight light bleed on very dark pictures. I haven't had a chance to really push the TV to it's limits on gaming but gaming on the Switch was flawless. All in, very happy and would recommend this TV.
author: Mabbs

body:
My first impression of the Hisense 75E7STUK – It’s BIG, fast, and surprisingly good! For both the picture and sound it is very good value for money.
The good - Stunning picture quality for the money. Replacing my 55 inch OLED I was worried that the picture would not hold up. Overall, I had nothing to be concern about! It’s clean, and responsive. Gaming (I’m a PS5 gamer) is great. The Game mode kicks in and supports variable refresh rate, Auto Low Latency Mode etc making it a pleasure to use. Even at close range (couple of meters away) it looks good. 
The sound is balanced and the built-in subwoofers provides surprisingly robust audio, way better than the TV it’s replacing. I have a soundbar/sub but haven’t plugged it in as I’m not sure it’s needed! Likewise, the OS works very well, with fast access to apps. The Freely tuner is also very good, making it much easier to watch programmes without changes between the on demand apps i.e. it lets you watch live TV over Wi-Fi without needing an aerial, and it just works. I’ve also found the supporting mobile app really good and allows use of the TV without the remote. 
The less good - Contrast in low light. Being a QLED, the black levels and local dimming cannot match the blacks of my older OLED and you can see the backlighting “Leak” from the edges where the picture on the TV is dark. 
To conclude - Value for Money! - Massive 75" screen, that’s great for gaming, a surprisingly good sound, and great tech makes it a no brainer for the price.

body: The Hisense 65E7STUK PRO delivers a genuinely impressive viewing experience for its price point. The picture quality is crisp and clear, with strong colour accuracy and sharp detail that really stands out whether you’re watching films, sports, or gaming. Motion handling is very responsive, and the 144Hz Game Mode Pro makes fast‑paced content feel smooth and immediate. The app store is decent, covering all the essentials without feeling bloated. VIDAA is straightforward to navigate, and the TV gives you a good amount of user modifiability — from picture presets to advanced calibration controls, it’s easy to tune the display exactly how you like it. Audio is the one area where the TV shows its mid‑range positioning. The speakers are perfectly usable once you spend a few minutes adjusting the equaliser, and they can sound reasonably balanced after tuning. However, they’re not on the same level as the mid‑range speakers you’d find on competing brands, especially when it comes to depth and fullness. A soundbar will noticeably elevate the experience. Overall, the E7STUK PRO is a strong performer with excellent picture quality, fast responsiveness, and a flexible user experience

body: Out of the box, the Hisense 50E7STUK PRO TV feels well made, and I was surprised by how light it is, useful for wall mounting. The remote control is easy to use, with buttons well laid out and dedicated buttons for all the major streaming services. Setup was very easy with no TV aerial connection needed. You just plug in the power cable and you’re ready to watch content. Speaking of content, this is the first TV I’ve used with Freely, and I was impressed with the service. There is a couple of seconds delay between switching channels, which takes some getting used to. But the Freely interface, TV guide, and navigation are excellent. After adjusting the picture settings, the quality is very good, with accurate colors and sharp details. The standard settings felt very bright, 100% backlight washed out blacks and made highlights too white. I found Cinema picture mode a good starting point, reducing the backlight to 75, brightness to 45, contrast to 70, color saturation to 60, and sharpness to 0. For my room and lighting, this produced the best results. The TV performs well across all types of content, from regular TV shows and movies to fast-action sports. The sound quality is good for a flat panel TV. I didn’t notice a significant improvement with Dolby Atmos, maybe I would with a compatible external speaker system. Our current amplifier and speakers connect to the TV via HDMI ARC, but the Hisense TV supports HDMI eARC. I need to upgrade our amplifier to use our existing speaker setup.  We connected a FreeSat box via HDMI, switching to this input, the sound was much quieter, we had to increase the volume to compensate. This caused an issue, because switching back to Freely the volume was now too loud. Turning on the auto volume control setting which prevents sudden volume changes when switching inputs, didn’t help. Maybe if’s a compatibility problem but now we have Freely built-in, we probably don’t need FreeSat anymore. Aside from the volume issue, the TV is a pleasure to use. The interface is well laid out, and very responsive. You can organise the home screen moving quicklinks for your favorite services around. Download new apps and mini-games. The games are fun and easy to play, but the ads are frustrating. The built-in screen sharing works seamlessly, letting you wirelessly share your mobile screen. It’s great for quickly playing videos, sharing photos, and more with others.

body: The standout feature of this TV is the display. Whether I’m watching freeview in SD or streaming in 4K, the quality and watching experience cannot be faulted.  That's the  most important thing right? I sit side on to the screen, my seat is at a 45 degree angle to the screen and the matte screen means that the reflection is minimal. I connected a high end sound bar/sub and it works perfectly.  The sound, albeit an external speaker, is flawless.  I have the option to make lip sync adjustments but I didn't need to.   The added bonus is that via ARC I could access the sound bar’s interface using the Hisense remote. The only issue is that I still need a separate remote to control the volume.  In terms of interactivity, the most important factor for me is lag.  A few milliseconds delay in response to the remote would degrade the user experience.  But the Hisense is instant; it helps that the menu items are logically organised - think Mrs Doubtfire navigating Miranda’s kitchen with ease - “everything is so logical and practical”.  The remote itself has shortcut buttons to the popular streaming services, and to freeview.  A couple of nice touches from the remote include the find me option, if you lose the remote you can just press a button on the TV and it makes the remote beep.  Also, it doesn’t take batteries, it’s got a solar panel that works from your internal light bulbs.  So you never need to change the batteries and you can’t lose it!   Initially I set the TV up without the frame, as I prefer a minimalist look.  But using the TV in art mode is really enhanced by the “picture frame” that comes included.  I had some family over that haven’t been to my home for a few months, so I left the TV in VIDAA Art Mode and they genuinely thought it was a hanging painting.  They only knew it wasn’t actual art when the image changed from Monet’s Water Lilies to Van Gogh’s Starry Night. The problem I have is that people keep going up to it and touching the screen to see if it’s real. So if cleaning curious fingerprints is the only downside to this TV, I'm happy with that! One final comment: it's lightening fast to turn on.

body:
The idea of a TV so lovely you won't turn it off is pretty innovative. From unboxing, though the set up and operating, the whole process was easy and well thought out. Each part is labelled with clear instructions how to put everything together, so I was quickly up and running. 

The app worked well, and getting the channels set up was very simple. There’s more than enough inputs for adding external devices like consoles, Blu-ray players and hard drive devices if you want to store/access other media.

To show this TV off to its fullest, it's designed to be hung on the wall like a picture frame (wall mount is provided), however initially I set it up on the stand (also provided) to check the features. It's much lighter in weight than my previous TV (so I was able to lift and install without needing another person to help), but this doesn't mean they have skimped on the build or picture quality. The colours are vibrant, with lots of sound and picture settings to suit the occasion (film, sports, speech etc). 

The detachable wooden frame sets the screen off perfectly, and can be removed/changed to suit your room decoration, and the matt screen eliminated the glare you get when the sun hits the screen , so you don’t have to hide your TV away in a dark corner of the room. 

As expected with such a slim TV, you don't get a really loud base rumble on this set, however, coupling with a sound-bar or surround speakers really creates a home cinema feel. The high picture resolution enables the painting to look totally realistic when looking at the TV in 'art' mode. 

I really liked the fact that loads of free digital channels are already included, with the option of easily adding more apps via the menu options, or using voice activated commands.

I’m not familiar with the brand HiSense, but if this is typical of the quality of their tech, I’ll certainly be looking to purchase their products in future.

I recently purchased the Hisense 50U7STUK, initially intending to use it as a bedroom TV. After spending some time with it, I can confidently say it’s a genuinely good product that delivers incredible value for the money, though it definitely brings a "large room TV" energy to a smaller space.
Here is my breakdown of what makes this TV stand out, along with a couple of tips if you plan on setting it up yourself.
### The Screen & Picture Quality
The screen on this TV is absolutely fantastic. Because it uses Mini-LED technology, the contrast is superb. * **Rich Colours:** The Quantum Dot (QLED) tech really shows here. The colors are incredibly vibrant and punchy, making everything from movies to games look incredibly rich and lifelike. * **Very Bright:** This panel gets *seriously* bright. It handles HDR content beautifully and easily fights off daytime glare. However, because it gets so bright, it can almost feel a bit overwhelming in a pitch-black bedroom at night! You might find yourself turning the backlight down before going to sleep.
### Interface & Features
Hisense packs a lot into this model. It comes loaded with features, including support for Dolby Vision, Dolby Atmos, and high refresh rates (144Hz) if you are into gaming.
Despite the mountain of features, the smart interface (VIDAA) is surprisingly snappy and reasonably easy to navigate. It doesn't lag or stutter, and finding my favorite streaming apps was straightforward and intuitive.
### A Note on Wall Mounting (Read Before You Install!)
If you are planning to put this on the wall, **make sure you get the correct screws.** The TV requires specific VESA mounting screws (often M6), and the standard ones that come bundled in generic wall-mount kits might not be the exact length you need. Do yourself a favor and check the TV's manual for the exact screw depth required before you start drilling, or you'll be making an unexpected trip to the hardware store mid-installation.
### The Verdict
I bought this for the bedroom, but honestly, it performs like a premium main-room TV. Between the incredibly bright Mini-LED panel, the rich colors, and the sheer amount of features, it punches well above its weight. Just be prepared for a cinematic, large-room experience right at the foot of your bed—and double-check your wall bracket hardware before you start! Highly recommended."

body: Before you buy this TV, double-check your wall mount! It requires a specific 400 x 300 bracket. I wrongly assumed my old equal-hole bracket would work and had to learn the hard way. Once it is up, the build quality is impressive for a mid-range set. The ultra-thin bezel gives it a premium, modern look that looks well in the room. The initial setup is very user-friendly too. The VIDAA app prompts you through the Wi-Fi connection process in just a few simple steps, and you are up and running in no time. The software is where this TV really shines. The operating system feels exceptionally snappy and responsive. The TV features two full-bandwidth HDMI 2.1 inputs that fully support a 4K resolution at a smooth 144Hz refresh rate.  You will want to spend a few minutes adjusting the picture settings out of the box. Initially, the factory colours looked a bit oversaturated, and I noticed some slight backlight clouding during darker scenes. Luckily, switching the TV straight into Filmmaker Mode instantly balanced the contrast and helped with the issue. The biggest surprise by far is the audio quality. The built-in 2.1-channel speaker system delivers deep bass and clear dialogue. It packs enough of a punch that you might not even need to buy a separate soundbar.  I don't think I will need one. Overall, this is an impressive TV at this level.

Picture quality is equally strong. Straight out of the box it looks good, but with a little fine‑tuning initially the tv is really bright in light controlled room so I turned that down slightly the colours become natural and vibrant without drifting into oversaturation. Contrast is solid, motion is smooth, and Dolby Vision support gives films a noticeable boost. Whether you’re watching live sport or streaming your favourite series, the overall viewing experience feels consistently high‑quality.
Ease of use is another highlight. The TV is thin, lightweight, and simple to set up, with clear instructions and a responsive operating system that makes navigating apps and menus easy. Everything loads quickly, and although there are plenty of pre‑installed apps, you can remove what you don’t need to keep things tidy. The Freely app meansyou can stream live TV without needing an aerial as long as you’re connected to Wi‑Fi.
After spending some time with it, this feels like a well‑rounded, easy‑to‑use TV that offers excellent performance for the price — especially if you want great sound without adding a soundbar.

The built in remote is also quite comfortable and its bluetooth, so I do not need to point it at the TV to control it. Straight out of the box, the build quality feels robust, and the nearly borderless, slim bezel gives it an elegant presence in my living room without looking overly bulky. Fast-moving sports and action sequences stay crisp without nasty motion blur, this will be great to watch FiFa World Cup 2026. Navigating the VIDAA smart platform is swift and straightforward. Apps load almost instantly, and switching inputs is snappy. The integrated voice control responds well to natural commands, making hands-free searches simple. The remote control feels functional, though its layout takes a brief period to get used to. Acoustically, the built-in sound system supports Dolby Atmos and delivers clear dialogue along with a noticeable punch of bass, which is rare for standard built-in TV speakers. While the audio is great for daily viewing, adding an external soundbar could enhance the deepest cinema low-ends even further.  Ultimately, this display has massively upgraded my home entertainment setup, merging bright performance with serious gaming power.
author: localhost

body: After getting the Hisense 55U7STUK unboxed and mounted on the wall right above my desk, I am incredibly impressed with how it performs as a primary display. At fifty-five inches, the 4K picture quality is incredibly sharp. Because I sit relatively close to the screen at my workstation, the high pixel density makes a massive difference, allowing me to read small text, fine details, and complex instrument dials without any blurring. ​The Mini-LED backlighting is definitely the standout feature for me. The contrast is brilliant, delivering deep, true blacks that make dark or nighttime scenes feel completely immersive. There is no annoying backlight bleed, and the screen gets bright enough to easily handle room reflections during the day. ​What really seals the deal for gaming and fast-paced simulation is the native 144Hz refresh rate. Fast movement is fluid and completely stable, completely eliminating the motion blur I used to get on slower screens. The AI upscaling also does a fantastic job keeping older content looking crisp. On top of the visuals, the built-in subwoofer and audio system offer surprisingly rich, balanced sound right out of the box. It has truly transformed my desktop environment.
author: JayG33

body: I had the opportunity to test the 55U7STUK TV. This is a big step up in picture quality, the TV features the latest MiniLED backlighting technology. This greatly improves lighting control, enhances the contrast, giving the most natural picture possible. It has a powerful processor for detailed blur-free images and you get the optimal contrast levels whatever the time of day and from whichever signal input. The new AI Smooth Motion and AI Sports mode technology makes this TV great for sports and movies as the processing smooths the picture flow. Filmmaker Mode lets you experience the cinematic vision, by using the correct aspect ratio, colour and frame rate.  Game Mode reduces input lag, ensuring quicker reaction times. It's fitted with a built-in subwoofer,  for a deeper bass response and smoother immersive sound. It has the latest Freely TV system with the options of live TV channels and catch-up content. Freely also allows you to ‘pause’ live TV as well as restarting programmes on certain channels. This new service enables the use of just an Internet connection so there is no need for an aerial or satellite dish There’s also one-touch, direct access to the most popular apps - Netflix, Disney+, Amazon Prime etc. It seems the possibilities are endless on this TV and personally I have only just started exploring them all.  What I can say to sum it up is that it is a great way to get a truly cinematic experience in your own living room and it's a gamers dream.

body: Fantastic TV - Quick and easy set up followed by exceptional quality This quality comes in the form of amazingly crisp image for all types of viewing, whether that is film, TV shows or Youtube videos. With particularly bassy shows I sometimes stopped it as I thought that the sound was coming from somewhere else! I particularly love the screen mirroring as it allowed me to show pictures and videos from my camera roll on the big screen without there being a drop in quality over the air. The 50 inch screen also fit perfectly where we wanted it and it has a almost existent bezzle and central stand. This meant we didn't have to change our set up at all. Overall it has been 10/10 - haven't watched so much TV in my life! Would definitely recommend to a friend (and already have!)

body: The Hisense 85U7STUK television made a strong first impression. The design is impressive with a large screen housed in a slim profile. Once installed, the picture is exceptionally crisp and clear with vibrant colours. The Dolby Vision technology produces deep blacks that enhance the colour saturation. The sound quality is also superior to any television I have owned previously. Developed in conjunction with Devialet, it provides a better sound experience for users without an additional soundbar. While the hardware is impressive, the installed software has been somewhat disappointing. The Freely interface is novel and differs from my previous digital television experience. The combination of channels supplied via the aerial and over Wi-Fi is a promising development for the future of television broadcast. The television is capable of processing Dolby Atmos and Dolby Vision but most available apps and installed software only offer basic variations that do not utilise these features. It is surprising that the latest sound and vision technology is provided in the hardware but not accessible through the software.

You can also adjust the speed of this which is nice, only problem is my grandson wants to keep turning the TV on and off. It has 4 HDMI sockets so should be good for most people. The remote is nice and easy to use and will also operate the firestick and its functions which is handy. The operating system does sometimes suffer from some slight lag but it is not a frequent or major problem. The WIFI connection speed is good so hopefully no problems there going forward. body:
The HISENSE 55U7NQTUK 55 Smart 4K Ultra HD HDR Mini LED TV offers everything I wanted at a lower price than LG, Samsung, and Sony. It supports 120 Hz refresh rates and HDR10+, ideal for PS5 gaming, with an easy-to-access gaming menu that activates AMD FreeSync and displays settings for various genres of video game i.e. FPS, RTS, RPG, Sport. 

While it has a specific mode for Black Myth: Wukong, I can’t assess its quality since I don’t own the game. The FPS monitor doesn't sync accurately with visual frame rates, but this could be how I am using it with the PS5, it may work better with a PC setup. The HDR10, HDR10+, and Dolby Vision provide great picture quality, but I had to adjust the settings to my liking. Apple TV and Prime Video support Dolby Vision, enhancing the viewing experience, especially with the smooth frame setting for better motion in animations.

The Freely App enables live TV, which I use for sports on BBC and ITV due to its better output quality, nevertheless, standard apps like iPlayer and ITVX are available to download. The remote is user-friendly, with quick access to Netflix, Disney+, YouTube and Prime, plus the convenience of solar charging and USB-C compatibility. It also controls the PS5 menu and Fire TV, although it recently stopped working with the Fire Stick, likely due to the Fire settings, not the TV.

Overall, I’m very pleased with this purchase, as it enhances my gaming and 4K HDR viewing experience while offering plenty of customizable settings. The 4 HDMI ports are also welcomed, although only 2 of them support the higher frame rates for gaming, which should be sufficient.

body:
This TV is a great value option. It has very good brightness, colours and clarity. Out of the box the picture settings aren't the best for accurate colours but its not difficult to adjust the settings to get it how you want it. It has a lot of local dimming zones for the backlight which makes the blacks look darker, not as good as OLED but for the price can't complain. The model I got uses a VA panel which usually have really good contract levels and colours that pop more if you like turning saturation up a lot (I don't)

It comes with a lot of streaming apps pre-installed. Hisense's OS is pretty easy to navigate and I haven't noticed any serious slowdowns or lag yet.

There is HDMI eARC for those that want to hook up their own AV receiver for speakers and it works very well. The TV recognises immediately when you have an ARC device connected and will switch the audio output to that automatically

The built in speakers are actually decent compared to other TVs I've heard. Not as good as standalone home theatre speakers but it's got good clarity, has some type of woofer which adds more depth with the bass. Overall an ok speaker

body:
Review of the Hisense 55U7NQTUK TV

Thanks to Feefo and Hisense for giving me the opportunity to review the Hisense 55U7NQTUK TV. It’s an excellent TV with a lot to offer. Here’s my take:

- Setup and Usability:
Setting up the Hisense 55U7NQTUK was super easy. As soon as I switched it on, I was taken straight to the home screen, which was a nice touch. Even assembling the stand was a breeze, and I'm not particularly DIY savvy.

- Performance:
The TV is incredibly fast and responsive. The remote works seamlessly, and there are no annoying loading screens. It's like using a high-end computer. Navigating through apps is simple too, with everything accessible right from the remote.

- Screen Mirroring and Connectivity:
I did encounter a couple of issues with screen mirroring. I couldn’t mirror my phone when using a VPN, and sometimes, when watching movies, the playback would get choppy for 5-6 seconds. However, this choppy mirroring issue is common with many TVs to varying degrees.

- Gaming Modes: 
The TV offers different modes for gaming, enhancing the overall gaming experience. 

- Sound Quality: 
The sound quality is really good, providing clear and immersive audio. - 

- Ease of Use:
Because of its simplicity and ease of use, my elderly parents could navigate through YouTube and other apps easily. The added bonus of voice control, which they got used to from using YouTube on an iPhone, makes it even more user-friendly. As I'm tech savvy I'm usually the one navigating and fixing tech issues like the WiFi etc for my parents, so if this sounds like you too the simplicity is a massive win!

- Temperature and Overall Recommendation:
Even after many hours of use, the TV's temperature remained normal, which is impressive and speaks to its quality. Despite the minor hiccups with mirroring, I’m really impressed with the Hisense 55U7NQTUK. The size, speed, ease of setup, and overall simplicity make it a fantastic choice, If you’re in the market for a new TV, this one is definitely worth considering.

Thanks again to Feefo and Hisense for the opportunity to review this excellent TV. Please don't hesitate to reach out again!

body:
This product is a definite must-buy. You'd end up paying twice the price for another brand offering the same level of quality.
Local dimming works wonders across all TV program genres, especially noticeable during scene transitions to black and the contrast on credits and titles. The TV can reach impressive brightness levels, which is a boon in well-lit rooms. However, in complete darkness, the effect is akin to being in a theater. Occasionally, there's a slight lag in brightness adjustment after a scene change, but this is rare.
Gaming performance is top-notch. I've had no issues playing at 120Hz with audio output through the TV. While my Nvidia graphics card doesn't support over 120Hz via HDMI, gaming at 144Hz would require a display port to HDMI adapter. I've experienced occasional frame drops and screen blackouts, but I'm unsure if this is due to the TV or my HDMI cable. Overall, gaming experience is excellent, with no noticeable latency.
Connecting other devices like sound systems and streaming boxes was hassle-free. Everything worked seamlessly upon setup.
Regarding HDR, there's a bit of uncertainty. SDR content often looks better than HDR, with Dolby Vision on Netflix appearing washed out. However, BBC iPlayer shows in HDR HLG are stunning, making it feel like the animals are in the room. Personal HLG content via Plex also looks good, suggesting the TV may struggle with certain HDR formats.
Surprisingly, the TV does an impressive job of sharpening highly-compressed content, such as streamed shows. For instance, even though "Trigger Point" is only 1080p on ITVx, the quality is noticeably better via the app compared to the sky box.
Additionally:
* The TV has a sleek design and doesn't heat up much, potentially making it more energy-efficient than older LCD models.
* The remote has a nice tactile feel and is easy to use even in the dark.
* The four HDMI ports come in handy, although only two support 144Hz

Improvement Points: The Vidaa operating software is good but Google TV is better and is used on Hisense TVs in the US why not Europe? The sport mode is a great all-round setting for most viewings, punchy colours and good contrast. Watched Alien and the back light struggled a little with the space, star field scenes, though lots of Led TVs do. Hopefully some of these issues can be helped with firmware updates. For the technology involved it's a bargain. The equivalent Sony from last year was twice the price. Highly recommended.

body:

Motion blur is limited when watching Sports or whilst gaming giving you a quality picture with fast moving objects. Available ports HDMI 2.1 x 2 (eARC x 1) - HDMI 2.0 x 2, is able to run Dolby Vision IQ/HDR10+/HDR10 and Hybrid Log Gamma (HLG)

Audio: The rear speakers have excellent sound distribution and are possibly the best I have heard from a slimline TV. The speakers have 20W of power with Dolby Atmos.

Connectivity: App controls from Smart Device are excellent - allowing the user to use physical body gestures or smart commands to control the TV without the need of a remote control (although I still believe the remote is the easiest choice of operation) - Voice commands are also available via the Vidaa application (this can be done in any language which is a great accessibility feature more TV's should have!) Tv has built in WiFi as well as Bluetooth 5.0.

Improvement Points: Stand: As the stand is curved it would limit any possibility of adding a sound bar. The sound from the TV is excellent but for those who would want a sound bar directly under would have to seek a different method.

App Store: This could be good or bad but I feel like the app store could do with some more additions. The TV has the basics covered, BBC iPlayer, ITVX, Channel 4, Netflix, Prime, Disney+, YouTube, and more streaming services.

Remote Control: This is a personal preference but feel like the remote doesn't match the TV appearance, would prefer colour matching.

body:
Good Points: This TV offers an immersive viewing experience that surpassed my expectations. Its stunning picture quality, innovative features, and sleek design set a new standard for home entertainment. 

Incredible Picture Quality:
The ULED technology employed by Hisense takes the visual experience to the next level. With the 4K Ultra HD resolution, every scene comes to life with exceptional clarity, sharpness, and vibrant colours. The combination of Quantum Dot Colour and Dolby Vision HDR further enhances the picture quality, delivering deeper blacks and brighter whites.
Cutting-Edge Features:
The TV is packed with an array of advanced features that enhance both convenience and entertainment. The built-in voice control capabilities (powered by AI I think), allow you to navigate through the TV's functions effortlessly. Whether it's adjusting settings, searching for content, or accessing popular streaming platforms, a simple voice command is all it takes. The TV also supports popular voice assistants like Amazon Alexa or Google Assistant, providing seamless integration with your smart home ecosystem.
Smart TV Functionality:
It's a fully-fledged smart TV, offering a comprehensive range of applications and streaming services. With its integrated Wi-Fi connectivity, it easily connected to our home network and we quickly enjoyed our favourite content from the likes of Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, YouTube, and more. The intuitive user interface makes navigation a breeze, ensuring quick access to a vast library of movies, TV shows, and online content.
Immersive Audio Experience:
Complementing the stunning visuals, the audio performance of the 55U7KQTUK is equally impressive. With the inclusion of Dolby Atmos technology, the TVs built in speakers deliver a three-dimensional sound experience that immerses you in rich, detailed audio. We enjoyed watching action-packed movies and playing video games, the soundstage is wide and enveloping, providing an enhanced sense of realism.
Sleek Design and Connectivity Options:
The Hisense 55U7KQTUK TV has a sleek and modern design that effortlessly blends into our (and any) living space. The near-borderless display and slim bezels maximize the screen real estate, offering an immersive viewing experience. Additionally, the TV provides a wide range of connectivity options, including multiple HDMI ports, USB ports, and Bluetooth, ensuring easy integration with various devices such as gaming consoles, soundbars, or streaming devices.

Conclusion:
Thi Hisense 55U7KQTUK 55" ULED TV shines in the highly competitive TV market. Its stunning picture quality, cutting-edge features, smart functionality, immersive audio, and sleek design make it a top choice for anyone after low-cost high-quality device.

Improvement Points: While the Hisense 55U7KQTUK 55" ULED TV has many positive attributes, it does have a few drawbacks. Some small things I found were:
Unable to play sound through the soundbar and tv speakers at the same time, my old TV was able to do this so I was used to this. 
This point is only a small one, when watching Freeview, the channel information appears at the top of the screen and gets in the way of the picture, I would like to be able to move it to the bottom of the screen, but I have not been able to find a menu option to do this. The TV also has a limited viewing angle, which isn't a problem for my living room but other environments may pick up on this. 
However, when weighed against its numerous positive features, these limitations do not overshadow the overall appeal and value of the TV, particularly for those seeking an immersive and feature-rich home entertainment experience.

body:
Good Points: I compared this to a similar Samsung QLED T.V,  the results are interesting. So, first off physically the T.V is nice and light, easy to setup and the remote keys have a nice grippy feel to them (unlike the SS). The menu UI is VERY easy to navigate (easier than SS) as it is pretty basic but you get what you are looking for very quickly.
The image quality is ULED tech which is supposed to be somewhere between QLED and OLED, the picture is very similar to my SS TV but is very clear and vibrant.
There's lots of HDR presets, I changed mine from default to HDR night as it displayed best for PS5 games.
As for the 144hz I only used upto 120hz as I have no games that output that fast, but still it's very nice to have now that some PS5 games are outputting 120hz in their settings. No sign of image tear but be sure to use a high quality/speed HDMI cable!!

The system has a built in Sub Woofer and outputs audio brilliantly, the audio can get very loud as I barely go over 30.

It also has advanced features and HDMI linking so you can control your ps5 main menu through the TV remote if needed.

I had no problems with the TV, but I would not spend quad figures on it. If you can get it for less then you won't be disappointed.

Overall, a very nice modern T.V, excellent picture quality and easy to use. Would recommend.

Improvement Points: It generates quite a bit of heat around the back of the TV, and it uses a little more energy consumption than the Samsung but that could be because it has a built in subwoofer.

body:
"Brilliant Display. I've been looking for a new TV for my home office, I wanted something that was versatile enough for gaming and general use.

The 55U7QTUK PRO has not disappointed, after years of using other brands TV's throughout my house, I may have just been converted, the screen is bright and vivid, whilst there is glare from the window, that is to be expected as most TV's would have this unless it was a matte panel anyway.

The inclusion of Freely makes watching TV quick and easy, a great option to get started especially for less tech savvy people, I hooked up a handheld pc with an EGPU to it. 
It took a while to get the correct settings for the 165hz display, but this was a windows thing not a TV thing, but once I got it set up, it's been working perfectly, no issues at all. 

The only "negative" I have is that HiSense include their own OS (VIDAA), which is lacking a bit compared to Android TV offerings. I use an android based device on my other TV's so I'll be doing the same for this one, it's just a shame that in this day and age with such widespread options HiSense have opted for their own proprietary offering. 

This is not by any means a deal-breaker, it's easily rectified with an android TV stick if required, but this is more to my use-case and may not affect others in the slightest.

Overall I would highly recommend this product, and I will certainly be replacing my other TV's with HiSense options when they eventually give up."

"Hisense 55U7QTUK PRO - Gamers Delight. I'm fairly new to Hisense, and had done some research previously. However what attracted me to this was the 165Hz Game Mode Ultra. Wow, just wow! Immersive gaming, either playing sport simulation games, to first-person shooters, the picture, colours and refresh rate are just amazing. Then add the 2.1.2 Channel sound with Dolby Atmos, and it is next level. I also liked that fact that there is a built-in subwoofer. It means you need to play around a bit, but once you get it right, the sound for gaming and movies adds to the experience (without the need for additional speakers). Some nice additional features, including IMAX Enhanced and Filmmaker mode - allowing you to watch the film just the filmmakers intended! Also has Freely built in - which allows you to watch a mixture of live channel and catch up content using an internet connection. Still finding my way, but has some nice features, including allowing you to 'pause' live TV. Finally all the usual mainstream apps are integrated, Amazon Prime Video, Disney+ and Netflix to name a few. Oh a small mention for the remove control - it has a nice solar remote for sustainable power. Excellent touch. All in all a great TV!

"Thank you Hisense!. Just got this TV and I love it! It was super easy to set up. The build quality feels solid and modern, and the picture is impressive. It's really sharp and the colors are vibrant – the mini led screen makes everything look amazing.
The remote is actually one of my favorite things. It’s super easy to use, and it charges itself with solar power! No more battery swapping. It also has handy shortcut buttons at the top, for things like YouTube and Netflix, so you can jump right in with just one click.
Apps load really fast too, switching between them usually takes less than a second, which is very helpful.
The picture stays clear even in a bright room, which I really appreciate. The menu is simple to navigate, nothing confusing or clunky.
As for sound, it seems pretty good, but we usually use a separate sound system (my husband’s choice), so I can’t really comment too much on the built-in sound.
It comes with the Freely option, you can watch live UK channels over the internet, no aerial needed.
The only small downside is that since it’s a Chinese brand, it doesn’t come with Google built in, so no Google Assistant or Play Store. But honestly, we haven’t missed it.
All in all, super happy with this TV., totally worth it! Thank you Hisense!"

body:
"Quality picture with superb sound . Having finally jumped onto the 4K TV bandwagon, I have to honestly say I’m truly impressed by the increased picture quality.

I normally just use Sky to watch TV and my subscribed apps (purely because they’re all located in one place) . I also have the HD package for the channels. After going from a non-4K TV to one that is, with the added benefit of an AI chip installed, the picture clarity is greatly improved. The usual text you see on programs and films like the intro text and end credits are crystal clear. I literally haven’t seen one blurred word or number since plugging it in. I’ve also set the picture smoothing settings to low which improves the quality without getting the soap opera effect.

The sound quality is fantastic. You can hear every word spoken clearly and the TV automatically knows when an action heavy scene is showing and kicks in the subwoofer.

Setting up the TV was really quick when you use the VIDAA app at the same time. Settings like connecting to the WiFi is super quick as it matches the WiFi your phone or tablet is connected to, thus saving you time putting the password in manually.

The smart features are simple and easy to use as well as switching to your other input sources.

I am yet to try Game Mode as I need to get my PS3 (yes I know it’s old!) out of storage. Honestly I don’t use it for gaming anymore but still use it to watch my Blu-ray movies. Can’t wait to see what the extra hertz and upscaling looks like.

For me, the size of the TV is great and fits in the room just fine. Either way, I’d happily recommend this TV whatever size you pick."

body: I bought this Sony Bravia 3 as a replacement for my previous LG OLED. My main priority was finding a lower-budget 55-inch TV with a built-in Chromecast and Google TV/Android system. I needed this specifically to download international apps that LG, Samsung, and even the Amazon Fire Stick do not support due to app store limitations. Watching programs through a web browser was too messy, so this Sony completely solved that problem for me. I am very happy to finally have all my international apps directly on the home page.In terms of image quality, this Sony is definitely more basic compared to an OLED. It lacks the deep colors, contrast, and realistic depth of my previous TV, where I could see every fine detail like skin pores. Darker scenes are also harder to perceive. I managed to improve the picture slightly by following online tutorials and turning off the motion smoothing filters, but I still miss the OLED quality. However, given the lower price point, you cannot have everything, and the TV meets my main priority.Cons: The TV takes a bit of time to connect to the internet and load the home page at start-up. My previous TV didn't have this delay, though it could be related to my internet connection.Final Verdict: If you are used to an OLED, you will notice the drop in picture quality. However, for anyone upgrading from a standard or mid-range TV, the quality will be perfectly fine. It is an excellent budget choice if you need a smart TV with great app availability.

On our old TV you could scan through the info for each channel to decide what to watch, while it still showed the programme you are on.
Setting it up was also a 'clunky' as it asked you to choose options for the Satellite set up which most people wouldn't have heard of.  It then took a looooong time to scan for channels.

We had been very pleased with that one, and this new one is fine too, but not exceptional. I had hoped the operating system would have improved more over the last ten years. Overall, it works well enough, and the picture is just as good as the previous model. We use an external sound bar which is needed as the incorporated speakers are as poor as you'd expect. Interaction with the connected Apple tv is inconsistent - sometimes each will switch the other on and off, and sometimes not. Also, the tv takes far longer to start up than I expected, given the rate of progress in electronics over the last decade. However, despite being about the same size as the set I bought ten years ago, this new one was half the price, so I can't really complain. Another plus, is that this model doesn't use an external power brick - the set plugs directly into the mains.

body:
We bought this new Sony TV a few weeks ago. Had it installed and setup by TV supplier. It needed some resetting within a week as some faces appeared plastic and stretched (very unflattering) and there was intermittent glitches on the screen that started maybe once an hour, but by the time the installer came about a week later, the glitches were about every 20 minutes and annoying. The glitches only lasted a second or so, but disturbed our concentration on the programme. 
The repairer came and reset everything and it now works much better.  
I’ll wait to see if it keeps working OK, otherwise I’ll have to call the shop back to send their repair er person to fix it, or replace it.  Hopefully that won’t be necessary. 
One reason we chose this particular TV is because if the 5-year guarantee-warranty.   As it seems modern TVs are not as good as old fashioned TVs that lasted for years and years without any problems.  Like most modern goods these days, modern smart TVs appear to be built to fail instead of lasting for many years.

body:
My K-43S3 is a massive disappointment. I bought it to replace my Sony KDL-40W605B (probably about 15 years old) which no longer gave me access to BBC iPlayer etc. (Sony blamed the BBC for this, but it was actually Sony to blame). Some 99% of TV stations are SD and my old Sony TV had a slightly better clarity of picture than the new TV. HD is marginally better than my old TV. 
Only plus points is that I now have access to BBC iPlayer, Channel 4 etc. As for Google TV I haven't quite worked out yet what exactly it is. A manual would have been helpful (I'm fully aware that there is a digital manual via the TV but that involves having to go back and forward from one to the other).

body: This TV replaced its predecessor dur to an accident leaving the previous 12month old one not repairable.  Whilst there is a possible slight improvement on the picture, it he functionality has dramatically gone down hill. To watch live Tv or iplayer, bbc sounds etc, you now have to access these via Sonys ‘Live TV & catch up app which is diabolical & practically next to useless. The app doesn’t always load & can sometimes take half an hour of trying to get in to it! Why would I want to access these through another app when previously they were on the main screen with all the other services?!?! Because if this the process the ‘TV’ button in the remote doesn’t work - so why is it there? At the same time whilt watching live Tv you can no longer press the down arrow to get the guide at the bottom of the TV something else that has gone backward. Honestly compared to its 12 month old predecessor it’s terrible. Would never have bought it if I’d known. Sony when you update your models make sure you are making them better & easier to use, not slower & frustrating to use. I do not recommend this TV - especially if you are a previous Sony Tv owner. body:
For a personal Christmas present, both me and my dad wanted to put our money together towards a brand new TV for my bedroom. In the Hughes store, we were quickly drawn to this TV with it's beautiful picture quality and ideal size. From early on, we knew this was a descent TV!

Through Hughes, we did run into fitting issues, which were amended at a later date. We had fitters coming to mount a TV which had not been delivered on time. We were able to reschedule the fitting and get the TV mounted. The Hughes mounting team quickly setup the TV and I was all good.

It has been very convenient having many 'Smart' features built-in the TV, for easy access. Unfortunately, I have noticed when the electricity socket is completely switched off, this TV is very slow with it's start-up. This is a problem with many modern TVs, particularly Smart ones. Old fashioned TVs were quick to start-up, even when electricity sockets had been turned off.

The voice command remote control is fantastic, this has been the only TV remote I have had to use. It came with another TV remote which is still in it's packaging. It has been very easy to use to voice command to find things faster than navigating through various menus.

Overall, I am very happy with the purchase.

body: Excellent high definition picture, quick response to program selection etc

We bought this a couple of weeks ago, chiefly because our Freesat box had begun to give a warning that iPlayer would cease to work on it in January. Buying a new TV with Satellite built in seemed the obvious answer, and it would also give us access to ITVX, which our old TV couldn't deliver.

As a device, our new TV is probably all that you would expect of a modern Sony TV - classy picture, good sound (we also bought a cheapish soundbar to help with my wife's failing hearing). I really dislike the home screen, which is basically just a lot of advertising for subscription-only channels that we don't have, but I can more or less live with that. Initial installation was pretty easy, which got us to viewing the OTA channels. But then the less satisfactory aspects began to show. It took ages to find out how to install iPlayer - which after all was the trigger for buying it in the first place. Finally, after hours of online searching I found I had to download and install yet another app. Well, okay, now it works fine, but why is this not pre-installed for the UK market? 

Then I integrated it with Alexa so we could use voice control. That worked for about a day, and now Alexa keeps saying it can't contact the TV. I'm sure I can sort that out, but it's just more hassle. And then we get to the programme guide... This is almost completely useless. One key on the remote takes you to the guide... which shows you a list of channels with absolutely no program information at all! To see what's on a channel, you have to click on it, let the current program load, and then go back to the guide. To see your viewing choices for the evening on OTA TV, you have to do this for EVERY channel in turn. An internet search says this is likely because of poor signal, but our old Freesat box never had any trouble. I'm still working on this, but why does it not just work out of the box? Most unsatisfactory.

This leaves me with very mixed feelings about the purchase, and I'm wondering if I should have found another solution to the original problem.

body:
Only had it a week or so but it’s already giving good results, easy to set up and the picture is as good as my larger Bravia in the main room. Off centre viewing is better than others I looked at and the standard colour setup needed little tweaking for my taste. Sport viewing has good sharp movement viewing and I’ve had no buffering on watching a variety of media via apps. Sound is fairly good via front projection speakers and decent options so maybe only use a soundbar for an intense 
movie experience. 

Only very minor (and easily resolved) issue is that watching ITV X on the Bravia has a second app at the right hand end of the app menu bar so you’ll find it easiest to delete the first one and move the other app into its place, now working perfectly and less than 5 minutes to fully setup. All round an excellent quality TV, there are cheaper ones available but this is a different league and close on as good as ones double the money, I’m happy and recommend it (and yes, I did pay for it and got no special incentive to do so. I’m not an influencer and just a buyer happy to pass my views on for others to consider).

It does a good job though, as expected from Sony, with a great deal of tuning options. It is not quite as immersive, though, as OLED technology can be.
I am very pleased with the sound options and quality.
This model, due its miniLED technology, has good power consumption rating, another aspect I cared about, and does switch itself off when there is no activity for about 10 minutes.
The Google TV integration of all Apps into s single menu is great and its connectivity to WiFi is very reliable, so J expect the buffering to be optimised as WiFi speed varies.
Overall a pretty good telly, worth the money it cost, and expected to last for well over a decade, given Sony’s product reliability.

body:
This page contains 0 information on actual performance and is clearly intended to prey on the uninformed purchaser using buzz words like 4k so I'm here to give the actual facts.

Despite the monitor being able to support a 120hz refresh rate, its lack of hdmi 2.1 support limits this to 60hz, the same you could get on an ancient lg tv.

The settings are god awful. They limit what options can be changed depending on the device you are using, gamma control is completely unexplained and the range of contrast and brightness are far too small to create an accurate image. This accurate image can however be created using the products "movie mode", a mode which is unavailable if you are using hdr. To worsen this, hdr is forced depending on the device you are using, such as my PC always being set to hdr despite my lack of need or want of it.

Bought this as my last few TVs have been Samsung and I have been super happy with them, but this has been so bad that I think thereÕs something wrong with it!
While the picture and features of the tv are excellent- as expected- using the remote control is a joke! There is a 2-3 second delay between pressing a button and something happening in the menu. This sounds like an exaggeration but honestly, this is exactly what is happening. ItÕs also random if you get 2 or 3 presses instead of one, or if it even registers the press in the first place.
IÕve tried new batteries in the remote and even used brand new from the packet, but itÕs still the same. IÕve reset to factory defaults, done a restart, run the health check, everything I have tried and itÕs still the same.
ItÕs such a shame because I also have effectively the same TV but with the Bixby version (the nice remote with only a few buttons) and itÕs awesome! This one with the ugly brick remote with 500 buttons is just junk.
Anyone want a free tv?

body:
I bought this tv to replace a faulty Q6 tv. The image on streaming and hd services is superb however on "standard" broadcasts the image has a slightly blurred quality to it - never noticed this on the Q6, in fact felt the images were better. 
The second reason for the low score is I have an Samsung sound bar which is 5 years old but it still does the job. However, due to the tv no longer supporting Bluetooth or TV Connect (possibly the something), I have to use the optical connection. This would be OK if, once selected, the new tv's  remote could change the volume on the Samsung sound bar - you'd think it would but no. It sounds like a minor thing but it a busy family having to hunt down two remote (one of which is tiny) can be a real pain. 
I knew the TV only had 2 hdmi ports but in removing options for connectivity (Bluetooth) Samsung should really have upped this number. 
All in all feels like it's lacking in thought,  a bit of a rush job.

body:
The display and screen panel failed literally less than two weeks after receiving the product. Whilst the TV does switch on, the back-light will flicker and then automatically switch-off, implying that either the panel, bulb, or capacitator have failed.

I bought this tv because Samsung are (or were ) synonymous with reliability, yet the TV appears to have broken down not after 12 years, but after barely 12 days! Worst of all, Samsung do not appear keen to assign an engineer or technician to assess the appliance, which suggests there are known issues with this model.

I would expect a firmware failure with a Bush, Hitachi, JVC etc TV (where issues with build quality and where the panel isn't secured within the unit abound). But not with a Samsung TV....ever!

Until now! :(

body: We had wanted a Bravia tv for a long time and had been impressed by the picture quality. We purchased the 55 inch and are happy with the colour depth and overall picture. However, the sound is another matter. Several times a day, we lose the "lip synch" on all channels. Actors or newsreaders voices are totally out of synch with the show being viewed. We are constantly implementing the hard restart, as described in Sony's troubleshooting steps. This is a very annoying fault. The screen also pixelates for a couple of seconds, now and then. Actually, this sometimes seems to trigger the lip synch problem. Today, while watching the tv news, the sound just went off completely. Nobody in the house was anywhere near the remote control. It would not come back on until I restarted the tv again. These problems have taken away all the fun and excitement, of having a new tv. The picture for the most part is fine but this sound problem really does need attention by Sony. I actually spoke to a friend in the US who has the same tv. My friend also confirmed that they are regularly having to restart the tv, with the same lip synch problem. I think Sony really needs to address this issue.

body: The Sony K-55XR8A has completely exceeded my expectations. From the moment I switched it on, I was blown away by the incredible picture quality. Colours are rich, vibrant, and lifelike, while blacks are deep and detailed, creating a truly cinematic experience in my living room. What really sets this TV apart is the stunning clarity and processing. Whether I'm watching films, live sport, or streaming high-definition content, everything looks exceptionally sharp and smooth. Fast-moving scenes are handled effortlessly, and the level of detail is remarkable. The sound quality is equally impressive. Unlike many modern TVs that require an immediate soundbar upgrade, the K-55XR8A delivers clear dialogue, excellent balance, and a surprisingly immersive audio experience on its own. The smart TV interface is fast, intuitive, and packed with features. Apps load quickly, navigation is seamless, and the overall user experience feels premium and refined. Sony has clearly paid attention to every detail. Build quality is another highlight. The television looks elegant and sophisticated, with a sleek design that enhances any room. It feels like a genuinely high-end product. Overall, the Sony K-55XR8A is a fantastic investment and an absolute pleasure to use every day. If you're looking for superb picture quality, excellent sound, premium design, and a smooth smart-TV experience, this television delivers on every front. Highly recommended!

body: I can’t talk technically (it’s all modern stuff now !)  I moved house and promised myself a better TV system and so I toddled of to the local tv dealer in our town to view and talk about tvs , I felt it may be important to inform him I have been a staunch Samsung believer and have been for many years !  I had a quick demo ( that’s all that was needed really)  of a couple of TVs of varying types normal HD but the newer types and the OLED ones !  Being an old fan of HD TVs when you view that type it’s as if someone was  a dirty piece of plastic in front of the screen compared to the Bravia OLED 55” , that was crystal clear and bright !  Just a quick view was all that was really needed and once I’d seen the Sony Bravia models , the clarity , colours and sharpness of them I knew that was the type I was going to buy , had to buy to be more precise , there was just no real comparison, yes they were more expensive but what the heck , the old house would pay for that and with a 5 year guarantee, what’s not to like ?  By by Samsung  !  The TV Engineers came on Wednesday to help set it up and they were very polite and efficient and did so and took away any unnecessary ‘bits and pieces!  ‘ So now it was left to me to figure out all these apps and free to view programmes, well that in itself is another full booklet to describe and I thought I would be quite good at this , however it was dragging on but not affecting the football but I made my mind up that I would still purchase a second tv for my bedroom and the  England matches were getting tighter as the games went on and the kick off times were not doing my sleep any good at all and especially at my age !  So back to the retailers and without any hesitation (I knew which type I wanted) I did the deal on a Sony Bravia 48” this time , I was so impressed with the TV and picture quality etc it was not a hard choice at all !  I’m still finding my way around the new set ups, how to find this programme or switch back to normal tv , is there such a thing as normal these days ?  I doubt it !

I've done the factory reset yet again and also adjusted everything in the picture motion settings and this hasn't fixed the issue. I'm now waiting and hoping that Sony will release another update that will fix this.
Overall I do love this TV for it's sound and it's Google operating system but will maybe think twice about purchasing again.

body: I have always had Sony TVs from the early Trinitrons in the very early 80s so I guess you could say I'm very pro Sony TVs. This Bravia 65" 8a replaces a 10 year old 55" Bravia 4k which was a fine TV but the Apps like iPlayer,Plex etc were no longer supported. body: Had it a month now and needed a full factory reset as the usb ports  stopped working.TV is lovely with one all too common exception. It's a high quality TV but Sony have cut corners to save money. Why oh why don't they provide all 4 HDMI with the 120Hz this TV deserves. 1 is reserved for the ARC soundbar system which only leaves 1 of the remaining 3 ports with the quality 120Hz ports. If like me you have a firestick as well as a TV Box you have a dilemma. Which one gets the it. Your only option is to buy an HDMI splitter box to share the port but if you do that make sure you buy one with a remote control otherwise you'll have to keep getting up to manually switch between the boxes because the first Switcher I bought was advertised as an auto switcher (with no remote needed) which can detect you switching to another input and auto switch to it. Only it can't because firesticks do not fully power down rendering the auto switch unable to switch. This type of annoying 'get around' could all have been avoided if Sony were to make all 4 HDMI inputs the high quality 120Hz ports we should be given. Hope this helps you make a happy purchase without the disappointment of realising what else you need to look into.

body: Phenomenal TV.

I have no doubt that this is a great TV picture-wise. Sound quality from the screen speakers is pretty dire unfortunately and is in desperate need of an add-on sound bar, sub-woofer and ideally, rear speakers. I could not get my existing non-4K system to work with it. Sony have their own versions of all 3 add-ons, but are ridiculously expensive, adding the equivalent cost of the TV again. I have bought the sound bar and will be adding the sub-woofer shortly. The rears can wait for now. 
The great advantage of the Sony add-on products is that they so easy to set up. The TV itself, is not quiet so. You need to realise that this is a Google TV and will require a Google Account in addition to a Sony one. There are a few things in the set up that worry me, from a privacy point of view, so just be careful as you give permissions.
Colour calibration was not too bad straight out of the box, but be aware, trying it yourself can be tricky if you don't understand the technicalities - it's far more than brightness and contrast. The supplied documentation is pretty useless, but there are some informative videos on the net that demonstrate how the parameters work. I've been tweaking for a few days now and I'm pretty close to how I like it.
I'm pretty pleased with the product now that it is enhanced, but I could not live with it sound-wise in just the boxed state. That makes it a very expensive option that I sort of new might be the case, but still comes as a shock.

I got this tv about 2 weeks ago and I must say I'm pretty impressed so far. I'll start with the caveat that my previous telly is a 14 year old LG 3d Smart Telly, so I might mention features that have been around for a bit, but I think these comments are mostly product specific features.

I'll start with the only slight negative. The initial set-up was a bit onerous, even, for someone who just about still considers on the right side of tech savvy - this was for setting up the Google Home and Bravia Connect features of the telly. Ultimatley i think it was worth it it, but it might intimidate those of an older generation. (though i think you can skip all this process in favour of not using the full potential of the telly)

One of the things I did like in the set up was how it calibrates the sound of the telly in your room. It turns on it's microphone, tells you to be quite and fires a mutlitude of star wars-esque sounds into the room and listens to itself!

So onto the goodstuff - the positives:
- it asks you at the start to name all your streaming subscriptions (ie apple +, netflix, prime, disney etc), and then gives you recommendations and new releases on the home menu based on the subscriptions you are a part of which i find really useful!
- the screen itself is actually a speaker and apparently the sound corresponds with where say the speaker on screen is located on screen. I don't know about that, but it makes for a very crisp sound (from someone who is used to **** sound from flat screen tellys and having to use a soundbar instead)
- I made a point of watching movies with a lot of dark/night scenes (the Batman, Titanic) in it to check out the dark contrast. So much definition even in the darkness!
- I watched the Olympics too, and couldn't believe live coverage could be so crisp and clear
- I also got the playstation going on it and delighted with the picture and sound, though will have to find an adapter to connect my old nintento wii to it!
-The control gently lights up when you nudge or pick it up. Not a feature i thought i needed but so useful when watch something with the lights off!
- The look of it. I know, a telly is a telly, and they kinda all look the same, but the little stand that comes with it is actually quite elegant, and has a few variations to allow you to sit something under it. Equally the fact that the screen itself has very little 'frame' around it is what sets it apart from my old telly, which is of a similiar size (see picture) but the 8" difference in screen size is mostly accommodated in the smaller framing

This pic is not great, i haven't yet committed to the faff of taking the old telly off the wall, and wall mounted the new one, probably should have paused the movie for a photo too, but hopefully you get the picture!
author: Brian Keane

body:
For the purpose of transparency, we have moved from a 12 year old 26" TV to this one so everything is very much updated from that! That said, we have been very impressed with this product. In the week since it was delivered we have thoroughly tested it with all manner of things from 4K UHD movies to gaming and on everything we have been blown away. Gaming playback was very smooth and we saw details that we hadn't been able to before. We even compared Disney+ on our previous HD streaming device through the TV to the built in Google TV app and the difference was amazing. Picture detail and colour are so much better. The TV also automatically switches to show the best quality picture available which means no messing about with settings every time you change content.

An unexpected bonus of this product has been the sound which comes out of the screen like it does in a cinema and gives us a sort of surround sound without the use of additional speakers.

Set up out of the box was pretty straight forward but you do need to have it connected to the Internet to maximise the functionality. Buyer beware that this means that everything is going through Google. You will also need 2 people to get it out of the box and then onto the TV stand as it's obviously a mighty beast but it was easy to do after that!

Overall this is a great future-proof product that is ready for the streamers' content to catch up with it.
