body:
First thought upon opening the box, was that it was a fair weight. The legs are sturdy and the quality of the TV could be seen by the eye.
I turned the TV on and plugged my Apple TV in, the TV went into setup mode which took only a few minutes. Once set up, it brought up a scene in the grand canyon... me and my Wife both said ''WOW''. The colours and quality were outstanding!

We went straight onto Disney+ to watch something in 4K! I never want to go back to watching a film in HD again. Surprisingly, the speakers on the TV itself are great. I usually have 2 x Apple HomePods as a surround sound system. I would 100% recommend the Sony Bravia 8

This is the highest spec TV I've ever owned. I used to watch a 43" LG smart TV that was pretty damned good, but this Bravia is a whole new experience! 

*Out of the box - super slim, sleek and attractive
*Very easy to set up (including adding the feet - doddle). I particularly liked the accessibility feature of having a voice assistant to take you through every single step of the set-up process, this was easy to turn off however and I did so. If my 75 year old mum was setting this up she would be able to follow the voice instructions and not have a meltdown! 
*Apps are easy to set-up, I was watching Netflix within about 5 minutes of plugging it in.
*Settings are pretty straightforward to access and play with, to be honest the factory settings for picture were pretty spot on for my preferences so I left it almost as it is. I had a good play though, to explore what's possible.
*I am now using the surround sound feature for audio, and it does make a difference - impressed. The speakers are pretty decent for a TV, no distortion at high volume, not annoying at high volume either. I love that you can zoom in on the voice, this is fab for me as my hearing has declined a bit of late (age lol) and this feature makes it so much easier to hear dialogue.
*Amazing range of brightness, contrast etc, I have set it to auto adjust to the light in the room. 
*Picture clarity is fantastic, no matter what angle you're watching from! My living room has a sofa directly in front of the TV and one at 90 degrees to the TV - those sitting and viewing from the side can see the picture perfectly with no problem. 
*Colours are vivid and distinct, easily adjustable and super realistic. Blacks are deep and velvety. Image is super sharp and realistic - husband stood and stared and said it felt like it was in 3D - this is his first experience of a high spec TV too, he was extremely impressed.
*It's got plenty of eco features which I love! There are some features in settings to do with picture and audio that aren't accessible if you have the TV on energy saving mode which is a pain, but obviously you can turn this on and off - if I'm watching a nature documentary or something that required the highest quality viewing experience (rather than re-runs of Friends haha) then I will turn the energy saving mode off for the duration. easy.
*The only drawback for me is the amount of reflection - I have had a look at other reviews of the product and apparently this TV handles reflection well but I'm not sure I agree.  Maybe it's because the screen is glossy and I'm not used to that with my older TV. It's not a massive issue though.  When there's less light / night time, the watching experience is absolutely fantastic, faultless. It's just that I can see the venetian blinds very clearly reflected during a sunny day (which it has been since I got the TV!

Overall, an awesome piece of technology, and there are still some bits that I have not yet explored, but so far so great. Very impressed, well done Sony!

OLED tvs. I don’t think there’s many of these around now, but if you get a chance grab one, it’s a Truly stunningly TV and the fact you can use it as a centre channel for a proper AV set up is great. Even the remote which is quite long is well built. Doesn’t flex doesn’t Creek and the fact that it has a gentle backseat key set up when moved is perfect. It’s just bright enough to say at night time without being glaringly bright. It’s a shame they couldn’t have included a slightly smaller remote. The new one is being. I think I did a bit better but it’s also quite nice to have almost every six conceivable button on one remote control anyway, which is very slim and very light and so much better than the old plastic remotes. I was glad I managed to get one of these. It’s a perfect set for my needs works brilliantly with the PS5 Google TV. Well the interface is a bit cluttered but you can cut that back and Bravia core has so much detail, but the file sizes are quite large so you need a good Internet connection. All in all there isn’t much difference between this TV and the ones coming out this year. In fact I would say this one is probably better built than some of the newer ones which use soft plastic. The A90J you could say was definitely over built but that’s not a bad thing at all the current prices it’s a bargain and you won’t really notice any difference. Compare with the current sets Sony are pushing out this year it’s just a shame they’re still stuck on Android 10. It be nice to see this and if you have a set upgraded to android 11 or 12. The only thing that lets it down is a rather cluttered interface and a lack of information about what every single setting does. Unlike most android products there seems to be so many ways to get to the same place. I can get a bit confusing at times, but once you get used to it end navigation is so far through the menus it’s a joy to use and put a grin on my face when I sit back and watch it in the evening or game on it during the day. Custom is probably the best setting and personally under clarity, I do use reality creation on auto it’s almost free do you like and the extra detail that AI puts into the image is quite incredible. body:
I have had the TV now for about 5-6 months and is my first true smart TV. I use it for both internet based apps access such as BBC iPlayer etc but also Freesat from an external dish (old Sky dish). The picture quality is excellent in all cases.  The TV's sound is very good for what it is with surprisingly good bass.  However it is not going to sound the same a a proper AV set-up with separate amp and speakers obviously. As with most smart TV's using native TV speakers etc there is a problem with clarity and volume when it comes to dialogue particularly in films.  There are some settings you can

 use to try and tweak it a bit but basically at least a centre speaker needs to be added.

Whilst on the subject of sound the TV has lost sound on apps such as TVX or iPlayer and no amount of changing settings will bring it back.  The only way is to switch off unplug at the mains and leave it.  I don't knowhow long you need to do this for some on forums say 10 mins I left mine 24 hours as I was away anyway.  All was well once plugged  back in.

Updates are another weird thing I have  set it to automatically keep up to date but it has randomly started updating whilst we are watching a program.  I could do nothing but leave it and eventually after 30 mins or so I was able to get to react to the remote once again.

However I can live with these few foibles as overall this a fantastic TV.  I am yet to try other sources such as DVD player etc but I have no doubt it will equally impressive.

My only reservation is  for how long software updates will be available.  My son has a Sony smart TV that is just about 5 years' old and updates are no longer provided therefore apps can no longer be supported/used

body:
I bought the TV in January and all I can say is this has one hell of a picture.  After playing around with the settings I have got the picture to look amazing. At times it is so clear and vivid it is simply captivating. All built on apps work amazingly. With full HDR in YouTube and the Dolby vision presentation on Disney plus is stunning. One other thing I have noticed is the sound. The TV uses the screen as the speakers and this can truly trick you into thinking you have speaker positioned behind you at times. I've had no problems with motion and when playing the PS5 it looks incredible.  Being OLED the blacks are black and the colours are so deep and bright it's just so impressive.  
 
Design wise, it's very nice, although mine 8a wall hung so don't get to appreciate just how thin it is. Wall mounting was easy with an off the shelf bracket as well. The ports available are what is required. 2 hdmi 2.1 port are provided for 4k120 signals from ps5 and with the latest update, VRR has been activated.  The one downside to the ports is the ethernet socket. It is not a gigabit port so is limited to 100mbps. The WiFi on the other is much faster and there is also a usb 3.0 port so a usb to ethernet adapter can be used to get full gigabit wired ethernet. 
 
All in all I can not fault the set. The picture is so much clearer than even my old Sony 4k TV and the HDR quality when watching something like toy story 4 on Disney plus is just breathtaking. At times the lights on the fairground rides are so bright and vibrant it looks real.

body:
This is my first new TV in 12 years. I'm a bit annoyed that you have to sign your life away to use a TV these days, in the same way as mobile phones and computers. Bloatware everywhere, T&C's, updates, load this, do that, agree to let everyone track all your info and do what they want with it.
And then the TV actually crashed the first time I signed into my Google account! Not a good start at all.
Regarding the picture quality, I'll be honest, I didn't research enough regarding the difference between HD and 4K/UHD.
If you watch 4K/UHD content on this TV (there's a growing number of boxsets/movies on Prime, Netflix, Sky etc) the picture is stunning, absolutely superb. I have no complaints there at all.
However, if you watch HD content (which is basically everything on normal terrestrial channels), I've found the upscaling a bit ropey sometimes. Maybe it's because it's a 75" screen, so any image fuzziness or jagged edges on text on the screen really stands out a lot. Also, it seems worse for the first 10-15 minutes after switching the TV on, and then seems to get better. It's almost like the processor takes a bit of time to wake up before it starts working properly.
I've only had the TV a week so maybe it's just a case of getting used to it, as my old TV was only 45". I hope so, because right now I have very mixed feelings about this product.

I have been bowled over by the new TV which I have had wall-mounted, and although the 55" screen is by far the largest I have owned its slimline looks fit effortlessly into the surroundings and provide an excellent focal point for the room. 

The picture quality is excellent, often breath-taking with OLED showing true colours without garishness.     The sound is very natural with an excellent spread, and after two

body:
Definitely the most impressive and capable television I've ever owned. Brilliant picture. Fantastic audio. The app ecosystem is great (although still limited at the moment - no BBC iPlayer, ITV Hub, or Sky Go, for instance). The ability to use Steam Link baked into the TV with no extra hardware is fantastic.

But we haven't been without issue: Apps like Netflix, Prime Video, or other content directly cast to the TV would close for no apparent reason. In one case the TV via aerial wouldn't start. To fix these required different approaches: app caches to be cleared, the TV restarted, and in one case a factory reset. It's really taken the shine off an otherwise brilliant TV.

So, in summary, a fantastic television for video and audio and capability, but just too many software bugs to ever feel confident that's it's not going to just stop at any moment.

body: I bought this Sony Bravia 3 as a replacement for my previous LG OLED. My main priority was finding a lower-budget 55-inch TV with a built-in Chromecast and Google TV/Android system. I needed this specifically to download international apps that LG, Samsung, and even the Amazon Fire Stick do not support due to app store limitations. Watching programs through a web browser was too messy, so this Sony completely solved that problem for me. I am very happy to finally have all my international apps directly on the home page.In terms of image quality, this Sony is definitely more basic compared to an OLED. It lacks the deep colors, contrast, and realistic depth of my previous TV, where I could see every fine detail like skin pores. Darker scenes are also harder to perceive. I managed to improve the picture slightly by following online tutorials and turning off the motion smoothing filters, but I still miss the OLED quality. However, given the lower price point, you cannot have everything, and the TV meets my main priority.Cons: The TV takes a bit of time to connect to the internet and load the home page at start-up. My previous TV didn't have this delay, though it could be related to my internet connection.Final Verdict: If you are used to an OLED, you will notice the drop in picture quality. However, for anyone upgrading from a standard or mid-range TV, the quality will be perfectly fine. It is an excellent budget choice if you need a smart TV with great app availability.

Neither can you scroll through info for other channels while watching a channel.  You have to go to the EPG to look up what is on - that's if you are lucky enough to have the info on there!.  On our old TV you could scan through the info for each channel to decide what to watch, while it still showed the programme you are on.
Setting it up was also a 'clunky' as it asked you to choose options for the Satellite set up which most people wouldn't have heard of.  It then took a looooong time to scan for channels.
So, in conclusion, I have to say that I am disappointed with the very limited EPG but satisfied with the picture quality.  This Smart TV isn't very smart in certain areas.

Overall, it works well enough, and the picture is just as good as the previous model. We use an external sound bar which is needed as the incorporated speakers are as poor as you'd expect. Interaction with the connected Apple tv is inconsistent - sometimes each will switch the other on and off, and sometimes not. Also, the tv takes far longer to start up than I expected, given the rate of progress in electronics over the last decade. However, despite being about the same size as the set I bought ten years ago, this new one was half the price, so I can't really complain. Another plus, is that this model doesn't use an external power brick - the set plugs directly into the mains.

body:
We bought this new Sony TV a few weeks ago. Had it installed and setup by TV supplier. It needed some resetting within a week as some faces appeared plastic and stretched (very unflattering) and there was intermittent glitches on the screen that started maybe once an hour, but by the time the installer came about a week later, the glitches were about every 20 minutes and annoying. The glitches only lasted a second or so, but disturbed our concentration on the programme. 
The repairer came and reset everything and it now works much better.  
I’ll wait to see if it keeps working OK, otherwise I’ll have to call the shop back to send their repair er person to fix it, or replace it.  Hopefully that won’t be necessary. 
One reason we chose this particular TV is because if the 5-year guarantee-warranty.   As it seems modern TVs are not as good as old fashioned TVs that lasted for years and years without any problems.  Like most modern goods these days, modern smart TVs appear to be built to fail instead of lasting for many years.

body:

Only plus points is that I now have access to BBC iPlayer, Channel 4 etc. As for Google TV I haven't quite worked out yet what exactly it is. A manual would have been helpful (I'm fully aware that there is a digital manual via the TV but that involves having to go back and forward from one to the other).

To watch live Tv or iplayer, bbc sounds etc, you now have to access these via Sonys ‘Live TV & catch up app which is diabolical & practically next to useless. The app doesn’t always load & can sometimes take half an hour of trying to get in to it! Why would I want to access these through another app when previously they were on the main screen with all the other services?!?! Because if this the process the ‘TV’ button in the remote doesn’t work - so why is it there? At the same time whilt watching live Tv you can no longer press the down arrow to get the guide at the bottom of the TV something else that has gone backward. Honestly compared to its 12 month old predecessor it’s terrible. Would never have bought it if I’d known. Sony when you update your models make sure you are making them better & easier to use, not slower & frustrating to use. I do not recommend this TV - especially if you are a previous Sony Tv owner. body:
For a personal Christmas present, both me and my dad wanted to put our money together towards a brand new TV for my bedroom. In the Hughes store, we were quickly drawn to this TV with it's beautiful picture quality and ideal size. From early on, we knew this was a descent TV!

Through Hughes, we did run into fitting issues, which were amended at a later date. We had fitters coming to mount a TV which had not been delivered on time. We were able to reschedule the fitting and get the TV mounted. The Hughes mounting team quickly setup the TV and I was all good.

It has been very convenient having many 'Smart' features built-in the TV, for easy access. Unfortunately, I have noticed when the electricity socket is completely switched off, this TV is very slow with it's start-up. This is a problem with many modern TVs, particularly Smart ones. Old fashioned TVs were quick to start-up, even when electricity sockets had been turned off.

The voice command remote control is fantastic, this has been the only TV remote I have had to use. It came with another TV remote which is still in it's packaging. It has been very easy to use to voice command to find things faster than navigating through various menus.

Overall, I am very happy with the purchase.

body: Excellent high definition picture, quick response to program selection etc

We bought this a couple of weeks ago, chiefly because our Freesat box had begun to give a warning that iPlayer would cease to work on it in January. Buying a new TV with Satellite built in seemed the obvious answer, and it would also give us access to ITVX, which our old TV couldn't deliver.

As a device, our new TV is probably all that you would expect of a modern Sony TV - classy picture, good sound (we also bought a cheapish soundbar to help with my wife's failing hearing). I really dislike the home screen, which is basically just a lot of advertising for subscription-only channels that we don't have, but I can more or less live with that. Initial installation was pretty easy, which got us to viewing the OTA channels. But then the less satisfactory aspects began to show. It took ages to find out how to install iPlayer - which after all was the trigger for buying it in the first place. Finally, after hours of online searching I found I had to download and install yet another app. Well, okay, now it works fine, but why is this not pre-installed for the UK market? 

Then I integrated it with Alexa so we could use voice control. That worked for about a day, and now Alexa keeps saying it can't contact the TV. I'm sure I can sort that out, but it's just more hassle. And then we get to the programme guide... This is almost completely useless. One key on the remote takes you to the guide... which shows you a list of channels with absolutely no program information at all! To see what's on a channel, you have to click on it, let the current program load, and then go back to the guide. To see your viewing choices for the evening on OTA TV, you have to do this for EVERY channel in turn. An internet search says this is likely because of poor signal, but our old Freesat box never had any trouble. I'm still working on this, but why does it not just work out of the box? Most unsatisfactory.

This leaves me with very mixed feelings about the purchase, and I'm wondering if I should have found another solution to the original problem.

body:
Only had it a week or so but it’s already giving good results, easy to set up and the picture is as good as my larger Bravia in the main room. Off centre viewing is better than others I looked at and the standard colour setup needed little tweaking for my taste. Sport viewing has good sharp movement viewing and I’ve had no buffering on watching a variety of media via apps. Sound is fairly good via front projection speakers and decent options so maybe only use a soundbar for an intense 
movie experience. 

Only very minor (and easily resolved) issue is that watching ITV X on the Bravia has a second app at the right hand end of the app menu bar so you’ll find it easiest to delete the first one and move the other app into its place, now working perfectly and less than 5 minutes to fully setup. All round an excellent quality TV, there are cheaper ones available but this is a different league and close on as good as ones double the money, I’m happy and recommend it (and yes, I did pay for it and got no special incentive to do so. I’m not an influencer and just a buyer happy to pass my views on for others to consider).

I found the Sony Bravia 5 a fantastic TV and it would appeal to anyone who wants a real cinema and gaming experience at home.
The picture quality is outstanding thanks to the Mini LED technology. I found the Sony Bravia 5 makes movies look sharp, bright, and colourful with great contrast. I also found blacks are very dark and seem comparable to an OLED TV for quality. The sound is also very impressive. Instead of feeling like it comes from the screen itself, voices and effects seem to come directly from the action and I found the TV sound very immersive. Although for an evening better sound I have paired it with a Sony soundbar that I already owned and this makes an even bigger step up in sound quality. What I also really like is the TV stand is adjustable and is an economical design to accommodate a sound bar on the feet of the stand but if you don't have a soundbar the stands can be lowered. For films, the Bravia 5 supports Dolby Vision, Atmos, DTS:X, and IMAX Enhanced, plus you get access to Sony Pictures Core with 10 bonus streaming credits. I found this a nice extra, as it allows you to download recent films and there are some older films that are also free to watch too, as Sony give you 24 months access to Sony pictures Core with the TV. I find navigating menus easy with Google TV, and the voice controls with Google Assistant are handy. There are two remote controls with the TV, personally I would have liked an all in one remote but they are both simple to use and one controls the Google TV, so it may be that both controls are now simple rather than having a more complex all in one remote control.
Also, for those interested in energy saving, the Eco Dashboard allows you to view you energy use while using the TV. I think gamers will enjoy the Sony Bravia 5, as it handles 4K at 120fps smoothly, supports VRR and ALLM, and even has a dedicated game menu. PlayStation owners will really enjoy the PS remote play feature. Overall I rate the Sony Bravia 5 a fantastic choice, with fantastic picture quality for movies, streaming, and gaming. The Google TV ecosystem and navigation system of the Sony Bravia 5 in general is also easy to use. The sound is good but I would highly recommend a Sony soundbar to get the best experience from the Sony Bravia 5 and this provides a fantastic cinema experience when combined with the quality not the picture.

body:
The Sony Bravia 5 certainly lives up to expectations, from the moment it‚Äôs unpackaged and plugged it, you can see and hear the quality of this television. 
The two legs to support the unit have 2 different height settings which can be adjusted to accommodate a sound bar below.
Set up is intuitive and simple from the remote control, with QR codes onscreen to sign you into your relevant accounts. Once you actually start to watch something the incredible Ultra HD quality virtually jumps off the screen at you, and even without any additional soundbar the built in speakers provide depth and realism to the sound quality. There is an optical audio output for connecting a separate soundbar or surround sound system, USB ports and HDMI ports all easily accessible at the left hand corner of the unit, which give plenty of flexibility for additional input devices such as a games console.
There is also a specific preset mode for games consoles which gives the games a sharpness and crispness which is often lacking on lower quality televisions.
The television comes with 2 remotes but you do really only need the smaller one that can provide full functionality with individual buttons for one press access to the most popular streaming services.
One of my favourite Sony features is Motionflow which can be adjusted to suit your tastes and still works very effectively in my opinion (I know it does divide opinion, but of course you can always turn it off completely)

I’m greatly impressed by the Sony Bravia 5 X the TV gives a stunning picture experience due to its mini LED screen and resolution. It replaces a 5 year old Sony Bravia A8 which I wasn’t sure, it could be bettered but I was wrong... it’s 4K Ultra HDR capability is fantastic which works well on streaming services, which I’ve tried them all it has all the built in Apps and the Google play store for any you need extra  it has Disney, Netflix, Prime, YouTube, Crunchyroll and Sony pictures all at a touch of a button (on the 2nd remote)and luckily upgraded our internet to superfast 900mbps and the TV keeps up with all its asked to do! I also had some very high definition holiday video and pictures which the old TV struggled to play without hanging...but not the bravia 5! It didn’t buffer or lag, just played them with ease although there is only 3 usb ports on the TV, not an issue for most people. The TV is on a cabinet, for sound reasons you can choose in the setup where it is to be mounted i.e wall, cabinet  etc  although I have found the sound was a bit hollow and lacking in bass in my opinion which may be different when wall mounted – I will update this review when that’s completed!
I have used my existing sound bar which gives the required level of bass I’m happy with so no problem at all. Although my soundbar isn’t a Sony I’ve read that the Theatre sound bar is amazing so that may be next on my list of acquisitions.
All in all I can recommend this TV fully ,even the unboxing was designed to be simple and help someone remove  it!  Good job Sony!!

body: I've had this TV for a couple of weeks now and I've had some time to get used to it. The picture is fantastic, good uniformity, great upscaling, its very bright and fantastic colour and contrast. I had to decide between the 7 ii and 8 ii and I'm confident I made the right choice having compared them side-by-side. Why only 3 stars then? Well it has a bug which still hasn't been fixed, when you use an Apple TV and try to play some content the screen will go black, you have to press the home key and select the HDMI input again. I read this bug was introduced a couple of firmware updates back and that Sony is aware. It's not like the Apple TV is a niche product is it? Second star was removed because of how dreadful Google TV is now, its just a giant advert on your home screen, you have to navigate around through the adverts to get to the app you want to use. I just have it start on the Apple TV input straight away. With that said, it's probably the least intrusive smart tv you can buy right now. It is a great TV though, good tech, excellent picture, sound is decent, I don't regret buying it, I just hope Sony sorts out the software.

body: We had wanted a Bravia tv for a long time and had been impressed by the picture quality. We purchased the 55 inch and are happy with the colour depth and overall picture. However, the sound is another matter. Several times a day, we lose the "lip synch" on all channels. Actors or newsreaders voices are totally out of synch with the show being viewed. We are constantly implementing the hard restart, as described in Sony's troubleshooting steps. This is a very annoying fault. The screen also pixelates for a couple of seconds, now and then. Actually, this sometimes seems to trigger the lip synch problem. Today, while watching the tv news, the sound just went off completely. Nobody in the house was anywhere near the remote control. It would not come back on until I restarted the tv again. These problems have taken away all the fun and excitement, of having a new tv. The picture for the most part is fine but this sound problem really does need attention by Sony. I actually spoke to a friend in the US who has the same tv. My friend also confirmed that they are regularly having to restart the tv, with the same lip synch problem. I think Sony really needs to address this issue.

body: There is little doubt, this is an exceptional TV, Sony are now the top of their game compared to other brand which have sold themselves out to cheaper and poorer quality products. body: Had it a month now and needed a full factory reset as the usb ports  stopped working.TV is lovely with one all too common exception. It's a high quality TV but Sony have cut corners to save money. Why oh why don't they provide all 4 HDMI with the 120Hz this TV deserves. 1 is reserved for the ARC soundbar system which only leaves 1 of the remaining 3 ports with the quality 120Hz ports. If like me you have a firestick as well as a TV Box you have a dilemma. Which one gets the it. Your only option is to buy an HDMI splitter box to share the port but if you do that make sure you buy one with a remote control otherwise you'll have to keep getting up to manually switch between the boxes because the first Switcher I bought was advertised as an auto switcher (with no remote needed) which can detect you switching to another input and auto switch to it. Only it can't because firesticks do not fully power down rendering the auto switch unable to switch. This type of annoying 'get around' could all have been avoided if Sony were to make all 4 HDMI inputs the high quality 120Hz ports we should be given. Hope this helps you make a happy purchase without the disappointment of realising what else you need to look into.

body: Phenomenal TV.

I have no doubt that this is a great TV picture-wise. Sound quality from the screen speakers is pretty dire unfortunately and is in desperate need of an add-on sound bar, sub-woofer and ideally, rear speakers. I could not get my existing non-4K system to work with it. Sony have their own versions of all 3 add-ons, but are ridiculously expensive, adding the equivalent cost of the TV again. I have bought the sound bar and will be adding the sub-woofer shortly. The rears can wait for now. 
The great advantage of the Sony add-on products is that they so easy to set up. The TV itself, is not quiet so. You need to realise that this is a Google TV and will require a Google Account in addition to a Sony one. There are a few things in the set up that worry me, from a privacy point of view, so just be careful as you give permissions.
Colour calibration was not too bad straight out of the box, but be aware, trying it yourself can be tricky if you don't understand the technicalities - it's far more than brightness and contrast. The supplied documentation is pretty useless, but there are some informative videos on the net that demonstrate how the parameters work. I've been tweaking for a few days now and I'm pretty close to how I like it.
I'm pretty pleased with the product now that it is enhanced, but I could not live with it sound-wise in just the boxed state. That makes it a very expensive option that I sort of new might be the case, but still comes as a shock.

body:
I got this tv about 2 weeks ago and I must say I'm pretty impressed so far. I'll start with the caveat that my previous telly is a 14 year old LG 3d Smart Telly, so I might mention features that have been around for a bit, but I think these comments are mostly product specific features.

I'll start with the only slight negative. The initial set-up was a bit onerous, even, for someone who just about still considers on the right side of tech savvy - this was for setting up the Google Home and Bravia Connect features of the telly. Ultimatley i think it was worth it it, but it might intimidate those of an older generation. (though i think you can skip all this process in favour of not using the full potential of the telly)

One of the things I did like in the set up was how it calibrates the sound of the telly in your room. It turns on it's microphone, tells you to be quite and fires a mutlitude of star wars-esque sounds into the room and listens to itself!

So onto the goodstuff - the positives:
- it asks you at the start to name all your streaming subscriptions (ie apple +, netflix, prime, disney etc), and then gives you recommendations and new releases on the home menu based on the subscriptions you are a part of which i find really useful!
- the screen itself is actually a speaker and apparently the sound corresponds with where say the speaker on screen is located on screen. I don't know about that, but it makes for a very crisp sound (from someone who is used to **** sound from flat screen tellys and having to use a soundbar instead)
- I made a point of watching movies with a lot of dark/night scenes (the Batman, Titanic) in it to check out the dark contrast. So much definition even in the darkness!
- I watched the Olympics too, and couldn't believe live coverage could be so crisp and clear
- I also got the playstation going on it and delighted with the picture and sound, though will have to find an adapter to connect my old nintento wii to it!
-The control gently lights up when you nudge or pick it up. Not a feature i thought i needed but so useful when watch something with the lights off!
- The look of it. I know, a telly is a telly, and they kinda all look the same, but the little stand that comes with it is actually quite elegant, and has a few variations to allow you to sit something under it. Equally the fact that the screen itself has very little 'frame' around it is what sets it apart from my old telly, which is of a similiar size (see picture) but the 8" difference in screen size is mostly accommodated in the smaller framing

This pic is not great, i haven't yet committed to the faff of taking the old telly off the wall, and wall mounted the new one, probably should have paused the movie for a photo too, but hopefully you get the picture!
author: Brian Keane

body:
For the purpose of transparency, we have moved from a 12 year old 26" TV to this one so everything is very much updated from that! That said, we have been very impressed with this product. In the week since it was delivered we have thoroughly tested it with all manner of things from 4K UHD movies to gaming and on everything we have been blown away. Gaming playback was very smooth and we saw details that we hadn't been able to before. We even compared Disney+ on our previous HD streaming device through the TV to the built in Google TV app and the difference was amazing. Picture detail and colour are so much better. The TV also automatically switches to show the best quality picture available which means no messing about with settings every time you change content.

An unexpected bonus of this product has been the sound which comes out of the screen like it does in a cinema and gives us a sort of surround sound without the use of additional speakers.

Set up out of the box was pretty straight forward but you do need to have it connected to the Internet to maximise the functionality. Buyer beware that this means that everything is going through Google. You will also need 2 people to get it out of the box and then onto the TV stand as it's obviously a mighty beast but it was easy to do after that!

Overall this is a great future-proof product that is ready for the streamers' content to catch up with it.

body:
First thought upon opening the box, was that it was a fair weight. The legs are sturdy and the quality of the TV could be seen by the eye.
I turned the TV on and plugged my Apple TV in, the TV went into setup mode which took only a few minutes. Once set up, it brought up a scene in the grand canyon... me and my Wife both said ''WOW''. The colours and quality were outstanding!

We went straight onto Disney+ to watch something in 4K! I never want to go back to watching a film in HD again. Surprisingly, the speakers on the TV itself are great. I usually have 2 x Apple HomePods as a surround sound system. I would 100% recommend the Sony Bravia 8

This is the highest spec TV I've ever owned. I used to watch a 43" LG smart TV that was pretty damned good, but this Bravia is a whole new experience! 

*Out of the box - super slim, sleek and attractive
*Very easy to set up (including adding the feet - doddle). I particularly liked the accessibility feature of having a voice assistant to take you through every single step of the set-up process, this was easy to turn off however and I did so. If my 75 year old mum was setting this up she would be able to follow the voice instructions and not have a meltdown! 
*Apps are easy to set-up, I was watching Netflix within about 5 minutes of plugging it in.
*Settings are pretty straightforward to access and play with, to be honest the factory settings for picture were pretty spot on for my preferences so I left it almost as it is. I had a good play though, to explore what's possible.
*I am now using the surround sound feature for audio, and it does make a difference - impressed. The speakers are pretty decent for a TV, no distortion at high volume, not annoying at high volume either. I love that you can zoom in on the voice, this is fab for me as my hearing has declined a bit of late (age lol) and this feature makes it so much easier to hear dialogue.
*Amazing range of brightness, contrast etc, I have set it to auto adjust to the light in the room. 
*Picture clarity is fantastic, no matter what angle you're watching from! My living room has a sofa directly in front of the TV and one at 90 degrees to the TV - those sitting and viewing from the side can see the picture perfectly with no problem. 
*Colours are vivid and distinct, easily adjustable and super realistic. Blacks are deep and velvety. Image is super sharp and realistic - husband stood and stared and said it felt like it was in 3D - this is his first experience of a high spec TV too, he was extremely impressed.
*It's got plenty of eco features which I love! There are some features in settings to do with picture and audio that aren't accessible if you have the TV on energy saving mode which is a pain, but obviously you can turn this on and off - if I'm watching a nature documentary or something that required the highest quality viewing experience (rather than re-runs of Friends haha) then I will turn the energy saving mode off for the duration. easy.
*The only drawback for me is the amount of reflection - I have had a look at other reviews of the product and apparently this TV handles reflection well but I'm not sure I agree.  Maybe it's because the screen is glossy and I'm not used to that with my older TV. It's not a massive issue though.  When there's less light / night time, the watching experience is absolutely fantastic, faultless. It's just that I can see the venetian blinds very clearly reflected during a sunny day (which it has been since I got the TV!

Overall, an awesome piece of technology, and there are still some bits that I have not yet explored, but so far so great. Very impressed, well done Sony!

body:
I have had the TV now for about 5-6 months and is my first true smart TV. I use it for both internet based apps access such as BBC iPlayer etc but also Freesat from an external dish (old Sky dish). The picture quality is excellent in all cases.  The TV's sound is very good for what it is with surprisingly good bass.  However it is not going to sound the same a a proper AV set-up with separate amp and speakers obviously. As with most smart TV's using native TV speakers etc there is a problem with clarity and volume when it comes to dialogue particularly in films.  There are some settings you can

 use to try and tweak it a bit but basically at least a centre speaker needs to be added.

Whilst on the subject of sound the TV has lost sound on apps such as TVX or iPlayer and no amount of changing settings will bring it back.  The only way is to switch off unplug at the mains and leave it.  I don't knowhow long you need to do this for some on forums say 10 mins I left mine 24 hours as I was away anyway.  All was well once plugged  back in.

Updates are another weird thing I have  set it to automatically keep up to date but it has randomly started updating whilst we are watching a program.  I could do nothing but leave it and eventually after 30 mins or so I was able to get to react to the remote once again.

However I can live with these few foibles as overall this a fantastic TV.  I am yet to try other sources such as DVD player etc but I have no doubt it will equally impressive.

My only reservation is  for how long software updates will be available.  My son has a Sony smart TV that is just about 5 years' old and updates are no longer provided therefore apps can no longer be supported/used

body:
I bought the TV in January and all I can say is this has one hell of a picture.  After playing around with the settings I have got the picture to look amazing. At times it is so clear and vivid it is simply captivating. All built on apps work amazingly. With full HDR in YouTube and the Dolby vision presentation on Disney plus is stunning. One other thing I have noticed is the sound. The TV uses the screen as the speakers and this can truly trick you into thinking you have speaker positioned behind you at times. I've had no problems with motion and when playing the PS5 it looks incredible.  Being OLED the blacks are black and the colours are so deep and bright it's just so impressive.  
 
Design wise, it's very nice, although mine 8a wall hung so don't get to appreciate just how thin it is. Wall mounting was easy with an off the shelf bracket as well. The ports available are what is required. 2 hdmi 2.1 port are provided for 4k120 signals from ps5 and with the latest update, VRR has been activated.  The one downside to the ports is the ethernet socket. It is not a gigabit port so is limited to 100mbps. The WiFi on the other is much faster and there is also a usb 3.0 port so a usb to ethernet adapter can be used to get full gigabit wired ethernet. 
 
All in all I can not fault the set. The picture is so much clearer than even my old Sony 4k TV and the HDR quality when watching something like toy story 4 on Disney plus is just breathtaking. At times the lights on the fairground rides are so bright and vibrant it looks real.

body:
This is my first new TV in 12 years. I'm a bit annoyed that you have to sign your life away to use a TV these days, in the same way as mobile phones and computers. Bloatware everywhere, T&C's, updates, load this, do that, agree to let everyone track all your info and do what they want with it.
And then the TV actually crashed the first time I signed into my Google account! Not a good start at all.
Regarding the picture quality, I'll be honest, I didn't research enough regarding the difference between HD and 4K/UHD.
If you watch 4K/UHD content on this TV (there's a growing number of boxsets/movies on Prime, Netflix, Sky etc) the picture is stunning, absolutely superb. I have no complaints there at all.
However, if you watch HD content (which is basically everything on normal terrestrial channels), I've found the upscaling a bit ropey sometimes. Maybe it's because it's a 75" screen, so any image fuzziness or jagged edges on text on the screen really stands out a lot. Also, it seems worse for the first 10-15 minutes after switching the TV on, and then seems to get better. It's almost like the processor takes a bit of time to wake up before it starts working properly.
I've only had the TV a week so maybe it's just a case of getting used to it, as my old TV was only 45". I hope so, because right now I have very mixed feelings about this product.

body:
I have been bowled over by the new TV which I have had wall-mounted, and although the 55" screen is by far the largest I have owned its slimline looks fit effortlessly into the surroundings and provide an excellent focal point for the room. 

The picture quality is excellent, often breath-taking with OLED showing true colours without garishness.     The sound is very natural with an excellent spread, and after two 
weeks use I do not think it will require back-up from a sound-bar for any types of programme (which for me includes classical music).

One thing made me hesitate on purchase: the absence at present of UK streaming services for BBC iplayer, ITV Hub, All4 and My5 as noted by others.    Apparently the word from Sony is that these will be added over the coming months when licenses are in place for this new model.   However the purchase of a Fire TV Stick (very inexpensive and tucked away behind the screen) provides everything immediately.

This TV is expensive, but its performance for me so far leaves me in no doubt that it is value for money.

body:
Definitely the most impressive and capable television I've ever owned. Brilliant picture. Fantastic audio. The app ecosystem is great (although still limited at the moment - no BBC iPlayer, ITV Hub, or Sky Go, for instance). The ability to use Steam Link baked into the TV with no extra hardware is fantastic.

But we haven't been without issue: Apps like Netflix, Prime Video, or other content directly cast to the TV would close for no apparent reason. In one case the TV via aerial wouldn't start. To fix these required different approaches: app caches to be cleared, the TV restarted, and in one case a factory reset. It's really taken the shine off an otherwise brilliant TV.

So, in summary, a fantastic television for video and audio and capability, but just too many software bugs to ever feel confident that's it's not going to just stop at any moment.

body: There is no doubt that this is a very competent TV. I had the 55-inch ag9 previously and this TV is marginally better, but whether it's worth an additional £1000 is subjective.

The PQ on the TV is only OK, considering the price. To be honest, based on my experience, I feel I’ve paid a high price to be a beta tester. Despite having very good download speeds, apps constantly crash with either no sound, picture frozen or both. The operating system is slow to respond and has failed to respond far too many times in the two weeks since arriving. Only a plug pull has brought the TV back to life. Add to that the fact the A90J lacks the advertised UK catch-up TV services, the A90J has proven a very expensive mistake. One can only hope as time goes by and Google TV matures, the stability of the system does too, maybe then I will enjoy it but, not before.

body:
I received my TV approximately two weeks ago. Where do I start? Firstly this tv was very well packed, in fact this is probably the best packed tv I have ever had. Setting up was a doddle and the Google tv interface is very easy and intuitive to use. The higher of the two different leg positions meant it could happily accommodate my AV centre speaker. I suppose when it boils down to it, people really want to know what the picture quality is like. This, I can honestly say, is far and away the best picture I have ever had the pleasure to experience in a TV. The SD upscaling is spot on and when feeding a 4K HDR blue ray through the TV then you can see where the money went into making this incredible beast. The secular highlights, jump out at you and the pure blacks that OLED televisions are renowned for, make the picture almost appear 3D due to the contrast. I may be biased because this is the first OLED I have ever owned, my last 2 4K tv’s have been of the Qled type and whilst they were good, this television is in a league of it’s own.
If you are currently in the market for a ne TV and it falls within your budget range, I would highly recommend it to you. You will find it hard to see a better set this year. Great product SONY.

body: I bought this Sony Bravia 3 as a replacement for my previous LG OLED. My main priority was finding a lower-budget 55-inch TV with a built-in Chromecast and Google TV/Android system. I needed this specifically to download international apps that LG, Samsung, and even the Amazon Fire Stick do not support due to app store limitations. Watching programs through a web browser was too messy, so this Sony completely solved that problem for me. I am very happy to finally have all my international apps directly on the home page.In terms of image quality, this Sony is definitely more basic compared to an OLED. It lacks the deep colors, contrast, and realistic depth of my previous TV, where I could see every fine detail like skin pores. Darker scenes are also harder to perceive. I managed to improve the picture slightly by following online tutorials and turning off the motion smoothing filters, but I still miss the OLED quality. However, given the lower price point, you cannot have everything, and the TV meets my main priority.Cons: The TV takes a bit of time to connect to the internet and load the home page at start-up. My previous TV didn't have this delay, though it could be related to my internet connection.Final Verdict: If you are used to an OLED, you will notice the drop in picture quality. However, for anyone upgrading from a standard or mid-range TV, the quality will be perfectly fine. It is an excellent budget choice if you need a smart TV with great app availability.

body:
I was persuaded to buy this tv over another brand by the salesperson who highlighted the superior picture quality.  The picture is good from many angles.  The reason I have given it 3 stars is that while it does receive satellite signals, it doesn't have Freesat.  Having previously had a TV which did, this seems like a backwards step.  In addition, the EPG is pretty useless.  It rarely displays info for all channels despite being set to acquire this info in standby mode.  Neither can you scroll through info for other channels while watching a channel.  You have to go to the EPG to look up what is on - that's if you are lucky enough to have the info on there!.  On our old TV you could scan through the info for each channel to decide what to watch, while it still showed the programme you are on.
Setting it up was also a 'clunky' as it asked you to choose options for the Satellite set up which most people wouldn't have heard of.  It then took a looooong time to scan for channels.
So, in conclusion, I have to say that I am disappointed with the very limited EPG but satisfied with the picture quality.  This Smart TV isn't very smart in certain areas.

Overall, it works well enough, and the picture is just as good as the previous model. We use an external sound bar which is needed as the incorporated speakers are as poor as you'd expect. Interaction with the connected Apple tv is inconsistent - sometimes each will switch the other on and off, and sometimes not. Also, the tv takes far longer to start up than I expected, given the rate of progress in electronics over the last decade. However, despite being about the same size as the set I bought ten years ago, this new one was half the price, so I can't really complain. Another plus, is that this model doesn't use an external power brick - the set plugs directly into the mains.

body:
We bought this new Sony TV a few weeks ago. Had it installed and setup by TV supplier. It needed some resetting within a week as some faces appeared plastic and stretched (very unflattering) and there was intermittent glitches on the screen that started maybe once an hour, but by the time the installer came about a week later, the glitches were about every 20 minutes and annoying. The glitches only lasted a second or so, but disturbed our concentration on the programme. 
The repairer came and reset everything and it now works much better.  
I’ll wait to see if it keeps working OK, otherwise I’ll have to call the shop back to send their repair er person to fix it, or replace it.  Hopefully that won’t be necessary. 
One reason we chose this particular TV is because if the 5-year guarantee-warranty.   As it seems modern TVs are not as good as old fashioned TVs that lasted for years and years without any problems.  Like most modern goods these days, modern smart TVs appear to be built to fail instead of lasting for many years.

body:
My K-43S3 is a massive disappointment. I bought it to replace my Sony KDL-40W605B (probably about 15 years old) which no longer gave me access to BBC iPlayer etc. (Sony blamed the BBC for this, but it was actually Sony to blame). Some 99% of TV stations are SD and my old Sony TV had a slightly better clarity of picture than the new TV. HD is marginally better than my old TV. 
Only plus points is that I now have access to BBC iPlayer, Channel 4 etc. As for Google TV I haven't quite worked out yet what exactly it is. A manual would have been helpful (I'm fully aware that there is a digital manual via the TV but that involves having to go back and forward from one to the other).

body: This TV replaced its predecessor dur to an accident leaving the previous 12month old one not repairable.  Whilst there is a possible slight improvement on the picture, it he functionality has dramatically gone down hill. To watch live Tv or iplayer, bbc sounds etc, you now have to access these via Sonys ‘Live TV & catch up app which is diabolical & practically next to useless. The app doesn’t always load & can sometimes take half an hour of trying to get in to it! Why would I want to access these through another app when previously they were on the main screen with all the other services?!?! Because if this the process the ‘TV’ button in the remote doesn’t work - so why is it there? At the same time whilt watching live Tv you can no longer press the down arrow to get the guide at the bottom of the TV something else that has gone backward. Honestly compared to its 12 month old predecessor it’s terrible. Would never have bought it if I’d known. Sony when you update your models make sure you are making them better & easier to use, not slower & frustrating to use. I do not recommend this TV - especially if you are a previous Sony Tv owner. body:
For a personal Christmas present, both me and my dad wanted to put our money together towards a brand new TV for my bedroom. In the Hughes store, we were quickly drawn to this TV with it's beautiful picture quality and ideal size. From early on, we knew this was a descent TV!

Through Hughes, we did run into fitting issues, which were amended at a later date. We had fitters coming to mount a TV which had not been delivered on time. We were able to reschedule the fitting and get the TV mounted. The Hughes mounting team quickly setup the TV and I was all good.

It has been very convenient having many 'Smart' features built-in the TV, for easy access. Unfortunately, I have noticed when the electricity socket is completely switched off, this TV is very slow with it's start-up. This is a problem with many modern TVs, particularly Smart ones. Old fashioned TVs were quick to start-up, even when electricity sockets had been turned off.

The voice command remote control is fantastic, this has been the only TV remote I have had to use. It came with another TV remote which is still in it's packaging. It has been very easy to use to voice command to find things faster than navigating through various menus.

Overall, I am very happy with the purchase.

body: Excellent high definition picture, quick response to program selection etc

We bought this a couple of weeks ago, chiefly because our Freesat box had begun to give a warning that iPlayer would cease to work on it in January. Buying a new TV with Satellite built in seemed the obvious answer, and it would also give us access to ITVX, which our old TV couldn't deliver.

As a device, our new TV is probably all that you would expect of a modern Sony TV - classy picture, good sound (we also bought a cheapish soundbar to help with my wife's failing hearing). I really dislike the home screen, which is basically just a lot of advertising for subscription-only channels that we don't have, but I can more or less live with that. Initial installation was pretty easy, which got us to viewing the OTA channels. But then the less satisfactory aspects began to show. It took ages to find out how to install iPlayer - which after all was the trigger for buying it in the first place. Finally, after hours of online searching I found I had to download and install yet another app. Well, okay, now it works fine, but why is this not pre-installed for the UK market? 

Then I integrated it with Alexa so we could use voice control. That worked for about a day, and now Alexa keeps saying it can't contact the TV. I'm sure I can sort that out, but it's just more hassle. And then we get to the programme guide... This is almost completely useless. One key on the remote takes you to the guide... which shows you a list of channels with absolutely no program information at all! To see what's on a channel, you have to click on it, let the current program load, and then go back to the guide. To see your viewing choices for the evening on OTA TV, you have to do this for EVERY channel in turn. An internet search says this is likely because of poor signal, but our old Freesat box never had any trouble. I'm still working on this, but why does it not just work out of the box? Most unsatisfactory.

This leaves me with very mixed feelings about the purchase, and I'm wondering if I should have found another solution to the original problem.

body:
Only had it a week or so but it’s already giving good results, easy to set up and the picture is as good as my larger Bravia in the main room. Off centre viewing is better than others I looked at and the standard colour setup needed little tweaking for my taste. Sport viewing has good sharp movement viewing and I’ve had no buffering on watching a variety of media via apps. Sound is fairly good via front projection speakers and decent options so maybe only use a soundbar for an intense 
movie experience. 

Only very minor (and easily resolved) issue is that watching ITV X on the Bravia has a second app at the right hand end of the app menu bar so you’ll find it easiest to delete the first one and move the other app into its place, now working perfectly and less than 5 minutes to fully setup. All round an excellent quality TV, there are cheaper ones available but this is a different league and close on as good as ones double the money, I’m happy and recommend it (and yes, I did pay for it and got no special incentive to do so. I’m not an influencer and just a buyer happy to pass my views on for others to consider).

I read this bug was introduced a couple of firmware updates back and that Sony is aware. It's not like the Apple TV is a niche product is it? Second star was removed because of how dreadful Google TV is now, its just a giant advert on your home screen, you have to navigate around through the adverts to get to the app you want to use. I just have it start on the Apple TV input straight away. With that said, it's probably the least intrusive smart tv you can buy right now. The EPG is right there, you would be on it to set a recording up, but then you have to MANUALLY PROGRAM ALL OF THE SCHEDULE DETAILS YOU WANT TO RECORD - like a video recorder from 30 years ago. All of the information you need is in the EPG, but no, you cannot select it and pass that information through to the Scheduler, you have to remember it all. My opinion, this feature is so bad it should be withdrawn, and not mentioned in any marketing. To be clear, this is software, it is entirely in the hands of the manufacturer to provide, they can even put it in an update, but it is not there, and no plans to include it.

body:
Very good value for the price point. The picture is sharp and clear. Audio through the built in speakers is poor. All flat penel TVs suffer in this respect in varying degrees.My previous Panasonic was better on audio.

Facilities are good, with the 3x HDMI connections being very useful for PVR and DVD connections.

USB is also very useful, but you cannot browse your local network for media such as photos or MP4 videos to view.. This means transferring to USB to watch. Unnecessary, given the network connection built-in!

Ther network connectivity is good, but has very limited control and information about the connection status and speed..Sony could do better here, and allow local network access to make this TV more useful.

The menu structure is a bit difficult, some things easy tgo find, others buried elsewhere. Some settings do not 'stick' and have to be made again.

The auto chamnnel update seems to drop channels every night, meaning a re-scan is required tro restore them. Turning off auto-update does appear to solve this strange event..

As a basic TV it is fine, just do not expect too much (which you would expect from a quality brand like Sony!) and it is fine within its limitations, and at the lower end of the market..

body:
We've had a Sony Bravia KDL-40EX503 for well over a decade now and it still works like new and has a picture that is comparable with today's best.
During this timespan we've had 5 cheap to mid range 32" TVs that my Bravia has put to shame, all of which had pretty poor screens in comparison and didn't last long at all, you buy cheap, you buy twice, or in our case 5 times.
I thought it was about time to stop buying cheap over and over again and buy my wife a good, reliable TV that will maintain it's excellent quality, hopefully, for as long as mine has, the Bravia KD32W800 was the obvious choice.
Having a wonderful, bright, sharp picture with lifelike colour, wide viewing angle and easy to set up, it's way, way better than any of the other 32" telly's we've had .
Also, being a smart TV with Wi-Fi connectivity, it now gives her a huge choice of programmes to watch.
We both love it.

body:
I found this TV easy to assemble (2 x legs) and connect up to hdmi and aerial inputs. 
This TV comes with Chromecast built in so there was no need for me to connect my old Chromecast. 
 
On initial power up the unit goes into setup mode. As this is an android TV I was able to quickly connect to my Google account using my phone. This allowed me to quickly access the play store and download apps. 
 
Once the TV channels we're setup I was able to view the HD channels and the images were crystal clear, really good quality. I was especially impressed with how good the sound quality was, even when the volume was turned up loud there was no distortion. 
The remote control had a record button which isn't available to use it of the box. I discovered that if you insert a usb memory stick in the rear usb slot and setup as external storage, the record function is available. You can also pause and rewind TV too. You can only record the channel you are watching, if you change channel it will stop recording though and you can't say a record for a future program on the guide like on a PVR. It did appear to keep recording if the TV is turned off though. 
 
Many apps come preinstalled such as Netflix, Spotify etc which all worked well. 
There is WiFi to connect to the network and Bluetooth to connect the remove and headphones. 
 
One of the best features is the mic button on the remote which opens the Google assistant and allows you to request apps to be opened, or select a TV channel if you don't know the number. See my video for more features. 
 
The TV bezel is very small making this a very compact unit as well as being very light. 
I was impressed with all features and could find no faults, it's a fantastic smart television.

body: It is a very wonderful product with a clear picture, good sound quality and we are enjoying the product.

I expected far more from this TV, especially considering the price.

The OLED panel does provide excellent contrast and a very sharp picture, but in my experience the colour reproduction is disappointing. I have tried numerous picture modes and settings, yet I still cannot get the image to look as natural as I would expect from a premium television.

The sound quality is also poor. In fact, I have older TVs that sound noticeably better, which is difficult to justify on a product at this price level.

My biggest issue, though, is how unnecessarily complicated LG has made the whole experience. There are far too many menus, settings, options and customisations for what should be a simple household device. I work in IT and am very comfortable with technology, yet I have still found this TV frustrating to set up and difficult to configure exactly how I want it.

There is also too much LG advertising and promotional content built into the interface, along with screensavers and other features that are far harder to disable than they should be.

The TV feels like a product designed by engineers who have forgotten that most people simply want to switch it on, watch something and have it look and sound good. Instead, LG has turned a basic everyday item into something unnecessarily complex and over engineered.

I would be particularly concerned about recommending this to an older person or anyone who is not confident with technology, as I think many people would find the setup and menu system overwhelming.

For the money, I expected excellent picture quality, good sound and a polished, simple user experience. What I got was impressive contrast, disappointing colour, poor sound and an interface that constantly gets in the way.

At this price, that is simply not good enough.

I would not recommend this TV.

body: Best TV I've ever had. Picture quality is excellent.

I couldn't be happier with the LG OLED65C55LA. From the moment I switched it on, the picture quality was simply breathtaking. The OLED panel delivers incredibly deep blacks, vibrant colours, and outstanding contrast that make films, TV shows, and games look absolutely stunning. Whether watching in a dark room or during the day, every scene feels immersive and lifelike.

The 65-inch screen is the perfect size for creating a true cinema experience at home. HDR content really shines, with excellent brightness and detail in both dark and bright scenes. Sports are smooth and clear, while movies look exactly as the directors intended.

Gaming performance is equally impressive. The low input lag and smooth refresh rate make fast-paced games feel responsive and fluid. Features like HDMI 2.1 support ensure the TV is ready to get the best from modern gaming consoles.

The smart TV features are intuitive and easy to use. LG's webOS platform is fast, responsive, and provides access to all the major streaming services. Navigation is straightforward, and the Magic Remote makes finding content effortless.

The design is sleek, modern, and premium-looking. Its ultra-thin profile and minimal bezels allow the screen to take centre stage and look fantastic in any living room.

Overall, the LG OLED65C55LA delivers exceptional performance across the board. The combination of stunning OLED picture quality, excellent gaming features, user-friendly smart functionality, and elegant design makes it one of the best televisions I've ever owned. Highly recommended to anyone looking for a premium TV experience that truly impresses every time you switch it on.

body: Mediocre for the price. Pictures OK, Sounds OK. Does not support FreelyTV - but that is partly the fault of the way Freely is implemented. Live channel information and program guide is very flaky and unreliable. At least 50% of the time, the TV can not tell you what programme is currently playing or what/when the next program will be. This is frustrating, but the real kicker is that you can not change channel when the information is not available - the TV can not 'remember' what the channel map is, so if you try to go to a channel and there is no 'current' information, then the TV refuses to change channel. This is infuriating. You have to resort to scrolling through a hundred channels to reach the one you are interested in - and then if you don't want to watch it - you have to scroll all the way back again. I guess TVs are aiming themselves at streaming services and don't care about live broadcast channels any more. If you shut this TV off while watching a live channel, then turn it back on, it reverts to the digital streaming home page, rather than opening the channel you were previously watching. Overall - the TV is fine - but it has been a very underwhelming experience, and I wish I had saved some money.

body:
I’ve spent some time looking into the 55-inch LG C5 OLED evo AI 4K Smart TV, and honestly—it’s one of those TVs that’s just really easy to like.

The first thing you notice is the picture. It looks seriously good. Blacks are properly black (not that washed-out grey you get on cheaper TVs), and colours pop without looking fake. Watching movies on it feels a bit more “cinema-like,” especially in a dim room. It’s also brighter than older LG C-series models, which helps if you’re not always watching in the dark.

Where it really surprised me is gaming. If you’ve got a PS5 or Xbox, this thing is kind of a dream—super smooth, very responsive, and it supports all the modern features without any fuss. It just works, and it works well.

The smart TV side is solid too. LG’s interface isn’t perfect, but it’s fast enough and has all the apps you’d expect, so you’re not fighting the system just to watch something.
That said, it’s not flawless. The sound is… fine. Not bad, but definitely not impressive—you’ll probably end up wanting a soundbar. And while it’s bright for an OLED, it’s not the brightest TV out there, so if your room gets a lot of sunlight, that’s something to keep in mind.

It’s a really well-rounded TV. Nothing about it feels gimmicky—it just delivers great picture quality, excellent gaming performance, and a smooth everyday experience. If you want a premium TV without overthinking it too much, the C5 is a very safe bet.

body:
I recently bought the LG 65” C5 OLED, and after spending some time with it, I can honestly say it’s one of the best TVs I’ve ever owned.

The picture quality is phenomenal. The OLED panel delivers perfect blacks and incredible contrast, which makes movies and shows look stunning, especially in dark scenes. My favourite profile is Filmmaker Mode giving near accurate colours, and the level of detail in 4K content is outstanding. Watching Dolby Vision content on this TV genuinely feels cinematic.

The brightness is impressive for an OLED especially after the recent firmware update.

For gaming, this TV is fantastic. With HDMI 2.1 ports, 4K at 120Hz, VRR, and extremely low input lag, it pairs perfectly with my PS5. Motion is smooth and responsive, making fast-paced games feel incredibly fluid.

The webOS interface is fast and easy to use, with all the major streaming apps available. Navigation is smooth, and the Magic Remote makes browsing and searching surprisingly easy.

Overall, the LG C5 65” delivers exceptional picture quality, top-tier gaming performance, and a premium design. If you're looking for a high-end OLED TV that excels for movies, streaming, and gaming, this one is absolutely worth it.

I upgraded to the LG C5 55” from a Philips Ambilight TV and couldn’t be happier with the decision. The picture quality is genuinely stunning — blacks are inky deep, colours are vibrant without being over-saturated, and HDR content looks incredible. Whether it’s films, sport, or gaming, everything looks noticeably sharper and more lifelike. The brightness is excellent for an OLED and holds up well even in a bright room. Motion handling is smooth, and the upscaling of HD content is far better than I expected. Gaming performance is also top-tier with low input lag and flawless support for next-gen consoles. webOS is fast, intuitive, and far more responsive than the smart system on my previous TV. Apps load quickly and the interface is clean and easy to navigate. The design itself is sleek and premium, with incredibly thin bezels that really let the picture take centre stage. I was a bit unsure about losing Ambilight, but the sheer quality of the display more than makes up for it. This TV feels like a proper step into the high-end OLED experience. Highly recommended.

body: I chose this model because it was highly rated by Which?, to replace a TV that was 9 years old. The picture quality is the really stand-out thing compared to the TV I'm replacing: it's exceptional, vivid, and the blacks are true black. The TV definitely warrants a 5 star for picture quality.The sound is fine, it's clear and I've no complaints about the depth or bass. We don't have a soundbar, and I don't feel a need to get one.The only reason I scored the TV 4 stars rather than 5, are the menus and to some extent, the magic remote. I'm definitely tech savvy, but it's taken me a few days to find my way around fundamental functions on the TV (e.g. I found it easier to set up "favourite channels", but then it took another couple of days to figure out how to actually access "favourites"). I like the pointer on the Magic Remote, which definitely makes things easier, but the remote is let down by a very simple design flaw: both the "volume up/down" and the "channel up/down" buttons are pure black rubber. There is no visual marking on the buttons, so it's hard to see which is which. I know I'll get used to is, but in the meantime I've actually put a dab of white paint on the +/- and up/down symbols so that they are visible. The menu itself is cluttered, and there doesn't seem to be a way of hiding some the channels (e.g. I've no need for the LG channel at present, and we don't subscribe to channels like Disney, so those apps don't need to be visible on my list ... but they are, and they make it look cluttered.Overall, this is a BRILLIANT TV, and if you can put up with a cluttered menu, an overly-complex system for watching TV, and a good but imperfect remote, then I would recommend this.

body:
This review is for the 42" C55LA - Genuinely beautiful screen and picture quality. I spent ages researching this TV before buying and went to see various TV's in person in a Curry's before purchasing directly from LG online. The OLED display on the C5 looked night and day better than pretty much all of the other screens in store. It looked marginally better than the main rival's OLED display but I noticed odd flickering on the other brand's OLED on certain scenes (across various TV's) and also felt that the build and material quality of the LG C5 was significantly more premium than that of its rival at this size.The 42" is perfect for our space, and it looks awesome - super thin and really nice thin bezel. 
All in all picture quality - deep blacks - super nice with films and even standard TV - looks brilliant.The only downsides are -UK version ships with a pretty poor remote - it feels cheap and it's poorly laid out + very clunky and big. I believe the rest of the world get a nicer remote..
The OS is a bit cumbersome and bloated - there's a few tweaks to make it less so but it's still not a very nice experience. Also the remote cursor thing is genuinely annoying - you should be able to turn that off.
The other downsides are the audio quality - obviously this is a thin device but the audio is poorer than I expected it to be, and I didn't have much home in the first place + the legs that the TV stands on (42" version) are a bit flimsy but they look good.None of the downsides overshadow what is genuinely an unbelievable device with outstanding picture quality (which I find plenty bright btw). If you can get a good deal on this TV just buy it - it's a genuinely wonderful device despite its minor shortcomings.

body: It is a very wonderful product with a clear picture, good sound quality and we are enjoying the product.

I expected far more from this TV, especially considering the price.

The OLED panel does provide excellent contrast and a very sharp picture, but in my experience the colour reproduction is disappointing. I have tried numerous picture modes and settings, yet I still cannot get the image to look as natural as I would expect from a premium television.

The sound quality is also poor. In fact, I have older TVs that sound noticeably better, which is difficult to justify on a product at this price level.

My biggest issue, though, is how unnecessarily complicated LG has made the whole experience. There are far too many menus, settings, options and customisations for what should be a simple household device. I work in IT and am very comfortable with technology, yet I have still found this TV frustrating to set up and difficult to configure exactly how I want it.

There is also too much LG advertising and promotional content built into the interface, along with screensavers and other features that are far harder to disable than they should be.

The TV feels like a product designed by engineers who have forgotten that most people simply want to switch it on, watch something and have it look and sound good. Instead, LG has turned a basic everyday item into something unnecessarily complex and over engineered.

I would be particularly concerned about recommending this to an older person or anyone who is not confident with technology, as I think many people would find the setup and menu system overwhelming.

For the money, I expected excellent picture quality, good sound and a polished, simple user experience. What I got was impressive contrast, disappointing colour, poor sound and an interface that constantly gets in the way.

At this price, that is simply not good enough.

I would not recommend this TV.

The design is sleek, modern, and premium-looking. Its ultra-thin profile and minimal bezels allow the screen to take centre stage and look fantastic in any living room.

Overall, the LG OLED65C55LA delivers exceptional performance across the board.
