author: Chris Smith

body:
This is a review on a Sharp 50HM5345K QLED 4K Ultra HD Dolby Atmos TiVo TV. I was given this to review and whilst I'm able to keep it, this review will be a true honest account of my use of it. 

The legs were very easy to attach. The tv itself contains three HDMI ports, two USB 2.0 ports as well as an ethernet port, optical digital output port, earphone port, Sat in, RF in and AV in ports. 

Once switched on the tv screen comes on quite quickly. The initial setup was quick and very easy to follow, I particularly liked the fact that the tv talked to me when you click on something or move to the next step as it describes what it is, which is great for the visually impaired. This can be turned off if you so wish. Please note this has nothing to do with the usual audio description when a program is playing and the tv describes what the actor/s are doing or feeling etc. When tuning the tv there was three options; cable, antenna and a third I fail to recall (apologies). Whilst we don't have an antenna as we are in a fair new house that the builders failed to install one but we actually use the internet and wifi, hence why we use smart tv's.The pros and cons. 

The pros; The tv remote has an individual button for Netflix, Prime Video, Disney, YouTube, Freely only. The "source" button is called the "input" with Sharp, which when pressed takes you to a pop box list of all the outputs such as TiVo, Home, Live TV, HDMI 1,2,3 etc which when selected takes you straight to that output.

The TiVo button takes you to the main menu page to either select my apps, Live TV etc.

There is free content on the TiVo+Free, which has dedicated channels for various content on soaps or films or documentaries mainly via either Pluto or Plex, which is a bit like an app / tv channel I kinda likened it Sky entertainment but without the Sky1, Sky Witness etc but it's more old school content with liveTV or content you can search for.

The screen is amazing as it is edge to edge with great quality picturing but sometimes the screen plays up, in what I call glitching so you have to pause the program or come out of it every so often, this has happened 10 times in a space of 7 days.

The tv has three HDMI ports, two USB 2.0 ports as well as an ethernet port.


The Cons; 
The sound when playing a program or film appears lower than usual, and so you need to raise it to 12-14 when watching a program or 14-16 when watching a film whereas my old tv, Hisense 43inch from 2024 you'd have it at 10 for programs and 12 for films. The issue I believe is the speakers on the Sharp tv all appear to be based around the rear of the tv therefore, not projecting forward the sound. 

The tv itself is rated as F for it's energy rating, and does use a fair bit of electricity over £1.00 worth if your home all day watching tv. This doesn't sound alot but in a fairly new house when your daily rate is just short of £3.00 or less, that seems alot as when we wake up in the morning the digital meter says 85-90pence.

We have Netflix, Disney, Prime Video and NowTV but unfortunately Tivo and this Sharp tv isn't set-up to allow you to add/download/upload any tv apps nor is it setup to configure NowTv or even AppleTv apps. So we called the 0330 024 0803 for customer support for help but they advised us there is nothing we can do for now accept just keep an eye out on the "my app" to see if and when they are added by TiVo/Sharp. So we've had to cancel the NowTv, which is highly annoying as it has shows we watch such as SWAT, Rookie and allows us to watch Sky1, Sky Atlantic or Sky Witness.

The Bluetooth doesn't work, it just keeps circling a circle of doom/death as I had thought I could share from my mobile phone or ipad the NowTV but it's not working. I have tried this on four different occasions/time of day and still no joy. I tried casting directly from my ipad but my ipad would not locate the Sharp tv.

There is no Alexa so you cannot link it to that or your Alexa setup that we have or you may have already. We have an Alexa plug in the kitchen for music whilst cooking. We have the kettle in the kitchen linked up to Alexa as well as the livingroom lamp in the livingroom, which can be controlled via voice control on Alexa or via your mobile phones. We have a front doorbell camera, an internal camera for our dog whilst we are out at work along with other camera's that are linked up to the Alexa and our mobiles too. Our old tv Hisense 43" dated 2024 was linked up to Alexa so you got notified of any announcements by Alexa on the tv and you could switch the tv on/off via voice control on Alexa or by your mobile phones - it just seems in today's world not having Alexa on the tv, not having Appletv, NowTV and being unable to upload/download other apps to your tv is a massive step backwards in today's technology and for us is a massive turn-off.

The cost of the tv approx. £395.00 depending on where you purchase it from but with Black Friday deals it was even cheaper but is it worth it, yes if you don't have Alexa or NowTv or AppleTv. But for me the Cons far outway the Pros and I wouldn't buy this tv.

This is a review on a Sharp 50HM5345K QLED 4K Ultra HD Dolby Atmos TiVo TV. I was given this to review and whilst I'm able to keep it, this review will be a true honest account of my use of it. 

The legs were very easy to attach. The tv itself contains three HDMI ports, two USB 2.0 ports as well as an ethernet port, optical digital output port, earphone port, Sat in, RF in and AV in ports. 

Once switched on the tv screen comes on quite quickly. The initial setup was quick and very easy to follow, I particularly liked the fact that the tv talked to me when you click on something or move to the next step as it describes what it is, which is great for the visually impaired. This can be turned off if you so wish. Please note this has nothing to do with the usual audio description when a program is playing and the tv describes what the actor/s are doing or feeling etc. When tuning the tv there was three options; cable, antenna and a third I fail to recall (apologies). Whilst we don't have an antenna as we are in a fair new house that the builders failed to install one but we actually use the internet and wifi, hence why we use smart tv's.The pros and cons. 

The pros; The tv remote has an individual button for Netflix, Prime Video, Disney, YouTube, Freely only. The "source" button is called the "input" with Sharp, which when pressed takes you to a pop box list of all the outputs such as TiVo, Home, Live TV, HDMI 1,2,3 etc which when selected takes you straight to that output.

The TiVo button takes you to the main menu page to either select my apps, Live TV etc.

There is free content on the TiVo+Free, which has dedicated channels for various content on soaps or films or documentaries mainly via either Pluto or Plex, which is a bit like an app / tv channel I kinda likened it Sky entertainment but without the Sky1, Sky Witness etc but it's more old school content with liveTV or content you can search for.

The screen is amazing as it is edge to edge with great quality picturing but sometimes the screen plays up, in what I call glitching so you have to pause the program or come out of it every so often, this has happened 10 times in a space of 7 days.

The tv has three HDMI ports, two USB 2.0 ports as well as an ethernet port.


The Cons; 
The sound when playing a program or film appears lower than usual, and so you need to raise it to 12-14 when watching a program or 14-16 when watching a film whereas my old tv, Hisense 43inch from 2024 you'd have it at 10 for programs and 12 for films. The issue I believe is the speakers on the Sharp tv all appear to be based around the rear of the tv therefore, not projecting forward the sound. 

The tv itself is rated as F for it's energy rating, and does use a fair bit of electricity over £1.00 worth if your home all day watching tv. This doesn't sound alot but in a fairly new house when your daily rate is just short of £3.00 or less, that seems alot as when we wake up in the morning the digital meter says 85-90pence.

We have Netflix, Disney, Prime Video and NowTV but unfortunately Tivo and this Sharp tv isn't set-up to allow you to add/download/upload any tv apps nor is it setup to configure NowTv or even AppleTv apps. So we called the 0330 024 0803 for customer support for help but they advised us there is nothing we can do for now accept just keep an eye out on the "my app" to see if and when they are added by TiVo/Sharp. So we've had to cancel the NowTv, which is highly annoying as it has shows we watch such as SWAT, Rookie and allows us to watch Sky1, Sky Atlantic or Sky Witness.

The Bluetooth doesn't work, it just keeps circling a circle of doom/death as I had thought I could share from my mobile phone or ipad the NowTV but it's not working. I have tried this on four different occasions/time of day and still no joy. I tried casting directly from my ipad but my ipad would not locate the Sharp tv.

There is no Alexa so you cannot link it to that or your Alexa setup that we have or you may have already. We have an Alexa plug in the kitchen for music whilst cooking. We have the kettle in the kitchen linked up to Alexa as well as the livingroom lamp in the livingroom, which can be controlled via voice control on Alexa or via your mobile phones. We have a front doorbell camera, an internal camera for our dog whilst we are out at work along with other camera's that are linked up to the Alexa and our mobiles too. Our old tv Hisense 43" dated 2024 was linked up to Alexa so you got notified of any announcements by Alexa on the tv and you could switch the tv on/off via voice control on Alexa or by your mobile phones - it just seems in today's world not having Alexa on the tv, not having Appletv, NowTV and being unable to upload/download other apps to your tv is a massive step backwards in today's technology and for us is a massive turn-off.

The cost of the tv approx. £395.00 depending on where you purchase it from but with Black Friday deals it was even cheaper but is it worth it, yes if you don't have Alexa or NowTv or AppleTv. But for me the Cons far outway the Pros and I wouldn't buy this tv.

Set-up
The set-up process is straightforward, although the HDMI ports located at the bottom are somewhat awkward to access. Installing all the software only takes a couple of minutes.
Picture Quality
The picture is clear and sharp, but the refresh rate can struggle at times. This is particularly noticeable during fast-paced sports like football, where slight lag can occur.
Sound
The sound quality is fairly basic. More frustratingly, I was unable to get the optical connection to work with my Sonos soundbar. The audio often felt unreliable and would occasionally distort quite heavily.
Overall
For the price point, this is a decent TV and one I would generally recommend. However, if you regularly watch sports, it may be worth spending a bit more for better performance.
Overall Score: 7.5/10

body:
The TV is light and a breeze to install - I managed to get it up and running without any help from the hubby. Video and sound quality were pretty decent - TBH I didn't notice much change from my previous TV, but I put this down to the live TV signal received rather than the equipment itself. What I liked the most about this new Sharp TV is (1) the Freely feature - all channels got synced via wifi without the need of an aerial or box and (2) Freely gives you the ability to pause and rewind live TV, something that we had before via the (quite expensive) Virgin TV (3) the remote has separate buttons to access Netflix, Prime, YouTube and others directly, significantly simplifying navigation to switch between stream services. 
The only thing I wasn't very keen on was the voice narrating all my actions, but I found out how to disable this feature before too long (I guess this is useful for those visually impaired...) 
In summary, I'm very pleased with the new TV! Recommend!

body: We recently upgraded to this 50-inch 4K Ultra HD smart TV powered by TIVO and it’s been brilliant for our family. It looks sleek in our living area, blending in without dominating the space. Films and TV look sharper and more vibrant than ever. Im thrilled watching the Kardashians and Love Island in such crisp detail, while my husband dives into World War II documentaries with stunning clarity. The interface is straightforward, the sound is solid, and the kids love the built-in apps. It’s become the centrepiece of our evenings together, and we absolutely recommend it.

Overall the user experience on the Sharp 50″ 4K Ultra HD Smart TV powered by TiVo was of a high standard. From the picture quality and refresh rate of the image to the crisp sound which made you feel immersed in the programme, the set offers a exemplary viewing experience. The user interface felt intuitive and finding the relevant features that I wanted to use came naturally. Of particular ease was the Tivo aspect of the set which was handy in bringing all my watchlists together in a way that cut through more convoluted methods that I have experienced before. I would recommend this product to others.

Easy and straight forward to unpack and setup, it took around 5 minutes. 
After connecting the cables to the Sky Q box the television settings for sound and picture quality were easy to adjust.
The television picture was clear and sharp and the sound quality was good.
It was straight forward to download the Apps and have all the features the television offers up and running in a very short time.
In my opinion the television offers a wide choice of features for the all ages a family would need.
I would recommend the television to family and friends if they were replacing or upgrading their old television.
All in all a good product.

Firstly, this is an excellent TV for the money. Much brighter than my similarly priced and relatively current 50" Hisense TV. The user interface is friendly and generally quick to respond. The remote works well too and I haven't had any issues. The TV speakers are adequate however I also tested the TV with my 5.1.2 surround sound with Dolby Atmos and it all worked perfectly without issue. The build quality of the TV itself seems great including metal legs as opposed to plastic, which is a nice touch. I noted the TV has a good selection of connections available.

I didn't notice any apps that were missing, all the usual suspects are there such as Netflix, Disney+, YouTube, Prime Video, BBC iPlayer etc. All of the apps that I used were responsive and never did I feel like I was waiting around for the TV to load. 

What is TiVo? TiVo is the whole UI/UX experience of the TV, the home screen/main menu where you choose your apps/TV channels. TiVo works exceptionally well, I had no issues with setup and it all worked well. Freely is used for viewing normal TV channels without the need for an aerial connection works well too. I do not watch a lot of TV but I tested it and didn't experience any issues, the picture quality was reasonable.

title: Far from Perfect
body: I had already read here that the feet were difficult to screw but my god, it took me and another person 40 minutes to get it right. The initial set up was easy. The browse function is not, as manually search and bookmark the websites I needed took time. The buttons on the remote are small and too near each other, so it's easy to press by mistake the home button and have to restart all over again what you were doing before. After a couple of days I dared to pair my tv box remote to this smart tv. Since then, whenever I use the mute button on both remote controls, the mute icon flashes continually on screen. I then found out online that this is a common Samsung glitch that will stay forever. I tried everything to sort it, in vain. This morning the connected tv box froze and it had no sound, so I had to reboot it. Samsung tv plus does not have the most common channels like BBC, ITV etc, so you'll have to tune them and watch through an aerial (this is what the inbuilt Freeview means). I bought it just 6 days ago so I'm monitoring for other issues and decide if to keep or not.

title: Does The Job - But Only Just!
body:
This TV was purchase as a replacement for a Samsung 32" TV that was 16 years old. I expected this much newer TV to be superior. However, that wasn't the case (ignoring features that weren't available on the old TV).
Screen brightness is just about adequate, requiring brightness, contrast and shadow detail at maximum during daytime. Sound quality was an immediate disappointment - no bass and very 'boxy'. So I purchased a soundbar - this worked well with connection through HDMI using eARC. There's no need to go for an expensive soundbar - just about anything will be an improvement. Do bear in mind the TV sits on very short legs, so a soundbar in front of the TV would likely block some of the screen. I purchased one that splits in two, providing a speaker at each end of the TV.
There isn't an audio jack on the TV, so I couldn't connect my jack connected wireless headphones.
General operation is slow, often taking seconds to respond to a button on the remote - the operating system seems underpowered, making apps such as the Internet browser very slow.
The remote has a curved back, making it difficult to press buttons when the remote is on a flat surface as the remote will then rotate.
An unexpected bonus was the Samsung TV channel, providing free to view older TV programmes and lesser known films.
Brightness aside, the picture quality is good and the receiver sensitivity better than my old TV.
Although this is a smart TV it doesn't support recording to external storage, though it does support playback (I haven't tested this).
The TV is close to being good, but really needs better speakers and faster operation.

title: Excellent picture and sound for the price
body: I have had this model for about 5 months now and, for the price, its excellent value. Easy to use, set up and install. It comes with all sorts of apps and all the big hitters in the streaming world. The picture for the price is incredible and the sound can be adjusted to all types of specs including movie, sport and gaming. There is, however, one BIG drawback....there is NO freely or Freeview!!!! So unless you go on the apps you cannot watch live TV!! Samsung claim about their network having something like 1000 channels....do not be decieved by this as it doesn't include ANY of our normal channels like BBC, ITV etc....instead you do get quite enjoyable channels like Dragons Den 24 hours, Mr Bean 24 hours etc etc, which can be quite enjoyable at first but repeats soon bore you. So if you are looking for a brilliant TV with brilliant sound and pictures and only want apps...then this TV is for you. Just as a footnote, this is probably excellent for a teen-agers bedroom as they probably won't want conventional TV like us fuddy duddies, and at an amazing price.

title: Great Display for the Price
body:
This is a nice "little" TV (32").   I bought it as a Christmas present to replace a Phlips 24" for our annexe sitting room which is still functioning but which I thought was too small.  My wife has a horror of screen creep, but I think I could have got away with a 40" in the space :)  Next time :)  She's happy with the 32" for now.

The screen itself has a good quality picture (HD) and the audio is fine for our purposes.  I've mounted it flush to the wall so the cheap plastic feet don't matter and I probably get increased volume bounced back into the room.  For larger rooms, a soundbar might be good, but then I'd probably recommend a larger screen anyway.  Also at this size and viewing distance, there's no point with a 4K TV: most content we get is HD anyway which would need to be upscaled, so HD seems optimal for this display.

Wall mounting needs a 200x200 VESA mount.  I needed to use spacers to get the correct offset, but the mounting wasn't difficult.  One of the HDMI ports is on the side which makes access easier (still tight with the mounting option I used).

Initial setup was straightforward via an app on my phone.  I just needed to set up a Samsung account and pass in eg details of the Wifi password which I could do via my phone.  This is much easier than previous TVs I've had to deal with.  Kudos to Samsung here.  I didn't try the TV tuner - that often takes a while to set up/scan channels, but with a Wifi connection there is access to live channels anyway.

The TV has a good range of ports/connections.  Aerial, 2 HDMI (one with eARC), Wifi, Ethernet, USB, Bluetooth.  As usual these days the manual doesn't show the connections (helpful when you're planning an install), but they seem to be shown in the online installation guide.

I don't care about the actual TV tuner function - we only get a few stations here and the signal can be poor - so I have connected it to a Sky Q mini box via HDMI.  Again this was straightforward to do.  Samsung TV plus comes up by default on startup and seems to offer good options and a reasonable user interface including for broadcast channels, but I don't expect to use any of the "smart TV" capabilities.  Others have said the UI was "slow" but I didn't really notice that - maybe when loading apps such as Netflix?  It's definitely more responsive than my 2015 Sony KDL. The remote seems well made and has the usual features, but we won't be using that unless there are settings we can't get at using the Sky remote or it doesn't change to the HDMI input. Switching input to the HDMI port was simple, and renaming it is also not too hard.

Overall, I'm very happy with this at the price and my wife is very happy with the final result

title: Where technology meets art
body:

For movies, it delivers a true cinematic feel — vivid colors, sharp details, and lifelike depth that make every scene unforgettable. Gaming is fluid and immersive, with smooth motion, ultra-low lag, and stunning contrast that pulls you right into the action. Watching football is just as thrilling: every pass, tackle, and fast play is crystal clear, with vibrant colors and perfect sharpness.

When I’m not using it for entertainment, I switch to Portrait Mode and it becomes a beautiful piece of wall art — displaying landscapes, paintings, or personal photos so realistically that guests often think it’s a framed canvas.

The matte display is a highlight, reducing glare and reflections for a soft, premium look that’s easy on the eyes, even in bright daylight. It also enhances art mode, making it blend naturally into my décor.

With its sleek, minimalist design and ultra-thin bezels, this TV isn’t just for watching — it’s part of my home’s style. It’s my cinema, my gaming arena, my stadium, and my art gallery, all in one.

I use it chiefly for streaming foreign-language films on Netflix, and each and every time the picture quality dazzles my eyes.  I should point out, too, that the subtitles come through with excellent clarity.  

Please also observe that the streamlined remote control is a marvel in itself.  No more having to hunt down the right button to push from 50+ buttons (or whatever) on a standard remote control these days!  Your fingers can find at once the needed button--and you're off and running (er, viewing).  

I've had my Samsung TV hanging on the wall as well as sitting on a table:  both ways work fine.  (A table allows for more movebility, of course.)

All in all, the Samsung TV is perfect for my needs, and I highly recommended it.

body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I recently purchased the Samsung Frame TV, and it has completely transformed my living space. With the ability to display various artworks or personal photos, along with customizable frames, it blends effortlessly into any décor.

The QLED display delivers vibrant colors and outstanding picture quality, making everything from movies to artwork look stunning. Its slim, minimalist design ensures it doesn’t resemble a traditional TV, which enhances the aesthetic appeal of any room.

Setup was simple, and I love that it mounts flush against the wall, just like a real picture frame. Additionally, Samsung’s customer service is incredibly efficient—even more streamlined than Apple’s. If any issues arise, they can diagnose the problem over the phone and send a service professional directly to your home for a quick resolution.

Overall, the Samsung Frame TV is an excellent choice for those looking to combine functionality with style. I highly recommend it!

title: Tizen OS issues with DirectTV Stream
body:
Purchased the 32" Class The Frame TV and installed.  Have yet to try out the art subscription, but that likely will happen soon!  It's unfortunate that the One Connect cable for this model is not the same (it's quite large and not very flexible) as the other models which have the "invisible" cable.  We managed to conceal the cable and the One Connect Mini box in an open wall niche, directly behind the TV as I did not want this visible.  So far so good. 

A major complaint is not being able to sign-in to DirectTV Stream with the Tizen OS App downloaded from the App page for Samsung.  The app installs, but does NOT let me login, with error Care Code 201.  I have no problem signing into the DirectTV streaming app on other devices, including FireTV.  Why doesn't the Tizen app for DirectTV stream provide a QR code to scan on your phone for immediate sign-in?  It's only there for new subscribers.  I am a long time DirectTV sat subscriber.  The login credentialing on the Tizen app needs to be updated to include both DirectTV Stream (only) subscribers AND DirectTV Sat subscribers with (former) AT&T/DTV credentials.

title: A Highlight of our Kitchen Remodel!
body: We recently had our kitchen remodeled and needed to replace a small television that my wife had used for morning and early evening news programming to stay abreast of events. The remodel required us to replace the TV and our consultant recommended a Frame TV. I had heard of them but didn't really know much. We purchased the Samsung 32" Frame Smart TV and mounted it on a kitchen wall along with framed prints that complements our new design. When the TV is not in use, we now have artwork from all over the world, including photography, some from the great masters such as Monet and Van Gogh and Elliott Erwitt and the archives from Life magazine in photography displayed. It has become a real conversation piece from the remodel and we enjoy it so much. The TV comes with an assortment of images of art but we "splurged" and paid a reasonable subscription fee for a year of a wide selection of images to be displayed. There are collections that can be based upon season or geography or specific museum collections and with one push of a button on the remote, you can read info about the pieces. The TV itself has a wonderful display and because it is a Smart TV we can stream from any of our services so I enjoy cooking even more while a favorite program is on. We really do love our Samsung Frame TV.

[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I've been using the Samsung The Frame LS03CB QLED 4K TV (2023) for a while now, and it has completely transformed my living room. The TV is not just a piece of technology but has become the focal point and centerpiece of the space. The way it seamlessly blends into the room, looking like an elegant piece of art when it's off, is truly amazing. The slim frame and customizable bezels allow it to match the rest of my decor perfectly, making my living room feel more stylish and sophisticated.

The 4K picture quality is stunning—vibrant colors, deep contrasts, and incredible clarity whether I'm watching movies or streaming shows. I’ve especially enjoyed how easy it is to switch to Art Mode and have world-class artwork displayed on the screen when it’s not in use. It adds a touch of luxury and personalization to the space, making it more inviting.

Every guest who walks in notices the TV and compliments how it elevates the entire room. It has become more than just a place to watch TV; it's a conversation starter. Overall, I couldn't be happier with how The Frame LS03CB has enhanced both the look and feel of my living room!

title: Tip top
body:
Je possède la Samsung The Frame depuis un peu moins d’un mois et je suis vraiment satisfait de mon achat. Tout d’abord, le design est remarquable. Le concept de téléviseur qui se transforme en œuvre d’art lorsqu’il est éteint est non seulement esthétique mais aussi très fonctionnel. Il s’intègre parfaitement dans mon salon et apporte une vraie touche de sophistication, surtout avec le cadre personnalisable qui s’adapte à la décoration intérieure.

En termes de qualité d’image, je n’ai rien à redire. L’écran QLED offre des couleurs vives et des noirs profonds, parfaits pour regarder des films et des séries. Les modes d’image sont variés et ajustables, ce qui permet d’obtenir un rendu optimal selon les conditions de luminosité de la pièce. La résolution 4K est nette et rend chaque détail visible.

La partie “Art Mode” est un vrai plus : avoir un écran qui affiche des œuvres d’art plutôt qu’un simple écran noir est un concept brillant. Je suis agréablement surpris par le catalogue d’œuvres disponibles, et le fait de pouvoir afficher ses propres photos est un bonus.

Côté fonctionnalités, l’interface est fluide, la télécommande minimaliste et intuitive, et l’accès aux applications se fait sans accroc. L’installation a été facile, tout comme la connexion avec mes autres appareils.

En résumé, après près d’un mois d’utilisation, je ne vois que des points positifs. La Samsung The Frame allie design, qualité d’image et fonctionnalités modernes à la perfection. Je la recommande sans hésitation, surtout pour ceux qui cherchent un appareil alliant technologie et esthétique.

title: 2nd Frame Purchase for our Primary Bedroom
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] After falling in love with our large 65 inch Frame TV, it wasn't hard convincing my husband to purchase another one for our new home's primary bedroom.  I wanted a calming, serene space and knew that artwork on the wall, instead of a black screen, would fit the bill.  We both absolutely love it and I have had lots of fun changing the pictures out with the seasons and our decor.  It provided that calming refuge of a place that I had envisioned.  Love being able to watch my shows at night and really appreciate the quality of the tv itself.  With Alexa commands I can turn it on and off and have it take me to my Netflix, Prime and Hulu shows by voice.  We can also control the volume, so if the remote gets lost in the covers, we can still control the TV through the built in Alexa.  Both of our kids followed us and have also purchased them for their home and my daughter even added one to her design studio for beauty and function.  I took out the membership for the Art Store the first year, but quickly learned how to add my own art to the frame, and love the option that the subscription to the Store is optional.  We will never get another television for our main living area or bedroom again.  A great compromise of a quality TV that looks beautiful.

title: Un musée à la maison !
body:

Le mode Art est vraiment un must le choix des tableaux est vraiment bien fourni et il y en a pour tout les goûts
Au besoin vous pouvez rajouter vos propres photos !

Côté installation le système de fixations est bien pensé.
Un gros plus aurait été un système de rail verticaux assisté et ultra fin pour avoir la possibilité de rehausser l écran en mode tableau ! Actuellement on est obligé de trouver un compromis entre le mode télé et tableau .... Dommage :(
Le boîtier déporté avec le fil presque invisible est un plus indéniable ( moi je l ai fait passé ds le placo)
Une prise USB en face avant aurait été plus pratique pour brancher une clé contenant des photos lorsque le boîtier est logé dans un meuble TV avec un accès réduit...
Certe on peut toujours mettre une rallonge mais ça fait bricolo.
Côté Télé je n ai pas encore fait le tour ...la télécommande minimaliste demande un temps d adaptation certain ! Heureusement mon ancienne télécommande Samsung est partiellement compatible. ( Pour sélectionner les sources les sous titre ...)
Plutôt que d avoir des touches dédiées amazon ou Disney j' aurai aimé 4 touches de couleurs programmables pour aller directement a des endroits précis du menu paramètre !
J ai aussi acheté une barre Samsung compatible ... C est pas mal mais la télé ne garde pas toujours l association barre + télé en paramètre " sortie HP " et le fait d aller dans les paramètres pour le réactiver n est pas top quand on regarde une émission !
J ai jumelé une Freebox révolution et la sélection de celle ci dans Source " n allume pas ou pas toujours ma box quand elle est éteinte ! Obligation de se lever pour aller chercher la télécommande de celle ci pour l allumer :(
Un dernier point embêtant : lors de l utilisation d' un casque bluetooth on est obligé de reprendre la télécommande pour valider la connection :((((  c est contraignant . La connection avec mon ancienne Samsung était automatique !
Un dernier point ... Avoir la possibilité sur une ( ou toutes ) source de mettre un gap en plus ou en moins pour la sortie son afin de moduler la différence de niveau sonore . (+4 ou moins 5) ...

Sinon .... Que du bonheur !

title: Fantastic tv
body:
I purchased the 32” Frame tv for a bedroom, and it’s size is perfect.
The tv itself, I love - sleek styling, easy to operate (comes with 2x remote controls - a standard one and a slimline ‘smart’ remote, the latter charged by solar power).
I have found the picture to be very good and the audio is great.
The panel to attach it to the wall is great, very slim.
Should you not want your tv on the wall; the supplied legs are smart and modern.
The standard remote is good.
The smart remote is quite intuitive and the more I use it, the more I like it.
My only gripe is with the supplied cables.
A ‘connect’ cable is supplied which runs from the tv (exiting at either the right hand side or bottom centre - when looking at the screen), and that cable is only 2 metres long, grey and reasonably thick (approx 6mm). The only way to truly hide it, is to have the wall behind the tv channeled for cables in some way. By the time the cable has run along the edge of the tv screen 20 or cm is already taken up and so 2 metres is not particularly generous. 
That cable then plugs into the connect box - which is not very big, but is black.
There is then a standard Samsung cable from the connect box to your power socket, which is also black.

The larger model Frame tv’s come with a 5 metre ‘barely visible’ cable from the tv to the connect box.
Much more discreet and if a decent length.
How I wish the 32” Frame tv also had a 5m connect cable!

Beware of the 5m connect cables being sold separately online - they’re expensive and not compatible with all models.

With wires suitably concealed, this tv looks fab on the wall.

Decent TV hampered by extraordinarily dumb design choices. 
I have had this TV for around a year,  mostly happy with it functionally aside from the poor software. Recently we decided to purchase a to license in order to watch live TV and when we tried to connect the aerial we realised there was no antenna port on the one connect box included with this model. The only option is to connect the aerial directly to the back of the TV, however, because we have the TV wall mounted there is no way to fit the aerial cable as well as the one connect cable behind the tv, not to mention how ugly this would be - effectively eliminating the point of buying a ‘frame’ in the first place.

Simply put, a pretty TV that makes it impossible to watch live TV.

O facto do suporte, cabo e box virem incluídos ajudou muito na instalação. Tive oferta de uma moldura na compra, e o aspecto final é maravilhoso.
A TV inclui ainda 2 meses de oferta para a Samsung Art Store, o que é muito útil para começar a explorar as possibilidades de exposição de media.
Acho o interface muito acessível, e tenho adorado ver conteúdos 4K com esta qualidade de renderização. O som deixa algo a desejar, mas é facilmente melhorado com a inclusão da ligação optical digital para ligar a uma aparelhagem ou sem fios para ligar a soundbars e colunas. Apesar do preço a colocar fora do alcance de muitos consumidores que procuram este tipo de especificações AV, recomendo aos que queiram, como eu, investir numa peça de entretenimento que também acrescente à decoração do espaço.

title: Bonne image mais software télé catastrophique
body:
Bien que la qualité de l'image et le concept de the frame soient bons, the frame présente de sérieuses limitations en termes de fonctionnalités.

 Par exemple, la fonction "Art" qui permet d'afficher des œuvres d'art ou des photos sur l'écran est très limitée.

 Il n'est pas possible de créer un diaporama avec de la musique, et le délai minimum entre chaque affichage d'image est de 3 minutes, ce qui semble excessivement long. Il n'y a aucune possibilité de réduire ce délai, même si l'on souhaite afficher les images plus rapidement.

De plus, les applications du catalogue de Samsung sont très décevantes et ne rivalisent pas avec celles de Google TV. C'est vraiment regrettable.

Quant aux paramètres des réglages de la télé, il est très confus et peu intuitifs. Retrouver où certains paramètres de trouvent est parfois très difficile

Enfin il faut savoir que le catalogue des œuvres d'art est payant 

En résumé, bien que l'idée soit bonne et la qualité de l'image soit au rendez-vous, the frame souffre de graves limitations dans ses fonctionnalités, notamment en ce qui concerne la fonction "Art" et le catalogue d'applications de Samsung

title: Efficace
body:
C'est un bon compromis objet déco et télévision. Certes ce n'est pas le meilleur en télévision, même si comparé avec un modèle moyenne gamme de 2015, c'est une vraie révolution. Le gros avantage c'est l'écran mat, quel confort dans un salon très lumineux, plus besoin de fermer les rideaux.
L'angle de vision n'est pas mal non plus, la luminosité très bien. Et le rétroéclairage Edge plutôt discret même sur les noirs profonds.

L'image reste de belle qualité notamment avec les flux UHD 4K HDR10+
De nombreux format audio et vidéo compatibles. Il vous faudra juste trouver le réglage image qui vous convient, au départ on est un peu dessus sur le côté "documentaire" des images proposées. Les paramètres sont bien faits sur ce point et pas trop nombreux.
L'installation avec smarthing depuis mon S20 est top. La calibration de l'image avec téléphone assez efficace.
Le son est pas "top" sur ces écrans très minces, c'est le cas ici mais c'est tout à fait acceptable. Après en sortie optique et un 5.1 même ancien, c'est top.
L'OS tizen est satisfaisant, plutôt rapide, application à jour.
Et il y a la possibilité d'une double connexion casque bluetooth.
Et puis les compatibilités Google, amazon, smarthing, fait que l'on peut piloter la télé à distance sans trop de difficultés.

Le mode art (tableau) est assez impressionnant, d'autant que l'on peut choisir des oeuvres de sa propre collection.

Au final, je suis satisfait du produit surtout qu'il remplace d'un produit daté. Après nous l'avons eu avec une sacré promotion, plus la remise de 100 euros de Samsung. Ce qui a aussi décidé notre achat. 

En promo, je conseille sans hésiter pour la combinaison intéressante et l'écran mat.

title: TBien mais
body:
Le design de la tv et le rendu dans la pièce est superbe. 
J’ai pris The Frame uniquement pour cet aspect de rendu dans la pièce. 
Installation fluide je me retrouve parfaitement avec mon Apple TV pour tout piloter ou bien via le “Smart Tv” de la TV. 
La fonction “frame” est superbe le rendu des tableaux est extra. 
Donc je suis très satisfait. Mais. 
Je trouve que le réglage de l’image de la tv n’est pas optimal. Oui j’essaie de régler la tv car :
- quand je regarde un film en 4K (ex: Wakanda 2) seul le centre de l’image n’est pas flou. Le reste est flou. 
Est- ce du au film ou à la tv ? Je ne sais pas mais c’est très désagréable. 
- sur un autre film (donjon & dragons) c’était également visible. 

Donc j’essaie de régler ce problème. Si cela vient des films alors c’est ok. Mais si ça vient de la TV alors gros bris de glace je suis déçu. 

Ensuite il y a la fonction “automatique confort” (je n’ai pas le nom) qui régule automatique la luminosité et autre: 
C’est tout simplement nul. 
Avec le JT ça augmentait et baisser constamment. 
Sur un match de coupe du monde de rugby également en fonction des plans j’avais soit la luminosité au max soit au plus bas. 
Horrible. 

Donc me concernant j’ai cette tv pour son aspect Frame et c’est ok. 
Pour les réglages techniques c’est à revoir par rapport au prix de la tv… je précise avoir passé plusieurs heures dans les réglages et c’est un calvaire. Rien d’intuitif.

title: Not baked yet - avoid
body:

After 1/2 hour jacking with this I removed the app, reinstalled and that fixed this problem - reminds me of 1995 Windows 95 :/
Instructions of any kind are minimal but conveniently every document is in many languages so 6 or 7 pages to sort through to find one paragraph in English that barely gave any information.
Today both Frames switch to Samsung TV after a few minutes and most of the two dozen online conversations about the problem indicate it happened after a July software upgrade.  
Also - I bought these just to display photos - as advertised - but its primary function seems to be as a TV and there does not seem to be away to default it to photo mode on startup.

Anyway - NOT READY FOR PRIMETIME!

title: Beautiful screen, awful uild wuality and customer
body:
There is a 2.5" vertical mark on the screen which I have been told is accidental damage. Samsung's response to this was that it is a "horizontal thin line observed on your screen may be the result of either a surface scratch or a dried liquid splatter", there was no mention of the vertical mark which was queried (shown in image). The TV has been cared for incredibly to the point where a dust sheet is placed over it when work is being done in other areas of the house. I believe the damage must have been then when the screen was delivered, but as I didn't open the package within the 2 week cooling off period for fear of damaging the TV whilst moving, I was told that nothing can be done. In additon, the proprietary wall mount bracket supplied with the unit has failed, meaning the locking mechanism has jammed and the TV is permanently stuck to the wall. As this fault has occurred within 6 months of purchase, under the Consumer Rights Act of 2015, it is presumed to have been present at the time of delivery. The Act (Section 23) states that any repair or replacement must be carried out "at no cost" to the consumer. It is worth noting that this applies to the retailer, not the manufacturer, however in this case the TV was purchased from Samsung directly. When this was queried with Samsung, I was told "As damage has already been identified on the Television, we are unable to offer an in-warranty repair. I apologise for any inconvenience this may cause.". To reiterate, this relates to a mark on the screen which Sansung described as a "horizontal thin line observed on your screen may be the result of either a surface scratch or a dried liquid splatter". To claim that a dried liquid liquid splatter on the screen would cause a mechanical wall mount on the rear of the tv to fail is implausable. I have been advised that should any consequential damage be caused to the wall or screen during removal, I should seek to recover these costs from Samsung via the Small Claims track (MCOL).

In summary, the customer service I have recieved from Samsuing as a retailer is the worst I have ever experienced. This is the second Samsung TV I have purchased, in additon to a samsung fridge freezer, mobile phone and washing maching. Although the product is stunning, Under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, the retailer is legally responsible for resolving this, including the costs associated with the faulty unit. Based on this, I would never recomend purchasing directly from Samsung.

title: Excellent, but not quite perfect
body:
Its main function as a TV is generally superb. The picture quality is great and I particularly like the excellent anti-reflective coating. My previous Samsung TV was almost unwatchable in bright sunlight because the reflections were so bad. The slim profile makes it less obtrusive than many similar sized TVs, and the art mode is a nice touch. People have genuinely thought it was a picture when in art mode.

The built in speakers are better than I expected, having read reviews of other The Frame TVs. It's also nice to be able to attach multiple bluetooth headphones simultaneously when more than one person wants to listen without disturbing others.

The wireless One Connect box doesn't live up to the range claims. I have it only about 4 metres away from the TV with clear line of sight and it often complains about a poor connection). 

The SmartThings app for Android leaves a little to be desired, as it asks me to log in virtually every time I use it, which is incredibly annoying.

Responses to button presses can be a bit laggy, which just shouldn't happen on a high end TV, and documentation of how to do things like soft reset (hold down the power) or kill an app (hold down the back button) seems lacking and can take time to figure out. These things could be made menu options within the OS rather than just magic button presses.

On balance, I'm very happy with my purchase despite the few issues. If those could be fixed in a future version (or even by firmware update), it would transform a great product into a fantastic one.

title: Great picture and design, but frustrating AI featu
body:
I’ve had this TV since early June, and while the quality is undeniable, my overall experience has been mixed – and at this price point, that's a real letdown.


---

📺 Picture & Sound Quality

Visually, this TV delivers sharp, vivid images with impressive contrast. The matte screen finish is a really nice touch – it avoids that usual glassy reflection you get on many TVs. Instead, when the screen is off, it just remains a soft, non-glossy black. It gives the TV a more premium, picture-frame-like appearance and works especially well in bright rooms.

However, the AI processing causes major frustrations:

Sound Fluctuations: While watching Clarkson’s Farm, I noticed the volume would randomly spike then drop, despite the volume setting staying the same. This was eventually fixed by turning off the Sound Amplify feature – but that’s something I’d expect the AI to manage more intelligently.

Brightness Issues in Dark Rooms: The brightness constantly fluctuated when switching between bright and dark scenes. At first, I thought it was a fault, but it turns out it’s due to the AI reacting to light bouncing off the walls. Again, switching off AI Mode resolved it – but it defeats the point of having intelligent adaptive features.


I really expected the AI to handle environmental conditions – such as louder audio during noisy moments (like when a hoover is on) and a softer tone in quiet environments. Likewise, backlighting should adjust subtly based on room brightness, not just the content on screen. The concept is great, but the execution feels half-baked and more annoying than helpful.


---

🖼️ "The Frame" Concept – A Missed Opportunity

The Frame is marketed as a TV that doubles as a stylish photo frame when off, complete with the option to add custom bezels. However, I was disappointed that:

No bezel is included – not even a voucher towards one, which is surprising given the premium price.

It's like buying a photo frame and being told the actual frame costs extra – not a great first impression.



---

🧠 Smart Features

As a smart TV, you'd expect full app access, but:

There’s no option to install apps from unknown sources, which is limiting.

The app store is decent, but doesn’t offer the flexibility that other systems like Android TV provide.



---

🎮 Remote Controls

You get two remotes in the box:

A standard Samsung remote

A smart remote that charges via indoor solar panel or USB-C


The smart remote is a brilliant idea – it saves the constant hassle of digging through drawers for batteries you “definitely put in a safe place.” I haven’t needed to charge it yet thanks to ambient light, and the slim, minimal design fits the premium feel of the TV.


---

🧱 Mounting & Setup

The wall-mount system requires two brackets, which are meant to be universal for the different Frame Pro sizes – which is a plus. But aligning two separate mounts perfectly level with each other is a challenge. One single, solid mount would have made installation far easier and more foolproof.

On the positive side:

The One Connect Box is genuinely impressive. All devices are now tucked neatly inside my TV unit, with just one cable running to the TV. I’ve even hidden that by recessing a socket behind the TV, so now there are zero visible wires. It’s a game changer for living room aesthetics.



---

⚠️ Reliability Concerns

Since installation:

No sound on 5th June – resolved by powering off at the wall for 5 minutes.

Same issue on 15th June – again, fixed by a power cycle.

No further problems as of 29th June, but I’ll be keeping an eye on it and may contact Samsung if it happens again.



---

💭 Final Thoughts

With AI features disabled and no bezel included, the only real benefit I’m getting from this TV is its slim profile and wall-hugging design – and even that wasn’t as flush as advertised, despite proper installation.

Would I recommend it? Not really. Knowing what I do now, I could’ve bought a quality smart TV at a quarter of the price and been just as satisfied.

It’s a nice TV, but for what it costs, it’s just not worth it – especially with AI features that are more disruptive than helpful.


---

TL;DR:
✅ Beautiful picture quality
✅ Excellent cable management via One Connect
✅ Matte screen reduces reflections
✅ Solar-charged remote is a great addition
❌ Disappointing AI performance
❌ No included frame bezel
❌ Difficult two-part wall mounting
❌ Not great value for money

Final Verdict: 3 out of 5 stars – Premium product with some standout features, but let down by poor execution of key selling points.

title: Great picture and design, but motion artefacts let
body:
I had high hopes for the 2025 version of Samsung The Frame. The design is excellent — slim, modern, and genuinely looks like a piece of art when in ambient mode. Colour accuracy and clarity were both top-notch. Standard 4K HDR content looked fantastic, with vibrant colours and crisp detail.

But the dealbreaker? The motion smoothing.

When watching content with smoothing enabled (or even auto settings), the artefacts were distracting to the point of being unwatchable. Faces and moving objects would blur or leave trails, and it was especially bad during panning shots. It completely ruined the viewing experience for sport, films, or anything with fast movement.

I tried adjusting motion settings, but nothing resolved it. For a premium TV, this kind of issue shouldn’t exist.

I ended up returning it — reluctantly — because the picture quality was otherwise excellent. But for anyone sensitive to motion artefacts or who watches a lot of fast-paced content, this might not be the right choice.

title: I can't imagine going back to a normal TV now
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Setup was much more difficult than expected, but now that it's complete, I love the TV!

The setup manual is for multiple models, not just specifically this model. It would have helped to have one diagram that pointed to exactly where the TV controller and the plug for the power cord are.

The remote didn't work with the TV out of the box. I had to do an AI search to pair the remote. Eventually, I found the remote pairing instructions in the TV remote documentation. If it's something a customer will have to do during setup, it should be in the setup document.

Some online videos produced by the manufacturer for setup would have been helpful: a video for setup, one for TV operations, one for art functions, etc.

The Wireless Connect Box connected to the TV easily.

As far as the TV functions go, the picture and sound quality are very good. I assumed I would be buying a soundbar, but don't think I need it! I thought I had heard that the quality of these "Frame" TVs' picture wasn't spectacular, but I think it's very nice!

Onto the "Frame" functionality: The art collection is extensive, but I should probably slow down the rotation time, as I've seen it all within a few days. I decided to spend the money to get the Samsung library of art. It doesn't look like I can make playlists like one would do with music, but I might be able to control what is is shown by putting the pictures in the favorites folder. That should be good enough. I've slowed the rotation time and put a mat on the pictures. I'm having a lot of fun playing with the art.

All-in-all, this is a great TV for my needs; particularly because I wanted a TV that doubles as a piece of art when not being watched.

title: Worth the Hype!
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I have wanted the Samsung Frame TV for YEARS, and now that we finally have it, I can honestly say it completely lived up to the hype. It instantly changed the entire feel of our living room and somehow manages to be both functional and beautiful at the same time.

The biggest thing for me was wanting a TV that didn’t dominate the room or feel like a giant black box hanging on the wall. This truly looks like framed art. We had it professionally installed so it would sit perfectly flush against the wall, and I’m really glad we did because that clean built-in look makes such a difference. I also added a thin wooden magnetic frame around it, which made it feel even more custom and high-end.

We ended up getting the Pro version, and honestly… GO PRO. The wireless slim box is one of the coolest features. We hid ours inside a nearby cabinet, so there are zero visible cords and no need to fish wires through the walls. It keeps everything looking incredibly sleek and minimal.

The art mode is probably my favorite feature. We did the yearly art subscription, and there are so many beautiful options to choose from. I love changing the artwork depending on the season, mood, or room vibe, and my kids are obsessed with the fact that we can upload family photos too. People genuinely don’t realize it’s a TV at first, which still makes me laugh every time someone notices.

It’s also super smart and easy to use. All the apps are already built in like Netflix, YouTube, Hulu, and we use the multi-view feature constantly. Being able to have a baseball game on one side while someone else watches a show on the other has already become one of our favorite features.

The picture quality is beautiful and super crisp, clear, and bright without looking harsh or overly processed. Sports look amazing on it, movies feel cinematic, and even cartoons somehow look elevated. The matte screen also helps cut down glare during the day, which I love since our living room gets a lot of natural light.  I was also surprised by how good the sound quality is. The audio feels full and balanced for such a slim TV, and dialogue comes through really clearly without constantly adjusting the volume.

Also, the tiny remote is weirdly adorable. My kids think it’s the coolest little gadget ever. I just need to AirTag it before it disappears into the couch forever.

One minor gripe is that I wish there were more free art options included right out of the box without a subscription, but I’m glad you can at least upload your own content to customize it.

Picture quality on the Neo QLED panel is noticeably sharper and more vibrant than I expected from a "lifestyle" TV. HDR content looks great — the blacks are deep and highlights have real pop. It's not quite OLED territory, but it's impressive for what this thing is. Local dimming handles most scenes well, though I did notice a tiny bit of blooming around very bright objects on a dark background if you're being picky about it.
Art Mode is genuinely cool. I have it set to display a rotating gallery and guests always ask if it's a real print. The matte finish on the screen kills glare in our bright Texas living room — no more repositioning furniture around sun angles.
A few things to keep in mind: the Art Store subscription is required if you want the full catalog (30 free pieces per month otherwise), and the price point is definitely premium. But if you want a TV that looks like décor when you're not watching it and still performs well for movies and sports — this hits both marks.
Would buy again. No regrets.

title: Total Scam. Forced Accounts & Blocked Soundbars!
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Honestly, do not buy this TV. I am so incredibly mad I wasted my money on this Samsung TV.

First off, they literally force you to make a Samsung account just to use the TV you paid hundreds of dollars for. You can't watch a thing without signing up for their  account first. Why do I need to give Samsung my email and info just to watch my own TV? It's absolute corporate greed and data mining.

To make things even worse, I have a perfectly good Vizio soundbar that I’ve used for years. But guess what? Samsung locks their "immersive" sound feature so it only works if you waste more money on a Samsung brand soundbar. Because I have a Vizio, the TV blocks the feature from working together. It’s a total scam to force you into buying only their products.

This TV is nothing but a headache. Constant pop-ups, forced logins, and they block your other speakers from working right. Save your sanity and stay far away from this TRASH.

title: Love the picture, the remote and menus not so much
body: This is a re-write of my review, as requested by Samsung:  For the picture on this TV I would give it 5-stars.  The picture and the screen's abilities to provide an excellent picture are outstanding.  It is able to provide anything you might prefer from quite dim to absolutely brilliantly bright.  Contrast can be adjusted to the same level of extremes as the brightness.  The uniformity of the picture is also all that you could ask of a set, especially in this price range.  Being a 4K TV, its ability to upscale is something to really appreciate and is apparent when watching media that was made pre-1080I, as the upscaling feature does improve the lower resolution of those productions in most cases.  The sound is fairly decent considering the set is a simple two-speaker, down-firing system, with a relatively low-powered amplifier.  Sadly though, like so many manufacturers today have done, the only audio out is for optical devices only.  Long gone are any "legacy" hook-ups and I should point out here that not only includes the sound output, buy the video input as well.  You can no longer use RGB, component or even the traditional fall-back default of RCA composite connections.  There's HDMI in and Optical audio out.  There is a single USB A port that can be used to input from USB memory media devices for movies, videos, etc.  All of these things are pluses for this set and we like them.  Now, for what we don't like:  One, the included remote is sorely lacking in what it is able to control on the TV, mostly due to it being done in a "minimalist" style.  What I'm saying here is Samsung has attempted to move as much control from the included remote to the screen itself.  If you've been paying attention to what has been happening in new cars with the manufacturers removing buttons and knobs from the dashboards, and placing them on a screen on the dash instead, well they've done on this TV.  Samsung has tried to strike a similar aesthetic here on this TV and probably all of their sets.  To put it simply, we don't like what they've done.  The few buttons that remain on the remote are very poorly labeled, and some of them don't move in an intuitive manner.  For example, there are two very small rectangular buttons that stick up from the surface of the remote about 1/16th of an inch.  It took me quite some time to realize you needed to use these to change the channel, but you don't "push down" to get a response.  You must "catch" the top edge of these little buttons to "rock" or "nudge" them either forward or backward.  If you're anything like the average person you will frequently find your fingers simply sliding over the top of the button because they're very small, they do not stick up very far and the plastic is very smooth, almost slippery.  This is very much how the design of the entire included remote is done.  Not easy to use, almost indecipherable and actually small enough that you can easily have it fall out your hand if you aren't careful with it.  Now, our second dislike and it looms large for us.  This isn't our first 4K Samsung set.  Our first Samsung 4K set is now about 10 years old, but its menu system is far more intuitive, logical and understandable.  Our new MiniLED set's menus are very trying, not logical and many times the only way to actually pull something up that you want is to use the search function.  We are keeping the TV because we love the picture and sound, and we found an excellent work-around so that we can use our new set.  The remote from our 10 year old Samsung 4K set works perfectly with the new set, and the way it was laid out brings back the logic and control that was missing due to the included remote being almost useless for us.  With the old remote we now can access every feature on this new TV and do not have to hunt and depend on moving a little cursor around on the screen to back control.  Good TV, bad remote and software.

title: My 2nd Samsung  Tv
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I'm really happy with my Samsung TV overall. The picture quality is definitely the standout for me The brightness is excellent, especially in a bright room, and the contrast gives the image a really nice sense of depth. Colors look vibrant without being overdone, and everything just looks sharp clean, and detailed
I'm also very pleased with the screen uniformity. Bright and dark areas look consistent, and I haven't noticed anything distracting that takes away from the viewing experience,
The responsiveness of the TV did take a bit of getting used to. The menus, apps, and general interface feel a little different from what I was used to, so there was a bit of a learning curve. That said, once you spend some time with it, it becomes easier and more intuitive
My main disappointment is the sound. I would much rather have the TV audio go through my AV receiver and external speaker setup. The built-in speakers are fine, but if you already have a proper audio system, the integration could definitely be smoother and more straightforward
Overall though, I'm very pleased with it. The brightness, contrast, vibrancy, sharpness, and overall picture quality are all excellent. There's a bit of adjustment needed with the interface, and I'd prefer better integration with an external receiver for sound, but none of that really takes away from how good the picture is
Great picture and a very enjoyable TV overall

title: Poor user interface
body:
This is thee worst user interface I've ever used on any TV in my lifetime. I had a 65" Samsung TV and it was nice, that's why I bumped up to a 75". Big mistake. All the user controls are hidden in a maze of confusion that takes you minutes to find for adjustment. For live TV you literally have to go and make sure the guide is on which ever TV channels you're using. If you're watching Samsung TV and you switch to OTA content, want to change the channel, you literally have to go back into the maze, find the menu for OTA channels and click on that or your channel will change back to Samsung TV channels. Super horrible interface!!
Next, there's no optical out. WHAT IN THE WORLD‽‽
99% of the home theater systems use optical for their audio. But not this one, right? If your system doesn't support eARC audio, you're screwed...
Next, when you watch a streaming service, it automatically switches from whatever TV screen mode you're using, over to film maker mode. Yup... You now have to go back into the maze and manually turn your mode back to whatever you were using...
In short, whoever developed the user interface for this TV should, needs to be fired!!!
This will be the last Samsung TV that I'll ever buy, FACT!!

title: Brighter Than Most, But Falls Short Outdoors
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] We set this TV up on our beach property under a shaded structure, where cutting through heavy sunlight and reflections is our main goal. Compared to a standard 4K LCD TV, this model is noticeably brighter and performs significantly better in ambient light.

​However, it still falls a bit short of what we were hoping for in our specific setup. Even under shade, the outdoor glare and natural brightness are tough to overcome, and it doesn't quite cut through the reflections as much as we needed during peak daylight hours.

​It's a solid, vibrant TV that would probably excel in a bright indoor living room, but if you're using it in an outdoor covered patio or beach setup, it might still leave you wishing for a bit more glare resistance and peak brightness.

title: Fantastic Budget TV
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I've been using the 43-inch M70H for both everyday entertainment and gaming, and it's exceeded my expectations. After spending some time adjusting the picture settings, the image quality really comes to life. The brightness is excellent for daytime viewing, while the contrast provides deep blacks and vibrant colors that make movies and games look fantastic.
One thing that really stood out is the screen uniformity. Large bright scenes and darker scenes look clean and consistent without distracting patches or uneven lighting. The TV is also very responsive, making menu navigation feel smooth and gameplay enjoyable with very little noticeable delay.
I also appreciate how much control Samsung gives over picture calibration. Being able to fine-tune the image made it easy to find a look that feels natural and accurate for my room. Whether I'm watching shows, playing games, or streaming videos, the picture stays sharp and immersive.
Overall, this has been a reliable, high-quality TV that delivers an excellent viewing experience. It's easy to recommend to anyone looking for a well-rounded display with great picture quality and responsive performance.

title: Very good in it's class and range!
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] In it's class and price range the Samsung M70H Series Mini LED 4K tv is really exceptional. The color is rich and uniform across the screen and the contrast is deep and all facets of the picture have a good range of adjustment. The picture is very bright and the sound is more than acceptable so external speakers are not a necessity. The other feature which works well is the judder control. Using it motion is very smooth, even more so than tv's costing much more. The blacks are acceptable in day or brighter room lights but are not inky in lower light situations. If it had local dimming on the array (which it does not) this would be better. The only other thing that could use a bit of improvement is the off angle viewing which becomes washed out fairly quickly. So for straight on or nearly so viewing it is an easy budget conscious recommendation but if you have off angle seating... I would look elsewhere. Still all in all a good value and nice picture with good motion control.

Setup took just a few minutes, and I love having instant access to Samsung TV Plus for thousands of free channels without needing an extra subscription. title: Perfect Family TV
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] We've been using the Samsung 55-inch M70H Mini LED TV as our main family television, and it has been a fantastic addition to our home. It was surprisingly easy to set up, the remote is laid out well and the SmartThings app makes it easy to monitor my other Samsung appliances. 
Picture: The 4K picture quality is sharp and vibrant, with excellent color reproduction that makes movies, sports, and family shows look impressive. The Mini LED technology provides strong contrast and bright, detailed images, while Samsung's 4K upscaling helps older content look clearer and more enjoyable. The Motion Xcelerator feature keeps fast-moving scenes smooth, which has been especially great for watching sports and action movies together.

What we appreciate most is how easy the TV is for the whole family to use. The Tizen smart platform gives us quick access to streaming apps, Samsung TV Plus,, while built-in support for Apple AirPlay, Google Cast (what we use), and voice assistants makes sharing content simple. The sound quality is surprisingly immersive thanks to Object Tracking Sound Lite and Q-Symphony compatibility, and the overall experience feels premium for a family living room. Whether we're having movie nights, gaming, or just relaxing with our favorite shows, the Samsung M70H has delivered reliable performance and excellent value.

title: Great purchase!
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] We were looking to replace our bedroom television. The set was almost 20 years old and just not giving us the experience we wanted. Enter the Samsung 55” M70H Mini LED in 4K

Set up was super easy. The set is extremely light. Overall, it took less than 15 minutes to complete.

It was like a brand new experience watching our favorite shows and movies. The sleep function is also helping improve our sleep function and quality of life. 

To keep it simple, I’m outlining our pros and cons. 

Pros
* Vibrant color. You can change the mode, I personally like the movie theater setting. 
* Budget-friendly price point for mini-LED technology.
* Samsung software updates all downloaded through their Tizen operating system.
* Love how you can hook everything into your Samsung smart app.
* Decent audio performance.

Cons

* There can be screen glare in brightly lit rooms. It wasn’t distracting for me, but my hubby noticed it frequently.
* No direct voice control.
* Occasional lag during smart menu navigation or movement between apps.
* Sound could be better, but it’s good overall. 

Overall, this is a great buy. The price point is extremely reasonable and we may  officially be a Samsung tv household.

title: Vibrant colors
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Honest Review – Great Sound, Strong Picture, But Needs Some Tweaking
After spending some time with this TV, I’d say it’s a solid overall experience with a few things worth noting.
First, the sound quality really stands out. I wasn’t expecting much from built-in speakers, but this one is surprisingly full and clear. Dialogue comes through crisp, and it has enough depth that I haven’t felt the need to immediately add a soundbar.
The picture quality is generally very good—bright, sharp, and easy to see even in a room with a lot of natural light. It handles daytime viewing well, which was important for my setup. That said, I’ve had a harder time getting the color settings just right. Depending on the content, tones can look a little off or overly saturated, and it takes some adjusting to find a balance that looks natural.
I also experienced an occasional screen glitch where part of the image briefly distorts or shifts horizontally. It doesn’t happen constantly, but when it does, it’s definitely noticeable and interrupts the viewing experience.
On the plus side, the TV itself looks sleek and modern, and setup was quick and easy.
Overall: great sound, strong brightness and clarity, but color calibration and occasional screen issues hold it back a bit. If those were ironed out, this would easily be a top-tier experience.    I did contact Samsung and they were able to help me resolve my problems! They were very helpful and nice!

title: 55” Class M70H Mini LED 4K
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I recently bought this 55” Mini LED TV and I’m honestly really impressed with it so far. The picture quality was the first thing I noticed right away. The colors are super vibrant, and the brightness makes everything look crisp and clear, even during the daytime with sunlight coming in. Watching shows and movies feels more immersive because the contrast is so strong, especially in darker scenes where you can actually see details instead of everything blending together.

The smart TV interface is also really easy to use. Setting it up took no time, and I like how all the main apps like Netflix, Hulu, and Disney are right there and load quickly. The layout feels clean and not cluttered, so it’s easy to find what you want without scrolling forever. I also noticed that older shows look better than I expected, which I’m assuming is from the 4K upscaling, and that’s been a nice bonus.

Design wise it fits perfectly in my space. It has a slim, modern look that doesn’t take away from the room, and it actually makes everything look a little more put together. The sound quality is also solid for a TV on its own, clear enough that I don’t feel like I need extra speakers right away.

Overall, I’m really happy with this purchase. It looks great, performs well, and is super easy to use. If you’re thinking about upgrading your TV, this is definitely one I would recommend checking out.

title: Unreal
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] First, let me just say that upon receiving the box, it was extremely light.   I have had many t v s over the years fifty five inch up and I have never felt or handled the t v that was so lightweight at this size. It's so easy to set up and move if needed.

Next, Right out of the box, the setup was extremely easy and I even used the SmartThings app.\nAs this was the first t v I ever tried it with. Within 2 minutes, it was not only set up in all my accounts were there, but everything was signed in and it even set up the TV just like my projector and my other t v!

Next, I have seen great image quality on products from this brand but this one takes the cake. The blacks were much deeper.The colors were more vibrant , and I even had to tone down the brightness , because the t v itself would light up my entire living space in the evening and it was almost too bright. When?\nSmooth, TV's first came out versus tube TV's.I remember my eyes having to adjust to a great picture quality versus when I was used to.  And this is almost the same.  There is a difference vs even my led 4k tv.

Next, sound on t v's like this have always been hit or miss. On my older models, I would have to change the soundtrack to 2.1 channel versus 5.1 channel just because scenes with a lot of action would be too loud but scenes when people talk would be too soft.  Not only does this alleviate that , but the sound actually seems to come from certain sides of the t v , depending on where the dialogue is or the action is , which is very clear to understand but it also seems like the sound moves with the scene!

Lastly, I was very skeptical about using AI on a TV.But after trying this out , it's just like using a I on the phone only it's tailored to images, movies, music and videos.  I gave the AI several task of finding pictures.Short clips, movies and even things that I knew the title of but just described a part of a scene to see if it would find it and it never missed!

Very well made tv!

I'd never seen nor heard anything about "mini LED" screens before buying this one, so I was a little worried. I didn't know what that meant! Everything of Samsung's I'd owned so far, including phones,tablets, and laptops too, have always been OLED, AMOLED, or Super AMOLED. I didn't really know what that meant either, just knew I was guaranteed a beautiful picture quality! Well not only did this TV not disappoint, actually turned out to be even better, but now I understand why, and what all that stuff means! The screens prior to this had a single backlight. The mini LEDs like mine, and now their new "Neo" stuff, instead have thousands of tiny LEDs instead! That, along with the quantum dot technology, (QLED) and the dynamic range, (this one is 4k) gives the screen ultra precise control over the detail clarity, the range of colors, and the brightness and contrast to every tiny pixel on for screen. The settings available also allow you to control how it's done, so you get the best picture for your environment - if the room is darker or brighter, or your eyes have certain sensitivities, or if whatever you're viewing has a certain way it's meant to be displayed. If you're gaming, you want super fast response for movement and detail clarity; if watching a movie in the dark, you'll want to see it a the creator intended, while not straining your eyes. No matter what, the picture is just perfect! I honestly can't imagine it could be better than this, even though I know there are available options like 8k, Neo, and their newest micro RGB out there, but of course those will come with a much higher price tag. While I'm sure those are great, I am perfectly happy with this one, and absolutely do not feel like I'm missing out on anything! It's got all the smart features, is super easy to set up and control, compatible with everything, and I'll say it again, has the best picture quality you could possibly imagine! HIGHLY recommend this TV!

title: Solid pick for the basement setup
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Picked this up because I needed a second tv for my basement and didnt want to drop flagship money on a room I mostly use for movie nights and the occasional console session. The M80H ended up being the right middle ground between cheap/budget TVs and flagship models. 

Picture is good. Not the same level as my Neo QLED but for a Mini LED at this price point Im not complaining. HDR content looks pretty solid and the upscaling does a decent job on older 1080p stuff. Black levels are where you can tell its a step down from the higher end, blooming shows up a bit in dark scenes if youre paying attention but most people watching probably wont notice.

Setup was straightforward. Plugged in my console, ran through the network setup, signed into my Samsung account which pulled in most of my app preferences from the upstairs unit which saved me some time. The basement has weird angles and low ambient light but the screen handles it fine.

Built in speakers are decent for what they are. Clear enough for shows and dialogue and they get loud enough for the room. I ended up plugging in a soundbar I already had since Im picky about audio for movie nights but they could absolutely get the job done on their own if you werent looking to add anything.

120Hz refresh rate is enough for what I do down there. My girlfriend ends up using it more for shows than I do anyway. For the price its hard to argue with.
