title: So much more than a TV
body:
I bought this TV as an upgrade from my 65" Samsung 4K TV that was 7 years old. I have had this new version for 5 days & here are my thoughts on it. Straight away, the Home Page looks very different. It is nicely set out & very easy to use. A lot of platforms that I use, such as Netflix, Disney+, etc., were already installed with their icons showing on the Home Page ( though this may have been done by the person who installed my TV ). If you want to remove any, go to the Edit List icon at the end of the row. There are a multitude of options for finding what you want to watch, with Continue Watching very near the top. If you are used to a Smart TV, you will soon get the hang of it. 
  Picture quality is excellent, as to be expected. I'm not going to go into great detail about the settings. There are expert sites on the net for that ( although do ignore the ones I saw that said to have the brightness set at zero, that's ridiculous). Also, settings are subjective. Sound quality is very good. I have a soundbar but haven't been able to connect it yet as I need a longer HDMI cable, so I can't comment on any improvements it may make. If you connect a soundbar, there is something called Q Symphony sound that you can use. I think it entails listening to the TV with the sound coming from both the TV's speakers & the soundbar.
  The ports for your various cables are at the back on the right-hand side of the TV as you are looking at it from the front. There are 3 for HDMI, 2 for USB & 1 for Ethernet. WiFi & Bluetooth are also supported.
  There are 2 remotes. One large one with lots of buttons that will rarely be used by me. This one requires batteries. The other remote is smaller with hardly any buttons & will be used a lot by me. It is solar-powered, so no extra batteries are required. There is a solar panel on the back. You leave it face down & it will charge from the light in your room. It can also be charged via a USB cable. This is not supplied, though. If you have a Samsung phone, you can use its cable. If you open Settings on your TV, go to General & Privacy, scroll down to Remote Control & click, you can see what battery percentage you have left. The remote has dedicated buttons for Netflix, Prime Video, YouTube & Samsung TV Plus.
  The TV comes with two Voice Assistants built in, Alexa & Bixby. As I already have an Alexa in my living room very close to the TV, I opted to use Bixby to avoid confusion. You can choose a male or female voice. I've used Bixby a few times & it seems pretty good. When your TV is off ( not at the mains but in standby mode ), you can ask Bixby ( or Alexa ) to turn your TV on. It will open your platforms for you, change channels & volume & other settings, as well as answer your questions.
  As mentioned in my subject header, this is so much more than a TV. Other features include a gaming hub, an art hub, & another hub called Daily+, which is Samsung's own Smart Things hub. 
  If you have a Smart home already, you are going to want to dive into the Daily+ hub. There really is too much content for me to tell you everything here. Anyway, it will be more fun for you to look for yourself.
  I'm not a gamer, so the gaming hub is not for me. If you are a gamer, though, this is a nice touch. What I do know about it is that there are payments/subscriptions needed to play. However, you don't need a console to play the games available; all you need is a Bluetooth controller.
  The art hub is also a nice touch, but to get the best out of it requires a subscription. I did find a couple of free things to do. Scroll down to Generative Wallpaper & you can create your own pictures with the aid of AI. I think you can create 10 pictures per day. Scroll down from this a bit further to Complimentary, where you will find some nice animated wallpapers in Cinemagraph. You can also upload your own photos from your phone. Again, there is a lot to look at on this hub, so check it out.
  Lastly ( Thanks if you've read this far ), the TV comes with 2 support stands that clip on. They can be placed near each other centrally, or further apart at each end of the TV. The latter choice would be best if you want to place a sound bar right under the TV. Of course, you can also wall mount the TV. Something I did find hidden away that you may want to take notice of is the amount of storage space you have on your TV ( as in GB & MB storage ). Go to All Settings> Support> Device Care> Manage Storage. You will see in the top right-hand corner the details. My details after only 5 days are 3.09 GB used & 752.05 MB ( 19% ) available. On this page, you will see a number of platform tiles. If you select one ( a blue tick appears ), you then have the option to delete it.
  Okay, so that's my review. Sorry it was long, but that's the kind of review I like to see, rather than one that says " It's great ". I hope you found it useful. For me, this has been a great upgrade & I'm very happy with my purchase.

title: Great Updated Television
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I recently purchased the Samsung 75 inch QN1EH Neo QLED TV, and so far I have been extremely happy with my purchase. The first thing that stood out to me was obviously the size. Going up to a 75 inch screen makes a huge difference, especially for movies, sports, and shows where you really want that theater like experience at home. Even with the larger screen, the picture is incredibly clear and sharp.

The picture quality is probably my favorite thing about this TV. The colors are bright and vibrant without looking overly saturated, and the contrast is impressive. Dark scenes actually look dark while still maintaining detail, and brighter scenes really pop. The Neo QLED technology definitely feels like an upgrade compared to other TVs I’ve owned. Everything from regular TV shows to streaming movies looks great, and the picture quality really shines with higher quality content.

Setup was also much easier than I expected for a TV this size. Once everything was connected, navigating through the menus and getting my streaming apps set up was pretty straightforward. The smart TV features are convenient, and I like having everything accessible in one place without needing to constantly switch between different devices.

The design itself is another plus. For such a large television, it has a clean, modern appearance and doesn’t feel bulky or outdated. It looks great in the room and definitely makes the space feel upgraded.

Overall, I’m very satisfied with the Samsung 75 inch QN1EH Neo QLED. Between the large screen, excellent picture quality, easy to use smart features, and sleek design, it has been a great upgrade for our home. If you’re considering moving up to a larger TV and want something that delivers a beautiful picture without being overly complicated to use, I would definitely recommend giving this one a look.

title: Excellent size
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] My family having the 55" Samsung Neo QN70H TV in our living room completely elevates the daily home entertainment experience. From the moment we turn it on, the display jumps out with vivid colors and striking brightness. Powered by Quantum Mini LED technology and Quantum Dot color, it delivers ultra-sharp contrast, deep blacks, and rich highlights that hold up effortlessly even in sun-drenched rooms.  
​At 55 inches, it strikes the ideal balance for most living spaces—large enough to feel immersive without dominating the room. Under the hood, Samsung’s NQ4 AI Processor dynamically upscales lower-resolution media into crisp 4K, making standard streaming shows, movie classics, and live sports look significantly sharper and more detailed.  
​The sleek AirSlim profile gives the display a virtually borderless, modern look whether mounted on a wall or placed on a media stand. Daily usability is just as smooth: the One UI Tizen smart interface makes navigation fast, organizing all your favorite streaming platforms and smart home controls in one central hub. Integrated audio features like OTS Lite and Q-Symphony dynamically match sound to movement on screen, pulling you straight into the action.  
​Ultimately, owning the Samsung QN70H means never settling for average picture quality again. It transforms movie nights, gaming sessions, and casual viewing into a premium theater-like experience right from the comfort of my couch.

title: High Performance High-Def
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] After a month of regular use with this unit, Samsung delivers reliable HD picture and performance in a variety of usage scenarios. I have noticed the picture is always sharp and clear, whether I'm streaming live sports, playing video games, or streaming YouTube from my phone while projecting to the TV. Sound quality is also reliably sharp and clear, whether I'm playing video games, watching TV, or even playing from physical media disc's from a peripheral DVD or BluRay device. The native Samsung menu and embedded software has also come a long way from what I experienced with earlier iterations of "smart" TV devices. The menu and interface is both more intuitive, and faster/performs better than any other TV I have owned in the last 15 years. Samsung continues to show with this model of TV why their devices remain extremely popular with individuals and families with a need for versatility and reliability in their home TV set, but without sacrificing performance, or having to pay an arm and a leg for it. I will happily recommend this Samsung TV to anyone looking for a great balance of performance and reliability in their TV set, at a reasonable price point. 
Bonus points: Initial set-up couldn't have been easier. I went from TV boxed, to in use in less than 30 minutes! The set was light enough for me to lift and install on the hearth over my fireplace by myself, one person of average height and strength.

title: Amazing clear TV compare to old Samsung
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The new Samsung Neo QLED 2026 model is to replace my aging half broken Samsung 55” (more than 10 years) LED TV. Installation to the wall is very simple. Samsung doesn’t include screws for wall mount. I had to remove the old TV and use the old screws. The new TV has very shallow mounting holes and I have to add spacer to the old longer screws to work. The placement of the mounts is also much narrower. If you don’t want to mount the TV on the wall, it does come with 2 stands to place the TV on a flat surface.
Setup is very straight forward. If you have a Samsung phone or a Gmail account, the TV will try to link up or back up what you have on your phone. But I skipped this step to make the setup faster. Later, I have the phone link up with the TV through the SmartThings app. Remote is a lot simpler to use compare to the old large one and you can use the phone app to control the TV
The picture quality is amazing and bright. Compared to my old TV, the new screen is much brighter and crystal clear. The upgrade almost feels like when people switched from old tube TVs to LED TVs. I actually have to tone down the brightness frok factory preset. This new TV has 4K resolution, and even regular YouTube content looks noticeably sharper and clearer when browsing.
There are a few hub connections in the back of the TV, includes 3 HDMI and one is eARC enabled, optical audio connection for sound bars, and couple USB connections which I used one for Amazon Firestick.
There are many features that I’m still trying to figure out with the new TV. However, the picture quality alone makes this a great TV option, especially if you’re looking for one at a good price.

body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I’ve been using the Samsung QN80H for a few weeks now, and it’s been a noticeable upgrade from older TV. The picture quality stands out right away, especially in darker scenes where blacks actually look dark instead of the grayish glow that you usually get. The contrast is impressive thanks to the Mini-LED backlighting, and bright scenes still pop without washing everything out. The AI picture features do a solid job in the background adjusting brightness, sharpening content, and even improving older, lower-resolution videos with upscaling, so you don’t really have to mess with settings much. It also includes Samsung’s automatic picture optimization, which helps fine-tune the image without needing a professional setup and eliminates the need for trying to figure out the best setting your self. 

The smart TV experience is smooth and convenient. All the major streaming apps like Netflix, YouTube, Hulu, Disney+, and Prime Video are built in and load quickly, so there’s really no need for an external streaming device. Navigation feels responsive, and the interface is easy enough to get used to after a little time. Gaming on a PS5 has also been great the high refresh rate make fps and racing games feel smooth and responsive, and overall motion handling is clean with no blur.

title: Thoroughly amazed..!
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] What a sweet surprise this was...  We unboxed the TV and we were happy to see that you can actually pick where you want the legs of the TV to go, either spread apart almost at the corners or more at the middle.  I don't recall ever seeing a TV that gives you that option, but boy is it a good one.. why?  Because it helps with cable management and also the atheistic of the TV change quite a bit depending on the stand placement. 

But let's get to the juicy details.. as soon as we turned it on to get the setup going, we were amazed.  The vibrant color, the SOUND,  the quality.. it was great.  We have quite a few TVs throughout the home and I can say without a doubt that this one is becoming my favorite, by a long shot.  The quality of the output it very sharp and makes everything look great.  We also enabled the dynamic sound and boy do we love that.  It adds more excitement to our TVs shows and movies, you truly do feel like it's immersing you in a deeper experience.  The remote is a standard size and it seems like they just did that on purpose as there is a lot of "dead" space on it.  So they made it big enough to fit comfortably in your hand.

One negative thing that I'll point out about it is that the glare is pretty bad on the TV, we tried different angles but nothing seemed to truly work when watching it during the day time with the shades open.  So for maximum enjoyment I would say that you need to place it where it gets the least amount of sun exposure.. or like us, enjoy it at night time :)

Aside from that, I highly recommend it.  Fits all of our needs and the picture quality is truly amazing.  5/5

title: Beautiful TV
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Recently, I thought I would only buy OLED TVs from now on. After using this TV I have to say QLED is right up there in terms of picture quality. Setting up the TV was very easy. It was a very different experience from setting up any other TV I’ve had before. I’m in the Samsung ecosystem and the setup went through SmartThings. Nice and easy. Now, I do not prefer the standard setup of any TV. You always get that soap opera effect. So, I had to do some digging to turn it off. Normally, it’s as easy as looking for something called ‘smooth motion’. Problem is every manufacturer has a different name for it. title: Design flaw with wall mounting and new power box!!
body: I normally replace my tv on a 2 year cycle so my last TV was the Samsung QN900C which I was massively pleased with. Some may ask why change and the answer to that is I get bored and like new technology. I haven’t had time to play with the setting yet but picture quality is fantastic and the anti glare feature works perfectly especially as my TV is positioned in my living room with bi folding doors so there is a lot of potential light and reflection opportunities that this TV eliminates. I do have a massive negative that no one in support can seem to help with though as the set is so new so a ticket has been raised. My previous TVs have had just the one connect box to power the TV and attach sources to. Frustrating to my set up currently, My AV rack sits to the corner of the living room and the one connect cable isn’t long enough so where my TV is wall mounted the cable kind of comes down from the centre of the tv diagonally down the wall to reach the one connect box positioned on my AV rack. Options to fix this would be to change location of one connect box which isn’t currently possible or buy longer one connect box cable so I can achieve preferred look of cable running straight down to floor and then along to meet AV rack. So this takes me on to the problem with this new TV that features wireless one connect box. So the idea was to still have the TV wall mounted, power cable from TV down to mains socket (i have one directly blow TV) and then position wireless one connect box anywhere in my living room (up to 10m). What isn’t clearly advertised, unlike the Frame Pro where this is how the set up works, the QN990F has a huge power box (similar size to the old one connect boxes) the powers the TV in addition to the wireless one connect box. If the TV was to be positioned on the stand this isn’t a problem as at attaches directly to this but for me wall mounting, I’m left with the same diagonal one connect cable and now an additional power box that I have to find room for in my AV rack therefore if you wall mount your TV, I feel this is a backward step compared to previous models seeing as this design is meant to be less clutter and more simplistic with the hiding of cables.

title: Massively underwhelming
body: Purchased this to replace a Samsung QLED which failed after just 2 years. Have had this for a month now, and unfortunately I'm underwhelmed with the TV's performance given its price bracket. I expected that by paying for a TV in the premium price bracket, I'd be receiving a TV of premium quality, but that isn't true with this TV most of the time. When playing UHD content the picture is great, so long as you mess about with the settings to adjust it to your preference. But even then it's inconsistent, it seems you have to continuously alter the picture settings depending on what you're watching, I can't seem to find a level that's consistent through watching different content. It suffers with blurring and/or judder just like a much cheaper LCD panel would when watching something with a fast paced environment. And colours can run into each other too. For instance a couple of weeks ago, I was watching the Scotland game in the FIFA World Cup, and the adidas stripes on the sleeves of their shirts were sky blue in colour throughout the entire first half. I double checked with a picture online at half time as I was sure they were meant to be white, and indeed, they were meant to be white. As another reviewer has mentioned, at times it seems as if everything has a blue tinge, which can make the whole picture look really ugly, especially when watching something like football and the entire pitch can have a very noticeable blue hue. Another thing previously mentioned is the lack of BBC iPlayer. I contacted Samsung support weeks ago about that as it's an app I use a lot normally, however they are yet to get back to me. A lot of the time the menu options are unavailable, not sure the parameters surrounding this but quite often menu options are blanked out so that you can't adjust them. I do have hope that Samsung can fix a lot of these issues with firmware updates going forward, as I do believe there is potential in this TV, without doubt. If you do manage to tweak the settings and get them just right for your content then the picture can look quite spectacular. But overall it has a long way to go, which is why at this point unfortunately I could not recommend this TV to anyone. The AI integration which is obviously marketed as the TV's selling point seems to be actually holding it back at this moment in time. The struggles with picture aside, I can't even figure out how to get AI sound to work! The advert on the product's selling page depicts a graphic of someone speaking into their remote to have the background music turned down, the singer's voice enhanced etc... Have tried and cannot even get this to pretend to work. I just get asked to set up voice recognition with bixby or alexa and even after doing so can only navigate the menu's via voice control, I can't instruct the TV using this feature at all!

title: Wow... Those Colors
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I'm big into picture quality, and our premium pick has always been OLED.
We decided to try this new Micro RGB display since it’s essentially a gateway into Samsung's next-generation panel tech. And wow... I have to say, I'm incredibly impressed. I definitely think this is designed for people who want cutting-edge picture quality but have some issue or another with OLED. 

Compared to OLED, the R85H uses thousands of microscopic, individual red, green, and blue LEDs to build the image. 

The main reason to consider this TV is the color purity and because there's virtually no filtering or color bleeding. Colors look incredibly rich without feeling artificial or over saturated. A bright landscape looks remarkably true to life, and It manages to deliver the deep, ink-like blacks you expect from OLED's while maintaining enough brightness to handle a well-lit living room during the day. Just super impressive overall.

I'm also a big fan of the 144Hz Refresh rate when gaming. 

Bottom line, if you genuinely appreciate color accuracy and want a high-performance screen for movies and gaming, and don't want ANY burn in risk from OLED, this is your TV. For us, it's been a stellar performer.
author: Munchys

title: Impressive Brightness and Color
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I’ve owned a lot of Samsung TVs over the years, so I had pretty high expectations going into this — and this one definitely delivered in a few key areas.

The first thing that stood out immediately is the brightness. This TV gets very bright, which makes a huge difference in my game room where there’s a lot of natural light during the day. Even with windows open, the picture still looks punchy and clear without needing to dim the room.

Colors are another strong point. Everything looks really vibrant without feeling overdone — especially with sports and streaming content. HDR content in particular looks great, with highlights really popping more than what I’m used to on older TVs.

I also appreciate how clean and responsive the interface is. Setup was straightforward, and it integrated quickly with my existing Samsung ecosystem. Navigation feels smooth and everything loads fast, which isn’t always the case with smart TVs.

For gaming, it’s been a solid experience so far. Motion looks smooth and input feels responsive, which is important for how I typically use this TV.

If I had to nitpick, darker scenes aren’t quite at the same level as some higher-end OLEDs I’ve seen, but in a brighter room setup like mine, that tradeoff is honestly worth it for the extra brightness.

Overall, this feels like a great balance between performance and practicality. If you watch a lot of TV in a well-lit space or just want something that really pops visually, this is a strong option. Definitely happy with it so far.

body:

When we're watching anything from movies, to shows, or sports, you see these colors are incredibly punchy and accurate without bleeding into each other. It really hits that sweet spot between the raw brightness of a traditional LED and the rich contrast of an OLED, and, you get zero anxiety about screen burn-in. title: Très belle image
body:
Après plusieurs semaines d'utilisation, je suis vraiment content de cette télévision.
 La qualité d'image offerte par la technologie **Micro RGB** est tout simplement exceptionnelle.
 Les couleurs sont d'une richesse remarquable, le contraste est quasiment parfait et le rendu global procure une véritable sensation de réalisme. 
Le design est également très réussi, avec une finition élégante qui met parfaitement en valeur le téléviseur.
 En revanche, je suis très déçu par la partie **intelligence artificielle**. Malgré de nombreux essais et différents réglages, je n'ai jamais obtenu un résultat satisfaisant. Au contraire, les traitements IA dégradent souvent l'image et produisent un rendu qui ne correspond pas à ce que l'on attend d'un téléviseur haut de gamme.
 J'ai finalement préféré désactiver la plupart de ces fonctions. L'autre point qui mérite d'être revu est la nouvelle interface. Elle est beaucoup trop complexe et manque d'intuitivité. Certaines fonctions demandent trop de manipulations et l'expérience utilisateur gagnerait à être largement simplifiée. 
Le réglage de l'image en HDR est peu simpliste sur ma tv Samsung précédente ,j'avais plus de réglage pour améliorer la qualité image.
 En résumé, Samsung réalise un véritable exploit sur la qualité d'image avec cette technologie Micro RGB, qui est sans doute l'une des meilleures que j'aie pu voir. En revanche, l'intelligence artificielle, l'ergonomie de l'interface  mériteraient d'être profondément améliorées afin d'offrir une expérience à la hauteur de l'excellence de la dalle.

title: Panel glitch
body:
I bought the 75" RGB in the middle of this June. TV itself is amazing no doubt. Anti-glare works great for the bright room, pic quality is really great,  colors popping up amazingly. Everything was working fine till yesterday until the right side panel started glitching. Then I contacted support team and he helped me with the troubleshooting. Now TV is working fine again after factory resetting. But it's really concerning for me that after just 2 months it started glitching and what if it happens again just after the 1 year of manufacturing warranty then I've to pay out of my pocket. I'm a Samsung user for almost 2 decades and preferred Samsung over Sony for this new RGB series.

title: TV Samsung équipée de la technologie Micro RGB
body:
[Cet avis a été recueilli en réponse à une offre.] Après plusieurs semaines d'utilisation, je suis vraiment impressionné par cette télévision.

La qualité d'image offerte par la technologie **Micro RGB** est tout simplement exceptionnelle. Les couleurs sont d'une richesse remarquable, le contraste est quasiment parfait et le rendu global procure une véritable sensation de réalisme. Le design est également très réussi, avec une finition élégante qui met parfaitement en valeur le téléviseur.

En revanche, je suis très déçu par la partie **intelligence artificielle**. Malgré de nombreux essais et différents réglages, je n'ai jamais obtenu un résultat satisfaisant. Au contraire, les traitements IA dégradent souvent l'image et produisent un rendu qui ne correspond pas à ce que l'on attend d'un téléviseur haut de gamme. J'ai finalement préféré désactiver la plupart de ces fonctions.

L'autre point qui mérite d'être revu est la nouvelle interface. Elle est beaucoup trop complexe et manque d'intuitivité. Certaines fonctions demandent trop de manipulations et l'expérience utilisateur gagnerait à être largement simplifiée.

Enfin, je regrette le choix des boutons de raccourci de la télécommande. Les touches dédiées à Netflix, Prime Video ou d'autres plateformes imposent des services que tous les utilisateurs n'utilisent pas. Il aurait été bien plus judicieux de proposer **trois boutons entièrement programmables**, permettant par exemple de lancer directement des applications comme **Orange TV**, **Molotov**, ou toute autre application choisie par l'utilisateur.

En résumé, Samsung réalise un véritable exploit sur la qualité d'image avec cette technologie Micro RGB, qui est sans doute l'une des meilleures que j'aie pu voir. En revanche, l'intelligence artificielle, l'ergonomie de l'interface et la personnalisation de la télécommande mériteraient d'être profondément améliorées afin d'offrir une expérience à la hauteur de l'excellence de la dalle.

Cet avis est équilibré : il met clairement en avant les qualités exceptionnelles du téléviseur tout en formulant des critiques précises et constructives sur les points à améliorer.

title: Premium bright room and gaming focused TV
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] To begin with: This is not OLED. It is Samsung’s new Micro RGB LCD-style display system using separate red, green, and blue LED backlighting for wider color and more precise light control. Let's dive deep:

1. Picture quality 4.6 / 5
Excellent overall. The R95H appears to deliver a very bright, colorful, high-contrast image that suits streaming, HDR shows, animation, sports, and games.
2. Brightness / HDR 4.7 / 5
A major strength. It is far brighter than most OLEDs and well-suited to daylight viewing and HDR gaming. It supports HDR10+, but not Dolby Vision.
3. Black levels 4.3 / 5
Very strong for an LCD-based TV, with unusually good local dimming and limited blooming. It still will not match OLED’s pixel-level black control in a dark room, and blooming can become more visible from wider angles.
4. Motion handling 4.0 / 5
Good, but not flawless. The panel supports up to 165Hz and has AI Motion Enhancer Pro, but at default settings the processing is too aggressive, you will have to adjust the settings.
5. Gaming performance 4.8 / 5
This is where the TV shines. You get 4 HDMI ports rated for 4K 165Hz, VRR, ALLM, Game Bar, AMD FreeSync Premium Pro, cloud gaming support, and ultra low input lag in Game Mode. PC gamers will have a blast with this!
6. Smart TV platform and app support 4.3 / 5
One UI Tizen is feature-rich: Samsung TV Plus, SmartThings, Matter, Apple AirPlay, Google Cast, Bixby, Alexa, Gaming Hub, and cloud gaming are listed. The interface is powerful, though Samsung’s smart TV UI can feel busier than Google/Android TV or Roku. I have personally loved the 24 hr ambient music channels on Samsung TV plus.
7. Sound quality 4.2 / 5
Better than average for built-in TV audio: 4.2.2-channel speakers, 70W output, Dolby Atmos, Object Tracking Sound+, Q-Symphony, and voice enhancement. I'd highly recommend a premium soundbar to go with this premium picture!
8. Design and build quality 4.4 / 5
Premium-looking, thin for its class, bezel-less, and uses Samsung’s Infinity Air Stand (Mirror finish on the front). It also supports Slim Fit wall mounting. One Wireless Connect Box is not included with this model which was a letdown. The TV supports it but I couldn't find it for sale anywhere.

Final Verdict: 4.5/5
Best for: Hardcore gamers wanting a future proof 165 Hz display, cloud gaming integration and near zero lag, even in bright lit rooms.
Not ideal for: Cinephiles who need Dolby Vision and zero bloom back levels during dark room viewing.

title: Samsung 65" R95H Micro RGB TV
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Samsung’s 2026 R95H brings Micro RGB display prices out of the to high to afford price and into a more reasonable price for a 65-inch set. After a week with it, I’d say it’s worth the money.

Setup and build
The TV arrives very well protected; packaging is thorough. Assembly is easier if accomplished with two people. The nearly bezel-less design when placed using a wall mount make the screen look like it’s floating on the wall.

The Screen
Peeling off the protective film reveals an effective anti-reflective coating making glare minimal, which is a big deal with such a bright TV in a well lit room. Picture quality is the highlight: colors come close to OLED, brightness exceeds OLED and matches Mini LED, and HDR highlights are bright without losing detail. Blacks and shadow detail are handled very well, this display is genuinely the best of both worlds. I didn’t notice ghosting or glare whether I was watching shows or playing games, and viewing angles remain excellent even in bright rooms.

Sound
The built-in speakers are good. I still prefer a separate soundbar for a true home theater experience, but out of the box the TV’s audio is perfectly acceptable.

Verdict
The R95H lives up to the hype. If you want a premium display and can afford it, this display needs to be included in what you look at purchasing.

The brightness of this TV is also amazing. I’ve got the TV mounted directly across from a window and I’ve never has any brightness or glare issues. Lastly, the TV has many AI features built in such as automatically adjusting display and sound settings based on content and an advanced up scaling algorithm for lower resolution content. title: Samsung 65" R95H Micro RGB TV Review
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Samsung's 2026 R95H brings its Micro RGB display technology down from an expensive niche product to a far more accessible price for this 65 inch model. After spending time with one, it's clear this TV is something special.

Setup and Build

Packaging is thorough and the screen arrives well protected. Assembly is easy enough, though an extra pair of hands helps. Once it's up, the bezel less design and near invisible stand give it a genuinely premium, floating look in a room.  Look at the attached photo with a plasma screen behind it to see the contrast in glare!

The Screen

The first wow moment comes early: peeling the protective film off reveals an antireflective coating that practically eliminates glare. For a TV this bright in a sunlit room, that's a bigger deal than it sounds.

Picture quality is the real story, though. Colors are very near OLED quality, brightness is better than OLED and on par with Mini LED, and HDR highlights are handled beautifully bright without blowing out detail, dark without losing shadow information. It genuinely is the best of both worlds.  I did not see any ghosting or glare, even with video games.  Wide angle viewing is great as well, even in a very bright room

Sound

Surprisingly good for built in speakers. Most people may  still want a soundbar for a full home theater setup, but out of the box it holds its own.  I have not bothered to add any external speakers yet.

Verdict

The R95H is one of those rare TVs that actually lives up to its hype. If you're in the market for a premium screen and can stretch to the price, this one is hard to beat.

Score: 9/10

[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Upgrading to the Samsung 55-Inch S85H OLED has completely transformed my home entertainment experience.  The picture quality is absolutely stunning and the colors are incredibly bright and vivid.  Whether I am watching a fast paced action movie or regular TV the picture has been great every time.  The blacks are truly pitch black and creating amazing contrast that makes every scene pop.  I am also thoroughly impressed by how natural the skin tones look.  People on screen look remarkably lifelike, just like a real person standing in front of you.  Navigating content is just as seamless thanks to the built-in Vision AI smart platform, which makes it incredibly simple to pull up and organize all my favorite streaming services like Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and HBO Max, etc. right out of the box.

Beyond movies and streaming, this TV has proven to be an absolute dream for gaming.  I hooked up my Nintendo Switch 2 and the graphics have honestly never looked better.  The colors are brilliant, and the motion is incredibly smooth, completely eliminating any stutter or blur during intense gameplay.  The combination of breathtaking visuals, easy app integration, and flawless gaming performance makes this model a massive step up from my previous setup.  If you are looking for a premium display that handles everything from cinema to next-gen gaming effortlessly, this 2026 model is a phenomenal upgrade.

title: Samsung Steps Up their Entry-Level OLED Game
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] As the entry-level OLED in Samsung's 2026 lineup, this model doesn't come with the anti-glare coating that I am a big fan of, so it's more of a bedroom / basement TV than a bright living room TV. The upside of the lack of coating is the improved contrast and black levels, which makes a difference when you're watching night scenes in sci-fi or horror movies. 

With HDR10+ support now available across Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Disney Plus, Apple TV+, and Paramount+, the lack of Dolby Vision is no longer an issue. This TV brings you the best of 4K and HDR, with no compromises. The processor on this TV is also pretty good at upscaling non-4K content. 

The overall user experience is pretty smooth, and Tizen OS has gotten pretty fast and responsive. The SolarCell remote light charging is pretty useful, it's nice not worrying about charging, but I really wish that Samsung would bring back the Input button or allow for a custom button. 

You will definitely want to pair this a soundbar, ideally a Samsung one to get the most out of the center channel Q-Symphony setup, although the feet on the TV makes the placement of certain soundbars a bit more tricky if you are not wall-mounting the TV.

If you've never used an OLED before or are looking for a home theater dark room TV, the S85H is the perfect way to get started. After trying it out you will find it hard to use any other type of TV again.

title: OLED is a game changer!
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] It has been around 8 years since I updated my main living room TV. I had a 58-inch 4K TV from another brand, and I was content with it. But when I connected the Samsung OLED S85H for the first time and saw the dazzling display of colors, I felt someone had removed a filter of dullness from my eyes, and that now I was actually seeing what true colors were really like in my living room!

Now, this is not my first rodeo with OLED screens. My cellphone and PC monitor are both OLEDs. But there is a marked difference from watching an OLED screen of 7/24 inches, to one of 55! The setup went smoothly, since it was automatically detected by my Samsung phone. The smart functions of the TV have all of the streaming apps you need, and it even has XBOX Game Pass remote included, so if you have a good connection, you can actually play Game Pass games on this TV with just a controller. The TV detected my soundbar without issue, and the setup only took like 10 minutes.

The image quality of this TV is magnificent.  The blacks are real blacks, not grey like my old TV. The colors pop with dazzling brightness and contrast, and the TV has different safeguards and functions to protect the OLED display from any burn-in. I connected my game console to the TV, and gaming here is a delight as well. 

Overall, this TV showed me how much TV technology has advanced in the past few years. I now regret not getting a Samsung OLED TV sooner, since I could have been enjoying my media consumption exponentially more. But better late than never! This is the best TV I have ever owned, and I would 100% recommend it to anyone.

title: Major upgrade in every way
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] When I unboxed the Samsung S85H OLED, the first thing that stood out was just how thin it really is. After getting the correct bolts to mount it to my existing setup (M8 machine screws, 1.25"), I was able to get everything installed without issue.

I paired the TV with my new Samsung Music Studio 7 speaker, and using the Q‑Symphony feature, the TV and speaker work together to deliver really impressive sound. It’s a noticeable step up and fills the room well.

One of the biggest improvements for me has been the lack of glare. In my living room, I usually deal with reflections from daylight and overhead LED lighting, but that’s no longer an issue.

Watching during the day or at night has been a much better experience overall.

The picture quality is outstanding. The image is extremely crisp, and blacks are truly pitch black without the light bleed you typically see on more basic HDTVs. I connected both an Apple TV and a Fire TV Stick, and everything looks fantastic on this display.

I also appreciate how seamlessly the TV integrates with the Samsung SmartThings app. Having additional control and getting notifications — like alerts from the washer or dryer — is a nice bonus that fits well into my existing setup.

I would highly recommend the OLED experience to anyone who hasn’t owned one yet, especially if you’re not impressed with your current TV’s performance or struggle with glare. This TV has been a major upgrade in every way that matters to me.

title: My Samsung TV
body:
If you’re referring to a specific TV, could you tell me the brand and model number (or send a photo of the product page)? That way I can explain its exact features and whether it’s good value.

In general, if it’s a modern smart TV with advanced features, you can expect benefits such as:

* 4K Ultra HD resolution for sharper, more detailed images.
* HDR support (such as HDR10, Dolby Vision, or HLG) for improved contrast and more vibrant colours, depending on the model.
* A Smart TV platform (Google TV, Android TV, webOS, Tizen, etc.) with access to streaming apps like Netflix, Disney+, Prime Video, and YouTube.  
* Voice control using Google Assistant or Alexa on supported models.  
* Built-in Chromecast or screen mirroring for casting content from your phone or tablet.  
* Gaming features such as HDMI 2.1, Variable Refresh Rate (VRR), Auto Low Latency Mode (ALLM), and 120 Hz refresh rates on higher-end models.  
* Wi-Fi and Bluetooth connectivity for wireless accessories and internet access.
* Multiple HDMI and USB ports for consoles, soundbars, and external storage.

If you share the model number, I can tell you:

* its strengths and weaknesses,
* whether it’s worth buying,
* how it compares with similar TVs,
* and whether it’s suitable for movies, sports, or gaming.

title: Great TV just wish setting it up was easier
body:

I am not a techie and I really could have done with a paper manual not trying to do it electronically. For me clear concise  instructions to set up to what would serve for 90% of users as base settings would have been helpful.

I watched a documentary on IPlayer and the screen kept changing from full screen to a screen with the top and bottom missing and black ( about an inch at the top and one and half inches at the bottom). I found the same when watching live TV where some programmes were on the full screen others on the reduced screen (BBC/ITV/C5/C4)
I am not sure how to best optimise the screen settings for picture quality I know how to change them but not what would be the optimum setting for every day use
When I set up the tv and connected it to my satellite dish I tuned into Freesat but mysteriously after a day I found myself watching Samsung TV with what looks like Freeview with a whole host of extra channels. This may not be the end of the world but don't understand how or why it happened but I am assuming that as I am not receiving this through my Terrestrial aerial I will not loose the signal when raining as often happens when I used to use my Terrestrial aerial 

In fairness to Samsung I have not as yet contacted them (or the retailer) to ask for support as I have had the TV less than a week and I am still trying to work out what I really need help on - last night the screen was either full screen when I watched TV but missing the top and bottom when I was watching a recorded film . I have yet to establish if the freeview is reliable in bad weather so if it is then I would not need to revert back to Freesat and could benefit from the extra channels

I am confident that in time I will really appreciate this excellent TV for what it is I just wish that it was easier to set up ( I really miss those old fashioned TV retailers who when you bought the TV delivered it and set it up for you and gave elementary instructions -  )
Below I have given features only 4 stars but this is because there are probably too many for me which is the problem -  I simply don't know how to use them or indeed want to use some (why would I want even to control my TV through my phone) As you can gather I am not a 20 something I want a TV simply to watch live TV, programmes recorded on recorder and things  on some of the apps like IPlayer

title: Design Flaw: QE48S90F Does Not Sit Straight
body:
I purchased a QE48S90F 48” OLED, and unfortunately this is now the second unit I’ve had to return due to the same issue.

The TV tilts noticeably backwards when mounted on the stand. The problem is not the surface or installation — the stand itself is not straight, which means the TV will never sit level. As a result, the screen leans backwards permanently.

What’s most frustrating is that customer support seemed unaware of the issue and couldn’t provide any clear explanation or solution.

For a premium OLED model at this price point, this is extremely disappointing. A television should sit straight on its own stand — that’s a basic expectation.

I would strongly advise others to check this carefully before purchasing.

title: The cinema experience without the crowds
body:
The last time I went to the cinema I was surrounded by people munching and slurping through tacos, burgers, popcorn, and beers. It utterly ruined the film for me and only spurred my desire for the cinema experience at home. It was a beast of a machine to get into the living room, and took three of us to remove it from the packaging and fit the stand, so I would recommend taking advantage of home delivery/setup if possible. 

My living room is painted black, so despite its size, the tv isn't very noticeable when switched off. The picture is great, and built-in sound very impressive, though I am now wondering how great Dolby Atmos would sound through a proper setup.

If this is your first 4k machine then, like me, you will find yourself searching for 4k content just to gasp at the crispness of picture and richness of blacks, and revisiting all your favourite movie to have that wonderful cinema experience from the comfort of your own living room.

I have barely scratched the surface of what is capable though the SmartThings app, but this tv will certainly be wowing myself and family for years to come.

title: Absolutely Great TV
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I absolutely love the S90H! 

First things first, the build quality is quite good. The TV itself is impressively thin and setting it up on a stand was rather straight forward. However, I didn't have it on the stand for very long, as this TV looks even better wall mounted. It can get very flush with the wall, so flush you could almost convince people it's a piece of art hanging on your wall.

Speaking of art, the pictures I took don’t do it any justice! The colors absolutely pops when watching movies and gaming. The anti-reflective coating makes it great for both day and nighttime viewing. My room has a trapezoidal window that's difficult to cover, so daytime light is unavoidable. This TV absolutely handles it like a champ! On most TVs, just a little light will turn the entire screen into a mirror. When the TV is off, you can see how the light diffuses across the screen but when actually watching content it completely disappears. In the image of Mario Kart World (on Rainbow Road in the stars) you can somewhat see it in the top right corner, but in most scenarios you are never going to notice it.

One thing that definitely surprised me with this TV is the sound quality. When I first turned it on, I put on Jeopardy and thought, “Wow the dialogue is pretty good!” Obviously Jeopardy isn’t a great test of audio quality, which is why I decided to watch Encanto! The opening song was a tad worrying, since the instruments were louder than the vocals. However, I think that might be a problem with the audio mix, because every other song sounded great! I wanted to test the AI audio features, however I couldn’t turn off the AI video features, which were not to my liking.

Finally, gaming on this TV was amazing! There are a few quirks with getting HDR set up on the Switch 2, but there are countless videos that help. Playing Pokopia was a blast! Seeing all the colors pop on the screen and hearing the game’s soundtrack on this TV was a real treat. 

I would highly recommend this TV to anyone as it looks fantastic! I can’t wait to watch more movies and games on it!

title: Superb
body:
This was the first ever TV that I bought for myself, thinking it would be ideal for my bedroom. It has been exactly that. Both the sound and picture quality are excellent, and the ease of use is remarkable. Having multiple remotes provided is useful, as I can use one to quickly access streaming platforms and the other when I want to watch live TV quickly. The auto brightness adjustment feature has been most beneficial when I am watching TV in the dark, and again in the full shine of the sun. It is also great for gaming on, having tested it with Nvidia Geforce Now. Two things to be aware of with gaming, though:
1. The TV will not exceed 60 hertz if it is not in 'Game Mode', which in itself is only possible when the TV is connected via HDMI to a console or PC. So if you are using platforms like Nvidia Geforce Now, you will only be able to achieve a maximum of 60 fps.
2. If you are using a cloud platform and have to sign in to an account in a game, (for example signing into your Xbox account when playing Forza) you cannot do this with either of the remotes provided, or an Xbox controller. In my case, I had to plug in a wireless keyboard and mouse to enter my account information. This is something that can be easily fixed by having an on-screen keyboard, but alas it was missing.

Overall, however, I have been remarkably impressed with this TV and would definitely recommend it!

title: One of the best OLEDs in the Market
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] After evaluating the 55-inch Samsung S90H OLED TV, I’m particularly impressed by the panel’s ability to deliver precise luminance control at the pixel level. The OLED structure enables true black levels with effectively infinite contrast, and this is evident in how well the display maintains shadow detail without introducing visible blooming or halo artifacts. Near-black performance is especially noteworthy, with smooth gradation that avoids banding in darker scenes.

Peak brightness is strong for an OLED panel, which helps sustain specular highlights and improves HDR impact. Highlights retain detail rather than clipping, and the tone mapping appears well-calibrated, balancing brightness with color accuracy. The color volume is also robust, allowing the panel to maintain saturation even at higher luminance levels, which contributes to a more lifelike image.

From a motion standpoint, the panel’s fast response time minimizes blur, and motion interpolation can be adjusted to reduce judder without introducing an artificial “soap opera” effect. Native refresh handling ensures consistent playback across different frame rates, which is noticeable when switching between cinematic and broadcast content.

Upscaling performance is solid, with effective noise reduction and edge refinement that preserves detail without over-sharpening. Compression artifacts are handled reasonably well, especially in streamed content.

The smart interface runs smoothly with minimal latency, and general responsiveness supports a seamless user experience. Build quality is excellent, with a thin panel design that feels structurally sound.

Overall, the S90H demonstrates strong technical execution across contrast, brightness, color accuracy, and motion handling, making it a highly capable display for both everyday viewing and more demanding visual content.

title: No more reflections!
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Upgrading to this 55” OLED was a huge change in more ways than one.

1. Display – an OLED display with a matte finish works perfectly for my bright room. Its screen is plenty bright enough to be viewable where the blacks still look very much deep black. The matte finish doesn’t take away from the picture quality at all. The best part of the of a matte screen is the lack of reflection in a bright room which makes the experiencing of watching TV less distracting during the day.

2. Sound – I was really impressed by the audio from this TV. It has depth, range, and a richness I would expect from a soundbar. The TV’s volume also gets very loud. The audio is still very clear at a higher volume as well. With all confidence, I won’t be going with my sound bar and just using the audio from the TV instead. It’s that good especially for a small room I have the TV in.

3. Ecosystem – I have Samsung appliances, tablets, earbuds, and the like and these devices integrates with the TV seamlessly. They automatically connect once the devices are turned on. I’m able to get notifications on my TV as to when my laundry is done or my oven has preheated. I find it really useful if your already in the ecosystem

4. Form – This thin but the bottom of the TV does provide confidence in mounting this TV on wall mount. The bezel less design makes the TV look really good where it becomes a centerpiece in my room. In terms of heat, the panel doesn’t really get too warm where it would warm the room.

Overall – this TV fits the bill for all my needs

title: The Best TV I've Ever Owned
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Where do I start! This Samsung TV is literally the best I've ever owned and seen with my own two eyes. As I unboxed, I immediate noticed how super thin the edges are, literally thinner than my monitor which was shocking. I was so worried that there would be a crack or a dent from the shipment because of how thin the upper edges are. The lower half of the TV is a bit thicker as it had the meat and potatoes of the screen inside, but still very thin compared to other TVs of the recent past. 
The colors! This TV has such deep blacks, and such a range of color, it is incredible. Whether watching the NCAA final four tournament, or watching an episode of Game of Thrones, the colors are stunning and visually satisfying. Ai is built in to help with colors and things if you allow it which is pretty cool. 
I have a PS5 and have played NBA 2K, Assassin's Creed Mirage, and Ghost of Tsushima, I almost dropped drooled at the graphics on these games. So crisp, so clean, and there's a whole set of game mode settings which allow you to make adjustments that you'd like for your preferred viewing. 
The sound! This is the first TV I've ever had or been around where the sound sounds like they have real speakers built in! There is base, treble, all of the things and if I didn't already have a sound bar and a music frame, I wouldn't feel the need to buy one! 
The one thing I don't like. There is an auto detection mode where if you walk by the screen, it automatically turns on to the brief page (which gives you a summary of current events, weather, music). I don't like this mode so I turned it to manual instead. 
This TV is a 12/10, I don't see myself changing for years to come.

title: OLED without the worries! S95H 77"
body:
I avoided OLED for many years, opting for Samsung and QLED tech because of concerns over panel brightness and of course, the dreaded burn-in issues that while being far less of an issue in recent years, had kept me from making the leap.
When Samsung began producing this tech, I kept up on advancements and waited.
At last, I made the move with the S95H, hearing nothing but good things. 
I was not disappointed.
Everything about this TV hits the mark, then blows it up. My main concern, my bright room placement is gone. Even previous QLED models, while bright, still struggled with contrast and deep blacks along with panel reflections. All gone with the S95H. The anti reflective coating is absolutely perfect in defusing any type of light and making it a non-issue. 
Color reproduction is beyond expectations, providing the colors and deep black tones usually reserved for other TV brands. Now, you get all that along with unbelievable brightness levels effectively eliminating any type of room setup. I can't say just how amazing a panel this is in accomplishing such excellence in both these areas. 
Connectivity is curing edge as well, from HDMI, to WI-FI, to Bluetooth options, integration with Samsung Smartthings, to screen sharing and AI incorporation.
The UI is upgraded and did take some relearning, but if you've owned other Samsung TVs this is a small curve. Some will find the AI integration to be a tad heavy handed at times (which I did) but with a bit of time, most features can be tweaked to fit your operating style including integration with other components like a home theater system.  Power up time and responsiveness to remote and verbal commands were all excellent with very few issues in having to repeat a command. 
Picture quality across all types is simply class leading, from 4K content to upscaling standard def feeds, the display options and tools to refine what you see is excellent at all levels. Once setup, the uniform production between all types of content is simply great!
Panel design seems to be the one area that comes up in reviews online and is subjective to each owener. For me, this was a non issue. I LOVE the floating design and have mine wall mounted. I happen to like the "framed" look and it fits my room look.  
I've owned pretty much every variation of Samsung panel over that 25 years and finally having an OLED option from a trusted TV maker, I can't say I'm disappointed with any part of the S95H 77" . 
The only area that could be improved, is taking their foot off the AI being in your face right from the start. I think this can be done with software updates and refinement. 
Overall, I would agree this TV is an industry leading device that is nearly perfect and still could still be absolutely perfect with some software modifications to the UI. 
A masterclass in technology and design.

title: Surpassed my expectations - matte finish rocks
body:
Spent several days watching Youtube reviews before buying this TV. That gave me a good idea of what I was getting, but they undersold the impact of the anti-reflective coating. This TV sits in my living room with 3 large east-facing windows right next to it. No amount of brightness can compete with those morning windows. This TV looks like it's doing magic.
The reviews also mentioned the silver frame around the TV as a mix bag. In our case, it looks fantastic, mainly because this TV and its "art" mode are not meant to go un-noticed by lack of visual features, but instead fall into the background because of its visual features. In the same way artwork has a frame, this TV frame just "fits" with other things in the wall.
The frame around the TV also made it significantly easier to handle the TV as the delicate screen feels more protected with it acting as a bufffer.
Having 4 full-bandwidth HDMI ports was also very welcome, since it allowed me to move away from a third-party input switcher.
The negatives are very minor. There is no simple way to have the TV fall back to art mode when turning it off and it doesn't waste a moment to offer a subscription (you can load your own pictures or art with Smartthings app without cost). It has several AI features I have not bothered to use.
TV is VERY bright, even in Filmakermode menu items are "too" bright, which had me reducing the overall brighness of the TV, else it is too much at night.
One last small negative is that the TV slim mount is not included, but it is a must; just make sure to get the newer one and put effort into proper wall mounting (with recessed connections). 

This is an amazing TV for folks with bright living rooms, and even at night I don't see how it can be beat. Anyone discussing "raised blacks" because of the matte finish is making the wrong argument. During the day, the matte finish saves the image, and during the night, the true blacks are there to be enjoyed.

title: Beautiful image, mediocre setup/implementation
body:
The excellent
==============
I was blown away by the image and sound quality (I paired it with the HW-990H soundbar setup). This panel is definitely brighter than my decade-old Samsung UN55JS8500) with a wider color gamut.  The QSymphony audio settings are pretty amazing -- making me want to re-watch old movies just to see how good they sound.

The recommended ultra-slim mount really lives up to its name -- it makes the TV hang so close to the wall that you'd think it was bolted directly down.

The mediocre
==============
Setup was cumbersome -- needing to install an app and configure an online profile just to order a TV seemed a bit much, and overall intrusive. I had to do some online research to find out how to maximize my privacy and turn off all of the unwanted features (that I could).

The minimalist remote control for the TV has a few nice touches (like having solar cells to recharge its battery).  It also has a few glaring omissions, like a mute button, and an input toggle.

The bad
==============
The user interface is overwhelming -- I don't need to be bombarded with ads, suggestions on what movies to watch or games to play. There should be a pared down option to just have your show your available source inputs, as well as the apps you have installed.

The TV is slow on the pickup to content from the various inputs.  The S95H only has 3 HDMI ports available if you choose to go the HDMI eARC route to connect the sound bar.  If you've got a few gaming consoles and/or other devices, you're going to need a switcher or an AV receiver in order to handle the overflow.  When switching from one input source to another via the switcher, the TV takes a good 10+ seconds to go from displaying source 1 to showing "no source available" to switching over to source 2.  This is something that never happened with my older Samsung TVs configured in the same manner (with a switcher)

The neither here nor there
==============
The TV's aesthetic design could be considered a "choice" -- one that you really like or not. I personally don't think that the silver-gray frame that the OLED panel sits atop is necessary -- it does little more than increase the TV's footprint for the same 54.6" diagonal panel.

body:
I bought this model 3 weeks ago after considerable research. My reason for purchasing was that on my very long serving previous Samsung TV had stopped receiving updates hence my insistence on  2026 model so that I had the maximum amount of time to receive operating system and app updates (See later).

The picture colour and contrast are superb and the TV compensates for high sunlight in our sitting room which means nobody viewing gets reflections; great feature which beats the competition hands down.

title: The Great, The Challenging and the not for all....
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The Good, The challenging and the Not for all….

The day finally came and elevated my excitement to get started… Here are my thoughts on the new product offering from Samsung after unpacking, mounting and setting up the new S95H.
The Good/Great:
Once up and running, This TV is a marvel. Top HDR performance with near-perfect blacks and massive peak brightness highlights. This TV was touted as having an increase brightness and it shows. One of the few OLED panels available that will take dark rooms and bright rooms with the same aggressive visuals around. The matte covering is another element where this OLED shines, no pun intended. It handles bright windowed areas by reducing glare and reflection with the matte finish better than my current OLED and LED models. Colors are spectacular with vivid highlights which allows colors like reds and yellows to pop noticeably more than other OLED models on the market. The S95H has moved the ports back to the panel and now offers an external wireless connect one box that is purchased separately and allows to increase the HDMI ports from 4 to 8.
The Not so Great:
 While this can apply to most TV manufactures, Home Hub and auto app setup need some fine tuning. Initial setup took over 45 minutes using my Samsung Fold 7 in getting the tv up and running which caused a loss in excitement in viewing the tv immediately. The home hub, which is not just a Samsung issue, is a disorganized mess with unwanted apps and bloatware. Having a store which allows each individual the ability to add their preferred content is ideal, installing bloatware is not. Still no Dolby Vision by Samsung…
The Not for everyone:
The silver frame: It had been brought up in reviews and I do not want to pass judgement on people preferences. Does the frame serve a purpose? It helped in setup by allowing to avoid mishandling the OLED panel. It does provide an ability to act as a frame in wall mounting purposes but the color scheme decision is surprising. Not sure how many homes have silver framed portraits and this just takes away from the aesthetics. 
Overall, Samsung continues to lead in product development and design. The S95H bridges the gap between OLEDs and QLED/LED TV by increasing brightness and finding solution for better angle viewing and finding solution for reduction in glare and reflection in brightly lit rooms. A refined TV for all alike which shows why this model continues to be a high-end choice by TV aficio

There are also a bunch of other things that I've yet to learn with this TV, and a ton more things I can't fit into this review, but overall, this is the BEST TV I have ever used, and I highly recommend it if you're looking for a TV!

title: The engineers and developers thought of everything
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I've had Samsung TVs for years, and frankly they are so good I haven't felt the need to upgrade from my older model (7 years old). However, finally the last year the old software was just moving too slow, and wifi issues caused me to make the switch. Can't recommend the upgrade enough! You don't know what you don't know, and while I thought I was getting a great tv experience it is improved in every measurable way with the new tv, and the ai smart features have given things I didn't even know I wanted! The picture itself is crystal clear but most importantly it is almost totally glare free and it's so bright that even in direct light (ours is in a very well lit room) the picture clarity is better then my old tv with all the lights off at night! I did a side by side run of the best movie for tv ever, "Top Gun" and maybe that was too much adrenaline for a Tuesday... I felt like I was the one getting catapulted of that carrier deck just sitting on my couch! While the sound quality is good, I would still recommend pairing this up with a full surround system to match the picture quality, but at stock the speakers do a decent job. The software is really where this shines though... The is an auto dashboard that is customized via ai with whatever is most relevant to me at all times. It pops up anytime I walk in front of the tv (can be turned off) and displays anything from the fridge door forgetting to be closed, to recommended stretches after my volleyball match, to weekend weather based on my calendar. The speed and fluidity at how the menu and ui work is impressive and intuitive. I love that all of my devices and smart home, even my watch all work on one single eco system now and can work off one another seamlessly. Can't recommend this TV enough, and would definitely choose it again if I was needing an upgrade even if you think your tv "has it all" like I did.

title: Amazing!
body:
We bought this 83 incher to replace a 65” Samsung we’ve had for close to 15 years that was still going strong and will continue to be used down in my shop. It’s our first OLED and we’re thoroughly impressed. I would recommend NOT flush mounting it. Buy a nice low profile mount that holds the unit 2” to 3” inches off the wall and install bias lighting on the back. It really helps bring out the deep blacks and gives the TV a floating effect. I’ll never own an other TV without bias lighting. We were a bit worried about the addition of the silver bezel for this H model but, wow, we absolutely love it. Makes the TV look less like a black appliance sitting on the wall and gives is a high end architectural look. 

The first thing we did once it was installed was to turn off all of the settings that make everything look like a soap opera. After 30 minutes to an hour of fine tuning we had the picture exactly where we wanted it. The blacks are truly incredible, as are the colors. Also love how the TV boots up instantly. I’m a big hockey fan and many modern flat panels struggle with the speed of the game. Not so with the S95H. There’s zero blur and the large size of the 83” makes it infinitely easier to follow the puck. I can’t really comment on the built-in apps as we run everything through a separate streaming device, nor have I messed with the AI settings or voice control yet. Same with the sound since our system consists of high end audio separates, which I think a TV in this class really deserves.

Overall after a few days of viewing we couldn’t be happier with this unit. It’s not inexpensive, but it’s worth the money given the quality. And if it lasts as long as our last Samsung it’ll definitely live up to its value.

title: My Living Room Has Come to Life
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I just retired my old TV after 12 years. With my new Samsung OLED S95H TV I feel like I've stepped into the future and brought my living room to life.

The picture is insanely bright (even during the day thanks to the glare free screen), and you can tweak everything yourself or just let the AI dial it in. It’s razor-thin , packed with ports (my kids are very grateful their Nintendo Switch has a proper stage now), and honestly the built-in sound surprised me. I don’t even have a soundbar and it still fills the room nicely. The remote is simple, shortcuts are clutch, and jumping into YouTube or Netflix is instant. With Dolby Atmos, movie nights have quietly turned into events.

But the real surprise in our house? Art Mode. During the day while my wife and I are working, we keep it on and suddenly there’s  Landscape At Twilight  hanging in the living room. Who wouldn’t want a little Van Gogh on display? It genuinely changes the feel of the space.

Overall? Huge upgrade. The kids are obsessed, we’re obsessed… and I might be rewatching old movies just for the visuals (no shame).

title: I'd LOVE to be a fly on the wall next to this tv!
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Loving the Samsung S95H! The brightness on this thing is a huge improvement over previous gen models. When it comes to TVs, im pretty much set on OLED only, but I like the bright panels like how QLEDs can provide. This one, so far in terms of sheer punch, is hitting the right notes! You can see in the accompanying pictures provided, the colors absolutely pop yet in another image, youll see the contrast between lit and dark areas like in The Batman are perfectly displayed on the screen. The OTS+ speaker system actually does impress (once you get to about halfway volume). While the bass isn't exactly earth-shattering, the audio quality is clear enough that I haven't even felt the need to hook up my soundbar yet. I would obviously not expect the bass to shake the wall, so tempering my expectations, color me satisfied by the built-in sound. Now hearing all about this frame around the panel is what originally piqued my interest, so I definitely wanted to check out the Art Mode, which I really did dig to be fair. Even though the subscription for the full gallery costs a few bucks a month, the way the art looks on this panel is legit! It honestly looks like a real painting hanging on the wall, they lower the brightness of the screen so it looks dull (in a good way) which makes it come off looking more realistic, like paper/canvas. The frame design really sells that "canvas" look when it's just sitting there, but it's not distracting - when I'm locked into a game or a movie, i barely noticed it was there. Physically, the TV feels super stable. The feet look small, but they’re solid. I actually gave it a bit of a shake test just to be sure, and it stayed put (video included). I also appreciated how intuitive the cable routing is on the back, which helps keep everything looking clean and slim. Finally, drum roll, the Tizen OS is actually snappy now. Samsung UIs have been pretty sluggish in the past, so having a responsive menu is a very welcome improvement. Looking forward to mounting this on the wall!

title: The most amazing picture quality I’ve ever seen
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] My new Samsung S95H has the most incredible clarity in its screen that I’ve ever had in a TV, the blacks are so dark but it’s not muddy at all. I upgraded from a good quality LCD to this new OLED model and the difference is night and day! The TV looks great on my wall even without turning it on. The flush mounting makes it look more like a piece of art than a tv with the metal trim and thin bezel. The sound quality is also excellent straight out of the TV, I tested it before hooking up my soundbar (which auto detected and added itself automatically using the Samsung Smart things connectivity. There are a ton of ports on the back for whatever you want to hook up and they are all recessed allowing the tv and cables to sit flush against the wall for a clean install. The on screen display is intuitive and very responsive, and all of my favorite apps came pre installed and ready to stream. Using the Smart Things backup feature all my accounts were imported automatically so I was ready to go right after completing setup. No need to navigate through clunky menus either, the TV has a simple QR code setup that you simply take a photo of with your phone and step through the setup. That is a huge improvement over trying to set up WiFi using a remote control! My gaming looks crisp and the fast response rate means no lost frames so I can remain competitive in online gaming and when the games are over the built in Samsung TV channels give me tons of free content to choose from without paying for cable. All in all I am super happy with this new TV and can’t recommend it highly enough.

title: Bright and Crisp Picture
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I have upgraded my LED TV after 11 years with Samsung OLED S95H TV. 
Pros:
1)	The picture quality is much brighter compared to my LED TV which is good for day time viewing 
2)	You can customize the Color, Brightness etc or you can select from the preset modes or you can let the AI do all the settings for you based on your room and light conditions
3)	The TV profile is very slim as you can see from the picture which is excellent when you are mounting it on the wall.
4)	There are enough USB and HDMI ports as shown in the picture. Also has HDMI port for Gaming Device which is a nice addition for Gamers. I use HDMI eARC to connect to my Soundbar.
5)	The TV Sound quality is also good without any Soundbar attached to it.
6)	Simple remote which integrates well with the Samsung Soundbar and also enables Q-Symphony where the TV Speakers augment the overall sound coming from Soundbar
7)	Shortcuts on the remote open Youtube, Netfix and Samsung Plus. Samsung Plus is similar to Google Chromecast with simple neat UI and navigation
8)	Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos experience is excellent for viewing movies
Room for Improvement:
1)	This is not a improvement for Samsung but in general OLED TV has the retention issue because of which if there is static page it brings in the screen saver to avoid image retention. When you use Amazon Music it shows the lyrics and due the screen saver you cannot read the lyrics after some time as the screensaver pops up.
2)	Q Symphony should be made available when we have other brand Soundbar as well so that this feature can be a value add from Samsung
3)	The grey border surrounding the TV might not gel well with black soundbars but it gels well with the Samsung Soundbars which are usually dark grey in color. May be some way to customize it would help.

title: LOVE AT FIRST SIGHT!
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] LOVE AT FIRST SIGHT!
I bought the 2026 Samsung OLED S96H 4k about a week ago and have marveled at the outstanding picture quality and the intelligence capabilities built into this TV set.  I opted for the 55” version with Art Store bezel that allows you to mount it flush on a wall to look like a framed picture piece of art.  I used the 2 base feet, which fit perfectly on my TV stand.  Setup was intuitive and easy to follow – the only minor issue was installing to a 5 year Hopper 2 old DISH TV box, which has not been upgraded to Hopper 3.  Plenty of connection points for your hardware: 3 USB-A ports and 4 HDMI ports built-in,  including an eARC HDMI Audio Return Channel that allows a simple 1 HDMI cord hookup for your surround sound system.  I hooked my TV up to my Samsung HW-Q800F Soundbar.  Sound is awesome, only beaten back by the AWESOME picture quality.  Colors and sharpness are so vibrant that everyone in at home wanted me to dial back the color saturation, brightness, and contract levels.  Best part of this TV for me is the anti-reflective screen, which eliminates the glare from a front door and 2 windows that have always given me fits when trying to watch something on TV during daylight hours.  Sports and Movies look FANTASTIC from any angle or distance in the room as Artificial Intelligence optimizes your viewing experience!  Great for playoff hockey and I can’t wait to watch Fall football!  Everything appears lifelike and puts to shame the old HD tv that has been relegated to basement duty.  This TV is definitely smarter than me, as I’ve yet to figure out the Bixby, Alexa, and Google assistants.   It supports any streaming service you can throw at it, with Samsung TV built in.  So far, this Samsung TV is LOVE AT FIRST SIGHT!
