title: Out of this world Mini LED masterpiece
body:
I have had any interest in TV technology and especially picture quality for many years now, probably stemming from my career of over a decade in the cinema industry. I have always been looking for the 'perfect' picture! With so many advances in technology the quality is always improving and giving more 'wow' moments. Just when I think I have seen the best and nothing can beat it, something new comes along.

Back in 2016 I purchased the Sony 65ZD9 which was the flagship LED at the time. It was stunning. It's actually still stunning and to this day produces an amazing image. But time moves on and after eight years, (and a newly decorated living room), I thought it was about time to invest in something larger and enough time had passed for a true jump in performance.

Enter the Bravia 9 75"! 

The first thing to say is this TV is heavy. Roughly 45kg with the stand. You will need at least two people to lift it, with the instructions actually advising three. The TV is extremely well packaged with large polystyrene sections around the whole screen. Cardboard and a plastic sheet also wrap around the whole TV. Accessories and back panel segments are all securely packaged. 

The first thing to do is attach the feet. These are substantial in their weight, being made of metal and finished in a very dark brushed gunmetal. The feet can be positioned in four different ways depending on your requirements. Due to my current, relatively small TV stand , I fitted mine in the narrow position raised up to fit a soundbar underneath. They are very easy to fit with just two screws for each foot. 

AV connections are all on the left (as you look at the TV), and are all covered by a removeable panel. There are a few panels to fit once you have fitted everything which gives a very clean and tidy look - something first started by the ZD9! Cables can be run down behind the legs of the feet and plastic cover then keep them in place. Very simple, but a great idea to hide cables away from sight. 

With the panels in place, they are 'hidden' with a chequered effect across the whole of the rear of the TV. Again it keeps everything looking very clean. The mains adaptor is wired into the TV so there is no external power adaptor. The AV connections include two USB ports, an optical connector, ethernet port, cable TV ports and four HDMI ports. Only ports 3 and 4 are 2.1 compatible so you need to use those for 4k/120hz gaming etc. Also you need to turn on the enhanced mode for those inputs which is found in the TV settings. 

But enough of the rear as it's not something you will be looking at often!

The edges of the Bravia 9 are framed with a aluminium metal which is a nice, and quality finish, but nothing outstanding. I did actually prefer the subtle gold finish on my old ZD9. Whilst on the subject of the sides, the depth of the TV is something that stood out to me when compared to many wafer thin TVs on the market. It's definitely not an issue for me though as it will be down to the technology inside which is the most important.

The bezel on the the front of the TV is almost wafer thin though! The sides and top of the screen have an 8mm black bezel. The bottom of the screen has a slightly wider separate metal strip running across the front in the same finish as the feet. This features the SONY logo sitting on the left hand side in a subtle finish.

The Bravia 9 is a very well built TV (almost like a tank!) and looks good but I feel it would have benefitted from a slightly more classy finish in some areas especially around the edges.

Another item which could have been better is the remote. Mine actually came with two, a standard plastic one with two AAA batteries, and a recycled plastic version with USB charging. The latter is slightly more weightier but I feel, for a premium flagship TV, this should have been aluminium or  higher quality material. The USB version features blue specks within the black finish which is ok but not really my cup of tea. It also features a microphone and lights up when it senses motion if the ambient light is dark enough - definitely a nice feature. This remote also has buttons specifically for certain apps such as Sony Pictures Core and Netflix.

Starting the TV up is quick and straight forward but make sure you set the date and time correctly otherwise it may not connect to the internet - something I found out and spending five minutes checking all my connections! It is also worth checking for any firmware updates when you set it up.

The sound is one of the very first things to set up. The Bravia 9 will carry out acoustic diagnostics based on the dimensions of your room. This will help provide the best surround sound for your environment. 

This is the first big revelation of the TV. 

The sound is amazing! There are no options for different types of surround sound effect such as Sport, Stadium, etc. Just On, Off or Auto which detects what type of sound is coming from the original source. The surround sound in my opinion is just as good as some separate speakers and soundbars. The TV includes speakers to give sound height as well as depth. It's truly impressive from TV speakers. Of course you can also set the TV up to use external speakers (ARC is included on HDMI 3), and the Bravia 9 can even be configured as the centre speaker for a true surround sound set up. The bass is very impressive and you can also adjust certain aspects of the sound. Definitely the best sounding TV I have ever heard!

Returning to set up in general and the menus. There are a bewildering array of different picture modes and settings. One thing I have found an issue with is trying to find the correct menu screen when you want to change certain options. There are also numerous sub menus if you want to calibrate the TV. The menus themselves are very fast and fluid.

The picture mode I immediately went to was Professional as I like the picture to be as realistic as possible. There are different modes depending on your preference, such as Vivid, Calm and Photo.

This all leads on to the star of the show, the picture itself (although the sound up there!).

I knew that after 8 years of buying my last TV, the technology would have improved but the Bravia 9 is stunning! 

Starting with SDR and even in professional mode with the low brightness of 4, the picture is amazing even in my bright living room. The screen itself is very anti-reflective which also helps. The colours are exceptional with skin tones looking realistic. Thanks to the Mini LED technology, the amount of dimming zones and software, one thing I immediately noticed was hardly any blooming around bright objects. I have never watched an OLED TV which I know are famed for their black levels, but the black on the Bravia 9 is superb. So far I have stayed with the local dimming set to medium as I think it gives the best balance of black level whilst retaining detail. The photo of the Robocop film was from a UK cable channel in 1080 HD. 

The other immediate area which struck me was the motion. My old TV was very good at it but did suffer with some motion blur especially on sports programmes. So far I haven't noticed any motion blur which I believe is down to the improved reponse times of the Mini LED's. Personally I switch off all motion enhancing options but they are there if you need/like them. 

And now we move on to the absolute highlight, (in every sense of the word!).

HDR.

HDR is what the Bravia 9 was built for. This TV is so bright it could compete with the sun (possibly!). Bright flashes almost make you squint especially in a dark room. Scenes in movies come alive. And all with very little or no blooming. Coupled with the superb black levels, the contrast gives almost a 3D feel at times. And of course HDR is not just about how dark or bright the picture is, but it gives stunning colour and details within those colours. One of the first things I watched was a SONY HDR demo from a USB file. I had watched it on my ZD9 and it was amazing. On the Bravia 9 it's on another level I didn't think possible. In one scene the sun glints on water and it truly looks like you are looking out of a window, not at a screen!

I would definitely recommend watching the IMAX Enhanced demo which can be found through the Sony Pictures Core App. The Bravia 9 has been certified for this content and it really shows off the performance capabilities of the TV. SONY also gave credits to use to buy films through the service which was a very nice surprise! Whilst using the Core app I noticed another bewildering choice of options. You can obviously keep the picture mode set to your normal mode or you can choose the Sony Pictures Core calibrated mode OR Imax Enhanced mode! To be honest I can't see any difference between Professional and the latter two.

Gaming is also a huge improvement over what I have been used to. There is a game mode (with various sub picture modes for FPS games, etc) and of course 120hz support. 

At the time of reviewing the Bravia 9, I have only had it for a few weeks. I could live with the professional mode but I will have the TV professionally calibrated. I had my ZD9 calibrated and it made a huge difference. I don't think it will make as big a difference on the Bravia 9 as SONY have done a great job on the picture out of the box. But with a premium flagship TV I want to get everything out of it as don't plan on changing it for a good few years! 

I wanted to give the Bravia 9 5 out of 5 but there are a few niggles. The overall aesthetics of the TV, the remote and the sometimes confusing menus have made me drop a star. However, incredible sound and truly amazing picture blows me away every time.  

I have only just started to scratch the surface of what the Bravia 9 can deliver and as this is new state of the art technology from SONY, further firmware updates will only elevate this TV even further into the stratosphere and into orbit next to that other extremely bright object.

title: Einzigartiger Fernseher
body:
Die Bildqualität ist gestochen scharf, und die Farben wirken besonders intensiv. Dank der neuen Sony-Technologie passt der Fernseher die Farbtiefe automatisch an. Der integrierte Subwoofer bietet eine beeindruckende Klangqualität und kann fast ein vollständiges Soundsystem ersetzen. Die Dolby-Einstellungen sorgen zusätzlich für ein exzellentes Klangerlebnis.

Zusätzlich habe ich die Soundbar HT-A5000 von Sony als zweites Ausgabegerät angeschlossen. Diese habe ich hinter der Couch platziert, um zusammen mit dem Fernseher ein 360-Grad-Soundsystem zu schaffen. Anfänglich funktionierte dies gut, doch nach einiger Zeit traten Synchronisations- und Verbindungsprobleme auf. Ich hoffe, dass ein zukünftiges Update das Problem behebt.

Die meisten wichtigen Anschlüsse sind vorhanden, was das Anschließen externer Geräte erleichtert.

Ich habe den Fernseher auch mit Google Home getestet, was reibungslos funktioniert hat.

Die Einrichtung war sehr einfach: Der Fernseher lässt sich sowohl über das Smartphone als auch manuell mit der Fernbedienung einrichten, und beide Varianten funktionieren problemlos

body:
I have the Sony Bravia 9, 75-inch TV, and after unboxing my first impressions were that it is a big TV, with excellent build quality and a very sleek design. 
I currently have the TV mounted on the feet that are supplied with it. You have a choice of width of where you place the feet, which is great to cater for different sizes of TV cabinet. Plus, the choice of height to have the TV, which allows the placement of a soundbar at the bottom of the TV.
What I do like is that the TV comes with a choice of remote controls, one of which illuminates and is also USB rechargeable. The quality of the Eco-friendly plastics used for this is much improved on previous versions of remote controllers.
Setting up the TV I found was straightforward, almost like plug and play. After connecting to the WIFI, the TV recognised what I was connecting to it, (satellite service, sound bar and voice activated service) and then through the built in Google TV, logging on to my streaming services following the easy onscreen instructions and QR codes.
I was all set up and ready to watch and explore the features of this TV very quickly.

I am very impressed with the excellent picture quality from this TV. It adapts to its environment well, the picture is vibrant and sharp.  For me this TV reproduces well balanced vivid colours, contrasting shadows and highlights, in what to me looks very accurate representation and with true colour tones. 
The TV has several pre-defined viewing modes which you can change dependent upon the content you are watching. There is also the option to fine tune these picture settings to really make the picture you see personal to your taste. 
In addition, this TV also continues with the feature to provide the option to calibrate and optimise your feed from streaming services, again with the additional options to make the viewing adjustments for yourself.
Personally, I am more than happy with the output from the predefined picture settings provided and have not needed to fine tune or tinker with anything.
The picture produced by this TV is giving me an excellent immersive viewing experience that both me and my family are thoroughly enjoying.

Also contributing to this immersive experience is the audio that is produced by this TV. 
The TV adapts the sound to the size and shape of the room, and I can say that the sound direct from this TV is the best I have experienced. Again, you can utilise the built in equaliser function where you can adjust the sound output to suit your own taste. The sound output really does fill the room with clear vocals, good midtones plus a decent bass sound, this TV produces a very good sense of surround sound.

The built in smart TV functions are comprehensive and intuitive, and again linking to your streaming accounts was very simple, following the on-screen instructions.

Overall, I think that this is an excellent TV with the standout features being both a stunning picture and superb sound output. In addition, for me, being able to adapt both picture and sound qualities to your own personal taste / room qualities only enhances a truly immersive and thoroughly enjoyable viewing experience that I have from this TV.

title: Sowas habe ich noch nicht GESEHEN!
body:
Das Sony der Konkurrenz mal wieder einen Schritt voraus ist, beweist dieser TV bereits vor dem Einschalten:
Nachhaltig produziert, qualitativ verarbeitet, platzsparend und sicher transportiert, intuitive Montage, problemlose Inbetriebnahme.

Nach dem ersten Einschalten des Geräts möchte man am liebsten nichts anderes mehr tun!
Einrichtung ging ebenfalls super schnell und problemlos. Die Google-TV-Benutzeroberfläche leitet einen sehr smart durch die Einstellungen. Auch das nachträgliche Anpassen von Optionen ist extrem intuitiv!
Das die Fernbedienung aufgeladen werden kann und bei Benutzung eine Hintergrundbeleuchtung besitzt ist sofort von unschätzbarem Wert, wenn man im Dunkeln (bei schwarzem Pause-Bildschirm einer Serie) wieder Play drücken will!
Tonqualität extrem beeindruckend, wir haben unsere externe TV-Anlage nichtmehr benötigt!

Nun zum Herzstück - dem Bild:
Dass es sich bei diesem Fernseher nicht um einen OLED, sondern einen Mini-LED-TV handelt, erkennt man nur auf dem Papier: die Schwarzwerte sind absolut identisch in meinen Augen!
Gleichzeitig bietet die Mini-LED-Technik einen Haufen anderer Vorteile: energiesparender, hochauflösender und schneller. In meiner subjektiven Wahrnehmung ist das TV-Bild auch einfach SCHÖNER!!!
Aufgrund der räumlichen Gegebenheiten sitzen wir verhältnismäßig nah am TV und dennoch kann ich weder einzelne Pixel erkennen.

Ich bin mehr als beeindruckt und war zu Beginn wirklich sprachlos!
Offensichtlich habe ich mich so sehr an die scharf gestochenen und farbenfrohen Bilder gewöhnt, dass jeder andere Bildschirm (sei es Laptop oder Tablet) trist wirkt und überhaupt keinen Charme mehr besitzt!

Von mir gibt es für diesen TV nichts außer eine klare Kaufempfehlung!
Egel ob Gaming, Streaming oder TV, aus meiner Sicht gibt es aktuell kein vergleichbares Produkt auf dem Markt!
author: Lorenz

title: True Flagship QLED Masterpiece with finesse
body:
Design and Build 9.5/10
The Bravia 9 is incredibly built, everything from the heavy metal feet to the sleek frame exudes quality. The metal feet can be positioned in four different ways, making it versatile for different setups, including a raised position to accommodate a soundbar. The rear has panels to help tidy all your cables. My only gripe is the non-removable power cable. 

The design is sleek and modern, with a checkerboard rear and metal speaker grills, making the Bravia 9 look good from every angle. The metal frame and Sony's logo on the bottom strip give the TV a premium feel. However, the remote, while functional, could have matched the TV’s quality with a metal top panel. I do like that it's rechargeable via USB-C and has voice search capabilities as well as optimising the TVs audio.

Picture Quality 10/10
The first thing that impressed me about the Bravia 9 is the fact it’s the only TV I have not had to adjust any of the settings. Professional mode on the Bravia 9 is absolutely perfect for watching movies. Normally I spend hours tweaking picture settings to get them just right. With the Bravia 9, the only adjustment I made was setting live colour to medium; everything else was spot on. The Bravia 9 is spectacularly bright which means in bright rooms, the TV gets plenty bright enough. The reflection handling is also excellent which helps at being perhaps the best TV available for bright rooms. In darker rooms, if the brightness becomes too much, then simply turn on the ambient light sensor and the TV perfectly adjusts the light output to ensure it is comfortable.

The control of how well the brightness is managed on the Bravia 9 is its greatest strength. The Bravia 9 doesn’t just blast out the brightest image possible; it is so much more nuanced than that. Contrast is excellent and was able to produce blacks very close to OLED. In some cases, there was a very small amount of blooming but it was not in any way distracting.

Being a QLED, the colours pop and thanks to the astonishing high peak brightness, the colour volume is immense. Motion is also excellent. In terms of picture quality, the Bravia 9 is the most impressive LCD I have ever seen. 

Picture Quality for Films and TV shows 10/10
When it comes to films and tv shows, ‘natural’ and ‘cinematic’ are the two words that come to mind. Motion is flawless when watching Blu Rays and there’s something so natural about how the Bravia 9 presents everything. The colour pallet is very well controlled with plenty of volume and such nuanced control over the brightness. 

Ghostbusters Afterlife- Sony Pictures CORE
The big fight scene at the end with the proton cannons really showed how well the Bravia 9 controls the brightness, with excellent colour depth and the black letter box bars were inky black with no noticeable blooming. 

Top Gun Maverick – 4K Blu Ray
The scenes where they tried to reach Mach 10 were beautiful. Colours were spot on; contrast was excellent with perfect shadow detail. Again, professional picture mode is the way to go. Details were super sharp and the blacks in the cockpit were deep and inky. 

Planet Earth 2 – 4K Blu Ray
The opening scene with the white snow showed just how clean the Bravia 9 panel is and how bright the TV can get. The details on the eagle were razor sharp and the colours demonstrated how much colour volume the Bravia 9 has. The TV had no issue reproducing any colour; it looked absolutely stunning with the perfect amount of saturation to show off how colourful life can be on planet Earth. 

The Grand Tour- Prime Video
The scene with the Bugatti Chiron had my jaw dropped. The details in colour, contrast, edges and the way the lights shone with such finesse on the spectacular highlights really showed me how impeccable the Bravia 9 is.

Quantum of Solace -Blu Ray
Upscaling 1080p Blu Rays was handled very well, without looking overly sharpened. Again, in professional mode, the Bravia 9 was nothing short of a masterpiece for cinematic SDR content.

Kong vs Godzilla – 4K Blu Ray
The night time fight scene with the neon lights was spectacular on the Bravia 9. Blooming was not an issue at all, even for super bright scenes from Kong’s axe and Godzilla’s atomic breath. The neon colours popped off the screen and were punchy and vibrant.

Mad Max Fury Road – 4K Blu Ray
The flames in the desert chase scene were incredibly rich and vibrant and the specular highlights coming off the chrome trim on the car were dazzling.  

Picture Quality for broadcast TV
Standard definition content on a 75 inch TV is hard work, nonetheless, the Bravia 9 was up for the task. However, I would advise increasing the resolution on reality creation in the picture settings menu as this does improve the picture quite a lot. For HD content, the Bravia 9 does an great job of upscaling again without making anything look overly sharpened. Sports was brilliant as the screen can maintain its high brightness and the panel is exceptional clean.

Gaming 9/10
Sony has quite a lot of features for gaming. The Bravia 9 supports 4K 120Hz gaming with VRR. There’s also a new PlayStation remote play app, allowing you to use Remote Play from your PlayStation directly on the TV. There is a gaming menu that displays the frame rate, adds a crosshair, allows you to resize the playable area, and toggle VRR. There are also three gaming presets: Standard, FPS, and RTS. Using the PS5 auto optimisation settings, the colours were gorgeous and the contrast was excellent. 

There is also the option for motion blur reduction. This was very helpful for Black Myth: Wukong, as I prefer the fidelity mode on this game, which comes at the cost of frame rate. The motion blur reduction is essentially black frame insertion and made it a much better experience. I would leave this setting on low or medium if you decide to use it, as it does reduce the brightness significantly when set to high.

Input lag wasn’t an issue for me when playing Call of Duty: Black Ops 3 Zombies or Gran Turismo 7 online. Where the Bravia 9 really comes into its own is with games such as Spider-Man 2, Horizon Forbidden West, and The Last of Us Part II Remastered. Colours on Spider-Man 2 were punchy, and darker scenes in The Last of Us Part II were handled well with excellent shadow details.

Sound Quality 10/10
There are a total of 8 drivers on the Bravia 9, including 2 height channels and frame tweeters (clever stuff). The sound is optimized using the microphone on the TV remote to ensure you get the best sound from the seating position. I started off watching Top Gun: Maverick and was gobsmacked at how good the speakers are on this TV. I haven’t heard another TV quite like this. There was plenty of bass, way more than I have heard from any other TV. Dialogue was clear, and the two height speakers did an amazing job when the jet flew overhead. The sound system on this TV has to be heard to be believed. If you are looking at a budget to mid-range soundbar, I wouldn’t bother; the Bravia 9 is more than adequate. Obviously, it isn’t a replacement for a high-end soundbar or a dedicated home theatre; however, Sony still allows you to integrate the built-in speakers into a compatible home theatre setup.

I use a 5.1.2 home theatre setup and felt like I wasn’t getting the most out of the TV if I didn’t use the TV speakers as well. Thankfully, Sony has thought of a solution to this. With a compatible Sony AV receiver or soundbar, you can use the TV speakers as a centre channel, or in my case, a second centre channel with Sony’s S-centre speaker mode. This feature allows you to make the most of the Bravia 9, as using it expands where the sound is coming from and makes it feel more like it comes directly from the screen. The effects are very subtle, to ensure there isn’t a mismatch between the dedicated speakers and the TV speakers; however, it does add some more height to the centre channel, which I find great.

Features 9/10
The Bravia 9 runs Google TV, which is an excellent operating system as you can download apps from the Google Play Store and Chromecast from other devices. The menu is easy to use, runs smoothly most of the time. There is a lot that can be customized in terms of quick settings and quick access to input selection, as well as controlling your AV receiver/soundbar settings. It comes with 10 credits to redeem films on the Sony Pictures CORE app. This app is something all other streaming platforms need to take a note from as the CORE app streams 4K HDR movies at high bitrates which rivals 4K Blu Ray. The app has a huge list of Sony films you can choose from, including many that can be watched for free. The tv also has a PlayStation Remote Play app, allowing you to connect to a PS5 in another room in the house and play on the TV. handy feature, however I do have my PS5 connected directly to the Bravia 9. 

The Bravia 9 supports Dolby vision, HDR10 and HLG. Streaming apps including Sony Pictures CORE, Netflix and Prime Video have an option to turn on calibrated mode which automatically puts your TV in the best picture mode. The Bravia 9 also supports Calman software which makes calibrating the TV easier. This is not something I have done as the professional mode results in phenomenal picture quality as is. 

Conclusion 10/10
Overall, the Bravia 9 produces some of the best picture quality I have ever seen; the colour volume is excellent, blacks are deep and inky, motion is absolutely perfect and there is such nuanced control of the brightness. Furthermore, the Bravia 9 has top-tier build quality, stunning design, runs Google Tv and has the best sound system I have heard built into a TV. This TV is the complete package for everyone and is truly one of the best TVs I have ever seen. I would highly, highly recommend it.

title: Bravo Bravia!
body:
I’m a fiddler, and I haven’t had a fiddle for 2 weeks. There, I’ve said it.

I’m one of those people that can’t help but fiddle, tweak and interfere with settings, whether it be in the car or my HiFi – it’s a bad habit that achieves marginal amateurish results.

My worst habit is fiddling with TV’s.

I sit there and torment myself - could the black be blacker? Is it bright enough? What about the skin tones? You get the idea.

It drives my good lady wife mad, and she quite rightly questions why I have to do this anyway, surely the investment in the item should give me the best out of the box. And of course she’s right, as she is with most things.

This brings me to the Sony Bravia 9, this is what I can only describe as a “statement TV”, everything about it is statement’y. The box is a work of recyclable art and engineering, designed with such thought that the box even assists in assembling the legs for the included stand (so clever).

The actual screen itself is finished in premium materials that simply look amazing in any room. Guests have audibly gasped with delight upon first sight – and that’s even before it’s powered on.

Feed it a high-quality signal like 4K, HDR or Dolby Vision and OMG (as my kids said), it’s breathtaking and a real WOW moment. The definition, the brightness, the colour and a first for me is the fabric of the image – almost better than life like. Despite all the technical wizardry going on behind the scenes, I’ve never seen an image look so NOT processed and so real-world-like.

I stand proudly admiring the image and the reactions of my casual audience, but there is no pride for me personally, as this isn’t a result of my own fiddling and tweaking and therefore, I can’t claim (like I used to) that this greatness was down to my fine eyes and my ability to navigate and interpret the settings.

Sony’s very clever engineers have created a TV that calibrates itself based on not only the specific content you are viewing, but also how you are viewing.

It’s called Calibrated Mode, and it’s a game changer. Whether you are streaming through Netflix or Prime or even Sony’s own Sony Pictures Core streaming service, the TV understands what you are watching and therefore what you should see, as The Director intended. 

A studio and professional quality image out of the box without all the hours and hours of fiddling. Add in the optional Bravia Cam, and it will even take into account your viewing environment (including your seating position) and calibrate accordingly.

My torment and that constant search for the perfect picture is over, all that’s left for me to do is to enjoy the movie or the game, and that’s the way it should be.

Bravo Bravia.

title: A nightmare!
body:
I received my 85 inch Bravia 9 on June 22nd and have had a whole host of issues ever since.
1. Unacceptable antireflection which interferes with picture even in a dark room.
2. Continuous and repeated issues with AV sync from HDMI input!
3.  Unacceptable presets (all Presets) for SDR content via HDMI requiring a lot of changes to picture settings to get even a minimally acceptable picture which is still  hampered by ghosting and haloing from the anti-reflective coating.  Any changes to picture settings leads to worsening of AV sync issues.
4. A lot of juddering and sometimes even pixilating on some areas of the screen in SDR content.
5. When streaming directly from the TV, none of the preset picture settings provide adequate picture quality, and Netflix and Amazon Prime calibrated modes are even worse, even in a completely darkened room. There is no difference when watching either SDR or HDR content. Different movies or series require a lot of adjustments to picture settings which interferes with watching content.  Amazingly, HBO Max calibrated settings seem to work better.
I don't believe that XR Clear Processing is working on this TV.
I scheduled and had a phone consultation with a Sony Rep a week ago and he promised to get back to me via email about some of these issues, but he has not.
I am at the point where I will need to return this TV for a refund.

body:

Helligkeit: Der Kontrast zwischen hellen und dunklen Bereichen ist extrem exakt und teilweise zu gut (Spitzenhelligkeit des Gerät wie ein Autoscheinwerfer bei Nacht).

Reflektionen am Tag: Gibt es nicht mehr, keine Ahnung wie das funktioniert aber wir haben 3 große Fenster direkt gegenüber und man sieht keine Reflektionen auf dem Bildschirm, einfach nichts.

Farben: Die Farbtiefe und vorallem die Natürlichkeit ist wirkt fast real.

Schwarzwert: Ich hatte vorher ein OLED TV und ich sehe kein Unterschied dazu, alles Schwarz ohne Grautöne.

Schärfe: Für mich persöhnlich perfekt.

Interface: Es läuft mit Google TV und ist halt wie mans kennt xD

Esta pantalla tiene un brillo que no he visto en ninguna televisión, y aunque es imposible que logre la profundidad de color negro de una OLED, lo compensa con su practicidad para el uso día a día en habitaciones con mucha iluminación. En ese escenario, nadie le gana. El acabado mate de la pantalla elimina perfectamente lo reflejos que genera la luz del día, sólo notándose un poco en la noche las lámparas de luz indirecta, lo cual es despreciable cuando la TV está iluminada.La profundidad de los colores es impresionante, y la reproducción de contenidos HDR es excelente. En cuanto al escalado a 4K de contenidos 1080p, sin duda Sony sigue siendo el líder de la industria, y ahora potenciado con IA, el procesador de la TV logra un resultado maravillos prácticamente en cualquier contenido de calidad aceptable que le pongas a la Bravia 9, especialmente en las aplicaciones nativas de Google TV. Si tu prioridad es tener un televisor que funcione de la mejor manera en entornos de mucha luz, este es el que debes elegir sin dudar. También es importante que con la Bravia 9 II, no vas a invertir nada de tiempo en configurarlo, pues el modo Profesional y los modos calibrados "My Cinema" para películas, lucen espectaculares recién salidos de la caja. De día o de noche, TrueRGB no decepciona.

title: Avis téléviseur Sony Bravia 9 II 75 pouces
body:
L'acquisition du téléviseur Sony Bravia 9 II en 75 pouces, en remplacement de mon Sony X8505B 55 pouces datant de 2012/2014, représente un véritable bond technologique, aussi bien en qualité d'image qu'en restitution sonore.

Le téléviseur est relativement simple à régler et propose des paramètres adaptés selon les plateformes de streaming ou les contenus que l'on regarde. C'est un investissement conséquent, mais je ne regrette absolument pas d'être passé d'un écran de 55 à 75 pouces avec un recul de 2,80 m : l'immersion est tout simplement exceptionnelle.

La luminosité est un autre point fort. Elle peut être ajustée facilement en fonction de la configuration de la pièce, ce qui permet d'obtenir une image toujours agréable, de jour comme de nuit.

Personnellement, j'apprécie particulièrement le mode d'image IMAX Enhanced pour regarder les films. Le rendu est vraiment remarquable.

Regardant régulièrement du football, je trouve simplement dommage que Sony n'ait pas intégré un mode Sport dédié dès la sortie du téléviseur. Peut-être qu'une future mise à jour viendra combler ce manque. Cela dit, il est clair que ce modèle a été conçu avant tout pour offrir une expérience cinéma de très haut niveau.

En SDR, j'ai remarqué que les rouges peuvent paraître un peu trop prononcés avec les réglages d'origine. Heureusement, ce point se corrige très facilement en ajustant quelques paramètres. En HDR, ce phénomène n'apparaît pas.

Enfin, il peut arriver de percevoir un léger effet de blooming (halo lumineux), principalement sur les sous-titres ou du texte blanc affiché sur un fond noir. Pour ma part, cela reste très discret et ne gêne absolument pas le visionnage.

Je recommande donc ce téléviseur sans la moindre hésitation. Pour ceux qui recherchent une excellente qualité d'image, une très bonne partie audio intégrée et une expérience cinéma immersive, le Sony Bravia 9 II est un excellent choix.

title: ...Più vicino che mai al BVM-HX3110!
body:
Parlo da quanto possessore di soli TV Sony, ma soprattutto pazzo per l'ultima vera ammiraglia A95L avuta in tutti i suoi polliciaggi..avendo ormai quasi 4 anni ho deciso di commettere questa follia, trovare un degno successore del tanto mio adorato A95l è stata dura a smuovermi e convincermi su questo nuovo gioiellino che mamma Sony stava silenziosamente lavorando sotto da decenni! E devo ammettere che ció che Sony garantiva lo fá eccome! La nuova tecnologia "TRUE RGB" è straordinaria. Gamma cromatica eccellente molto vicina ad un QD OLED e ottima uniformità dell'immagine, a cui si aggiungono le migliori caratteristiche di Sony in termini di upscaling, elaborazione del movimento e dei video, risultando così uno dei migliori televisori (MiniLED) mai visti fin'ora. Non esiste il televisore perfetto, e questo vale certamente anche per il Bravia 9 ii, che presenta alcune lacune in primis il marchio MASTER Series? Cosa mi combini Sony? in secondo piano poco influente per quanto riguarda il gaming la presenza di sole due porte HDMI 2.1, di cui una con eARC ( anche se per me non è stato mai un vero problema). Per ultimo il prezzo, si tratta di un televisore molto costoso se confrontato con altri modelli basati su tecnologia MiniLED, ovviamente non comparabili minimamente alla qualità d'immagine. Detto questo, Sony continua a garantire una delle migliori qualità d'immagine se non la migliore, una riproduzione del movimento e un upscaling straordinari, posizionandosi chiaramente ai vertici della categoria. 

• Per i piu esigenti qualche pensiero in merito

L'impostazione migliore out of the box come sempre è "Professionale", poiché cerca di rispettare gli standard del settore e di produrre una qualità dell'immagine che replichi quella di un monitor professionale Sony BVM-HX3110 e in vari casi siamo molto vicini ai livelli di riferimento assoluto. L'impostazione "Professionale" include alcune elaborazioni, come MotionFlow e Reality Creation, attivate di default, che ho disattivato prima di effettuare le misurazioni.
Nel complesso per una TV del genere una calibrazione sarebbe consigliata se si vuole tirar fuori il pieno potenziale che questo mostro riesce ad avere sia in resa cromatica quanto luminosità (tracciamento PQ EOTF superbo!) Sicuramente sará "la TV piú discussa di quest'anno e nei prossimi mesi a venire. Brava Sony!

title: Exactamente lo que necesito en un tv
body:
Llevo poco tiempo con la bravia 9 II de 65".
En lo que a mi se refiere, he estado mucho tiempo investigando marcas y modelos, y puedo decir que esta tv me ofrece todo lo que buscaba.
Posee un alto contraste de colores, en especial de los negros y los blancos.
Hay muchas opciones de configuración y disponer de modo Cinema, al igual que de detalles como la amplificación de diálogos. las distintas opciones de sonido, hacen que realmente sea un aparato muy versátil para el más experto.
Pero lo más impactante es la pantalla mate, la cual, incluso apagada, es espectacular, en mi caso, suspendida en la pared con el Soporte de Sony. Es una ventaja muy importante para mí, poder disfrutar de una alta calidad de imagen, cuando el 90% del contenido que consumo es de día.
Poder ver una película con tan alta calidad de imagen, y que no tengas ni un solo reflejo, hacen que valga su peso en oro.
Las muchas posibilidades de conexión me ha resultado muy útiles, ya que yo las uso prácticamente todas. Si es cierto que echo de menos algún hdmi 2.1 más, ya que solo posee dos, de los cuales uno de ellos lo tienes que sacrificar para acoplar la barra de sonido.
A mi no me afecta, ya que, a parte de un reproductor para las películas, no tengo intención de usarlos para consolas o juegos.
Diría que es lo único que puede tener como punto débil, aunque, como digo, a mi no me afecta.
Dicho todo esto, creo que vale lo que pagas.
Aún teniendo más fondo que otras tv que presumen de ser ultrafinas, te puedo asegurar que, una vez la tienes instalada, sobre todo con soporte y suspendida, el resultado es un auténtico espectáculo.

title: Sony Bravia 9 MII 65"
body:
Televizi vlastním teprve 16 dní, ale už jsem stihl nasbírat první zkušenosti.

Televize je připojena přes HDMI k set-top boxu Octagon SF8008 pro příjem TV programů. O zvuk se stará AV receiver Onkyo TX-NR696, propojený přes eARC HDMI, díky čemuž bez problémů přehrává všechny podporované zvukové formáty. Dokoupil jsem také podsvícení Govee TV Backlight 3S Pro a univerzální ovladač SofaBaton U3.

Obraz

Kvalita obrazu samozřejmě závisí na zdroji signálu nebo kvalitě filmu. Současná filmová tvorba vypadá výborně a i běžné HD vysílání díky kvalitnímu upscalingu působí výrazně lépe než na starších LCD televizích. Barvy jsou živé, obraz je ostrý a televizor si skvěle poradí i při sledování z větších pozorovacích úhlů.

Filmy přehrávám po domácí síti přes DLNA (počítač mám o patro výš) pomocí aplikace Kodi přímo v televizi. Vše funguje naprosto plynule, nic se neseká a kvalita přehrávání je výborná. Samozřejmě i zde záleží na kvalitě samotného filmu. Například seriál Halo ve 4K vypadá naprosto úžasně. Pokud si pustíte 4K ukázky na YouTube, například od kanálu jennifergala, jen těžko budete chtít jinou televizi.

Televizi mám umístěnou ve světlém pokoji a používám automatické řízení jasu. Poprvé v životě nemusím odpoledne zatahovat žaluzie, když na obrazovku svítí slunce. Antireflexní vrstva funguje opravdu skvěle a obraz zůstává perfektně čitelný i za denního světla.

Má to ale jednu nevýhodu – antireflexní vrstva je velmi citlivá na otisky prstů. Bohužel se mi při čištění otisku dlaně podařilo v pravém horním rohu pravděpodobně částečně narušit její povrch. Naštěstí je drobná šmouha viditelná pouze při vypnuté obrazovce, během sledování není vůbec patrná. Přesto to byl infarktový okamžik. Doporučuji při manipulaci s televizí mít čisté ruce, případně použít bavlněné rukavice. Na YouTube se tomuto tématu věnuje také kanál WybierzTV. Jejich recenzi této televize mohu také doporučit.

Zvuk

Zvuk samotné televize mě příjemně překvapil. Podle mého názoru nemá smysl dokupovat soundbar. Pokud chcete ještě lepší zážitek, pak jedině domácí kino. Já používám receiver Onkyo a přes eARC fungují bez problémů všechny zvukové formáty.

Ovládání

Součástí balení jsou dva ovladače. Jeden klasický infračervený s větším množstvím funkcí a druhý Bluetooth ovladač pro každodenní používání. Ten je podsvícený, dobíjí se přes USB-C, reaguje velmi svižně a není nutné s ním mířit přímo na televizi.

Menu televize je přehledné a samozřejmě umožňuje instalaci dalších aplikací. Já jsem si pořídil univerzální ovladač SofaBaton U3, který bez problémů načetl všechna moje zařízení z databáze. Ovladač je podsvícený, má programovatelná tlačítka i displej, takže mi na stolku místo tří ovladačů stačí jediný.

Závěr

Po vybalení jsem televizor téměř nenastavoval. Provedl jsem pouze dvě drobné úpravy kvůli fungování podsvícení Govee. Celkově jsem s televizí maximálně spokojený. Jedinou nevýhodou je vysoká cena, i když vzhledem k tomu, co nabízí, je zřejmě opodstatněná. Podle mě jde o důstojného konkurenta OLED televizí. Nabízí špičkový obraz, výborný zvuk a díky antireflexní vrstvě je ideální i do velmi světlých místností.

title: À Sony de prouver qu'il est encore Sony !
body:
LES PLUS :
* Design tout en finesse et en élégance, vraiment réussi !
* Anti reflet excellent dans son efficacité, mais surtout en ce qui me concerne, pour le très subtil effet de texture qu'il apporte à l'image, la rapprochant ainsi de l'expérience de rendu de la projection en salle de cinéma.
* Un pic lumineux à 4000 nits très appréciables, non pas pour regarder ses programmes en plein jour (!!!), mais pour la marge de gradation et d'ajustement subtil que cela permet dans les hautes et basses lumières, et donc la façon dont cela magnifie l'image (à condition de la faire calibrer).
* Tout l'héritage, l'expérience, l'expertise, et le savoir faire unique de Sony en matière d'image et de cinéma, dans le rendu visuel de ce téléviseur...
* pour une image très cinéma, naturelle, riche, cohérente, homogène, organique...
* ... grâce à l'ADN de Sony et la qualité unique de son post-traitement vidéo, jusque là inégalé sur un téléviseur grand public !
* Par conséquent un TV qui mérite amplement d'être calibré par un professionnel  quelques temps après l'achat, pour en tirer le meilleur et lui permettre d'offrir ce pourquoi il est fait : un rendu visuel au plus proche des normes de l'industrie du cinéma, et donc de la vision du réalisateur !
* Rendu sonore très correct compte tenu de la finesse du châssis
* Fluidité de navigation de Google TV
* Télécommande rétro éclairée... enfin !

LES MOINS :
* Où est le label "Master Series" ?!  Un abandon impardonnable de cette certification qualité !
* Une qualité de fabrication qui s'en ressent : c'est soigné, mais pas à la hauteur de ce que ça pu être...
* Un cordon secteur ridicule et non détachable (qu'on ne peut donc pas remplacer) totalement indigne d'un tel téléviseur !
* Un pieds non réglable en hauteur : une barre de son trop haute pourrait masquer une partie du bas de l'écran si elle repose sur le même plan que le pieds du téléviseur...
* Un calibrage usine avec un un déséquilibre du rouge sur le SDR, non encore corrigé malgré une mise à jour firmware !!
* Seulement deux ports HDMI sur quatre, en 2.1a 48 Gbps
(À chacun de voir si c'est un réel manque ou non)
* Une prise Ethernet toujours honteusement limitée à 100 MBs
* Un écran d'accueil Google TV de plus en plus verrouillé et dont on ne peut pour ainsi dire plus personnaliser le contenu affiché !
* Une application "Sony Picture Core" qui aurait pu/dû être vraiment excellente, mais dont le concept (mêlant token, VOD, abonnement) est resté mal pensé, peu ergonomique, inutilement complexe, avec un modèle économique désagréable ! La qualité des flux audio/vidéo, le très gros point fort de l'application, a beau être excellente, à un moment ça ne suffit plus à l'utiliser avec plaisir..
* Des "Change Log" de firmware toujours aussi peu explicites : Sony continue de dissimuler en grande partie les détails des modifications apportées par chaque nouveau firmware !

body:
The picture is great vibrant. Bright. Integrated Google OS makes for excellent inter device communication. And the OS fies a great job of compiling suggestions from all my different streaming services. Better than their native applications. It's my first 4k device and I chose the p model because of it's nits rating 350 is pretty good in class. And qled doesn't suffer the burn in problems common with oled.  Gaming integration is pretty good as well the dedicated mode switching seamlessly when I activate a game.band apparently it can switch to a higher Hz display rating in applications which support that. It is mounted to a wall using a vepa mount and the mounting process was fairly easy.though it's a two person job with a 65inch screen. Sound is really very good to my previous TV. It actually has some bass. And reproduction is good enough to listen to some music and still enjoy the output. Overall I highly recommend this device. The only downside is that in a dark room on a black screen it's possible to see some led lights leak in a completely black image. Obviously this model doesn't have local dimming and it isn't oled. So for my needs that's fine. It doesn't affect dark movies or games. It's about relative light and dark, chiaroscuro. If there any light nearby on screen you will not see it ghosting. And it's only totally black images that seem to suffer with this. I have no issues with it personally. Tcl have done a good job of delivering a large, bright, and enjoyable viewing experience at a fair price. That doesn't compromise on sound or usability, with excellent software integration.
 A great buying experience from a great company, selling great products.  I cant reccomend them highly enough. Far out in front of their competitors.

body:
Firstly, the price and quality of this TV, and its intended use on my part, is pretty good. The unit feels solid, and the remote control has all of the functionality of what you expect at this price range. Picture quality is pretty good, too. Not quite up there with some of the more expensive counterparts on the market at 3 or 4 times the price. But it is good enough for the purposes I purchased this unit for. As for sound, well, let's just say that there is a reason for sound bars. It isn't like this model has the worst sounding speakers on the market. They are what they are for a television which is as thin and light as this unit it.

This model uses Google TV for its OS. This is excellent because some manufacturers use their own proprietary software, which, i feel, has limited functionality. Google TV just has a familiarity about it that makes me feel comfortable. And allows mole way more freedom to install apps that may not be available on proprietary operating systems. 

From when i first set this television up, there have been a couple of issues that I have found with this TV. I have experienced an issue that seems to only only occur when turning the television on from standby. The first is these multiple weird lines of graphical artifacts popping up and disappearing on screen. This has happened to me twice now inside of a week and I am unsure of why this happens. Another issue I have experienced has been an extreme brightness, again, when turning the unit on from standby.  It is like the whole screen is washed out in a very high brightness. With both issues explained above, simply turning the unit off into standby mode and switching back on again clears it.

Overall, I am happy with this model. I only use it for playing games on both PlayStation and Xbox, which does very well. With its low price and performance, for someone needing a unit for primarily playing video games on, you would be hard pressed to find a better alternative than this.
It is a good device, I am still exploring all the vast options which exist on this TV

body:
This TV is excellent value for money. I'd rate it at 4.5 stars but that was not an option here. It's a very smart looking TV with a narrow bezel and is only 95.9 cm wide. It came supplied with wide-spaced feet which didn't work for my location but easily remedied with an after-market VESA centre stand.

Picture quality is superb, lots of useful features and surprisingly very little interface lag. Channels can be selected through the EPG or added to favourites for convenience. The EPG has the option to view previous days' programmes and most are clickable to launch the relevant on-demand app and stream it, which is useful.

The remote is ergonomic and has a quality feel to it. It has dedicated buttons for quick access to Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video etc. and a useful voice search option. Hands-free voice search is available too.

Lots of apps included with more available directly through the Google Play Store. Freeview Play is included as is a satellite cable input which pulls in loads of Astra 19.2°E channels with a suitable LNB. 

Slight niggles:

1. There is an optical out socket on the rear but no option to select it in the menu. As a workaround I have ARC selected which results in muted internal speakers and a working optical soundbar, as required.

2. Dolby Vision streaming content is locked to a Dolby Vision preset which produces a poorer viewing experience for me than I've achieved with the Standard or Smart HDR presets.

3. Dolby Vision also changes movie brightness slightly out of sync to scene changes which is annoying. This could be fixed in a software update but is another reason that users should have the option to choose an alternative picture preset.

4. Unable to pause/rewind live TV despite having a USB 3 port on the rear.

Pros massively outweigh the cons. Highly recommended. Comes with a TCL manufacturer's 2 year guarantee.

It’s a budget tv, but it’s a good budget tv. The UI can be sluggish compared to the brands that cost twice as much, but the picture is better than what you would get on their similarly priced offerings. Four stars because the built in speakers are not very good - sound is increasingly tinny with volume, but add a soundbar or plug in to your hifi and you’re golden.

body:
Good Points: The TCL 43C645K stands out as the top Android TV in its price range, offering an impressive display and a ton of smart features. As an owner, I've been absolutely amazed by the performance and functionality this television brings to my entertainment setup.

The picture quality of this TV is simply outstanding. The 4K HDR Pro display delivers spectacular detail, vibrant colours, and enhanced contrast, making gaming on my PS5 an absolute delight. Although the panel has a 60Hz refresh rate, it doesn't hinder the overall experience. Sitting down in the evenings to watch HDR documentaries on Netflix or 4K films on Disney+ is a treat, and the value for the price is truly remarkable.

Equally impressive is the audio performance, thanks to Dolby Atmos technology. The sound is rich, immersive, and dynamic, creating a truly cinematic atmosphere. The bass is particularly impressive, and while a soundbar could enhance the experience further, I personally haven't felt the need for one.

The smart features of this television are up-to-date and user-friendly. Powered by an intuitive Android-based operating system, navigating through apps and streaming services is generally seamless. The built-in Wi-Fi makes it incredibly convenient to launch apps like iPlayer and ITV for catch-up TV, something I find myself doing quite often. 

In terms of design, the TV boasts a sleek and modern look. The bezel-less slim metal frame enhances the viewing experience by drawing focus to the content on the screen. Additionally, the slim profile adds a visually appealing touch to my bedroom.

Improvement Points: One minor drawback I've come across is that the remote control could be more user-friendly. While it gets the job done, it feels a bit clunky, and I haven't quite memorized the muscle memory for common buttons like volume controls or menu keys.

It’s worth noting that there can be occasional noticeable lag in the OS, especially when switching between apps. Thankfully, this doesn't significantly impact the TV's usability, but it's something to keep in mind.

body:
Beautiful bright pictures with detail
Easy to install (if you know what you are doing)
Can’t really think what else say as it appears perfect

I received this as an early Christmas present as my TV had broken at only 18 months old. 

Would I have picked the TCL, no but that’s due to not hearing of the brand. I’m tech savvy so installation was quick and easy. I enjoyed setting it up and playing with the settings. 

Pros: it looks sleek, has great features such as Airplay, Spotify and all known apps. The sound is fantastic. The screen to frame ratio is great. All round a good TV. 

Cons: To get to the App or TV it is convoluted. The steps to get to each one is long. It doesn’t support Freeview which is ridiculous. The screensaver cannot be turned off through ambient mode nor if you sign into your google account. The Home Screen is messy and unnecessary. I turned the TV on and sports mode had turned itself on and the picture was shaky and lagging. It took me a long winded route to turn it off. 
With the screensaver activating whenever I pause the tv especially in apps it always returns to the home page which annoys the hell out of me. I have been in advanced settings, forums and tried every which way. Turning energy’s saving off. Adjusting the time it comes on. Worst of all it never saves the settings for the pictures shown, it will say that it showing X theme but it will go back to google pictures which are like the windows pictures you see on windows screen savers so it’s not even aesthetically pleasing. 
I came home one day and the TV had turned itself on. 
The continue watching doesn’t go to the show and just start it goes to the home page of whichever app. So it’s pointless. 
Apps that you have to accept term and conditions it shows EVERY time you open. Which doesn’t happen on my Mac or my old TV(different make). 

Each of these issues I’ve researched and even gone on TCL for solutions but they never work. 

While I appreciate the high resolution and sound, not being able to pause a show to make dinner or go to the bathroom without a thousand steps doesn’t make it enjoyable or worth the price. That’s basic stuff. TCL need to work out these kinks. Also the basic TV such as freebies being unavailable is ridiculous, don’t give me TCL, give me normal channels that can be paused or recorded. 

I hate looking at the windows screensaver even tho I’ve selected entirely different ones if you’re going to force me to watch them if I pause the TV. I have selected the longest time (10 minutes) which in itself is ridiculous. But still the crappy ones show. I’ve tried this without signing into Google. Still happens. 

I’ve used each format to change the settings, still not avail. 

The Apps only option is no good and but do I want to see adverts every time I open the TV? No. The Home Screen should be what you’re watching, apps and TV options but signed in to Google and not, the first thing you see is adverts. 

Overall not sleek and appealing, with technical issues that don’t need to be a thing in 2025.

body:
I recently picked up the TCL 55C7K to replace my old TV, and overall, I’ve been really impressed. I'm coming from an older six-year-old HiSense with the sluggish VIDAA OS (it struggled to load certain apps, especially Amazon Prime), and I also have a much fancier LG OLED in another room, so I have a good baseline for comparison.

The TV was packaged well—everything was neat and there wasn't a ton of waste. The stand seemed a little thin initially but holds the TV up perfectly fine.

A quick note if you're wall-mounting: my existing slimline brackets were a minor headache. If I positioned the hangers to match position of previous TV on the wall, they got in the way of this TV's subwoofers. So I had to move the bracket on the wall slightly, but since there are no mounting standards between TV models about how high/low TV will be once mounted, I can’t blame TCL for that.

The initial setup was a breeze. The best part is the software. Google TV is simple and powerful, and I honestly prefer it over both the old VIDAA and the LG webOS. The TV was quick to scan channels from my antenna and the free channels from my satellite dish (Astra 28.2E).

Once it was running, the picture quality was sublime. The blacks are deep, and I noticed very little bloom. It’s not quite OLED level, but it gets incredibly close, and it is much brighter. That extra brightness really makes HDR videos pop off the screen. 4K content looks fantastic with rich colours and deep contrast right away.

The great thing is that this performance is straight out of the box—in standard picture mode with energy saving on—without needing any fiddling or calibration. Who wants to buy a new TV just to spend time adjusting the settings? Not me.

Another major plus is the audio. It sounds clearly richer and has more weight than I expected. In fact, the built-in sound is definitely better than the audio on my more expensive LG OLED in the other room.

Final Verdict

I'm truly impressed and delighted with this TV. Considering it's about 40% cheaper than a similar-sized OLED, you get some major benefits—huge gains in sheer brightness and genuinely better audio—for a lot less money. Highly recommend it for regular folks looking for a big upgrade.

body:
It's a great TV. It's my first 4k tv and I was on a budget, so I researched and the TCLC635 range got overall good results but with some caveats. The caveats are that the controls are a bit finicky - with settings being hidden in multiple layers within layers, but once you find where they are it's not so bad. Also, my particular one has a "fair" amount of LED panel bleed - to be expected I suppose - and overall it doesn't detract from the viewing experience, but it's slightly annoying in that I know it's there.
But... the actual picture is excellent - really good, and the different modes and settings can make for a wonderful home viewing experience, especially with 4K HDR content. The sound is actually pretty good too, not nearly as bad as a lot of reviewers say (as they're probably used to hearing everything through full surround setups).
Overall it's a really good TV and a great budget buy to try 4K home viewing.

I bought this for the living room but because of these problems I’ve had to swap it with my bedroom Toshiba tv. I can get more channels and it updates itself without any problem and it doesn't switch itself on during the night, unlike the Panacrap. Other than that I'd highly recommend it.

body:
Excellent TV for everyday viewing and streaming

I’m really impressed with the TCL P7K 50” QLED. The picture quality is sharp and vibrant, with great colours and strong brightness for both daytime and evening viewing. 4K content looks fantastic, and even HD channels are upscaled nicely.

Google TV runs smoothly and makes it easy to access apps like Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video and more, all in one place. The interface is fast and user-friendly, and voice control works well.

Sound quality is clear and decent for built-in speakers, and the TV feels well built with a modern, slim design that looks great in the room. Setup was quick and straightforward.

Overall, this is a reliable, high quality smart TV that performs very well for movies, sports and everyday use. Highly recommended.

body:
The picture is great vibrant. Bright. Integrated Google OS makes for excellent inter device communication. And the OS fies a great job of compiling suggestions from all my different streaming services. Better than their native applications. It's my first 4k device and I chose the p model because of it's nits rating 350 is pretty good in class. And qled doesn't suffer the burn in problems common with oled.  Gaming integration is pretty good as well the dedicated mode switching seamlessly when I activate a game.band apparently it can switch to a higher Hz display rating in applications which support that. It is mounted to a wall using a vepa mount and the mounting process was fairly easy.though it's a two person job with a 65inch screen. Sound is really very good to my previous TV. It actually has some bass. And reproduction is good enough to listen to some music and still enjoy the output. Overall I highly recommend this device. The only downside is that in a dark room on a black screen it's possible to see some led lights leak in a completely black image. Obviously this model doesn't have local dimming and it isn't oled. So for my needs that's fine. It doesn't affect dark movies or games. It's about relative light and dark, chiaroscuro. If there any light nearby on screen you will not see it ghosting. And it's only totally black images that seem to suffer with this. I have no issues with it personally. Tcl have done a good job of delivering a large, bright, and enjoyable viewing experience at a fair price. That doesn't compromise on sound or usability, with excellent software integration.
 A great buying experience from a great company, selling great products.  I cant reccomend them highly enough. Far out in front of their competitors.

body:
Firstly, the price and quality of this TV, and its intended use on my part, is pretty good. The unit feels solid, and the remote control has all of the functionality of what you expect at this price range. Picture quality is pretty good, too. Not quite up there with some of the more expensive counterparts on the market at 3 or 4 times the price. But it is good enough for the purposes I purchased this unit for. As for sound, well, let's just say that there is a reason for sound bars. It isn't like this model has the worst sounding speakers on the market. They are what they are for a television which is as thin and light as this unit it.

This model uses Google TV for its OS. This is excellent because some manufacturers use their own proprietary software, which, i feel, has limited functionality. Google TV just has a familiarity about it that makes me feel comfortable. And allows mole way more freedom to install apps that may not be available on proprietary operating systems. 

From when i first set this television up, there have been a couple of issues that I have found with this TV. I have experienced an issue that seems to only only occur when turning the television on from standby. The first is these multiple weird lines of graphical artifacts popping up and disappearing on screen. This has happened to me twice now inside of a week and I am unsure of why this happens. Another issue I have experienced has been an extreme brightness, again, when turning the unit on from standby.  It is like the whole screen is washed out in a very high brightness. With both issues explained above, simply turning the unit off into standby mode and switching back on again clears it.

Overall, I am happy with this model. I only use it for playing games on both PlayStation and Xbox, which does very well. With its low price and performance, for someone needing a unit for primarily playing video games on, you would be hard pressed to find a better alternative than this.
It is a good device, I am still exploring all the vast options which exist on this TV

Extremely disappointing – nowhere near the picture quality advertised

TCL advertises this TV as an impressive, high-quality television with a fantastic picture. Unfortunately, my experience has been completely different.

The picture is unclear and faces look strangely soft and over-smoothed. Fine details are missing, even on people sitting in a studio. I have spent three days trying different picture settings, adjusting almost everything possible, and unfortunately I still cannot get a natural-looking picture.

The colours are also very strange. The green is extremely aggressive and unnatural, and there is a noticeable blue/green cast. The screen does not look properly black either — dark areas often appear more like a very dark, dirty green.

I have tried different picture modes and settings, including adjusting brightness, contrast, sharpness and the various picture-processing options. Nothing has solved the problem.

This is a brand-new television, straight from the shop, so I am starting to wonder whether there is something wrong with the panel or the software. Whatever the reason, the result is the same: the picture is simply not good enough to enjoy watching TV.

What makes this even more disappointing is that my 13-year-old LG produces a much sharper, more natural and more detailed picture. I genuinely expected a modern TCL like this to be a huge improvement, especially considering how impressive the picture is made to look in TCL's advertising and online reviews.

Instead, I feel extremely disappointed with this purchase. I expected something genuinely impressive, but unfortunately the picture quality is nowhere near what I expected.

After this experience, I would seriously think twice before buying another TCL television.

author: KAYLEIGH

body:
Buckle up for this rollercoaster of a review

Each part of this reviews makes a star rating harder. I’m just going to tell you how it is….

I had an LG C3 65inch…. Long story short I needed a replacement. So…. I chose the Q7C 75inch

The installation, the good part. It was free, (you have to provide the bracket). That’s obviously great, you don’t have to pay for installation…. I used the same bracket the LG was on (saving them a job) the bracket was flat to the wall (my mistake, but worked fine on the LG). They turned up with the tv about 5pm ish (young guy with his even younger helper). It’s a massive TV box. They were happy to see the bracket on the wall… they took the tv out, and attached the brackets arms on the tv (these arms have an adjustable screw on top to help with alignment, very important part of the review)…. So they lifted up the tv and as they stood it up the younger lad peeled of all the protective screen covering (****, is he doing I thought) I asked him politely excuse me young chap why have you done that? That’s the last thing you do isn’t it? His reply was a disgruntled grunt… (English wasn’t his first language, but tbh I don’t have a 2nd language to fall back on). So they picked up the TV with their grubby hands now on the edges of the screen…. They proceed to clip the tv on to the bracket in place, instantly the tv is massively higher one side than the other…. No problem I thought just get your long screw driver out and make the adjustment…. Another problem arose, they didn’t have one…. So off the tv came, not as easy as you think Bcus the arms click in to place, and you have to pull the release strings whilst moving the tv towards you.. soooo the 2 guys did this whilst I’m pulling the strings…. And now if I had spoken a 2nd language it really would’ve come in handy at this point, Bcus they weren’t lifting at the same time I was pulling the strings, it became a difficult task…. So the tv came off and adjustments were made, and back on the wall it went, still not level. Off it came,,, (same break down in communication occurred). Further adjustments were made, back on the wall it went, I’m not going to bore you all, but this happened 5-6 times. They couldn’t figure out which way to turn the screws when it was off the wall and they didn’t understand me telling them… after 30/40 mins and tempers frayed, and I’m sure some derogatory language used (I could’ve leant a 2nd language in the time it was taken). We all got the tv on the wall and it was perfectly level (I had became an honorary member of their team). I then noticed a greyed out pixel (bottom left) it wasnt dead but wasn’t active. I mentioned this and again communication was an issue… I believe they said they could take it away again and I’d have to wait a week for another…. At this point they could see I wasn’t happy. Especially as I had already signed for it. So with it now being 6:30pm. Yep, one and a half hours to unpack and put it on the wall (I installed the LG C3 by myself in less time on the same bracket)… so they left and I got out a cloth to wipe there dirty sweaty finger prints off of the side of the tv……

So the TV

After some picture settings adjustments the picture is amazing…. UHD content is crystal clear and HD content is just as good. It does have to be seen to be believed that a £1000 75” TV is as good as the LG C3 (granted it is a new model). The game settings are also great… the sound is also another area that’s better than I thought especially with Dolby Atmos….. there’s not much to fault…. But here comes the downside…..

The menus are slow to react… there’s also an energy warning message when you change picture preset (and no it can’t be turn off) it gets annoying to say the least….

Oh the NOWtv app UHD isn’t compatible with the TCL TVS, (this is from the NOWtv support team) so don’t buy the NOWtv ultra boost. Don’t know why it’s just not compatible.

The discovery plus app is really laggy when watching HD/UHD live sport… apparently it’s to do with the processor of the TV (NETFLIX UHD works perfectly tho, so ***). The reason it’s the TVs processor is Bcus when I watch the Discovery Plus app through the Xbox, there’s no lag what’s so ever…

With it being an android tv… you’ll have to have a google account…. If you have that the tv is a breeze to set up once it’s connected to your WiFi.

Oh lastly the Disney app works fine in UHD and Tron really has to be seen to be amazed !!!

So the scores

Installation 0/5

(we can all agree on that)

Picture 5/5

Operating system 3/5

Sound 4/5

App 4/5

(When they work)

Value 5/5

Overall 4/5

If you want a tv with loads of features at the best price then this is the tv for you… but the cost comes with a few annoying features but size and actual picture isn’t two of them..!!

Mayb buy it else where or just get the LG C3 or C5 65” then you can’t really go wrong at all with those televisions.

UPDATED 14/03/26

Knocking it down

So the NEW scores

Installation 0/5

(we can all agree on that)

Picture 5/5

Operating system 1/5

Sound 4/5

App 2.5/5

(When they work)

Value 3.5/5

Overall 3/5

The operating system is so laggy… opening up Prime Video takes 20/30 seconds…. (Yes I know it’s not long but when comparing to opening the app on an Xbox, there’s a noticeable difference.)

You have to keep closing all the apps and deleting the cache, there’s an app called Safe Guard pre-installed, it specifically does the deleting, so obviously there aware of this issue.

Soooo….. would I buy it again knowing these issues??? I dunno tbh…. The picture is amazing… the system is terrible… so buy a fire stick, use a console with the apps on and these issues disappear… or buy an LG

27/3/26
There’s been a firmware update… and the operating system has been improved. Amazon Video App opens a lot quicker now!!!
Perfect for gaming and sports has options in sound settings for watching sports and one for gaming, has Google app store for your apps so no need for a fire stick

body:
Only had the TV for a couple of days, then returned it as it wasn’t what I expected. Don’t get me wrong, the value for money for an 85” is outstanding these days, but I just don’t have high picture quality expectations or expect it to pull off incredible HDR. 

Pros: size to value
          Ok picture quality 
          Cinematic size 

Cons: matte anti-reflective coating
           Micro stutter like all TCL TV’s
           Green push-in colour 
           Not that bright

So the size is amazing as you’re getting that cinematic immersion, with ok picture quality.
But the colours had a weird green tint out of the box, which I found very distracting. You can correct it to a degree with the white balance settings, but then you’ll be pushing other colours slightly off without realising it. Could have just been a slightly faulty unit though, so who knows as others may not be experiencing this. The matte screen is great, and you’ll love it if you only watch this tv in a sun-soaked room or a room with major lighting that you never turn off. It’s brilliant at handling reflections in these scenarios, but the downside of that is the contrast takes a massive hit. You have to keep this thing pretty much maxed out with brightness and contrast to actually look decent. So as soon as you dim the lights or switch them off, or you close your curtains as the sun’s gone down, then switch it into, say, filmmaker mode, which dims the unit down, then it struggled to look good as it’s having to fight the matte screen from within to push out the contrast to make the image look clean and clear, so it left it looking flat and dull, unfortunately.

So if you only watch in daytime bright rooms, then yes, get this tv but if you have a mixed usage and like watching in the evenings or darker room movie nights, then I’d probably skip this tv altogether.

body:
I recently picked up the TCL 55C7K to replace my old TV, and overall, I’ve been really impressed. I'm coming from an older six-year-old HiSense with the sluggish VIDAA OS (it struggled to load certain apps, especially Amazon Prime), and I also have a much fancier LG OLED in another room, so I have a good baseline for comparison.

The TV was packaged well—everything was neat and there wasn't a ton of waste. The stand seemed a little thin initially but holds the TV up perfectly fine.

A quick note if you're wall-mounting: my existing slimline brackets were a minor headache. If I positioned the hangers to match position of previous TV on the wall, they got in the way of this TV's subwoofers. So I had to move the bracket on the wall slightly, but since there are no mounting standards between TV models about how high/low TV will be once mounted, I can’t blame TCL for that.

The initial setup was a breeze. The best part is the software. Google TV is simple and powerful, and I honestly prefer it over both the old VIDAA and the LG webOS. The TV was quick to scan channels from my antenna and the free channels from my satellite dish (Astra 28.2E).

Once it was running, the picture quality was sublime. The blacks are deep, and I noticed very little bloom. It’s not quite OLED level, but it gets incredibly close, and it is much brighter. That extra brightness really makes HDR videos pop off the screen. 4K content looks fantastic with rich colours and deep contrast right away.

The great thing is that this performance is straight out of the box—in standard picture mode with energy saving on—without needing any fiddling or calibration. Who wants to buy a new TV just to spend time adjusting the settings? Not me.

Another major plus is the audio. It sounds clearly richer and has more weight than I expected. In fact, the built-in sound is definitely better than the audio on my more expensive LG OLED in the other room.

Final Verdict

I'm truly impressed and delighted with this TV. Considering it's about 40% cheaper than a similar-sized OLED, you get some major benefits—huge gains in sheer brightness and genuinely better audio—for a lot less money. Highly recommend it for regular folks looking for a big upgrade.

body: Nice android tv for the price

This TV is perfect for if you have a next generation console (PS5/XBOX SERIES X) and like high resolution and high quality gaming. Definitely use the game mode settings, when i first used the TV the first word used to describe it was crispy, it really is that quality sharp tv you’re looking for. The brand in general is one of the best on the market too, i’d definitely recommend over samsung and those others.

People should just make it their mission to see one of these brilliant Tv's in action! If people are not totally amazed at the quality in all areas that you get for the unbelievably low price then I have no idea what will! The only little gripe a have is that the pre-sets need to be tweaked, and to be honest I thought I would have to get my Tv professionally tuned, but I easily found the solution of how to do this on YouTube!

One of the very few budget smart TVs that support both Chromecast and AirPlay! Most TVs under £400 have stopped supporting Chromecast for some support, which should be a basic functionality really as casting from any phone is so convenient instead of using the keyboard with TV remote which is just painful. The TV quality is good too, sharp and vibrant with Google Assistant built in.
Fantastic picture quality and sound well worth the money

body:
It's a great TV. It's my first 4k tv and I was on a budget, so I researched and the TCLC635 range got overall good results but with some caveats. The caveats are that the controls are a bit finicky - with settings being hidden in multiple layers within layers, but once you find where they are it's not so bad. Also, my particular one has a "fair" amount of LED panel bleed - to be expected I suppose - and overall it doesn't detract from the viewing experience, but it's slightly annoying in that I know it's there.
But... the actual picture is excellent - really good, and the different modes and settings can make for a wonderful home viewing experience, especially with 4K HDR content. The sound is actually pretty good too, not nearly as bad as a lot of reviewers say (as they're probably used to hearing everything through full surround setups).
Overall it's a really good TV and a great budget buy to try 4K home viewing.

body:
The picture is great vibrant. Bright. Integrated Google OS makes for excellent inter device communication. And the OS fies a great job of compiling suggestions from all my different streaming services. Better than their native applications. It's my first 4k device and I chose the p model because of it's nits rating 350 is pretty good in class. And qled doesn't suffer the burn in problems common with oled.  Gaming integration is pretty good as well the dedicated mode switching seamlessly when I activate a game.band apparently it can switch to a higher Hz display rating in applications which support that. It is mounted to a wall using a vepa mount and the mounting process was fairly easy.though it's a two person job with a 65inch screen. Sound is really very good to my previous TV. It actually has some bass. And reproduction is good enough to listen to some music and still enjoy the output. Overall I highly recommend this device. The only downside is that in a dark room on a black screen it's possible to see some led lights leak in a completely black image. Obviously this model doesn't have local dimming and it isn't oled. So for my needs that's fine. It doesn't affect dark movies or games. It's about relative light and dark, chiaroscuro. If there any light nearby on screen you will not see it ghosting. And it's only totally black images that seem to suffer with this. I have no issues with it personally. Tcl have done a good job of delivering a large, bright, and enjoyable viewing experience at a fair price. That doesn't compromise on sound or usability, with excellent software integration.
 A great buying experience from a great company, selling great products.  I cant reccomend them highly enough. Far out in front of their competitors.
