body:
Buckle up for this rollercoaster of a review

Each part of this reviews makes a star rating harder. I’m just going to tell you how it is….

I had an LG C3 65inch…. Long story short I needed a replacement. So…. I chose the Q7C 75inch

The installation, the good part. It was free, (you have to provide the bracket). That’s obviously great, you don’t have to pay for installation…. I used the same bracket the LG was on (saving them a job) the bracket was flat to the wall (my mistake, but worked fine on the LG). They turned up with the tv about 5pm ish (young guy with his even younger helper). It’s a massive TV box. They were happy to see the bracket on the wall… they took the tv out, and attached the brackets arms on the tv (these arms have an adjustable screw on top to help with alignment, very important part of the review)…. So they lifted up the tv and as they stood it up the younger lad peeled of all the protective screen covering (****, is he doing I thought) I asked him politely excuse me young chap why have you done that? That’s the last thing you do isn’t it? His reply was a disgruntled grunt… (English wasn’t his first language, but tbh I don’t have a 2nd language to fall back on). So they picked up the TV with their grubby hands now on the edges of the screen…. They proceed to clip the tv on to the bracket in place, instantly the tv is massively higher one side than the other…. No problem I thought just get your long screw driver out and make the adjustment…. Another problem arose, they didn’t have one…. So off the tv came, not as easy as you think Bcus the arms click in to place, and you have to pull the release strings whilst moving the tv towards you.. soooo the 2 guys did this whilst I’m pulling the strings…. And now if I had spoken a 2nd language it really would’ve come in handy at this point, Bcus they weren’t lifting at the same time I was pulling the strings, it became a difficult task…. So the tv came off and adjustments were made, and back on the wall it went, still not level. Off it came,,, (same break down in communication occurred). Further adjustments were made, back on the wall it went, I’m not going to bore you all, but this happened 5-6 times. They couldn’t figure out which way to turn the screws when it was off the wall and they didn’t understand me telling them… after 30/40 mins and tempers frayed, and I’m sure some derogatory language used (I could’ve leant a 2nd language in the time it was taken). We all got the tv on the wall and it was perfectly level (I had became an honorary member of their team). I then noticed a greyed out pixel (bottom left) it wasnt dead but wasn’t active. I mentioned this and again communication was an issue… I believe they said they could take it away again and I’d have to wait a week for another…. At this point they could see I wasn’t happy. Especially as I had already signed for it. So with it now being 6:30pm. Yep, one and a half hours to unpack and put it on the wall (I installed the LG C3 by myself in less time on the same bracket)… so they left and I got out a cloth to wipe there dirty sweaty finger prints off of the side of the tv……

So the TV

After some picture settings adjustments the picture is amazing…. UHD content is crystal clear and HD content is just as good. It does have to be seen to be believed that a £1000 75” TV is as good as the LG C3 (granted it is a new model). The game settings are also great… the sound is also another area that’s better than I thought especially with Dolby Atmos….. there’s not much to fault…. But here comes the downside…..

The menus are slow to react… there’s also an energy warning message when you change picture preset (and no it can’t be turn off) it gets annoying to say the least….

Oh the NOWtv app UHD isn’t compatible with the TCL TVS, (this is from the NOWtv support team) so don’t buy the NOWtv ultra boost. Don’t know why it’s just not compatible.

The discovery plus app is really laggy when watching HD/UHD live sport… apparently it’s to do with the processor of the TV (NETFLIX UHD works perfectly tho, so ***). The reason it’s the TVs processor is Bcus when I watch the Discovery Plus app through the Xbox, there’s no lag what’s so ever…

With it being an android tv… you’ll have to have a google account…. If you have that the tv is a breeze to set up once it’s connected to your WiFi.

Oh lastly the Disney app works fine in UHD and Tron really has to be seen to be amazed !!!

So the scores

Installation 0/5

(we can all agree on that)

Picture 5/5

Operating system 3/5

Sound 4/5

App 4/5

(When they work)

Value 5/5

Overall 4/5

If you want a tv with loads of features at the best price then this is the tv for you… but the cost comes with a few annoying features but size and actual picture isn’t two of them..!!

Mayb buy it else where or just get the LG C3 or C5 65” then you can’t really go wrong at all with those televisions.

UPDATED 14/03/26

Knocking it down

So the NEW scores

Installation 0/5

(we can all agree on that)

Picture 5/5

Operating system 1/5

Sound 4/5

App 2.5/5

(When they work)

Value 3.5/5

Overall 3/5

The operating system is so laggy… opening up Prime Video takes 20/30 seconds…. (Yes I know it’s not long but when comparing to opening the app on an Xbox, there’s a noticeable difference.)

You have to keep closing all the apps and deleting the cache, there’s an app called Safe Guard pre-installed, it specifically does the deleting, so obviously there aware of this issue.

Soooo….. would I buy it again knowing these issues??? I dunno tbh…. The picture is amazing… the system is terrible… so buy a fire stick, use a console with the apps on and these issues disappear… or buy an LG

27/3/26
There’s been a firmware update… and the operating system has been improved. Amazon Video App opens a lot quicker now!!!
Perfect for gaming and sports has options in sound settings for watching sports and one for gaming, has Google app store for your apps so no need for a fire stick

body:
Extremely disappointing – nowhere near the picture quality advertised

TCL advertises this TV as an impressive, high-quality television with a fantastic picture. Unfortunately, my experience has been completely different.

The picture is unclear and faces look strangely soft and over-smoothed. Fine details are missing, even on people sitting in a studio. I have spent three days trying different picture settings, adjusting almost everything possible, and unfortunately I still cannot get a natural-looking picture.

The colours are also very strange. The green is extremely aggressive and unnatural, and there is a noticeable blue/green cast. The screen does not look properly black either — dark areas often appear more like a very dark, dirty green.

I have tried different picture modes and settings, including adjusting brightness, contrast, sharpness and the various picture-processing options. Nothing has solved the problem.

This is a brand-new television, straight from the shop, so I am starting to wonder whether there is something wrong with the panel or the software. Whatever the reason, the result is the same: the picture is simply not good enough to enjoy watching TV.

What makes this even more disappointing is that my 13-year-old LG produces a much sharper, more natural and more detailed picture. I genuinely expected a modern TCL like this to be a huge improvement, especially considering how impressive the picture is made to look in TCL's advertising and online reviews.

Instead, I feel extremely disappointed with this purchase. I expected something genuinely impressive, but unfortunately the picture quality is nowhere near what I expected.

After this experience, I would seriously think twice before buying another TCL television.

I recently upgraded from a 55” to the TCL Q7C 65” and honestly, I should have made the jump sooner. That extra 10 inches makes a bigger difference than I expected – the screen feels genuinely cinematic in my living room without being overwhelming.

I use it for everything – movies, sport, gaming, casual browsing – and it handles all of it brilliantly. But the picture quality is where this TV truly earns its stripes. The colours are rich and vibrant without looking overcooked, and the contrast is genuinely impressive for the price point. HDR content looks stunning, and even standard streaming holds up beautifully on that big panel. I noticed details in darker scenes I’d never picked up on my old TV.

author: KAYLEIGH

body:
Buckle up for this rollercoaster of a review

Each part of this reviews makes a star rating harder. I’m just going to tell you how it is….

I had an LG C3 65inch…. Long story short I needed a replacement. So…. I chose the Q7C 75inch

The installation, the good part. It was free, (you have to provide the bracket). That’s obviously great, you don’t have to pay for installation…. I used the same bracket the LG was on (saving them a job) the bracket was flat to the wall (my mistake, but worked fine on the LG). They turned up with the tv about 5pm ish (young guy with his even younger helper). It’s a massive TV box. They were happy to see the bracket on the wall… they took the tv out, and attached the brackets arms on the tv (these arms have an adjustable screw on top to help with alignment, very important part of the review)…. So they lifted up the tv and as they stood it up the younger lad peeled of all the protective screen covering (****, is he doing I thought) I asked him politely excuse me young chap why have you done that? That’s the last thing you do isn’t it? His reply was a disgruntled grunt… (English wasn’t his first language, but tbh I don’t have a 2nd language to fall back on). So they picked up the TV with their grubby hands now on the edges of the screen…. They proceed to clip the tv on to the bracket in place, instantly the tv is massively higher one side than the other…. No problem I thought just get your long screw driver out and make the adjustment…. Another problem arose, they didn’t have one…. So off the tv came, not as easy as you think Bcus the arms click in to place, and you have to pull the release strings whilst moving the tv towards you.. soooo the 2 guys did this whilst I’m pulling the strings…. And now if I had spoken a 2nd language it really would’ve come in handy at this point, Bcus they weren’t lifting at the same time I was pulling the strings, it became a difficult task…. So the tv came off and adjustments were made, and back on the wall it went, still not level. Off it came,,, (same break down in communication occurred). Further adjustments were made, back on the wall it went, I’m not going to bore you all, but this happened 5-6 times. They couldn’t figure out which way to turn the screws when it was off the wall and they didn’t understand me telling them… after 30/40 mins and tempers frayed, and I’m sure some derogatory language used (I could’ve leant a 2nd language in the time it was taken). We all got the tv on the wall and it was perfectly level (I had became an honorary member of their team). I then noticed a greyed out pixel (bottom left) it wasnt dead but wasn’t active. I mentioned this and again communication was an issue… I believe they said they could take it away again and I’d have to wait a week for another…. At this point they could see I wasn’t happy. Especially as I had already signed for it. So with it now being 6:30pm. Yep, one and a half hours to unpack and put it on the wall (I installed the LG C3 by myself in less time on the same bracket)… so they left and I got out a cloth to wipe there dirty sweaty finger prints off of the side of the tv……

So the TV

After some picture settings adjustments the picture is amazing…. UHD content is crystal clear and HD content is just as good. It does have to be seen to be believed that a £1000 75” TV is as good as the LG C3 (granted it is a new model). The game settings are also great… the sound is also another area that’s better than I thought especially with Dolby Atmos….. there’s not much to fault…. But here comes the downside…..

The menus are slow to react… there’s also an energy warning message when you change picture preset (and no it can’t be turn off) it gets annoying to say the least….

Oh the NOWtv app UHD isn’t compatible with the TCL TVS, (this is from the NOWtv support team) so don’t buy the NOWtv ultra boost. Don’t know why it’s just not compatible.

The discovery plus app is really laggy when watching HD/UHD live sport… apparently it’s to do with the processor of the TV (NETFLIX UHD works perfectly tho, so ***). The reason it’s the TVs processor is Bcus when I watch the Discovery Plus app through the Xbox, there’s no lag what’s so ever…

With it being an android tv… you’ll have to have a google account…. If you have that the tv is a breeze to set up once it’s connected to your WiFi.

Oh lastly the Disney app works fine in UHD and Tron really has to be seen to be amazed !!!

So the scores

Installation 0/5

(we can all agree on that)

Picture 5/5

Operating system 3/5

Sound 4/5

App 4/5

(When they work)

Value 5/5

Overall 4/5

If you want a tv with loads of features at the best price then this is the tv for you… but the cost comes with a few annoying features but size and actual picture isn’t two of them..!!

Mayb buy it else where or just get the LG C3 or C5 65” then you can’t really go wrong at all with those televisions.

UPDATED 14/03/26

Knocking it down

So the NEW scores

Installation 0/5

(we can all agree on that)

Picture 5/5

Operating system 1/5

Sound 4/5

App 2.5/5

(When they work)

Value 3.5/5

Overall 3/5

The operating system is so laggy… opening up Prime Video takes 20/30 seconds…. (Yes I know it’s not long but when comparing to opening the app on an Xbox, there’s a noticeable difference.)

You have to keep closing all the apps and deleting the cache, there’s an app called Safe Guard pre-installed, it specifically does the deleting, so obviously there aware of this issue.

Soooo….. would I buy it again knowing these issues??? I dunno tbh…. The picture is amazing… the system is terrible… so buy a fire stick, use a console with the apps on and these issues disappear… or buy an LG

27/3/26
There’s been a firmware update… and the operating system has been improved. Amazon Video App opens a lot quicker now!!!
Perfect for gaming and sports has options in sound settings for watching sports and one for gaming, has Google app store for your apps so no need for a fire stick
